# React Checkbox Components

> Create consistent cross-browser and cross-device checkboxes with our React checkbox components.

## Approach

`<CCheckbox>` renders the `<input type="checkbox">`. That is the whole control — no wrapper, no extra element. Checkboxes are for selecting one or several options in a list; for one option out of many, reach for a [radio](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/radio/).

The `label` property renders a sibling `<label>` already wired to the input with `htmlFor`, so the label can be styled from the input's state (`:checked`, `:disabled`). Wrap the pair in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) when you want the label, a description and validation feedback laid out for you.

The check and indeterminate marks are drawn with a CSS mask on the input's own `::before`, which is why their color is a token (`--cui-check-mark-color`) rather than a value baked into an SVG.

## Basic checkbox

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkDefault" label="Default checkbox" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkChecked" label="Checked checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Indeterminate

Checkboxes can use the `:indeterminate` pseudo-class when it is set from JavaScript — there is no HTML attribute for it, so `<CCheckbox>` sets it through the `indeterminate` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxIndeterminateExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CCheckbox id="checkIndeterminate" label="Indeterminate checkbox" indeterminate />
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` attribute; the associated `<label>` is styled to match, in a lighter color, to indicate the state.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkDisabled" label="Disabled checkbox" disabled />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox
          id="checkCheckedDisabled"
          label="Disabled checked checkbox"
          defaultChecked
          disabled
        />
      </CFormField>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Stacked

Any number of checkboxes that are immediate siblings stack vertically and are spaced by their `<CFormField>` wrappers.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxStackedExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="defaultCheck1" label="Default checkbox" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="defaultCheck2" label="Disabled checkbox" disabled />
      </CFormField>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Inline

There is no inline property: the control is an inline element, so a row is a flex container with a gap.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxInlineExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="d-flex gap-4">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineCheckbox1" value="option1" label="1" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineCheckbox2" value="option2" label="2" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineCheckbox3" value="option3" label="3 (disabled)" disabled />
      </CFormField>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Sizing

`size="sm"` and `size="lg"` size the whole row — the box, its label, and the space they sit in. Each sets one font size: the box is `1em`, so it follows, and so does the alignment margin, which is computed from the line. Nothing needs re-tuning per size, and a size of your own is one custom property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="d-flex align-items-start gap-4">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox size="sm" id="checkSm" label="Small" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkMd" label="Default" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox size="lg" id="checkLg" label="Large" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
    </div>
  )
}
```

Any other size is one custom property, and the alignment follows it:

```jsx
<CCheckbox style={{ '--cui-check-size': '2em' }} aria-label="..." />
```

## Without a label

A checkbox with no label text is the input on its own. Give it an accessible name some other way — `aria-label`, for instance. The name says what the checkbox does, like `aria-label="Select all rows"`, and replaces the `...` placeholder in the example below. See the [forms overview](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/overview/#accessibility) for details.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxWithoutLabelsExample = () => {
  return <CCheckbox id="checkboxNoLabel" value="" aria-label="..." />
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CCheckbox id="fieldCheck" label="Subscribe to the newsletter" />
      <CFormText>We send one email a month, and never share your address.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Checkbox toggle buttons

Create button-like checkboxes and radio buttons by using `button` boolean property on the `<CFormCheck>` component. These toggle buttons can further be grouped in a button group if needed. Toggle buttons use the deprecated `<CFormCheck>`'s button mode — it has no `<CCheckbox>` counterpart.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormCheck } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxToggleButtonsExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormCheck
        button={{ color: 'primary' }}
        id="btn-check"
        autoComplete="off"
        label="Single toggle"
      />
      <CFormCheck
        button={{ color: 'primary' }}
        id="btn-check-2"
        autoComplete="off"
        label="Checked"
        defaultChecked
      />
      <CFormCheck
        button={{ color: 'primary' }}
        id="btn-check-3"
        autoComplete="off"
        label="Disabled"
        disabled
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Outlined styles

Different variants of button, such at the various outlined styles, are supported.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormCheck } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxToggleButtonsOutlinedStylesExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormCheck
        button={{ color: 'primary', variant: 'outline' }}
        id="btn-check-outlined"
        autoComplete="off"
        label="Single toggle"
      />
      <CFormCheck
        button={{ color: 'secondary', variant: 'outline' }}
        id="btn-check-2-outlined"
        autoComplete="off"
        label="Checked"
        defaultChecked
      />
      <CFormCheck
        button={{ color: 'success', variant: 'outline' }}
        id="btn-check-3-outlined"
        autoComplete="off"
        label="Checked success"
        defaultChecked
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Theme variants

Modify the appearance of checked checkboxes with the [`theme`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) property — it sets the checked background and border color to the theme color.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxThemeColorsExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="d-flex flex-column gap-3">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox theme="primary" id="checkThemePrimary" label="Primary checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox
          theme="secondary"
          id="checkThemeSecondary"
          label="Secondary checkbox"
          defaultChecked
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox theme="success" id="checkThemeSuccess" label="Success checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox theme="danger" id="checkThemeDanger" label="Danger checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox theme="warning" id="checkThemeWarning" label="Warning checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox theme="info" id="checkThemeInfo" label="Info checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CCheckbox /&gt;](./api/#ccheckbox)
- [&lt;CFormCheck /&gt;](./api/#cformcheck)

# React Checkbox Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Checkbox component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCheckbox

```jsx
import { CCheckbox } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the input. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | - | Display the checkbox in an indeterminate state - there is no HTML attribute for it, only this property. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | The label rendered after the input, already wired to it with `htmlFor`. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement, HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on the native `change` event, when the user checks or unchecks the input. A radio unchecked by another one in its group and a form reset do not call it. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the checked state, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the choice it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the checkbox small or large. |
| `theme` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the checked state to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the checked state asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |

## CFormCheck

```jsx
import { CFormCheck } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `button` | `ButtonObject` | - | Create button-like checkboxes and radio buttons. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique in the whole document. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | - | Input Checkbox indeterminate Property. |
| `inline` | `boolean` | - | Group checkboxes or radios on the same horizontal row. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Set component validation state to invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | The element represents a caption for a component. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement, HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on the native `change` event, when the user checks or unchecks the input. A radio unchecked by another one in its group and a form reset do not call it. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the checked state, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the choice it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `reverse` | `boolean` | - | Put checkboxes or radios on the opposite side. |
| `theme` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `"checkbox" \| "radio"` | `checkbox` | Specifies the type of component. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Set component validation state to valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the checked state asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |

# React Checkbox Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Checkbox component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

React Checkbox reads its own custom properties, so restyling it does not touch radios or switches. Set them on the control itself — an ancestor cannot override a token the element declares for itself.

```scss
$check-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-check-size: var(--cui-control-size),
    --cui-check-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-check-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-check-border-radius: .25em,
    --cui-check-mark-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-check-mark-checked: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 20 20'><path fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-width='3' d='m6 10 3 3 6-6'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-check-mark-indeterminate: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 20 20'><path fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-width='3' d='M6 10h8'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-check-checked-bg: var(--cui-control-checked-bg),
    --cui-check-checked-border-color: var(--cui-control-checked-border-color),
    --cui-check-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-control-indeterminate-bg),
    --cui-check-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color),
    --cui-check-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-disabled-opacity),
    --cui-check-margin-top: calc((var(--cui-body-line-height) * 1em - var(--cui-check-size)) * .5),
    --cui-check-active-filter: var(--cui-control-active-filter),
    --cui-check-label-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $check-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-check-size': '1.25em',
  '--cui-check-checked-bg': '#198754',
}

return <CCheckbox style={customVars} />
```

### Shared variables

The checkbox, the radio and the switch share their size and their focus, active and disabled states. Those live on `:root` as `--cui-control-*`, so one declaration retunes all three at runtime:

```scss
--cui-control-size: 1em,
--cui-control-checked-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-checked-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-active-filter: brightness(90%),
--cui-control-focus-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color),
--cui-control-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-3),
--cui-control-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-transition-duration: .15s,
--cui-control-transition-timing: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1),
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one size class, and the same map drives both `.check-{size}` and `.radio-{size}` — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$check-sizes: defaults(
  (
    sm: (size: .875rem, margin-top: .21875rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm)),
    lg: (size: 1.25rem, margin-top: .3125rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-lg))
  ),
  $check-sizes
);
```

# React Bootstrap Checkbox Component

> Learn how to build accessible and consistent Bootstrap-style checkboxes in React using CoreUI components.

## How to use React Bootstrap Checkbox component

Use CoreUI’s `<CCheckbox>` to create cross-browser, accessible, and Bootstrap-styled checkboxes in React. Checkboxes are ideal for selecting one or more options from a list and can be styled, stacked, or grouped using layout utilities.

### Basic example

Use the `<CCheckbox>` component to render a standard Bootstrap-style checkbox.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkDefault" label="Default checkbox" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkChecked" label="Checked checkbox" defaultChecked />
      </CFormField>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Indeterminate state

Set the `indeterminate` property to render a checkbox in an indeterminate state, commonly used to indicate partial selections.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxIndeterminateExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CCheckbox id="checkIndeterminate" label="Indeterminate checkbox" indeterminate />
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

### Disabled state

Add the `disabled` prop to disable a checkbox and automatically style its label in a muted color, following Bootstrap conventions.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="checkDisabled" label="Disabled checkbox" disabled />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox
          id="checkCheckedDisabled"
          label="Disabled checked checkbox"
          defaultChecked
          disabled
        />
      </CFormField>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Stacked layout (default)

By default, multiple checkboxes stack vertically and are spaced evenly.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxStackedExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="defaultCheck1" label="Default checkbox" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="defaultCheck2" label="Disabled checkbox" disabled />
      </CFormField>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Inline checkboxes

Place multiple checkboxes on the same horizontal row with a flex utility wrapper.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxInlineExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="d-flex gap-4">
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineCheckbox1" value="option1" label="1" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineCheckbox2" value="option2" label="2" />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CCheckbox id="inlineCheckbox3" value="option3" label="3 (disabled)" disabled />
      </CFormField>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Reversed checkboxes

The reverse layout exists only on the deprecated `<CFormCheck>` — its `reverse` property places the control after the label.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormCheck } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxReverseExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormCheck reverse id="reverseCheckbox1" value="option1" label="Reverse checkbox" />
      <CFormCheck
        reverse
        id="reverseCheckbox2"
        value="option2"
        label="Disabled reverse checkbox"
        disabled
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Without labels

If omitting a label, remember to include `aria-label` for accessibility compliance.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox } from '@coreui/react'

export const CheckboxWithoutLabelsExample = () => {
  return <CCheckbox id="checkboxNoLabel" value="" aria-label="..." />
}
```

# React Chip Input Component

> React Chip Input component for CoreUI helps you create tag-like multi-value inputs for skills, categories, or recipients with keyboard support, selection, and form integration.

## Overview

The CoreUI **React Chip Input component** lets users enter multiple values as chips inside a single field. Use it as a tag input, multi-value selector, or token field for skills, categories, email recipients, and more. The chip input component supports keyboard-friendly entry, chip removal, and optional selection for bulk actions.

- Type values and press `Enter` or a separator to create chips.
- Chips can be removable and selectable.
- The input stays inline and grows as you type.
- Form integration through a hidden field the browser validates, submitted when `name` is provided.

## When to use Chip Input

Use the React Chip Input component when you need:

- A **tag input** or **token field** for free-form multi-value entry
- An **email or recipient input** where users add multiple addresses
- A **skills or category selector** in forms
- A **filterable multi-select** that integrates with standard HTML forms

## Basic example

Use `CChipInput` to render a multi-value field with predefined chips and inline input.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      id="skillsInputBasic"
      label="Skills:"
      defaultValue={['JavaScript', 'TypeScript', 'Accessibility']}
      name="chipInputBasicExample"
      placeholder="Add a skill..."
    />
  )
}
```

> Note: `CChipInput` renders the inline text input automatically, and a hidden `<textarea>` that carries the chip values separated by commas. When `name` is provided, that field takes part in standard form submission.

## Theme variants

Color the chips with [theme classes](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) to represent categories, status, or priority.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

const variants: Record<string, string> = {
  feature: 'theme-primary',
  approved: 'theme-success',
  'needs review': 'theme-warning',
  blocking: 'theme-danger',
}

export const ChipInputVariantsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      defaultValue={['Feature', 'Approved', 'Needs review', 'Blocking']}
      chipClassName={(value) => variants[value.trim().toLowerCase()] || ''}
      name="issues"
      placeholder="Add label..."
    />
  )
}
```

In the example below, chip color is assigned dynamically based on the chip text using the `chipClassName` callback.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputClassNameExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      defaultValue={['Feature', 'Blocking', 'Approved']}
      chipClassName={(value) => {
        const variants: Record<string, string> = {
          approved: 'theme-success',
          blocking: 'theme-danger',
          feature: 'theme-primary',
        }
        return variants[value.trim().toLowerCase()] || 'theme-secondary'
      }}
      placeholder="Type and press Enter"
    />
  )
}
```

## Sizes

Use `size="sm"` and `size="lg"` to match surrounding form controls. Default size is provided without a size modifier.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputSizesExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CChipInput
          id="skillsInputSm"
          label="Small"
          size="sm"
          defaultValue={['HTML']}
          placeholder="Add small tag..."
        />
      </div>

      <div className="mb-4">
        <CChipInput
          id="skillsInputMd"
          label="Default"
          defaultValue={['JavaScript']}
          placeholder="Add default tag..."
        />
      </div>

      <div>
        <CChipInput
          id="skillsInputLg"
          label="Large"
          size="lg"
          defaultValue={['TypeScript']}
          placeholder="Add large tag..."
        />
      </div>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Separator

By default, chips are created when the user types a comma `,`. Change the separator with the `separator` property.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ChipInputSeparatorExample = () => {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(['Item 1'])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput
        value={tags}
        onChange={setTags}
        separator=";"
        placeholder="Type and use ; to separate..."
      />
      <p className="fg-2 mt-3">
        <small>Use semicolon (;) as separator</small>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

### No separator

Set `separator` to an empty string or `null` to stop chips being created as the user types. They must press **Enter** instead.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ChipInputNoSeparatorExample = () => {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(['Item 1'])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput
        value={tags}
        onChange={setTags}
        separator={null}
        placeholder="Type and press Enter..."
      />
      <p className="fg-2 mt-3">
        <small>Separator disabled — use the Enter key to create chips</small>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Maximum chips

Limit how many chips can be added with `maxChips`.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ChipInputMaxChipsExample = () => {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(['Item 1'])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput value={tags} onChange={setTags} maxChips={5} placeholder="Max 5 chips" />
      <p className="fg-2 mt-3">
        <small>
          {tags.length}/5 chips — {5 - tags.length} remaining
        </small>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Create on blur

Typing a value and leaving the input creates a chip. Set `createOnBlur` to `false` to require **Enter**.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ChipInputCreateOnBlurExample = () => {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState(['Item 1'])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput
        value={tags}
        onChange={setTags}
        createOnBlur={false}
        placeholder="Must press Enter"
      />
      <p className="fg-2 mt-3">
        <small>Blurring will not create a chip — you must press Enter</small>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Empty state

Start with just the input and let users add chips as they type.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputEmptyStateExample = () => {
  return <CChipInput name="tags" placeholder="Start typing tags..." />
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place. The label goes inside the container as `.chip-input-label` — pass it through the `label` property, and the component points it at the text input it builds.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CChipInput
        id="techStackField"
        label="Tech stack"
        defaultValue={['Vue', 'Vite']}
        name="techStack"
        placeholder="Add package..."
      />
      <CFormText>Press Enter or comma to add a value.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## With label

Use a standard form label for accessibility.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputWithLabelExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="mb-4">
      <label className="form-label" htmlFor="techStackInput">
        Tech stack
      </label>
      <CChipInput
        id="techStackInput"
        name="techStack"
        defaultValue={['Vue', 'Vite']}
        placeholder="Add package..."
      />
      <div className="form-text">Press Enter or comma to add a value.</div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Validation

`CChipInput` carries its chips in a hidden `<textarea>` the browser validates, so `required` stops the submit of an empty field and the browser shows its message over the component. The state shows on the frame and on the text input, and the message after the frame is linked to the text input.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CChipInput, CForm } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputValidationExample = () => {
  const [recipientsState, setRecipientsState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <CChipInput
          feedbackInvalid="Add at least one topic."
          id="validationTopics"
          label="Topics"
          name="topics"
          placeholder="Add a topic..."
          required
        />
      </div>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <CChipInput
          defaultValue={['ana@example.com', 'bob@example']}
          feedback="bob@example is not a full address."
          id="validationRecipients"
          label="Recipients"
          name="recipients"
          onValidationStateChange={setRecipientsState}
          validationState={recipientsState}
        />
      </div>
      <div className="col-12">
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the hidden field blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled` or `readOnly`.
- A validation that reports the hidden field invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the frame and the text input show it invalid whenever the value is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the frame shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the hidden field, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the chips it was given for. When the user adds or removes a chip, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)`; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `value` keeps it, and so does an action that changes nothing, such as entering a value the field already holds. A reset asks once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same call, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the chips given by `defaultValue` or the `CChip` children, and leaves a controlled `value` to you.

## Disabled

Set disabled state on the component to make the input and chips non-interactive. Combine it with `removable={false}` for disabled, non-removable chips.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      defaultValue={['Read only', 'Locked']}
      disabled
      removable={false}
      placeholder="Input disabled"
    />
  )
}
```

## Readonly

Use readonly state when chips should stay visible and focusable, but values must not change.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputReadonlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      defaultValue={['JavaScript', 'TypeScript']}
      readOnly
      placeholder="Read-only values"
    />
  )
}
```

## Selectable chips

Enable selection for chips managed by Chip Input. In this example, `onSelect` updates a live list of selected values below the field.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputSelectableExample = () => {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput
        defaultValue={['Design', 'Backend', 'QA', 'DevOps']}
        selectable
        onSelect={setSelected}
        placeholder="Select chips"
      />
      <p className="mt-3 mb-0 small fg-2">
        Selected: {selected.length > 0 ? selected.join(', ') : 'None'}
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Paste support

Several values can be pasted at once. If the pasted text contains the separator, it is split into one chip per value.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ChipInputPasteExample = () => {
  const [tags, setTags] = useState<string[]>([])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput value={tags} onChange={setTags} placeholder="Try pasting: apple,banana,cherry" />
      <p className="fg-2 mt-3">
        <small>Paste comma-separated values to create multiple chips at once</small>
      </p>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

The chip list works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the chips |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultValue`, or the `CChip` children | the chip input, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `value` | your component |

`onChange` fires in **both** modes with the new list of values — so you can watch the chips without taking them over. A native reset of the form puts back the chips the input started with: uncontrolled, it sets them and calls `onChange` when that changes the chips; controlled, it asks for the first `value` through `onChange` and shows your `value` until you take it.

### Uncontrolled

Seed the list with `defaultValue`, as the basic example does, or with `CChip` children, and let the chip input manage it.

```jsx
<CChipInput defaultValue={['React', 'Vue']} />
```

### Controlled

Pass `value` and the chips render exactly what you pass — adding or removing a chip only fires `onChange`. Feed the change back, or nothing moves.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputControlledExample = () => {
  const [values, setValues] = useState<string[]>(['React'])

  return (
    <>
      <CChipInput value={values} onChange={setValues} placeholder="Controlled chip input" />
      <p className="mt-3 mb-0 small fg-2">Current value: {values.join(', ') || '-'}</p>
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the values belong to something else: form state, a query you persist, or a list shared with another control.

## Accessibility

The React Chip Input component follows WAI-ARIA patterns to ensure the chip input is fully usable with keyboards and assistive technologies.

- Associate a `<label>` with the ghost input for screen readers.
- Chips are focusable and keyboard navigable.
- Each remove button the component creates is named with `ariaRemoveLabel` and the chip's value, `Remove <value>` by default. Put `{label}` where the value goes, or pass a function of the value for another word order.
- Adding and removing chips is announced through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) in the live region of the page, or of the modal dialog around the set, one message per update: the values the set did not hold before, or else the values it no longer holds, joined with commas as in `Vue, Svelte added`, and nothing while the set is hidden; customize the wording with the `ariaAddedAnnouncement` and `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` props. A function in place of the word receives the values and returns the whole message, so a page can put the word first, agree it with the number of chips or give a count for a long list, as in `(values) => values.length > 3 ? values.length + ' chips added' : values.join(', ') + ' added'`.
- The container is a generic element, so `disabled` and `readOnly` are carried by the inner input rather than stamped on it.
- Use a descriptive `aria-label` or `<label>` on the chip input container to communicate its purpose (e.g., "Add skills" or "Recipients").

The full treatment is on the [accessibility](./accessibility/) page: semantic structure, ARIA attributes, focus management, visual indicators and keyboard support.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CChipInput /&gt;](./api/#cchipinput)

# React Chip Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Chip Input component and all available CChipInput props.

## CChipInput

```jsx
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaAddedAnnouncement` | `string \| ((values: string[]) => string)` | `'added'` | Sets the wording announced when chips are added: a word that follows their values, joined with commas, or a function that receives the values and returns the whole message. |
| `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` | `string \| ((values: string[]) => string)` | `'removed'` | Sets the wording announced when chips are removed: a word that follows their values, joined with commas, or a function that receives the values and returns the whole message. |
| `ariaRemoveLabel` | `string \| ((label: string) => string)` | `Remove` | Names each chip's remove button with the chip's value: a string has `{label}` replaced by it, or gets it appended when there is no `{label}` (`Remove React`); a function receives the value and returns the whole name. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Declarative `CChip` children used as the initial chips. Their values seed the uncontrolled value when `defaultValue` is not provided (parity with the vanilla Chip Input). |
| `chipClassName` | `ChipClassName` | - | Adds custom classes to chips rendered by the React Chip Input component. Accepts a static className or a resolver function based on chip value. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Adds custom classes to the React Chip Input component root element. |
| `createOnBlur` | `boolean` | `true` | Creates a new chip when the React Chip Input component loses focus with a pending value. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | `[]` | Sets the initial uncontrolled values rendered by the React Chip Input component. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Disables the React Chip Input component and prevents adding, removing, or selecting chips. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | - | Renders the chips as filter chips, each showing a leading check icon while selected. Implies `selectable`. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Sets the `id` of the internal text input rendered by the React Chip Input component. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Renders an inline label inside the React Chip Input component container. |
| `maxChips` | `number \| null` | - | Sets the maximum number of chips that can be created in the React Chip Input component. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the hidden field the chips are submitted under, separated by commas. Without it the chips are not submitted with the form. |
| `onAdd` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the React Chip Input component adds a new chip. |
| `onChange` | `((values: string[]) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the value list of the React Chip Input component changes. |
| `onInput` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the internal text input value changes in the React Chip Input component. |
| `onRemove` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the React Chip Input component removes a chip. |
| `onSelect` | `((selected: string[]) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the selected chip values change in the React Chip Input component. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user adds or removes a chip, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the chips it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Sets placeholder text for the internal input of the React Chip Input component. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Makes the React Chip Input component readonly while keeping values visible. |
| `removable` | `boolean` | `true` | Displays remove buttons on chips managed by the React Chip Input component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Makes the hidden field that carries the chips required, so an empty React Chip Input component blocks the submit, and marks the text input `aria-required`. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | - | Enables chip selection behavior in the React Chip Input component. |
| `selectionMode` | `"single" \| "multiple"` | - | Sets how many chips can be selected at once in the React Chip Input component. |
| `separator` | `string \| null` | `,` | Sets the separator character used to create chips while typing or pasting in the React Chip Input component. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Sets the size of the React Chip Input component to small or large. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the frame; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on the text input and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the chips asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string[]` | - | Controls the values rendered by the React Chip Input component. |

# React Chip Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Chip Input component with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and better form integration.

### CSS variables

A chip input is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables), so it reads the group's `--cui-control-*` tokens; `.chip-input` only re-points the ones it sets differently — padding, border colour and radius, and the gap between chips. Override any group token on the element `CChipInput` renders, through `style`, to restyle a single chip input.

```scss
$chip-input-tokens: () !default;
$chip-input-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-padding-y: .25rem,
    --cui-control-padding-x: .75rem,
    --cui-control-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-control-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),
    --cui-control-group-gap: .375rem,
  ),
  $chip-input-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-control-padding-y': '0.5rem',
  '--cui-control-border-color': 'var(--cui-primary-base)',
}

return <CChipInput style={customVars} placeholder="Add value" />
```

### Sass maps

Each size is one entry, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$chip-input-sizes: defaults(
  (
    "sm": (
      padding-y:     .125rem,
      padding-x:     .5rem,
      border-radius: var(--cui-radius-3),
      gap:           .125rem,
    ),
    "lg": (
      padding-y:     .375rem,
      padding-x:     1rem,
      border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
      gap:           .5rem,
    ),
  ),
  $chip-input-sizes
);
```

# React Chip Input Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility and keyboard support features implemented in the CoreUI React Chip Input component.

## Accessible React Chip Input

Chip inputs are commonly used for tags, labels, recipients, and tokenized multi-value entry. When used in forms, they should remain keyboard accessible, clearly labeled, and understandable to assistive technologies. This guide explains how CoreUI React Chip Input supports accessible usage patterns.

### Semantic Structure

- **Inline text input**: `CChipInput` renders a real text input for entering new values, which keeps typing, focus, and screen reader behavior predictable.

- **Chip list pattern**: Existing values are rendered as chips before the inline input, making the field readable as a tokenized sequence of values.

- **Form compatibility**: When `name` is provided, a hidden input is rendered so chip values can participate in traditional form submission.

### ARIA Attributes

CoreUI React Chip Input supports accessible labeling and chip state communication:

- **External labels**: Associate the input with a `<label>` using `id` and `htmlFor` for clear screen reader context.

- **Chip selection state**: Selectable chips expose `aria-selected` through the underlying `CChip` component.

- **Remove buttons**: Each remove button is named with `ariaRemoveLabel` and the chip's value, `Remove <value>` by default. Put `{label}` where the value goes, or pass a function of the value for another word order.

- **Announcements**: Adding and removing chips is announced through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) in the live region of the page, or of the modal dialog around the field, one message per update: the values the field did not hold before, or else the values it no longer holds, joined with commas as in `Vue, Svelte added`. Customize the wording with the `ariaAddedAnnouncement` and `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` props. A function in place of the word receives the values and returns the whole message, so a page can put the word first, agree it with the number of chips or give a count for a long list, as in `(values) => values.length > 3 ? values.length + ' chips added' : values.join(', ') + ' added'`.

- **Disabled and readonly states**: Disabled and readonly states are reflected so assistive technologies can identify interaction constraints.

### Focus Management

- **Input-first workflow**: Users can type directly into the inline input without extra setup.

- **Chip navigation**: When the input is empty, keyboard navigation can move focus to chips for selection or removal.

- **Selectable chips**: Focusable chips can be traversed with arrow keys once focus enters the chip list.

### Visual Indicators

- **Visible focus states**: The input and focusable chips provide visible focus styles for keyboard users.

- **Selected chips**: Active chips are visually differentiated when `selectable` is enabled.

- **Disabled and readonly styling**: Reduced emphasis communicates when the field or chips are not editable.

### Keyboard Support

The React Chip Input component supports keyboard interaction for both the input and the rendered chips:

| Key | Function |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Create a chip from the current input value. |
| <kbd>,</kbd> or separator key | Create a chip from the current input value when a separator is configured. |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd> | When the input is empty, move focus to the last chip. When a removable chip is focused, remove it. |
| <kbd>Left Arrow</kbd> | When the caret is at the start of the input, move focus to the last chip. When a chip is focused, move to the previous chip. |
| <kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> | When a chip is focused, move to the next chip. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> on a chip | Toggle selected state when `selectable` is enabled. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> | Move focus to the first focusable chip. |
| <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the last focusable chip. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Left Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> | Move focus and add the chip it lands on to the selection (`selectable`, `selectionMode="multiple"`). |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Extend the selection to the first or last chip (`selectable`, `selectionMode="multiple"`). |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select every chip (`selectable`, `selectionMode="multiple"`). |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Clear the current input value and blur the input. |

# React Bootstrap Chip Input Component

> Learn how to build Bootstrap-styled token inputs with the React Chip Input component in CoreUI, including variants, sizes, selection, and form integration.

## Overview

The CoreUI **React Bootstrap Chip Input component** lets users enter multiple values as chips inside a single field. Use it as a tag input, multi-value selector, or token field for skills, categories, email recipients, and more.

- Type values and press `Enter` or a separator to create chips.
- Chips can be removable and selectable.
- The input stays inline and grows as you type.
- Form integration is supported with a hidden input when `name` is provided.

## When to use Chip Input

Use the React Bootstrap Chip Input component when you need:

- A **tag input** or **token field** for free-form multi-value entry
- An **email or recipient input** where users add multiple addresses
- A **skills or category selector** in forms
- A **filterable multi-select** that integrates with standard HTML forms

## Basic example

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      id="skillsInputBasic"
      label="Skills:"
      defaultValue={['JavaScript', 'TypeScript', 'Accessibility']}
      name="chipInputBasicExample"
      placeholder="Add a skill..."
    />
  )
}
```

## Variants

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

const variants: Record<string, string> = {
  feature: 'theme-primary',
  approved: 'theme-success',
  'needs review': 'theme-warning',
  blocking: 'theme-danger',
}

export const ChipInputVariantsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      defaultValue={['Feature', 'Approved', 'Needs review', 'Blocking']}
      chipClassName={(value) => variants[value.trim().toLowerCase()] || ''}
      name="issues"
      placeholder="Add label..."
    />
  )
}
```

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CChipInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const ChipInputClassNameExample = () => {
  return (
    <CChipInput
      defaultValue={['Feature', 'Blocking', 'Approved']}
      chipClassName={(value) => {
        const variants: Record<string, string> = {
          approved: 'theme-success',
          blocking: 'theme-danger',
          feature: 'theme-primary',
        }
        return variants[value.trim().toLowerCase()] || 'theme-secondary'
      }}
      placeholder="Type and press Enter"
    />
  )
}
```

# React Combobox Component

> A select-like control written as components: a form-control toggle next to a popup list box. CCombobox runs the open state, the selection, the keyboard and form submission, and leaves the content of every option to you.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

`CCombobox` is a `.form-control` toggle followed by a `.popup` holding a [List box](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/list-box/). The toggle shows the current value and the list holds the choices; the component keeps the two in step — it opens and closes the panel, positions it against the toggle, tracks the selection, runs the keyboard through `aria-activedescendant`, and submits the value through a hidden `<select>` the browser validates.

Everything inside the panel is List box markup, so an option is whatever you put in it: plain text, an icon, a two-line label with a description. `CCombobox` never rewrites an option's content.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxExample = () => (
  <CCombobox ariaLabel="Item" placeholder="Select an item…" style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}>
    <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="3">Option three</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### When to use

<div class="table-responsive">

| Component | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Combobox | Picking from a list you wrote as components, with full control over what an option looks like. |
| [Autocomplete](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/autocomplete/) | Typing to narrow a list, with hints and a free-text value. |
| [Multi Select](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/multi-select/) | A native `<select>` enhanced in place, with chips, select-all and groups. |
| [List box](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/list-box/) | The list on its own, without a toggle or a panel. |

</div>

### Options from data

Pass `items` to render the options from data instead of children. Each entry takes the `CListBoxOption` shape — `value`, `label`, `description`, `disabled` — so the list keeps the order, the navigation and the ids.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const items = [
  { label: 'United States', value: 'us' },
  { label: 'United Kingdom', value: 'uk' },
  { label: 'Canada', value: 'ca' },
]

export const ComboboxItemsExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Country"
    items={items}
    placeholder="Pick a country…"
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  />
)
```

## Example

The options are `CListBoxOption` children, exactly as in a List box; an option without a `value` is worth its text. `CCombobox` fills in the rest: `.combobox-value` for the text, the caret, `type="button"`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, and it keeps the panel out of the document until the first open.

### Placeholders

`placeholder` is the text `.combobox-value` shows while nothing is selected. It carries `.combobox-placeholder` while it stands for an empty value, so it can be dimmed without being confused for a choice.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxPlaceholderExample = () => (
  <CCombobox ariaLabel="Country" placeholder="Pick a country…" style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}>
    <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### Pre-selected value

`defaultValue` seeds the uncontrolled selection and `value` drives a controlled one — pair the latter with `onChange`. Both take an array in `multiple` mode. A native reset of the form puts back the value the combobox started with; a controlled one asks for its first `value` through `onChange` and keeps showing your `value` until you take it.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxPreselectedExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Role"
    defaultValue="editor"
    placeholder="Choose a role…"
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="admin">Admin</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="editor">Editor</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="viewer">Viewer</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### With form field

`label`, `text` and the feedback props lay the control out with its label and description, and put validation feedback in the right place — the same [form field](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) the other controls use.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxFieldExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    label="Country"
    placeholder="Pick a country…"
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
    text="We ship to these three for now."
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

## Custom content

An option is an ordinary element, so it takes whatever markup belongs there. The toggle shows its text: the label alone when the option has a `description`, the option's own text otherwise — so an option with an icon and a description still reads as one word in the closed control.

### Icons

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cibCss3, cibHtml5, cibJavascript } from '@coreui/icons'

export const ComboboxIconsExample = () => (
  <CCombobox ariaLabel="Language" placeholder="Choose a language…" style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}>
    <CListBoxOption value="html">
      <CIcon icon={cibHtml5} /> HTML
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="css">
      <CIcon icon={cibCss3} /> CSS
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="js">
      <CIcon icon={cibJavascript} /> JavaScript
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### Descriptions

`description` adds a second line under the option's name. The toggle shows the name alone.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxDescriptionsExample = () => (
  <CCombobox ariaLabel="Plan" placeholder="Choose a plan…" style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}>
    <CListBoxOption description="Everything you need to start" value="starter">
      Starter
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="For a growing team" value="team">
      Team
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="Single sign-on and audit logs" value="enterprise">
      Enterprise
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### Checkbox indicator

`indicator="checkbox"` puts the check the multi-value pickers use in front of every option. The option keeps its `role="option"` and its `aria-selected`, and the mark is hidden from assistive technology.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxCheckboxIndicatorExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Skills"
    indicator="checkbox"
    multiple
    placeholder="Select skills…"
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="html">HTML</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="css">CSS</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="js">JavaScript</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### All together

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilBriefcase, cilHome, cilPaperPlane } from '@coreui/icons'

export const ComboboxCustomContentExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Address"
    indicator="checkbox"
    placeholder="Where should we ship it?"
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  >
    <CListBoxOption description="Weekdays after 6 pm" value="home">
      <CIcon icon={cilHome} /> Home
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="Weekdays, 9 am to 5 pm" value="office">
      <CIcon icon={cilBriefcase} /> Office
    </CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption description="Any time, with a code" value="locker">
      <CIcon icon={cilPaperPlane} /> Parcel locker
    </CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

## Search

`search` puts the List box's own search field at the top of the panel and hides what does not match. Because a hidden option leaves the navigation, everything downstream follows: the arrows skip it and the empty state appears when nothing is left. The focus moves into the field when the panel opens, and `aria-activedescendant` moves there with it, so typing and choosing happen in one place.

`searchPlaceholder` fills the field's placeholder and `ariaSearchLabel` its accessible name. Add a `CListBoxEmpty` child for the message shown when nothing matches.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const countries = [
  { label: 'United States', value: 'us' },
  { label: 'United Kingdom', value: 'uk' },
  { label: 'Canada', value: 'ca' },
  { label: 'Australia', value: 'au' },
  { label: 'Germany', value: 'de' },
  { label: 'France', value: 'fr' },
  { label: 'Japan', value: 'jp' },
  { label: 'Brazil', value: 'br' },
]

export const ComboboxSearchExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Country"
    placeholder="Select a country…"
    search
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  >
    {countries.map((country) => (
      <CListBoxOption key={country.value} value={country.value}>
        {country.label}
      </CListBoxOption>
    ))}
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results found</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

The panel is as tall as its content — cap it where you want a scroll container, with `max-height` and `overflow-y` on `.list-box-options`.

### Matching past the accents

`searchNormalize` compares both sides without their diacritics, so `zoe` finds `Zoë` and `oe` finds both. It normalizes to `NFD` and drops the combining diacritics, which leaves the labels themselves untouched — only the comparison changes.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxEmpty, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxSearchNormalizeExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Name"
    placeholder="Find a name…"
    search
    searchNormalize
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="zoe">Zoë</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="renee">Renée</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="joao">João</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ana">Ana</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxEmpty>No results found</CListBoxEmpty>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

### External search

`search="external"` builds the same field and filters nothing. Every keystroke calls `onSearch` with the query, and you answer with `items` — the list shows what you hand it, so the query is yours to interpret.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CCombobox } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const countries = [
  { label: 'United States', value: 'us' },
  { label: 'United Kingdom', value: 'uk' },
  { label: 'Canada', value: 'ca' },
  { label: 'Australia', value: 'au' },
  { label: 'Germany', value: 'de' },
]

export const ComboboxExternalSearchExample = () => {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(countries)

  return (
    <CCombobox
      ariaLabel="Country"
      items={items}
      onSearch={(query) =>
        setItems(
          countries.filter((country) =>
            country.label.toLowerCase().startsWith(query.trim().toLowerCase())
          )
        )
      }
      placeholder="Select a country…"
      search="external"
      style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
    />
  )
}
```

## Groups

Group options in a `CListBoxSection` and name it with `label`. The section carries `role="group"` and is announced with its name. A section whose options are all filtered out is hidden with its label.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption, CListBoxSection } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxGroupsExample = () => (
  <CCombobox ariaLabel="Language" placeholder="Select a language…" style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}>
    <CListBoxSection label="Frontend">
      <CListBoxOption value="html">HTML</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="css">CSS</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="js">JavaScript</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
    <CListBoxSection label="Backend">
      <CListBoxOption value="python">Python</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="ruby">Ruby</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="go">Go</CListBoxOption>
    </CListBoxSection>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

## Multiple select

`multiple` toggles options instead of replacing the selection, and the panel stays open so several picks cost one opening. The toggle shows the one label while a single option is selected and `selectedLabel` past that — a function of the count and the number of options, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. `selectionLimit` caps how many can be taken at once, and `onSelectionLimit` reports the limit together with the value it turned down.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxMultipleExample = () => (
  <CCombobox
    ariaLabel="Skills"
    indicator="checkbox"
    multiple
    placeholder="Select skills…"
    selectedLabel={(count) => `${count} skills`}
    style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
  >
    <CListBoxOption value="html">HTML</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="css">CSS</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="js">JavaScript</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="python">Python</CListBoxOption>
    <CListBoxOption value="ruby">Ruby</CListBoxOption>
  </CCombobox>
)
```

## Sizing

The toggle carries `.form-control`, so `size` reaches it unchanged and it stands exactly as tall as a text input of the same size.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const options = ['Option one', 'Option two', 'Option three']

export const ComboboxSizingExample = () => (
  <>
    <CCombobox
      ariaLabel="Small"
      className="mb-4"
      placeholder="Small select…"
      size="sm"
      style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
    >
      {options.map((option) => (
        <CListBoxOption key={option} value={option}>
          {option}
        </CListBoxOption>
      ))}
    </CCombobox>
    <CCombobox
      ariaLabel="Large"
      placeholder="Large select…"
      size="lg"
      style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
    >
      {options.map((option) => (
        <CListBoxOption key={option} value={option}>
          {option}
        </CListBoxOption>
      ))}
    </CCombobox>
  </>
)
```

## Disabled

`disabled` on the combobox turns the toggle off, so the panel cannot be opened. `disabled` on a single `CListBoxOption` takes that option out of the keyboard order and out of every selection the user makes, and `disabled` on a `CListBoxSection` does that for every option in it. A `value` or `defaultValue` naming a disabled option still selects it, as a native select does.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxDisabledExample = () => (
  <>
    <CCombobox
      ariaLabel="Disabled"
      className="mb-4"
      disabled
      placeholder="Nothing to pick here"
      style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
    >
      <CListBoxOption value="1">Option one</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="2">Option two</CListBoxOption>
    </CCombobox>
    <CCombobox ariaLabel="Availability" placeholder="Pick a slot…" style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}>
      <CListBoxOption value="1">Available</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption disabled value="2">
        Unavailable
      </CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="3">Available</CListBoxOption>
    </CCombobox>
  </>
)
```

## Form submission

`CCombobox` renders a hidden `<select class="combobox-select">` right after the toggle and keeps its selected options in step with the selection, so a combobox posts like a `<select>`, and like a `<select multiple>` in `multiple` mode: one key per value, `country=us&country=ca`. Set `name` to submit it; without a name the combobox is not submitted with the form. With nothing selected a single combobox posts `country=` and a `multiple` one posts nothing, as the native selects do. The select carries `.input-group-ignore`, so a toggle in an input group keeps its corners. A disabled combobox is not submitted, like any disabled field.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCombobox, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxFormSubmissionExample = () => (
  <form className="d-flex gap-4 align-items-end" onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
    <CCombobox
      label="Country"
      name="country"
      placeholder="Pick a country…"
      style={{ maxWidth: '20rem' }}
    >
      <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
      <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
    </CCombobox>
    <CButton type="submit">Submit</CButton>
  </form>
)
```

## Validation

The hidden `<select>` takes part in the browser's validation, so `required` blocks the submit while nothing is selected. When a validation reports it, the component lays it along the start of the toggle, so the browser shows its message under the combobox, and the focus it gets goes to the toggle. The state shows on the toggle as the `.is-*` class, and the message after it is added to the toggle's `aria-describedby`.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCombobox, CForm, CListBoxOption } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const ComboboxValidationExample = () => {
  const [roleState, setRoleState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <CCombobox
          feedbackInvalid="Pick a country."
          label="Country (required)"
          name="country"
          placeholder="Pick a country…"
          required
        >
          <CListBoxOption value="us">United States</CListBoxOption>
          <CListBoxOption value="uk">United Kingdom</CListBoxOption>
          <CListBoxOption value="ca">Canada</CListBoxOption>
        </CCombobox>
      </div>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <CCombobox
          defaultValue="admin"
          feedback="This project already has an admin."
          label="Role"
          name="role"
          onValidationStateChange={setRoleState}
          validationState={roleState}
        >
          <CListBoxOption value="admin">Admin</CListBoxOption>
          <CListBoxOption value="editor">Editor</CListBoxOption>
        </CCombobox>
      </div>
      <div className="col-12">
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the hidden select blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled`.
- A validation that reports the hidden select invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the toggle shows it invalid whenever the value is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the toggle shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the hidden select, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the value it was given for. When the user picks a different value, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)`; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `value` keeps it, and so does picking the value the combobox already holds. A reset asks once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same call, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the value given by `defaultValue`, and leaves a controlled `value` to you.

The toggle is a `<button>`, a role that has neither an invalid nor a required state, so it carries neither `aria-invalid` nor `aria-required`: a screen reader learns what is wrong from the message in its description, and that the field is required only from its label, so say it there, as the first field above does.

## Accessibility

The toggle is a real `<button>` carrying `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`; name it with `label` or an `aria-label`. The panel is a [List box](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/list-box/), so `role="listbox"` sits on `.list-box-options` and `role="option"` on every option, with `aria-selected` kept in step with the selection — name the list itself with `ariaLabel`.

The focus never enters the list. It stays on the toggle, or on the search field when there is one, and the highlighted option is reported through `aria-activedescendant` on whichever of the two holds it.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↓` / `↑` | Open the panel; once it is open, move the highlight to the next/previous option |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Open the panel; once it is open, select the highlighted option |
| `Home` / `End` | Move the highlight to the first/last option; the search field keeps them for the caret |
| `A` – `Z` | Move the highlight to the next option whose label starts with what you typed |
| `Escape` | Close the panel and return the focus to the toggle |
| `Tab` | Close the panel and move on |

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The toggle declares its own properties:

```scss
$combobox-toggle-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-combobox-toggle-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-combobox-toggle-show-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-combobox-toggle-placeholder-color: var(--cui-control-placeholder-color),
    --cui-combobox-toggle-caret-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-combobox-toggle-caret-size: .75em,
    --cui-combobox-toggle-caret-transition-duration: .2s,
    --cui-combobox-toggle-caret-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
  ),
  $combobox-toggle-tokens
);
```

The panel is the shared combobox surface, which only sizes itself:

```scss
$combobox-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-combobox-popup-min-width: 100%,
  ),
  $combobox-tokens
);
```

Everything inside it — options, section labels and the checkbox indicator — is a [List box](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/list-box/) and takes its `--cui-list-box-*` variables. `.list-box` declares them itself, so a value set on `.combobox-popup` or on `:root` does not reach it: set them with a rule on `.combobox-popup .list-box`, which covers the panels of Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select alike. The frame of the toggle is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables) and takes the `--cui-control-*` properties.
