# React Combobox Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Combobox component to control its value, the panel, the search field and form submission.

## CCombobox

```jsx
import { CCombobox } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | - | Provides an accessible name for the options of the panel. |
| `ariaSearchLabel` | `string` | `Search options` | Provides an accessible name for the search field. |
| `caretIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor"> <path d="M256 382.627 60.687 187.313l22.626-22.626L256 337.372l172.687-172.685 22.626 22.626z" /> </svg> )` | The caret drawn at the end of the toggle. Pass `false` to draw none. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The options, as `CListBoxOption` and `CListBoxSection` elements. Pass `items` instead to render them from data. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Adds custom classes to the React Combobox toggle. |
| `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| (() => Element \| DocumentFragment \| null) \| null` | - | The element the panel is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `defaultShow` | `boolean` | - | The initial open state of the uncontrolled panel — read once on mount. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` | - | The initial value for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `value` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Turns the toggle off, so the panel cannot be opened. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `indicator` | `ListBoxIndicator` | `none` | Puts a mark in front of every option. `checkbox` renders the check the multi-value pickers use. |
| `items` | `ListBoxOption[]` | - | Renders the options from data instead of children. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggles options instead of replacing the selection, and keeps the panel open while the user picks. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the hidden select the value is submitted under. With `multiple` it posts one key per value, as a `<select multiple>` does: `tags=a&tags=b&tags=c`. Without a name the combobox is not submitted with the form. |
| `onChange` | `((value: string \| string[] \| null) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the value changes. It reports an array in `multiple` mode, empty when nothing is selected; otherwise a string, or `null` once the single selection is cleared. |
| `onHide` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the panel closes. |
| `onSearch` | `((query: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired with the query of the search field, every time it changes. |
| `onSelectionLimit` | `((limit: number, value: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when `selectionLimit` refuses a pick. It reports the limit and the value that did not fit. |
| `onShow` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the panel opens. |
| `onShowChange` | `((show: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired when a gesture asks the panel to open or to close. In controlled mode update `show` yourself, or the panel stays as it is. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user picks a different value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` | - | The text the toggle shows while nothing is selected. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the panel through a portal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Makes the hidden select that carries the value required, so an empty combobox blocks the submit. |
| `search` | `boolean \| "external"` | - | Puts a search field at the top of the panel and hides what does not match. `'external'` hides nothing and only reports the query through `onSearch`. |
| `searchNormalize` | `boolean` | - | Compares the query and the option labels without their diacritics, so `zoe` finds `Zoë`. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `Search` | The placeholder of the search field. |
| `selectedLabel` | `CountLabel` | `'{count} selected'` | The text the toggle shows past one selected value in `multiple` mode. A function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. |
| `selectionLimit` | `number` | - | The number of values `multiple` mode accepts. |
| `show` | `boolean` | - | The controlled open state of the panel. Pair it with `onShowChange`. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the toggle small or large. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `typeahead` | `boolean` | `true` | Move the highlight to the option matching what the user types. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the toggle, with the matching feedback in the toggle's `aria-describedby`; `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. Picking a different value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string \| string[] \| null` | - | The controlled value. Pair it with `onChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultValue` instead. |

# React Date Input Component

> Create React date fields with a section-based input mask. Users type the day, month, and year in separate sections with automatic navigation and validation — like the native date input, but with full control over the format.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 5.27.0._

The React Date Input component renders a masked date field. The mask is split into day, month, and year sections — click or focus a section and type, use arrow keys to adjust values, and the caret moves to the next section automatically.

By default, the section order and separators are derived from the user's locale, so `12/31/2026` in `en-US` becomes `31.12.2026` in `de-DE` without any configuration.

The component follows the standard React controlled/uncontrolled pattern: use `defaultDate` for an uncontrolled field, or pair `date` with `onDateChange` for a controlled one — a committed change the parent doesn't accept is reverted, and `date` is compared by timestamp, so an inline `new Date(...)` re-created on every render doesn't disturb typing. A native reset of the form asks a controlled field for the `date` it started with through `onDateChange`.

A field holds what its format shows. The time of day of a `date` given to a field without a time is not kept: the first change the user makes reaches `onDateChange` at midnight, and a format with a time set later shows 00:00. Use `type="datetime"` or a format with a time when the time matters.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput label="Delivery date" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput defaultDate="2022-08-17" label="Delivery date" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Date and time

Set `type="datetime"` and the field carries the time as well. The hour cycle follows the locale, so a 12-hour locale gets an AM/PM section and a 24-hour one does not. Everything else on this page applies unchanged: the same typing, the same arrow keys, the same `onDateChange`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputDateTimeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput label="Appointment" locale="en-US" type="datetime" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          defaultDate="2026-07-14 14:30"
          label="Appointment"
          locale="en-US"
          type="datetime"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

Add `seconds` for a seconds section:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputSecondsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateInput label="Timestamp" seconds type="datetime" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

`type="time"` keeps only the time sections. That is the field [`<CTimeInput>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/time-input/) renders, with `time` and `onTimeChange` in place of `date` and `onDateChange`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputTimeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateInput label="Opening hour" type="time" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

A `format` overrides the type, because it names the sections itself. [`<CDateRangeInput>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-range-input/) takes both props too, so a range with time is the same two props on the range component.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <span className="form-label">Delivery date</span>
      <CDateInput locale="en-US" name="deliveryDate" />
      <CFormText>We deliver on working days only.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Formats

Set an explicit format with the `format` property. The parser accepts both dayjs/moment-style tokens (`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`, `YY`) and date-fns/Unicode-style tokens (`dd`, `MM`, `yyyy`, `yy`), so you can reuse the format strings from the date library you already use. Any other character becomes a literal separator.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CDateInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="dd.MM.yyyy" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CDateInput format="YYYY-MM-DD" label="YYYY-MM-DD" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDateInput format="MM/DD/YY" label="MM/DD/YY" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

Two-digit year sections expand with smart century assignment — values up to 50 years in the future resolve to the current century, older ones to the previous century.

The format doesn't have to include every section — a month-and-year mask works like the native `month` input and reports the first day of the month:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputPartialMasksExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput format="MM.yyyy" label="MM.yyyy" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput format="MMMM yyyy" label="MMMM yyyy" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

For picking whole weeks, use the [date picker](../date-picker/) with `selectionType="week"` — a masked week-number field has no native or MUI equivalent and isn't supported.

## Month names

Use the `MMM` or `MMMM` tokens for text month sections with localized short or full month names. Type letters to match a month by prefix — `m` selects <strong>M</strong>arch, continuing with `may` switches to <strong>May</strong> — and the caret moves on as soon as the prefix is unambiguous. Digits and arrow keys keep working too.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputMonthNamesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput format="DD MMMM YYYY" label="DD MMMM YYYY" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput format="MMM D, YYYY" label="MMM D, YYYY" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

Month names default to the grammatical form used inside a full date — e.g. Polish shows the genitive `14 lipca 2026`, not the standalone `lipiec`. To use a different form (or your own localization), pass all twelve names through the `monthNames` property; they are used for display, letter matching, and paste alike.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputMonthNamesCustomExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          format="DD MMMM YYYY"
          label="Standalone Polish month names"
          locale="pl-PL"
          monthNames={[
            'styczeń',
            'luty',
            'marzec',
            'kwiecień',
            'maj',
            'czerwiec',
            'lipiec',
            'sierpień',
            'wrzesień',
            'październik',
            'listopad',
            'grudzień',
          ]}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, the mask follows the locale set via the `locale` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputLocalesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CDateInput label="en-US" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CDateInput label="pl-PL" locale="pl-PL" yearPlaceholder="RRRR" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDateInput label="ja-JP" locale="ja-JP" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Min and max dates

Constrain the selectable range with `minDate` and `maxDate`. A completed date outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null` until the value is corrected. A date field compares the limits by the day. A field with a time compares them to the smallest unit it shows, and there a `maxDate` without a time of day covers its whole day.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputMinMaxExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Date in July 2026"
          maxDate="2026-07-31"
          minDate="2026-07-01"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Disabled dates

Beyond a simple range, the `disabledDates` property excludes specific dates — single `Date`s, `[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function. Unlike in the [date picker](../date-picker/#disabled-dates), there is no calendar to gray out: a completed date that hits a disabled entry gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null` until the value is corrected.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputDisabledDatesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          defaultDate={new Date(2026, 6, 10)}
          disabledDates={[[new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)], new Date(2026, 6, 16)]}
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Delivery date"
          maxDate={new Date(2026, 6, 31)}
          minDate={new Date(2026, 6, 1)}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          disabledDates={(date: Date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6}
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Business day"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Custom formats

The built-in token parser covers dayjs, moment, date-fns, and luxon format strings for date masks, so you can reuse the format string from the date library you already work with — the library itself isn't required to render or edit the mask. Pair it with `inputDateParse` when you want that library to also parse text pasted into the field, here with `date-fns`:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputCustomFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          defaultDate={new Date(2022, 8, 3)}
          format="MMMM DD, YYYY"
          inputDateParse={(value) => parse(value, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())}
          label="date-fns format"
          locale="en-US"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The field shows its validation state on the element and on its sections, and links the message that follows it, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. It keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over the field, which takes part in native constraint validation: a `required` field that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, and the browser, or `<CForm>`, puts focus on its first empty section, the browser with its own message over the field. A field that is not required does not block, and submits no date while it rejects one.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CDateInput, CForm } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputValidationExample = () => {
  const [pickupState, setPickupState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a delivery date."
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Delivery date (required)"
          name="delivery"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateInput
          defaultDate="2026-07-20"
          feedback="We have no pickup slots left on this date."
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Pickup date"
          name="pickup"
          onValidationStateChange={setPickupState}
          validationState={pickupState}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

The state comes from four places, in this order:

- The limits: a completed date outside `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates` makes the field invalid until it is corrected, whatever else is set, whether the user typed it or the field got it through its value, and again when the limits change. Until then the value field submits no date, also in a read-only field. A date before year 1 counts as before `minDate` even without that prop; when the field loses the focus, its year becomes 1.
- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, for example after a server has checked the date.
- A validation that reports the field invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which `<CForm>` and the [stepper](../stepper/) call as well. From then on the field shows it invalid whenever its date is invalid, until a native reset of the form.
- In a form with the `validate` property of `<CForm>` (the `data-coreui-validate` attribute), the `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` states of the value field, the same states the stylesheet reads on a native field. A field becomes `.is-valid` only when the form opts into success styling with `validate="valid"`.

A state you give is a verdict on the date it was given for. When the user changes the date, with a typed digit or letter, an arrow, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd>, a paste or a cut, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before `onDateChange`; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the second field above does. A key that leaves the field as it is asks nothing, and neither does a change your code makes through `date`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the field blocks the submit like any invalid field, with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none; a custom validity you set on the value field yourself stays as it is, and a disabled or read-only field does not block. An `aria-invalid` you pass is not read as a state. A native form reset returns the field to the date it started with; a `reset` listener that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the whole reset. A controlled field (`date` with `onDateChange`) keeps the value your page gives it, like a controlled `<input>`.

While the field is invalid, its `feedbackInvalid` text and an `.invalid-feedback` or `.invalid-tooltip` you render after the field yourself describe every section, so a screen reader reads the error with the field. A message rendered later, while the field stays invalid, is picked up when the field next renders, as it does when a parent of the field renders the message in reply to `onError`.

To react to validation transitions programmatically, use the `onError` callback: it receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty.

## Floating labels

Use the `floatingLabel` property. When the field is empty and not focused, the mask placeholders are hidden so the label can rest inside the field; focusing the field floats the label and reveals the mask.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateInputFloatingLabelsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateInput floatingLabel="Delivery date" format="dd.MM.yyyy" id="floatingDateInput" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.


## Accessibility

The date input implements the [spinbutton pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/) per section, mirroring the internal structure of the native date input:

- **Role attributes**: the container has `role="group"`, every section is a `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, and `aria-valuetext` (month sections announce the localized month name).
- **Roving tabindex**: the whole field is a single tab stop; arrow keys move between sections.
- **Labels**: `label` and `floatingLabel` name the group through `aria-labelledby`, and an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` you pass wins over both; without an `aria-label`, or with an empty one, the group also carries `aria-label="Date input"` (`Date and time input` with `type="datetime"`, `Time input` with `type="time"`), the name it is announced by when nothing else names it. Sections receive `aria-label`s (`Day`, `Month`, `Year`), each replaceable on its own — `ariaDayLabel`, `ariaMonthLabel`, `ariaYearLabel` — for localization.
- **Label click**: clicking the `label`, a `<label>` or `.form-label` an `aria-labelledby` you pass points at, or a `<label htmlFor>` pointing at the field's `id` moves focus to the first empty section, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Validity**: while the field is invalid (a date outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or in `disabledDates`, typed, pasted or given as the value, a date before year 1, `validationState="invalid"`, or a `required` field a validation has reported and that is still empty), every section carries `aria-invalid="true"`; the group, which takes no focus, carries none, and an `aria-invalid` you set on the field is not read. A disabled or read-only field is never reported as missing. With `required`, every section carries `aria-required="true"`.
- **Description**: the field is described by the `aria-describedby` you set, then its `text`, then the feedback that matches its state; that description reaches the first section, and every section while the field is invalid, together with an error message you render after the field, so the error is read wherever the focus sits.
- **Mobile input**: sections use `inputmode="numeric"`, so touch devices show the numeric keyboard.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>0</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> | Type into the focused section; the caret advances when the section is complete |
| <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> | In text month sections, match a month name by prefix; the caret advances when the prefix is unambiguous |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Increment / decrement the focused section, wrapping day and month around their bounds; an empty year starts at the current year |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous section; in a right-to-left layout the two keys swap |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last section |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clear the focused section; move to the previous section when already empty |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the focused section |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select the whole value; <kbd>Backspace</kbd> then clears all sections, typing restarts from the first section |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | Copy the selection — the whole formatted value after <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a date and fill all sections |

Apart from the shortcuts in the table, a key pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> changes nothing in the field and is not cancelled: arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move no focus and change no section, and a digit or letter is not entered. The key stays free for the browser, assistive technology and the picker around the field, where <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> opens the calendar. A character that <kbd>AltGr</kbd> or <kbd>Option</kbd> composes is still entered.

# React Date Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Date Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CDateInput

```jsx
import { CDateInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | - | Focus the first section right after mounting, like the native `autofocus` attribute. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `date` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled date — a `Date` or a date string like `'2026-07-14'`, one with a time part like `'2026-07-14 14:30'` on `type="datetime"`, or a time string like `'14:30'` on `type="time"`. Pair it with `onDateChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultDate` instead. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `defaultDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial date for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `date` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | - | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | - | The mask layout. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `inputDateParse` | `((value: string) => Date \| null)` | - | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `default` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Max selectable date. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Min selectable date. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | - | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `onDateChange` | `((date: Date \| null, formattedDate?: string \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the date changes; receives the `Date` (or `null` while incomplete or invalid) and the formatted value. |
| `onError` | `((error: DateInputError) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after the change callback, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean` | `false` | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived time layout. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `'date' \| 'datetime' \| 'time'` | `date` | Which sections the locale-derived layout carries. A `format` names the sections itself and overrides this. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. A field of a date range whose end is before its start draws no other state. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

# React Date Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Date Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The date, time, and date-time inputs share one set of styles under the `form-date-time` name. The field is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables), so its frame comes from the `--cui-control-*` tokens; the ones below style the sections inside it. Both sets sit on the field, the element `style` lands on, and can be set on a single input.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# React Date Picker Component

> The React Date Picker Component is an essential tool for any React-based application that requires date selection functionality.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## About

This component, provided by CoreUI for React.js, offers a user-friendly interface and various customization options to ensure an excellent user experience.

With its responsive design and support for all modern browsers, the React Date Picker Component can be easily integrated into any application. The component comes with an array of styling options, including color, size, and shape, that can be easily adjusted to fit the application's design.

The React Date Picker Component is also fully customizable, allowing developers to tailor the component to their specific needs. With its set of APIs, developers can control the default value, visibility, and date range of the component.

One of the standout features of the React Date Picker Component is its accessibility. CoreUI has ensured that the component is fully compliant with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), making it accessible to all users. The component supports keyboard navigation and screen readers, ensuring that users with disabilities can also benefit from its functionality.

## Example

Below is an example of a basic React DatePicker.

### Days

Basic examples demonstrating how to pick dates using the React Date Picker Component.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerDaysExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker label="Date Picker" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker defaultDate="2022/2/16" label="Date Picker" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

#### With footer

The `footer` prop projects your own content below the calendar. Pass a node, or a function receiving the picker's context — `setDate`, `today`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isDateSelectable`, `date` and `disabled` — so a projected button acts on the picker and reads its state. That is also how a "Today" button disables itself when today falls outside `minDate`, `maxDate` or `disabledDates`; the example checks when the panel renders and again on click, so a date that crosses a limit while the panel is open is not written.

Any descendant can reach the same context with the `useDatePicker()` hook.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerDaysWithFooterExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          footer={({ clear, close, isDateSelectable, today }) => (
            <>
              <CButton
                className="me-auto"
                theme="danger"
                disabled={!isDateSelectable(new Date())}
                onClick={() => isDateSelectable(new Date()) && today()}
                size="sm"
                variant="ghost"
              >
                Today
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={clear} size="sm" variant="ghost">
                Clear
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={close} size="sm">
                OK
              </CButton>
            </>
          )}
          locale="en-US"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          defaultDate="2022/2/16"
          footer={({ close, reset }) => (
            <>
              <CButton
                className="me-auto"
                theme="primary"
                onClick={reset}
                size="sm"
                variant="ghost"
              >
                Reset
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={close} size="sm">
                OK
              </CButton>
            </>
          )}
          locale="en-US"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## With time

Set `timepicker` to add the time half. The field switches to a date and time mask, the panel grows a row of time selects under the calendar, and picking a day no longer closes the panel — the two halves own different parts of one value, so the interaction is not over until the user says so. While no time is picked, or the field holds a time a list does not offer, each select stands on a `--` placeholder, so every enabled option, the first allowed one included, sets the time.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerTimeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker label="Appointment" locale="en-US" timepicker />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          defaultDate="2026/07/14 14:30:00"
          label="Appointment"
          locale="en-US"
          timepicker
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

`minDate` and `maxDate` can carry a time of day. Their day stays selectable in the calendar and the time selects disable the hours, minutes and seconds before `minDate` or after `maxDate` on that day. A time the panel sets beyond a limit, such as the current time when the day of `minDate` is picked, moves to the limit; a typed time beyond it marks the field invalid. Until a date is picked, the time selects work on today moved into the limits. A limit without a time of day covers its whole day.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerTimeLimitsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          label="Appointment"
          locale="en-US"
          maxDate={new Date(2026, 9, 30, 17)}
          minDate={new Date(2026, 9, 15, 9, 30)}
          timepicker
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

`seconds`, `minutes` and `hours` narrow what the time half offers, and are ignored without `timepicker`. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale; on a 12-hour clock an hour that only one period allows sets that period.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

A native reset of the form returns an uncontrolled picker to the date it started with and drops the state a submit set; a controlled one (`date` with `onDateChange`) asks for the date it started with through `onDateChange` and shows the date your page gives until the page takes it.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <span className="form-label">Delivery date</span>
      <CDatePicker locale="en-US" name="deliveryDate" />
      <CFormText>We deliver on working days only.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Cleaner and picker button

The field ends with two buttons: one clears the value, the other opens the calendar. `cleanerIcon` and `pickerIcon` swap their artwork for your own node, `cleaner={false}` leaves the cleaner out, and `pickerIcon={false}` leaves out the button that opens the calendar. Without that button the popup has no pointer opener and nothing reports the expanded state, though the field keeps the keyboard openers listed under [Keyboard support](#keyboard-support).

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilCalendarCheck, cilXCircle } from '@coreui/icons'

export const DatePickerButtonsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          cleanerIcon={<CIcon icon={cilXCircle} />}
          defaultDate="2022/08/17"
          locale="en-US"
          pickerIcon={<CIcon icon={cilCalendarCheck} />}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker cleaner={false} defaultDate="2022/08/17" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and renders the label itself — the text also becomes the field's accessible name. No wrapper markup is needed, and the mask placeholders stay hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
)
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Disabled dates

CoreUI React DatePicker component includes a feature that allows you to disable certain dates, such as weekends or holidays. This can be accomplished by passing an array to `disabledDate` prop to the component, which determines which dates should be disabled based on custom logic.

In week, month, quarter and year selection the calendar and the field judge the whole period: it is refused only when it lies wholly before `minDate` or after `maxDate`, or `disabledDates` covers every day of it that the limits leave. In week selection the limits count as whole weeks, so for a week that is all seven days.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerDisabledDatesExample = () => {
  const calendarDate = new Date(2022, 2, 1)
  const disabledDates = [
    [new Date(2022, 2, 4), new Date(2022, 2, 7)],
    new Date(2022, 2, 16),
    new Date(2022, 3, 16),
    [new Date(2022, 4, 2), new Date(2022, 4, 8)],
  ]
  const maxDate = new Date(2022, 5, 0)
  const minDate = new Date(2022, 1, 1)

  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDatePicker
          calendarDate={calendarDate}
          disabledDates={disabledDates}
          locale="en-US"
          maxDate={maxDate}
          minDate={minDate}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Disabling weekends

You can disable weekends by passing a function to the `disabledDates` prop. Here's how to do it:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const disableWeekends = (date: Date) => {
  const day = date.getDay()
  return day === 0 || day === 6 // Disable Sundays (0) and Saturdays (6)
}

export const DatePickerDisablingWeekendsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDatePicker disabledDates={disableWeekends} locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The picker shows its validation state on the frame and on the sections of its field, which the message after the picker describes, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. The field keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over it, so a `required` picker that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, as the [date input](../date-input/#validation) does. The picker also sets the state itself: a date the limits reject marks it invalid, for as long as it stands.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CDatePicker, CForm } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerValidationExample = () => {
  const [deliveryState, setDeliveryState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a start date."
          label="Start date (required)"
          locale="en-US"
          name="start"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDatePicker
          defaultDate="2026-07-14"
          feedback="We have no delivery slots left on this date."
          label="Delivery date"
          locale="en-US"
          name="delivery"
          onValidationStateChange={setDeliveryState}
          validationState={deliveryState}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

`validationState` gives a state: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases that ask to be dropped the same way, though only `validationState` can be cleared by the setter you pass. A given state is a verdict on the date it was given for. When the user changes the date, with a day picked in the calendar, a time picked with `timepicker`, the cleaner, a footer button that changes the date through the context, or typing in the field, or the form is reset, the picker calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before `onDateChange`; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the second picker above does. An action that leaves the date as it is asks nothing, and neither does a change your code makes through `date`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the picker blocks the submit with the text of the message after it, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

## Locale

CoreUI React Date Picker allows users to display dates and times in a non-English locale. This is useful for applications that have international users or need to support multiple languages. 

### Auto

By default, the DatePicker component uses the default browser locale, but it can be easily configured to use a different locale supported by the JavaScript Internationalization API. To set the locale, you can simply pass the desired language code as a prop to the DatePicker component. This feature enables to create more inclusive and accessible applications that cater to a diverse audience.

With server-side rendering, pass `locale` explicitly: by default the server writes the text in its own locale and the browser in the reader's, and React reports a hydration mismatch when the two differ.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerLocaleAutoExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDatePicker />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Custom container

_Added in 5.28.0._

By default the calendar is rendered in `document.body`. Pass an HTML element, or a function that returns one, to the `container` property to render it somewhere else — for example inside a scrollable panel or a modal, so that it scrolls together with the rest of the content.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerCustomContainerExample = () => {
  const [container, setContainer] = useState<HTMLDivElement | null>(null)

  return (
    <div ref={setContainer}>
      <CDatePicker container={container} locale="en-US" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

To render the calendar in place, right after the input group, set `portal` to `false` instead.

## Custom formats

The `format` property is a mask: it spells out the sections the field renders. Tokens are `dd` for the day, `ww` for the ISO week, `MM` (`MMM`, `MMMM` for names) for the month, `QQQ` for the quarter, `yyyy` for the year, and text in single quotes is a literal, even when it contains token letters — `'Week' ww, yyyy` renders `Week 29, 2026`. Without it the field follows the locale's own date format.

`inputDateParse` still applies to pasted text, turning a custom string into a `Date`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
import { es } from 'date-fns/locale'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerCustomFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDatePicker
          defaultDate="2022/08/17"
          format="MMMM dd, yyyy"
          label="Date picker"
          locale="en-US"
          inputDateParse={(date: string) => parse(date, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDatePicker
          defaultDate="2022/08/17"
          format="yyyy MMMM dd"
          label="Selector de fechas"
          locale="es-ES"
          inputDateParse={(date: string) => parse(date, 'yyyy MMMM dd', new Date(), { locale: es })}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Weeks

Setting `selectionType` to `'week'` narrows the field to the locale's week presentation — `Week 29, 2026`. Override it with a mask of your own: `yyyy-'W'ww` for the ISO form, or a localized label. The `showWeekNumber` property adds the week numbers to the calendar.

```html
import React from 'react'

export const DatePickerCustomFormatsWeeksExample = () => {

          format="yyyy-'W'ww"
          label="Date picker"
          locale="en-US"
          selectionType="week"
          showWeekNumber
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDatePicker
          defaultDate="2022W10"
          format="'Semana' ww, yyyy"
          label="Selector de fechas"
          locale="es-ES"
          selectionType="week"
          showWeekNumber
```
```html
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

The calendar works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the open state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultShow` | the picker, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `show` | your component |

`onShowChange` fires in **both** modes whenever the calendar requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `defaultShow` or `show` is set.

### Uncontrolled

Every example above is uncontrolled — the picker manages its own calendar. `defaultShow` seeds it open on mount.

```jsx
<CDatePicker defaultShow />
```

### Controlled

Pass `show` and the calendar renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes. Here a checkbox pins the calendar open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CCol, CFormField, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DatePickerControlledExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          checked={show}
          id="datePickerControlledShow"
          label="Keep the calendar open"
          onChange={(event) => setShow(event.target.checked)}
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CRow>
        <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
          <CDatePicker label="Date Picker" locale="en-US" onShowChange={setShow} show={show} />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the picker like the checkbox above.

## Accessibility

The field is a group of spinbutton sections, so its own arrow keys belong to the value and the popup opens on the native control's dropdown keys instead. The field takes its name from an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` you pass to the picker, otherwise from `floatingLabel` or, without one, from `label`, and it is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass to the picker, then by `text` and the feedback that matches its state. Clicking the label that names the field moves focus to its first empty section. Focus enters the calendar on the selected date, else on today or on the `minDate` / `maxDate` today falls outside of, also when that date cannot be picked: it is announced as unavailable and the arrows move on from it. In week selection it enters on the row of that week.

The toggle button carries the panel's state — `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` pointing at the popup while it is open, and `aria-expanded` — so a screen reader announces what the button does and whether the panel is showing. The panel itself is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, so focus moves into it on open, stays there while it is open, and returns to the element that opened it, the toggle or the field, when it closes.

The toggle's name ends with the date the picker holds, written in full (`Toggle calendar, Friday, August 14, 2026`, with the time after it with `timepicker`), so a screen reader reads the picked date when the popup closes and focus goes back to the toggle. A live message would be lost at that moment, so the calendar does not announce a pick that closes the popup onto that toggle. With `timepicker` the popup stays open, and the calendar announces the pick through `ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement`; it does the same without a toggle (`pickerIcon={false}`).

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the popup and move focus into it |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the popup and return focus to the field or the toggle that opened it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move within the open panel; the field is outside the dialog and stays out of the cycle |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused value |

Inside the grid, navigation follows the [calendar keyboard model](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/calendar/#keyboard-support): arrows move by day and week, <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> move to the first and last day of the week inside `minDate` / `maxDate` (the first and last week of the month with `selectionType="week"`), and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Page Up</kbd> (with <kbd>Shift</kbd> for years) move between months and years. A date that cannot be picked takes the focus like any other, and <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> do nothing there. A key pressed there with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> is neither handled nor cancelled, so it stays free for the browser and assistive technology.

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

# React Date Picker Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Date Picker component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) on the element `CDatePicker` renders, so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. Pass them through `style` to restyle one field.

The picker declares its local CSS variables on its panel, `.date-picker-popup`, and the calendar inside it declares its own on `.calendar`. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is supported too.

```scss
$date-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $date-picker-tokens
);
```

The time half declares its own on `.date-picker-time-body`, so it can be restyled without touching the panel around it.

```scss
$date-picker-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-time-body-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-body-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-width: 2.5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-font-size: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-font-size),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-y),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-x),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
  ),
  $date-picker-time-tokens
);
```

```scss
$calendar-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-calendar-table-margin: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-table-cell-size: 2.75rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-calendar-nav-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid var(--cui-calendar-nav-border-color),
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-padding-y: .25rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-bg: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-border-width: 1px,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-border-color: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),

```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, the combobox, autocomplete and multi select.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

Each part of the panel declares its tokens itself, and the panel is rendered into `document.body` unless `portal` is `false`, so a variable set on `CDatePicker` through `style` styles the field but reaches none of them. Set them with a rule on the part that declares them:

```css
.date-picker-popup {
  --cui-popup-bg: #f8f9fa;
}

.date-picker-popup .calendar {
  --cui-calendar-cell-hover-bg: #e9ecef;
}
```

# React Date Range Input Component

> Create a React start and end date field in one frame. Both ends use the section-based mask of the date input, and the range is validated as a whole.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

The React Date Range Input component is two [date input](../date-input/) fields and a separator in one frame, held together by the range it owns: both ends share the mask and the limits, and an end before the start marks the whole field invalid.

Each end follows the standard React controlled/uncontrolled pattern of its own: use `defaultStartDate` / `defaultEndDate` for an uncontrolled field, or pair `startDate` / `endDate` with `onStartDateChange` / `onEndDateChange` for a controlled one. A native reset of the form puts back the date each end started with, and a controlled end only asks for it through its callback.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput label="Stay" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          defaultEndDate="2026-07-20"
          defaultStartDate="2026-07-14"
          label="Stay"
          locale="en-US"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Date and time

Set `type="datetime"` and both ends carry the time. The hour cycle follows the locale, and `seconds` adds a seconds section to each field. The range compares its two ends by instant, so an end earlier in the day than the start on the same date marks the field invalid.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputDateTimeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={7}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          endName="shift-end"
          label="Shift"
          locale="en-US"
          startName="shift-start"
          type="datetime"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={6}>
        <CFormField>
          <CFormLabel id="dateRangeInputStayLabel">Stay</CFormLabel>
          <CDateRangeInput
            aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel"
            endName="stayEnd"
            locale="en-US"
            startName="stayStart"
          />
          <CFormText>Check-out has to be on or after check-in.</CFormText>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Formats

Set an explicit mask for both ends with the `format` property. The parser is the [date input's](../date-input/#formats), so dayjs/moment tokens (`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`) and date-fns/Unicode tokens (`dd`, `MM`, `yyyy`) both work, and any other character becomes a literal separator.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput format="dd.MM.yyyy" label="dd.MM.yyyy" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput format="YYYY-MM-DD" label="YYYY-MM-DD" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

A mask that leaves out sections works here too — a month-and-year range reports the first day of each month:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputPartialMasksExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput format="MM.yyyy" label="Reporting period" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

For picking a whole range on a calendar, use the [date range picker](../date-range-picker/).

## Month names

Use the `MMM` or `MMMM` tokens for text month sections in both ends; typing letters matches a month by prefix. Pass all twelve names through the `monthNames` property to override the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const POLISH_MONTHS = [
  'styczeń',
  'luty',
  'marzec',
  'kwiecień',
  'maj',
  'czerwiec',
  'lipiec',
  'sierpień',
  'wrzesień',
  'październik',
  'listopad',
  'grudzień',
]

export const DateRangeInputMonthNamesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput format="DD MMMM YYYY" label="DD MMMM YYYY" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          format="DD MMMM YYYY"
          label="Standalone Polish month names"
          locale="pl-PL"
          monthNames={POLISH_MONTHS}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, both masks follow the locale set via the `locale` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputLocalesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput label="en-US" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput label="ja-JP" locale="ja-JP" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Min and max dates

`minDate` and `maxDate` constrain both ends. A completed date outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class on its own field and that end reports `null` until the value is corrected.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputMinMaxExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Dates in July 2026"
          locale="en-US"
          maxDate={new Date(2026, 6, 31)}
          minDate={new Date(2026, 6, 1)}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Disabled dates

Beyond a simple range, the `disabledDates` property excludes specific dates from both ends — single `Date`s, `[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputDisabledDatesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          defaultStartDate={new Date(2026, 6, 10)}
          disabledDates={[[new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)], new Date(2026, 6, 16)]}
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Stay"
          maxDate={new Date(2026, 6, 31)}
          minDate={new Date(2026, 6, 1)}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          disabledDates={(date: Date) => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6}
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Business days"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Custom formats

The built-in token parser covers dayjs, moment, date-fns, and luxon format strings, so you can reuse the format string from the date library you already work with — the library itself isn't required to render or edit the masks. Pair it with `inputDateParse` when you want that library to also parse text pasted into either end, here with `date-fns`:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputCustomFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={6}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          defaultEndDate={new Date(2026, 6, 20)}
          defaultStartDate={new Date(2026, 6, 14)}
          format="MMMM DD, YYYY"
          inputDateParse={(value) => parse(value, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())}
          label="date-fns format"
          locale="en-US"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The frame shows the state of the range and each field shows its own, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. Each end keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over its field, which takes part in native constraint validation: a `required` end that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, and the browser, or `<CForm>`, puts focus on its first empty section.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CDateRangeInput, CForm } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputValidationExample = () => {
  const [stayState, setStayState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          defaultEndDate={new Date(2026, 6, 14)}
          defaultStartDate={new Date(2026, 6, 20)}
          endName="check-out"
          feedbackInvalid="Check-out has to be on or after check-in."
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Out of order"
          locale="en-US"
          startName="check-in"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          defaultEndDate={new Date(2026, 6, 20)}
          defaultStartDate={new Date(2026, 6, 14)}
          endName="to"
          feedback="Those dates are already booked."
          format="dd.MM.yyyy"
          label="Stay"
          locale="en-US"
          onValidationStateChange={setStayState}
          startName="from"
          validationState={stayState}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

The state comes from these places, in this order:

- The order: an end before the start is a state of the range, not of either date, and only dates the limits accept take part in it, so `.is-invalid` lands on the frame and both fields stay editable. Every section of both fields carries `aria-invalid="true"` until the order is fixed, and neither field is drawn valid meanwhile, whatever else is set.
- The limits: a completed date outside `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates` makes its own field invalid, which the frame picks up, and that field's value field submits no date until it is corrected. A date before year 1 counts as before `minDate` even without that prop; when the field loses the focus, its year becomes 1.
- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, a verdict on the whole range that lands on the frame and on both ends.
- A validation that reports a field (a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which `<CForm>` and the [stepper](../stepper/) call as well), and in a form with the `validate` property of `<CForm>` the `:user-invalid` state of each value field, with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state, as for the [date input](../date-input/#validation).

A state you give is a verdict on the range it was given for. When the user changes either end, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before it reports the change; pass your state setter there to drop the state from both ends and the frame, as the second range above does. A change your code makes through `startDate` or `endDate` asks nothing. While the given state is `'invalid'`, both ends block the submit with the text of the message after the frame, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the range is disabled or read-only. A native form reset returns both ends to the dates they started with; a `reset` listener that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the whole reset. An end your page controls keeps the value it gives it.

While an end is invalid, an `.invalid-feedback` or `.invalid-tooltip` you render after the range describes each of its sections.

### Blocking the submit

A `required` end that is empty, incomplete or rejected by the limits blocks the submit by itself. An end before the start does not, since both ends hold dates the browser accepts, and neither does an optional end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, which submits no date. Check the dates before you send them; `onStartDateChange` and `onEndDateChange` report `null` for an end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, so one condition covers both:

```tsx
const [start, setStart] = useState<Date | null>(null)
const [end, setEnd] = useState<Date | null>(null)

return (
  <CForm
    onSubmit={(event) => {
      if (!start || !end || end < start) {
        event.preventDefault()
      }
    }}
  >
    <CDateRangeInput onEndDateChange={setEnd} onStartDateChange={setStart} />
    <CButton type="submit">Book</CButton>
  </CForm>
)
```

## Floating labels

Each end can carry its own [floating label](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/) through `startFloatingLabel` and `endFloatingLabel`; the text is also that end's accessible name.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputFloatingLabelsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={6}>
        <CDateRangeInput
          endFloatingLabel="Check-out"
          locale="en-US"
          startFloatingLabel="Check-in"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep both labels [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the masks showing.

## Separator

The `separator` property takes a node, so the arrow between the two ends can be a word, an icon of your own, or anything else you render. It is hidden from assistive technology either way. Left out, the default arrow renders and flips for right-to-left.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangeInputSeparatorExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={6}>
        <CDateRangeInput label="Stay" locale="en-US" separator={<span className="fg-2">to</span>} />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

```html
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

```html
          disabled
```
