## Accessibility

Each end is a [date input](../date-input/#accessibility) with the spinbutton pattern per section, so the range is two labelled groups rather than one opaque control:

- **Role attributes**: each end has `role="group"`, every section is a `role="spinbutton"` with its value attributes.
- **Names**: `label` names the pair, because the frame around both ends is a `role="group"` pointing at it; the start and end are named separately — `ariaStartLabel` and `ariaEndLabel` by default, or the floating label text when one is set. Each end is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass, then by `text` and the feedback that matches the state of the range.
- **Label click**: clicking the label that names the pair moves focus to the first empty section of the start date, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Separator**: hidden from assistive technology, whatever you render into it.
- **Roving tabindex**: each end is a single tab stop; <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves from the start to the end.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>0</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> | Type into the focused section; the caret advances when the section is complete |
| <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> | In text month sections, match a month name by prefix |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Increment / decrement the focused section |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous section, crossing the separator from the last section of the start date into the end date and back; in a right-to-left layout the two keys swap |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last section of the focused end |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clear the focused section; move to the previous section when already empty |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the focused section |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move from the start date to the end date |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select the whole value of the focused end |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a date into the focused end |

Apart from the shortcuts in the table, a key pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> changes nothing in the field and is not cancelled: arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move no focus and change no section, and a digit or letter is not entered. The key stays free for the browser, assistive technology and the picker around the field, where <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> opens the calendar. A character that <kbd>AltGr</kbd> or <kbd>Option</kbd> composes is still entered.

# React Date Range Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Date Range Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CDateRangeInput

```jsx
import { CDateRangeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaEndLabel` | `string` | `End date` | The accessible name of the end field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaStartLabel` | `string` | `Start date` | The accessible name of the start field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | - | Focus the first section of the start date right after mounting. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `defaultEndDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial end date for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `endDate` is set. |
| `defaultStartDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial start date for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `startDate` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | - | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. |
| `endDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled end date. Pair it with `onEndDateChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultEndDate` instead. |
| `endFloatingLabel` | `string` | - | The floating label of the end field. The text is also that field's accessible name. |
| `endName` | `string` | - | Name of the value input carrying the end date. Without it the end date is not submitted with the form. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | - | The mask layout. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `inputDateParse` | `((value: string) => Date \| null)` | - | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `default` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Max selectable date. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Min selectable date. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | - | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `onEndDateChange` | `((date: Date \| null) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the end date changes; receives the `Date`, or `null` while that end is incomplete or invalid. |
| `onStartDateChange` | `((date: Date \| null) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the start date changes; receives the `Date`, or `null` while that end is incomplete or invalid. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes either end, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the range it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean` | - | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived time layout. |
| `separator` | `ReactNode` | - | The node rendered between the two fields. It is hidden from assistive technology. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large - both ends follow. |
| `startDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled start date. Pair it with `onStartDateChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultStartDate` instead. |
| `startFloatingLabel` | `string` | - | The floating label of the start field. The text is also that field's accessible name. |
| `startName` | `string` | - | Name of the value input carrying the start date. Without it the start date is not submitted with the form. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `'date' \| 'datetime'` | `date` | Which sections the locale-derived layout carries on both ends. A `format` names the sections itself and overrides this. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the frame; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on the sections of both ends and blocks the submit. An end before the start and an end the limits reject mark the frame invalid on their own. The user's next change of either end asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

# React Date Range Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Date Range Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The two ends are date inputs, so they carry the `form-date-time` tokens, and the frame around them carries the [form control group](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/) ones. The range adds no tokens of its own.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# React Date Range Picker Component

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

Explore basic usage of the Date Range Picker through sample code snippets that demonstrate its core functionality.

### Days

Select date ranges by day, from a basic picker to one with projected footer actions.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerDaysExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          label="Date range"
          locale="en-US"
          onStartDateChange={(date) => console.log(date)}
          onEndDateChange={(date) => console.log(date)}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2022/08/17"
          label="Date range"
          locale="en-US"
          defaultStartDate="2022/08/03"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

#### With footer

The `footer` prop projects your own content below the calendars. Pass a node, or a function receiving the picker's context — `setRange`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isDateSelectable`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `disabled` — so a projected button acts on the picker and reads its state. While a footer is present the panel stays open after the second date, because the footer's actions are what closes it.

Any descendant can reach the same context with the `useDateRangePicker()` hook.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerDaysWithFooterExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          footer={({ clear, close }) => (
            <>
              <CButton
                className="me-auto"
                theme="primary"
                onClick={clear}
                size="sm"
                variant="ghost"
              >
                Clear
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={close} size="sm">
                OK
              </CButton>
            </>
          )}
          locale="en-US"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2022/08/17"
          footer={({ close, reset }) => (
            <>
              <CButton
                className="me-auto"
                theme="primary"
                onClick={reset}
                size="sm"
                variant="ghost"
              >
                Reset
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={close} size="sm">
                OK
              </CButton>
            </>
          )}
          locale="en-US"
          defaultStartDate="2022/08/03"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

A native reset of the form returns an uncontrolled picker to the range it started with and drops the state a submit set; a controlled end (`startDate`, `endDate`) asks for the date it started with through its callback and shows the date your page gives until the page takes it.

```html
import React from 'react'

export const DateRangePickerFormFieldExample = () => {

      <span className="form-label">Reporting period</span>
      <CDateRangePicker endName="periodEnd" locale="en-US" startName="periodStart" />
      <CFormText>Both dates are included in the report.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Disabled dates

Our React Date Range Picker component features the ability to disable specific dates, such as weekends or holidays, by using the `disabledDates` prop. This prop takes an array and uses custom logic to determine which dates should be disabled.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerDisabledDatesExample = () => {
  const calendarDate = new Date(2022, 2, 1)
  const disabledDates = [
    [new Date(2022, 2, 4), new Date(2022, 2, 7)],
    new Date(2022, 2, 16),
    new Date(2022, 3, 16),
    [new Date(2022, 4, 2), new Date(2022, 4, 8)],
  ]
  const maxDate = new Date(2022, 5, 0)
  const minDate = new Date(2022, 1, 1)

  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          calendarDate={calendarDate}
          disabledDates={disabledDates}
          locale="en-US"
          maxDate={maxDate}
          minDate={minDate}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Disabling weekends

You can disable weekends by passing a function to the `disabledDates` prop. Here's how to do it:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

const disableWeekends = (date: Date) => {
  const day = date.getDay()
  return day === 0 || day === 6 // Disable Sundays (0) and Saturdays (6)
}

export const DateRangePickerDisablingWeekendsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker disabledDates={disableWeekends} locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The picker shows its validation state on the frame and on the sections of both fields, which the message after the picker describes, the way [`<CForm>`](../validation/) does for a native field. Each field keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over it, so a `required` end that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, as in the [date range input](../date-range-input/#validation). The picker also sets the state itself: a date the limits reject marks the range invalid, and so does an end before the start, for as long as it stands.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CDateRangePicker, CForm } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerValidationExample = () => {
  const [stayState, setStayState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <CCol lg={7}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2026-08-17"
          defaultStartDate="2026-08-10"
          endName="to"
          feedback="Those dates are already booked."
          locale="en-US"
          onValidationStateChange={setStayState}
          startName="from"
          validationState={stayState}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

`validationState` gives a state of the range: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases that ask to be dropped the same way, though only `validationState` can be cleared by the setter you pass. `feedbackInvalid` or `feedbackValid` is the message shown while that state holds, describing both fields, and `tooltipFeedback` shows it as a tooltip instead. A given state is a verdict on the range it was given for. When the user changes the range, with a day picked in the calendar, the cleaner, a preset or a footer button that changes it through the context, or typing in a field, or the form is reset, the picker calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before it reports the change; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the example does. An action that leaves the range as it is asks nothing, and neither does a change your code makes through `startDate` and `endDate`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, both ends block the submit with the text of the message after the picker, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

### Blocking the submit

A `required` end that is empty, incomplete or rejected by the limits blocks the submit by itself. An end before the start does not, since both ends hold dates the browser accepts, and neither does an optional end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, which submits no date. Check the dates before you send them; `onStartDateChange` and `onEndDateChange` report `null` for an end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, so one condition covers both:

```tsx
const [start, setStart] = useState<Date | null>(null)
const [end, setEnd] = useState<Date | null>(null)

return (
  <CForm
    onSubmit={(event) => {
      if (!start || !end || end < start) {
        event.preventDefault()
      }
    }}
  >
    <CDateRangePicker onEndDateChange={setEnd} onStartDateChange={setStart} />
    <CButton type="submit">Book</CButton>
  </CForm>
)
```

## Custom ranges

The `ranges` prop projects content beside the calendars — that is where range presets live. Pass a node, or a function receiving the picker's context; a preset button calls `setRange` with its own two dates.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerCustomRangesExample = () => {
  const today = new Date()
  const daysAgo = (days: number) => new Date(new Date().setDate(today.getDate() - days))

  const presets: [string, [Date, Date]][] = [
    ['Today', [today, today]],
    ['Yesterday', [daysAgo(1), daysAgo(1)]],
    ['Last 7 days', [daysAgo(6), today]],
    ['Last 30 days', [daysAgo(29), today]],
    ['This month', [new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), 1), today]],
    [
      'Last month',
      [
        new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth() - 1, 1),
        new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), 0),
      ],
    ],
  ]

  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol sm={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          ranges={({ setRange }) =>
            presets.map(([label, [start, end]]) => (
              <CButton
                theme="primary"
                key={label}
                onClick={() => setRange(start, end)}
                size="sm"
                variant="ghost"
              >
                {label}
              </CButton>
            ))
          }
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Locale

CoreUI's React Date Range Picker enables the display of dates and times in non-English locales, making it essential for international users and multilingual support.

### Auto

By default, the DateRangePicker component uses the default browser locale, but it can be easily configured to use a different locale supported by the JavaScript Internationalization API. To set the locale, you can pass the desired language code as a prop to the DateRangePicker component. This feature enables the creation of more inclusive and accessible applications that cater to a diverse audience.

With server-side rendering, pass `locale` explicitly: by default the server writes the text in its own locale and the browser in the reader's, and React reports a hydration mismatch when the two differ.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerLocaleAutoExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

```html
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Persian

The date range picker is Gregorian: with a locale whose own calendar has different months, like Persian, its calendar shows the Gregorian months in that locale's language and digits, and its fields hold Gregorian numbers.

## Custom formats

The `format` property is a mask: it spells out the sections both fields render. Tokens are `dd` for the day, `ww` for the ISO week, `MM` (`MMM`, `MMMM` for names) for the month, `QQQ` for the quarter, `yyyy` for the year, and text in single quotes is a literal, even when it contains token letters — `'Week' ww, yyyy` renders `Week 29, 2026`. Without it the fields follow the locale's own date format.

`inputDateParse` still applies to pasted text, turning a custom string into a `Date`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { parse } from 'date-fns'
import { es } from 'date-fns/locale'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerCustomFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2022/08/24"
          format="MMMM dd, yyyy"
          inputDateParse={(date: string) => parse(date, 'MMMM dd, yyyy', new Date())}
          label="Date range"
          locale="en-US"
          defaultStartDate="2022/08/17"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2022/08/24"
          format="yyyy MMMM dd"
          inputDateParse={(date: string) => parse(date, 'yyyy MMMM dd', new Date(), { locale: es })}
          label="Selector de rango de fechas"
          locale="es-ES"
          defaultStartDate="2022/08/17"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Weeks

Setting `selectionType` to `'week'` narrows both fields to the locale's week presentation. Override it with a mask of your own: `yyyy-'W'ww` for the ISO form, or a localized label. The `showWeekNumber` property adds the week numbers to the calendars.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerCustomFormatsWeeksExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2022W12"
          format="yyyy-'W'ww"
          label="Date range"
          locale="en-US"
          selectionType="week"
          showWeekNumber
          defaultStartDate="2022W10"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CDateRangePicker
          defaultEndDate="2022W12"
          format="'Semana' ww, yyyy"
          label="Selector de rango de fechas"
          locale="es-ES"
          selectionType="week"
          showWeekNumber
          defaultStartDate="2022W10"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

The calendar works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the open state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultShow` | the picker, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `show` | your component |

`onShowChange` fires in **both** modes whenever the calendar requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `defaultShow` or `show` is set.

### Uncontrolled

Every example above is uncontrolled — the picker manages its own calendar. `defaultShow` seeds it open on mount.

```jsx
<CDateRangePicker defaultShow />
```

### Controlled

Pass `show` and the calendar renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes. Here a checkbox pins the calendar open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CCol, CFormField, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CDateRangePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const DateRangePickerControlledExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          checked={show}
          id="dateRangePickerControlledShow"
          label="Keep the calendar open"
          onChange={(event) => setShow(event.target.checked)}
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CRow>
        <CCol sm={8} lg={6}>
          <CDateRangePicker label="Date range" locale="en-US" onShowChange={setShow} show={show} />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the picker like the checkbox above.

## Accessibility

Both fields are groups of spinbutton sections, so their own arrow keys belong to the value and the popup opens on the native control's dropdown keys instead. Each field is named by its floating label, or by `ariaStartLabel` and `ariaEndLabel` ("Start date" and "End date" by default), so a screen reader tells the two apart. They sit inside one `role="group"` named by `label`, and clicking that label moves focus to the first empty section of the start date. Each is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass to the picker, then by `text` and the feedback that matches its state.

The toggle button carries the panel's state — `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` pointing at the popup while it is open, and `aria-expanded` — so a screen reader announces what the button does and whether the panel is showing. The panel itself is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, so focus moves into it on open, stays there while it is open, and returns to the element that opened it, the toggle or the field, when it closes.

The toggle's name ends with the range the picker holds, written by the locale (`Toggle calendar, Thursday, August 20 – Sunday, August 23, 2026`), so a screen reader reads the picked range when the popup closes and focus goes back to the toggle. A live message would be lost at that moment, so the calendar does not announce the pick of the end that closes the popup. A pick that leaves the popup open, such as a new start that keeps the end or any pick with a `footer`, is announced through `ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement`, and so is every pick without a toggle (`pickerIcon={false}`).

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the popup and move focus into it |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the popup and return focus to the field or the toggle that opened it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move within the open panel; the field is outside the dialog and stays out of the cycle |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused value |

Inside the grid, navigation follows the [calendar keyboard model](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/calendar/#keyboard-support): arrows move by day and week, <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> move to the first and last day of the week inside `minDate` / `maxDate` (the first and last week of the month with `selectionType="week"`), and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Page Up</kbd> (with <kbd>Shift</kbd> for years) move between months and years. A date that cannot be picked takes the focus like any other, and <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> do nothing there.

| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaNavNextMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Next month'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next month in the React Calendar component. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. Customize for a more accessible calendar experience. |
| `ariaNavNextYearLabel` | `string` | `'Next year'` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next year in the React Calendar component. Screen readers utilize this label to inform users of the button's functionality, aiding in a more inclusive application. |

| `ariaNavPrevYearsLabel` | `string` | `'Previous 12 years'` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the previous page of years. |
| `ariaNothingToPickLabel` | `string` | `'Nothing on this page can be picked'` | Sets the description (`aria-describedby`) of a grid in which nothing can be picked, such as a page wholly outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or one that `disabledDates` covers, also announced when the calendar turns to such a page. An empty string leaves the grid without a description. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `Toggle calendar` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that opens the calendar, followed by the range the picker holds. |

An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement` | `string` | `'Selected range: {start} to {end}'` | Sets the message announced when a pick leaves both ends set, unless the pick closes the panel, which names the toggle with the range instead. `{start}` and `{end}` are replaced by the full names of its ends. An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaStartLabel` | `string` | `Start date` | The accessible name of the start field, used when it has no floating label. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaWeekNumberLabel` | `((weekNumber: number) => string \| undefined)` | - | Names each week number for screen readers: a function that takes the week number and returns its name. Without it the name is the locale's word for week and the number, such as `Week 36`. Keep the number in the name, so a voice-control user can say what they see. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `calendarDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Defines the initial date or reference date for the calendar. This date can be either a Date object or a string that can be converted into a valid date. Without it, the calendar opens on the picker's start date, else its end date. |
| `calendars` | `number` | `2` | Specifies how many individual calendars should be displayed side by side on desktop devices. Increasing this number allows your users to view multiple months (or years, etc.) simultaneously. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Adds a custom class name to the React Date Range Picker. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the button that clears the value. |
| `cleanerIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork of the cleaner button. Defaults to a cross drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| (() => Element \| DocumentFragment \| null) \| null` | - | The element the calendar is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dayFormat` | `"numeric" \| "2-digit" \| ((date: Date) => string \| number)` | `'numeric'` | Sets the format for days. Accepts either a built-in format ('numeric' or '2-digit') or a custom function to return any desired string or number for the day. |

| `defaultEndDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial end of the range for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `endDate` is set. |
| `defaultShow` | `boolean` | - | The initial open state of an uncontrolled calendar — read once on mount. |
| `defaultStartDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial start of the range for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `startDate` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggles the disabled state. |

This is useful for disabling weekends, holidays, or any dates that you need to restrict within your React Calendar component. In week, month, quarter and year selection a period is disabled when every day of it is. |
| `endDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled end of the range. Pair it with `onEndDateChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultEndDate` instead. |
| `endName` | `string` | - | Name of the end value input. Without it the end date is not submitted with the form. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `number` | `1` | Sets the first day of the week. This can be adjusted for different locales or preferences: - `0` = Sunday - `1` = Monday - `2` = Tuesday - `3` = Wednesday - `4` = Thursday - `5` = Friday - `6` = Saturday |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |

The metadata carries the cell's full name as `label`, for example for visually hidden text next to a short label. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `selectAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets whether days from adjacent months (shown at the start/end of the current view) are selectable. This only applies if `showAdjacentDays` is set to `true`. A picked day of an adjacent month keeps the month on screen and shows as selected with an outline on a subtle background instead of the solid fill. |
| `selectionType` | `SelectionTypes` | `day` | Specifies the selection type for the React Calendar component. Supports: - `day`: Regular day selection (default) - `week`: Select an entire week - `month`: Select an entire month - `quarter`: Select an entire quarter - `year`: Select an entire year |
| `separatorIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork between the two fields. Defaults to an arrow drawn on `currentColor`, mirrored in right-to-left contexts. |
| `show` | `boolean` | - | Control the open state. When set, the calendar renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `showAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | `true` | Controls whether the calendar should display dates from previous or next months (non-selectable if `selectAdjacentDays` is `false`). This can make the calendar visually continuous. |
| `showWeekNumber` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggles the display of week numbers (ISO 8601) in the calendar's left column. Particularly beneficial for applications where users need to see the week index for scheduling or reporting. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `startDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled start of the range. Pair it with `onStartDateChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultStartDate` instead. |
| `startName` | `string` | - | Name of the start value input. Without it the start date is not submitted with the form. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. A field of a date range whose end is before its start draws no other state. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | - | Controls the visibility of the calendar. |
| `weekdayFormat` | `number \| "long" \| "narrow" \| "short" \| ((date: Date) => string \| number)` | `2` | Sets the format or length of the weekday names displayed in the calendar header. You can use numeric values like 2 (two-letter abbreviations) or built-in string formats like `'long'`, `'narrow'`, and `'short'`, or provide a custom function to fully control how weekdays are displayed. |
| `weekNumbersLabel` | `string` | - | Defines the label that appears above the week numbers column. For example, you might label it `'WK'` or `'Week #'`. Without it the column is named for screen readers with the locale's word for week. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearFormat` | `"numeric" \| "2-digit"` | `'numeric'` | Sets how the year cells of the years view write the year: `'numeric'` (2026) or `'2-digit'` (26). The navigation always writes the full year. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

# React Date Range Picker Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Date Range Picker component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) on the element `CDateRangePicker` renders, so its frame, the separator, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. Pass them through `style` to restyle one field. The two ends are [date inputs](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-input/styling/#css-variables) and carry the `form-date-time` tokens.

The range picker shares the date picker's panel, `.date-picker-popup`, and declares its local CSS variables there; the calendar inside it declares its own on `.calendar`. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is supported too.

```scss
$date-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $date-picker-tokens
);
```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, the combobox, autocomplete and multi select.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

Each part of the panel declares its tokens itself, and the panel is rendered into `document.body` unless `portal` is `false`, so a variable set on `CDateRangePicker` through `style` styles the field but reaches none of them. Set them with a rule on the part that declares them:

```css
.date-picker-popup {
  --cui-popup-bg: #f8f9fa;
}

.date-picker-popup .calendar {
  --cui-calendar-cell-hover-bg: #e9ecef;
}
```

# React Form Field

> A layout wrapper for a form control, its label, description and validation feedback, built on CSS grid.

`<CFormField>` renders the `.form-field` wrapper, which gives a control the layout and spacing it needs alongside its label, description and validation feedback — so a form is spaced by the field itself rather than by margin utilities sprinkled over its parts.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="fieldText">Email address</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput type="email" id="fieldText" placeholder="name@example.com" />
      <CFormText>We&apos;ll never share your email with anyone else.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## How it works

- **Default layout** is a single-column grid: everything stacks vertically with one gap. Use it for text inputs, selects, textareas, ranges, input groups and any of the [PRO field components](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/).
- **Two-column layout** switches on through `:has()` when the input `<CCheckbox>`, `<CRadio>` or `<CSwitch>` renders (`.check`, `.radio`, `.switch`) is a direct child — the control pins to the first column, the label and description stack in the second. The deprecated `.form-check-input` triggers it too, so the markup the legacy `<CFormCheck>` and `<CFormSwitch>` render lays out the same way.
- **A field label** (`<CFormLabel>`, rendering `.form-label`) spans both columns and sits above the control row.
- **Grouped controls** — nest a `<CFormField>` per control inside an outer one to put several radios or checkboxes under a shared label with a shared description.

## Examples

### Select

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldSelectExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="fieldSelect">Country</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect
        id="fieldSelect"
        options={[
          { label: 'Choose one…' },
          { label: 'United States', value: '1' },
          { label: 'Canada', value: '2' },
          { label: 'United Kingdom', value: '3' },
        ]}
      />
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

### Textarea

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldTextareaExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="fieldTextarea">Message</CFormLabel>
      <CFormTextarea id="fieldTextarea" rows={3} />
      <CFormText>Be sure to include the relevant details.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

### Checkbox

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldCheckboxExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CCheckbox id="fieldCheck" label="Subscribe to the newsletter" />
      <CFormText>We send one email a month, and never share your address.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

### Grouped

Nest one `<CFormField>` per control inside an outer one, and give the group its own `.form-label`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormText, CRadio } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldGroupedExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <span className="form-label">Delivery</span>
      <CFormField>
        <CRadio name="fieldRadio" id="fieldRadio1" label="Standard" defaultChecked />
        <CFormText>Three to five working days.</CFormText>
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CRadio name="fieldRadio" id="fieldRadio2" label="Express" />
        <CFormText>Next working day, where available.</CFormText>
      </CFormField>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

### Switch

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormText, CSwitch } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldSwitchExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CSwitch id="fieldSwitch" label="Email notifications" />
      <CFormText>Turn this off and we will only contact you about your account.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Overhead label

When a check, radio, or switch needs a field title above it, add a `.form-label`. It sits on its own row above the control, while the control's own label and description keep their places:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldOverheadLabelExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <span className="form-label">Terms and conditions</span>
      <CCheckbox id="fieldOverheadCheck" label="I agree to the terms" />
      <CFormText>Please read them before agreeing.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Validation

Feedback elements are children of the field like any other, so they inherit its gap and land under the control. Set `validationState` on the form component and pass the message through `feedbackValid` / `feedbackInvalid`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormFieldValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="fieldValidation">Username</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput
        type="text"
        id="fieldValidation"
        defaultValue="jan kowalski"
        validationState="invalid"
        feedbackInvalid="A username cannot contain spaces."
      />
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

See [validation](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/validation/) for the full picture, including the server-side and browser-native flavours.

# React Form Field Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Form Field component with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

React Form Field uses local CSS variables for enhanced real-time customization. Set them on the field itself, or on an ancestor for a whole form.

```scss
$form-field-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-field-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-form-field-column-gap: .5rem,
  ),
  $form-field-tokens
);
```

`.form-field-card` and `.form-group` carry their own sets:

```scss
$form-field-card-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-field-card-padding-y: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-form-field-card-padding-x: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-form-field-card-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-form-field-card-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-form-field-card-checked-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-form-field-card-checked-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $form-field-card-tokens
);
```

```scss
$form-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-group-gap: .5rem,
  ),
  $form-group-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-form-field-gap': '0.75rem',
}

return <CFormField style={customVars}>...</CFormField>
```

```html
import React from 'react'
```

# React Floating labels

> React floating label component. Create beautifully simple form labels that float over your input fields.

## Example

Use `floatingLabel` property on `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>` or `<CFormTextarea>` to enable floating labels with textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>` and `<CFormTextarea>` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. The placeholder stays hidden while the label rests in the field, and shows under the floated label once the field has focus.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInput"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email address"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
      />
      <CFormInput
        type="password"
        id="floatingPassword"
        floatingLabel="Password"
        placeholder="••••••••"
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

You can create the same form control by wrapping a pair of `<CFormInput>` and `<CFormLabel>` elements in `<CFormFloating>` to enable floating labels with textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<CFormInput>` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. Write the `<CFormLabel>` first, so a screen reader announces it before the field's value. The control-first order keeps working.

```jsx
<CFormFloating className="mb-4">
  <CFormLabel htmlFor="floatingInput">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="email" id="floatingInput" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</CFormFloating>
<CFormFloating>
  <CFormLabel htmlFor="floatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="password" id="floatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••" />
</CFormFloating>
```

When there's a `value` already defined, `<CFormLabel>`s will automatically adjust to their floated position.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabels2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CFormInput
      type="email"
      id="floatingInputValue"
      floatingLabel="Input with value"
      placeholder="name@example.com"
      defaultValue="test@example.com"
    />
  )
}
```

Form validation styles also work as expected.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInputValid"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email addresss"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        defaultValue="test@example.com"
        validationState="valid"
      />
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInputInvalid"
        floatingLabel="Email addresss"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        defaultValue="test@example.com"
        validationState="invalid"
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Textareas

By default, `<CFormTextarea>`s will be the same height as `<CFormInput>`s.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsTextareaExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormTextarea
      id="floatingTextarea"
      floatingLabel="Comments"
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
    ></CFormTextarea>
  )
}
```

To set a custom height on your `<CFormTextarea>`, do not use the `rows` attribute. Instead, set an explicit `height` (either inline or via custom CSS).

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsTextarea2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CFormTextarea
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
      id="floatingTextarea2"
      floatingLabel="Comments"
      style={{ height: '100px' }}
    ></CFormTextarea>
  )
}
```

## Selects

Other than `<CFormInput>`, floating labels are only available on `<CFormSelect>`s. They work in the same way, but unlike `<CFormInput>`s, they'll always show the `<CFormLabel>` in its floated state. **Selects with `size` and `multiple` are not supported.**

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormSelect } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsSelectExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormSelect
      id="floatingSelect"
      floatingLabel="Works with selects"
      aria-label="Floating label select example"
    >
      <option>Open this select menu</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  )
}
```

## Date and time

Date, time, datetime-local, month, and week inputs also always show the label in its floated state. These controls do not support placeholders the way textual inputs do, so a `placeholder` is not required (and is ignored by most browsers on these types). For a field that formats its value by locale, use the [Date Picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-picker/#floating-labels) or the [Time Picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/time-picker/#floating-labels) with the `floatingLabel` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsDateTimeExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput type="date" id="floatingDate" floatingClassName="mb-4" floatingLabel="Date" />
      <CFormInput type="time" id="floatingTime" floatingLabel="Time" />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` boolean property on a `<CFormInput>`, a `<CFormTextarea>` or a `<CFormSelect>` to give it a grayed out appearance, remove pointer events, and prevent focusing.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CFormSelect, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInputDisabled"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email address"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        disabled
      />
      <CFormTextarea
        id="floatingTextareaDisabled"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Comments"
        placeholder="Leave a comment here"
        disabled
      />
      <CFormTextarea
        id="floatingTextarea2Disabled"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Comments"
        placeholder="Leave a comment here"
        style={{ height: '100px' }}
        defaultValue="Disabled textarea with some text inside"
        disabled
      />
      <CFormSelect
        id="floatingSelectDisabled"
        floatingLabel="Works with selects"
        aria-label="Floating label disabled select example"
        disabled
      >
        <option>Open this select menu</option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
        <option value="3">Three</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Readonly plaintext

Floating labels also support the `plainText` property, which can be helpful for toggling from an editable `<CFormInput>` to a plaintext value without affecting the page layout.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsPlaintextExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingEmptyPlaintextInput"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Empty input"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        plainText
        readOnly
      />
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingPlaintextInput"
        floatingLabel="Input with value"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        defaultValue="name@example.com"
        plainText
        readOnly
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Input groups

Floating labels also support `<CInputGroup>` — put the floating control next to the other addons:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsInputGroupExample = () => {
  return (
    <CInputGroup>
      <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
      <CFormInput type="text" id="floatingInputGroup1" floatingLabel="Username" placeholder="mdo" />
    </CInputGroup>
  )
}
```

When using `<CInputGroup>` and floating labels along with form validation, wrap the group in `.form-field`, mark the `<CInputGroup>` with `is-invalid`, and place the feedback outside it, so it renders under the whole group rather than inside the frame:

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormFloating,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsInputGroupValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CInputGroup className="is-invalid">
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormFloating className="is-invalid">
          <CFormInput
            type="text"
            id="floatingInputGroup2"
            placeholder="mdo"
            validationState="invalid"
            required
          />
          <CFormLabel htmlFor="floatingInputGroup2">Username</CFormLabel>
        </CFormFloating>
      </CInputGroup>
      <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Always floating

Set `floatingLabelAlways` on the form control, or `always` on `<CFormFloating>`, to keep the label floated and show the placeholder.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormFloating, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsAlwaysExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="alwaysFloatingInput"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email address"
        floatingLabelAlways
        placeholder="name@example.com"
      />
      <CFormFloating always>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="alwaysFloatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
        <CFormInput type="password" id="alwaysFloatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••" />
      </CFormFloating>
    </>
  )
}
```

The date and time pickers take `floatingLabelAlways` as well.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const FloatingLabelsAlwaysDatePickerExample = () => (
  <CDatePicker floatingLabel="Delivery date" floatingLabelAlways locale="en-US" />
)
```

By default, placeholders stay transparent until the control is focused. With `floatingLabelAlways`, the placeholder stays visible in both states, so keep it short on a textarea, where the floated label covers its first line.

## Layout

When working with the CoreUI for React grid system, be sure to place form elements within column classes.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CFormSelect, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsLayoutExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow xs={{ gutter: 3 }}>
      <CCol md>
        <CFormInput
          type="email"
          id="floatingInputGrid"
          floatingLabel="Email address"
          placeholder="name@example.com"
          defaultValue="email@example.com"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md>
        <CFormSelect
          id="floatingSelectGrid"
          floatingLabel="Email address"
          aria-label="Works with selects"
        >
          <option>Open this select menu</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

```jsx
import { CFormFloating } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `always` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |

# React Floating Labels Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Floating Labels component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

`.form-floating` carries the tokens, so a single field can be retuned without recompiling. Anything nested inside it follows them, including the date and time inputs, which drive their own float on `:focus-within` instead of `:placeholder-shown`.

```scss
$form-floating-tokens: () !default;
$form-floating-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-floating-height: calc(3.5rem + var(--cui-btn-input-border-width) * 2),
    --cui-form-floating-line-height: 1.25,
    --cui-form-floating-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-x),
    --cui-form-floating-padding-y: 1rem,
    --cui-form-floating-input-padding-t: 1.625rem,
    --cui-form-floating-input-padding-b: .625rem,
    --cui-form-floating-label-height: 1.5em,
    --cui-form-floating-label-opacity: .65,
    --cui-form-floating-label-transform: scale(.85) translateY(-.5rem) translateX(.15rem),
    --cui-form-floating-label-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    // The label is a sibling of the control, so it cannot inherit its background.
    --cui-form-floating-label-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-form-floating-label-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-form-floating-label-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-border-radius),
    --cui-form-floating-transition-property: #{"opacity, transform"},
    --cui-form-floating-transition-duration: .1s,
    --cui-form-floating-transition-timing: ease-in-out,
  ),
  $form-floating-tokens
);
```

# React Bootstrap Floating Labels Component

> Learn how to create clean and accessible floating form labels in React using CoreUI components styled with Bootstrap.

## How to use React Bootstrap Floating Labels component

Use CoreUI’s `<CFormFloating>`, `<CFormInput>`, `<CFormSelect>`, and `<CFormTextarea>` components with Bootstrap styling to create floating labels in React. Floating labels automatically animate above form fields when content is entered or focused.

### Basic example

Enable floating labels by setting the `floatingLabel` prop on supported form controls. A `placeholder` is required as the floating label effect relies on the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-class. The placeholder stays hidden while the label rests in the field, and shows under the floated label once the field has focus.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInput"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email address"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
      />
      <CFormInput
        type="password"
        id="floatingPassword"
        floatingLabel="Password"
        placeholder="••••••••"
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Using `<CFormFloating>`

You can also wrap a `<CFormInput>` and `<CFormLabel>` pair inside a `<CFormFloating>` container. Write the label first, so a screen reader announces it before the field's value; the input-first order keeps working.

```jsx
<CFormFloating className="mb-4">
  <CFormLabel htmlFor="floatingInput">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="email" id="floatingInput" placeholder="name@example.com" />
</CFormFloating>
<CFormFloating>
  <CFormLabel htmlFor="floatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput type="password" id="floatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••" />
</CFormFloating>
```

### Pre-filled values

Floating labels adjust automatically when inputs have a preset value.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabels2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CFormInput
      type="email"
      id="floatingInputValue"
      floatingLabel="Input with value"
      placeholder="name@example.com"
      defaultValue="test@example.com"
    />
  )
}
```

### Validation support

Floating labels integrate seamlessly with form validation styles.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInputValid"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email addresss"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        defaultValue="test@example.com"
        validationState="valid"
      />
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="floatingInputInvalid"
        floatingLabel="Email addresss"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        defaultValue="test@example.com"
        validationState="invalid"
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Textareas

Textareas styled with floating labels maintain the same height as inputs by default.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsTextareaExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormTextarea
      id="floatingTextarea"
      floatingLabel="Comments"
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
    ></CFormTextarea>
  )
}
```

To change the height, set an explicit `height` via inline styles or custom CSS rather than using the `rows` attribute.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsTextarea2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CFormTextarea
      placeholder="Leave a comment here"
      id="floatingTextarea2"
      floatingLabel="Comments"
      style={{ height: '100px' }}
    ></CFormTextarea>
  )
}
```

## Select elements

Floating labels also support `<CFormSelect>`. The label always appears in the floated state. **Note:** This is not compatible with `size` or `multiple`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormSelect } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsSelectExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormSelect
      id="floatingSelect"
      floatingLabel="Works with selects"
      aria-label="Floating label select example"
    >
      <option>Open this select menu</option>
      <option value="1">One</option>
      <option value="2">Two</option>
      <option value="3">Three</option>
    </CFormSelect>
  )
}
```

## Date and time

Date, time, datetime-local, month, and week inputs also always show the label in its floated state. These controls do not support placeholders the way textual inputs do, so a `placeholder` is not required (and is ignored by most browsers on these types). For a field that formats its value by locale, use the [Date Picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-picker/#floating-labels) or the [Time Picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/time-picker/#floating-labels) with the `floatingLabel` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsDateTimeExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput type="date" id="floatingDate" floatingClassName="mb-4" floatingLabel="Date" />
      <CFormInput type="time" id="floatingTime" floatingLabel="Time" />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Always floating

Set `floatingLabelAlways` on the form control, or `always` on `<CFormFloating>`, to keep the label floated and show the placeholder.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormFloating, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/react'

export const FloatingLabelsAlwaysExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="alwaysFloatingInput"
        floatingClassName="mb-4"
        floatingLabel="Email address"
        floatingLabelAlways
        placeholder="name@example.com"
      />
      <CFormFloating always>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="alwaysFloatingPassword">Password</CFormLabel>
        <CFormInput type="password" id="alwaysFloatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••" />
      </CFormFloating>
    </>
  )
}
```

The date and time pickers take `floatingLabelAlways` as well.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CDatePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const FloatingLabelsAlwaysDatePickerExample = () => (
  <CDatePicker floatingLabel="Delivery date" floatingLabelAlways locale="en-US" />
)
```

By default, placeholders stay transparent until the control is focused. With `floatingLabelAlways`, the placeholder stays visible in both states, so keep it short on a textarea, where the floated label covers its first line.

## Grid layout support

Use floating labels within the CoreUI Bootstrap grid system by nesting inputs inside column classes.

```html

  return (
    <CRow xs={{ gutter: 3 }}>
      <CCol md>
        <CFormInput
          type="email"
          id="floatingInputGrid"
          floatingLabel="Email address"
          placeholder="name@example.com"
          defaultValue="email@example.com"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md>
        <CFormSelect
          id="floatingSelectGrid"
          floatingLabel="Email address"
          aria-label="Works with selects"
        >
          <option>Open this select menu</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>

```
