# React Form Control Group

> Assemble an input, icons and action buttons into one control that looks and behaves like a single form field — the frame every CoreUI field component is built on.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

A control is often more than an input: it carries an icon, a clear button, a
toggle. `.form-control-group` draws **one** frame around all of it, so the
result reads as a single field rather than a row of parts. The PRO field
components — [autocomplete](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/autocomplete/), [chip input](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/chip-input/),
[date picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-picker/), [date range picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-range-picker/),
[multi select](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/multi-select/), [password input](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/password-input/) and
[time picker](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/time-picker/) —
emit this markup internally, which is why they all size, focus and validate the
same way. Reach for the classes directly when you are assembling a field of
your own.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlIcon>
        <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor">
          <path d="M479.6 399.716l-81.084-81.084-62.368-25.767A175.014 175.014 0 0 0 368 192c0-97.047-78.953-176-176-176S16 94.953 16 192s78.953 176 176 176a175.034 175.034 0 0 0 101.619-32.377l25.7 62.2L400.4 479.6a56 56 0 1 0 79.2-79.884ZM48 192c0-79.4 64.6-144 144-144s144 64.6 144 144-64.6 144-144 144S48 271.4 48 192Zm408.971 264.284a24.028 24.028 0 0 1-33.942 0l-76.572-76.572-23.894-57.835 57.835 23.894 76.573 76.572a24.028 24.028 0 0 1 0 33.941Z" />
        </svg>
      </CFormControlIcon>
      <CFormInput type="search" placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search" />
    </CFormControlGroup>
  )
}
```

## How it works

- **The group is the frame.** `.form-control-group` looks exactly like
  `.form-control` — same padding, typography, colours, border and transition,
  from the same `--cui-control-*` custom properties — and lays its
  children out in a row. Theme `.form-control` and the group follows.
- **The control inside keeps its own class.** Put `<CFormInput>` in the group:
  inside it the `.form-control` gives up its border, padding and background, so
  only the group's frame is drawn. There is no separate "ghost" class to remember.
- **Focus is answered by the group.** A `<div>` never fires `:focus`, so the
  frame lights up on `:focus-within`.

## Parts

| Component | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `<CFormControlGroup>` | The frame. Size every part at once with `size="sm"` or `size="lg"`. |
| `<CFormInput>` | The editable inside it. |
| `<CFormControlIcon>` | Decoration — an icon and nothing more. It ignores pointer events, and can sit in the group on its own or inside an action. |
| `<CFormControlText>` | Static text in the frame — a prefix or suffix like `https://`, `@` or `.00`. Inert and unselectable, so a click lands in the input and a drag over the field does not pick it up. |
| `<CFormControlAction>` | An interactive adornment: a real `<button>`. Give it an `aria-label`; it may hold a `<CFormControlIcon>`. |
| `<CFormControlCleaner>` | The action that clears the value — a real `<button>` with the clearing glyph built in (`ariaLabel` defaults to "Clear"). The field components render theirs automatically; in a custom group showing and hiding it is your job, since only you know whether the control holds a value. |

Icons take their size from the group, so they follow `size="sm"` and
`size="lg"` without being told. An icon inside an action follows the
button's colour, which is how a validation state reaches it.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlAction, CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupPartsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormInput type="text" defaultValue="Ada Lovelace" aria-label="Name" />
      <CFormControlAction aria-label="Clear">
        <CFormControlIcon>
          <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
            <path d="M.293.293a1 1 0 011.414 0L8 6.586 14.293.293a1 1 0 111.414 1.414L9.414 8l6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414 1.414L8 9.414l-6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414-1.414L6.586 8 .293 1.707a1 1 0 010-1.414z" />
          </svg>
        </CFormControlIcon>
      </CFormControlAction>
    </CFormControlGroup>
  )
}
```

## Clearing the value

`<CFormControlCleaner>` is the clearing action with the glyph built in. Render it only while the control holds a value:

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CFormControlCleaner, CFormControlGroup, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupCleanerExample = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('Ada Lovelace')

  return (
    <CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormInput
        type="text"
        value={value}
        aria-label="Name"
        onChange={(event) => setValue(event.target.value)}
      />
      {value.length > 0 && <CFormControlCleaner onClick={() => setValue('')} />}
    </CFormControlGroup>
  )
}
```

## Static text

_Added in 6.0.0._

Use `.form-control-text` for a fixed prefix or suffix that labels the value
rather than changing it — a scheme, a unit, a currency. It is inert: pointer
events pass through to the input, and the text cannot be selected, so
double-clicking to select the value never catches the adornment instead.

Which side it lands on is decided by where you put it, because the group is a
flex row and follows DOM order. Write it before the input for a prefix, after
for a suffix — there is no separate class for the end.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupStaticTextExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormControlGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormControlText>https://</CFormControlText>
        <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="example.com" aria-label="Website address" />
      </CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormControlText>@</CFormControlText>
        <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="username" aria-label="Username" />
      </CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlGroup>
        <CFormControlText>$</CFormControlText>
        <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="0" aria-label="Amount" />
        <CFormControlText>.00</CFormControlText>
      </CFormControlGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

It combines with the other parts, and dims with the group when the field is
disabled:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormControlText, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupStaticTextCombinedExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlIcon>
        <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
          <path d="M8 0a8 8 0 100 16A8 8 0 008 0zM1.5 8a6.5 6.5 0 1113 0 6.5 6.5 0 01-13 0z" />
        </svg>
      </CFormControlIcon>
      <CFormControlText>USD</CFormControlText>
      <CFormInput type="text" defaultValue="1250" disabled aria-label="Amount" />
    </CFormControlGroup>
  )
}
```

## Sizing

Add `.form-control-sm` or `.form-control-lg` to the group — the standard
control sizing classes, no per-component variants.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlGroup, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormControlGroup size="sm" className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small" />
      </CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Default" aria-label="Default" />
      </CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormControlGroup size="lg">
        <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large" />
      </CFormControlGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Validation

Put `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` on the group. The state also reaches the frame
from the control inside it, so a component that validates its own field lights
the frame up without any extra wiring. The validation icon is suppressed inside
a group — an action usually occupies that corner — and the actions carry the
state colour instead.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlAction, CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormControlGroup className="is-invalid">
        <CFormInput type="text" defaultValue="Not quite" aria-label="Invalid example" />
        <CFormControlAction aria-label="Clear">
          <CFormControlIcon>
            <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
              <path d="M.293.293a1 1 0 011.414 0L8 6.586 14.293.293a1 1 0 111.414 1.414L9.414 8l6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414 1.414L8 9.414l-6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414-1.414L6.586 8 .293 1.707a1 1 0 010-1.414z" />
            </svg>
          </CFormControlIcon>
        </CFormControlAction>
      </CFormControlGroup>
      <div className="invalid-feedback d-block">Please pick a different value.</div>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Disabled

Disable the control inside the group and the frame follows; use `.disabled` on
the group when there is no single control to disable.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormControlAction, CFormControlGroup, CFormControlIcon, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormControlGroup>
      <CFormInput type="text" defaultValue="Read only" aria-label="Disabled example" disabled />
      <CFormControlAction aria-label="Clear" disabled>
        <CFormControlIcon>
          <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">
            <path d="M.293.293a1 1 0 011.414 0L8 6.586 14.293.293a1 1 0 111.414 1.414L9.414 8l6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414 1.414L8 9.414l-6.293 6.293a1 1 0 01-1.414-1.414L6.586 8 .293 1.707a1 1 0 010-1.414z" />
          </svg>
        </CFormControlIcon>
      </CFormControlAction>
    </CFormControlGroup>
  )
}
```

> **Not to be confused with [input group](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/input-group/).** An input group
> joins *separate* controls and add-ons side by side — each keeps its own frame,
> and the seams between them are visible. A form control group is *one* control
> assembled from parts inside a single frame.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CFormControlGroup,
  CFormControlIcon,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormText,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlGroupWithFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="formControlGroupField">Search</CFormLabel>
      <CFormControlGroup>
        <CFormControlIcon>
          <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor">
            <path d="M479.6 399.716l-81.084-81.084-62.368-25.767A175.014 175.014 0 0 0 368 192c0-97.047-78.953-176-176-176S16 94.953 16 192s78.953 176 176 176a175.034 175.034 0 0 0 101.619-32.377l25.7 62.2L400.4 479.6a56 56 0 1 0 79.2-79.884ZM48 192c0-79.4 64.6-144 144-144s144 64.6 144 144-64.6 144-144 144S48 271.4 48 192Zm408.971 264.284a24.028 24.028 0 0 1-33.942 0l-76.572-76.572-23.894-57.835 57.835 23.894 76.573 76.572a24.028 24.028 0 0 1 0 33.941Z" />
          </svg>
        </CFormControlIcon>
        <CFormInput type="search" id="formControlGroupField" placeholder="Search…" />
      </CFormControlGroup>
```

# React Form Control Group Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Form Control Group with CSS variables and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The frame runs on the shared `--cui-control-*` custom properties, so it
is themed together with `.form-control`. The parts the group owns have their
own:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

## Readonly

Add the `readOnly` boolean attribute on an input to prevent modification of the input's value. Read-only inputs appear lighter (just like disabled inputs), but retain the standard cursor.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputReadonlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="staticEmail" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput
            type="text"
            id="staticEmail"
            defaultValue="email@example.com"
            readOnly
            plainText
          />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Password
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword" />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

# React Form Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Form Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CFormInput

```jsx
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `delay` | `number \| boolean` | `false` | Delay onChange event while typing. If set to true onChange event will be delayed 500ms, you can also provide the number of milliseconds you want to delay the onChange event. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called immediately after the `value` prop changes. |
| `onInput` | `InputEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on every `input` event of the field. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `plainText` | `boolean` | - | Render the component styled as plain text. Removes the default form field styling and preserve the correct margin and padding. Recommend to use only along side `readonly`. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `string` | `text` | Specifies the type of component. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| string[]` | - | The `value` attribute of component. |

# React Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

`.form-control` and `.form-select` declare the `--cui-control-*` tokens on themselves, and so does every field built on them: the [form control group](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) and every component that renders one — Autocomplete, Chip Input, Multi Select, the pickers, the password and number inputs — and the cells of the OTP input. Set a token on the field to restyle that field; a value set on an ancestor or on `:root` stops there. `className` and `style` on `CFormInput` land on the `<input>` itself. To restyle the frame of every field at once, change the [`--cui-btn-input-*` tokens](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/overview/#css-variables) it points to; buttons share their sizes, so they move too. The placeholder, disabled background and file button colours point at the palette instead and are set per field. `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` are themselves token overrides.

The checkbox, radio and switch are not fields: the few `--cui-control-*` tokens they share sit on `:root` and are listed with the [checkbox](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/checkbox/styling/#shared-variables).

```scss
$form-control-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-min-height: var(--cui-btn-input-min-height),
    --cui-control-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-y),
    --cui-control-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-x),
    --cui-control-font-size: var(--cui-btn-input-font-size),
    --cui-control-font-weight: var(--cui-btn-input-font-weight),
    --cui-control-line-height: var(--cui-btn-input-line-height),
    --cui-control-fg: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-control-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-control-border-width: var(--cui-btn-input-border-width),
    --cui-control-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-border-color),
    --cui-control-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-border-radius),
    --cui-control-box-shadow: var(--cui-btn-input-box-shadow),
    --cui-control-transition-property: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-property),
    --cui-control-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-focus-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-color),
    --cui-control-focus-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-bg),
    --cui-control-focus-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color),
    --cui-control-disabled-color: var(--cui-control-fg),
    --cui-control-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-control-disabled-border-color: var(--cui-control-border-color),
    --cui-control-action-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-control-action-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-control-action-transition-property: var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property),
    --cui-control-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
  ),
  $form-control-tokens
);
```

Two tokens are declared by the class that uses them rather than on every control: `--cui-control-plaintext-color` on `.form-control-plaintext`, and `--cui-control-color-width` on `.form-control-color`.

`.form-label` and `.col-form-label` carry the `--cui-label-*` tokens. Set them on a single label to restyle just that one, or on an ancestor to cover a whole form. The size classes are themselves token overrides: `.col-form-label-lg` sets `--cui-label-padding-y` and `--cui-label-font-size`.

```scss
$form-label-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-label-margin-bottom: .5rem,
    --cui-label-font-size: null,
    --cui-label-font-style: null,
    --cui-label-font-weight: var(--cui-font-weight-medium),
    --cui-label-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
  ),
  $form-label-tokens
);
```

`.form-text` carries the `--cui-form-text-*` tokens.

```scss
$form-text-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-text-margin-top: .25rem,
    --cui-form-text-font-size: var(--cui-small-font-size),
    --cui-form-text-font-style: null,
    --cui-form-text-font-weight: null,
    --cui-form-text-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
  ),
  $form-text-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

Each entry generates one `.form-control-{size}` and `.form-select-{size}` class, pointing the control at the matching `--cui-btn-input-{size}-*` values. Add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
$form-control-sizes: defaults(
  ("sm", "lg"),
  $form-control-sizes
);
```

# React Bootstrap Form Input Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s React input components styled with Bootstrap to create accessible, styled, and responsive form inputs.

## How to use React Bootstrap Form Input component

Use CoreUI’s `<CFormInput>` and related components styled with Bootstrap to create customizable and accessible form inputs in React. Easily control size, disabled state, readonly fields, file uploads, color pickers, and more.

### Basic usage

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CForm, CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <CFormInput
        type="email"
        id="exampleFormControlInput1"
        label="Email address"
        placeholder="name@example.com"
        text="Must be 8-20 characters long."
      />
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

To build more complex form controls with labels and help text, you can compose the form manually using CoreUI components:

```jsx
<CForm>
  <CFormLabel htmlFor="exampleFormControlInput1">Email address</CFormLabel>
  <CFormInput
    type="email"
    id="exampleFormControlInput1"
    placeholder="name@example.com"
    aria-describedby="exampleFormControlInputHelpInline"
  />
  <CFormText as="span" id="exampleFormControlInputHelpInline">
    Must be 8–20 characters long.
  </CFormText>
</CForm>
```

## Input sizing

Change input sizes using the `size` prop (`"sm"` or `"lg"`).

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput type="text" size="lg" placeholder="Large input" aria-label="lg input example" />
      <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Default input" aria-label="default input example" />
      <CFormInput type="text" size="sm" placeholder="Small input" aria-label="sm input example" />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Disabled inputs

Add the `disabled` prop to visually disable the input and remove pointer events.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        type="text"
        placeholder="Disabled input"
        aria-label="Disabled input example"
        disabled
      />
      <CFormInput
        type="text"
        placeholder="Disabled readonly input"
        aria-label="Disabled input example"
        disabled
        readOnly
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Read-only inputs

Use the `readOnly` prop to prevent editing while maintaining focus and tab behavior.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputReadonlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="staticEmail" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput
            type="text"
            id="staticEmail"
            defaultValue="email@example.com"
            readOnly
            plainText
          />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Password
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword" />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Plaintext read-only inputs

Add `plainText` for inputs that appear as plain text but retain layout spacing.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputReadonlyPlainTextExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="staticEmail2" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput
            type="text"
            id="staticEmail2"
            defaultValue="email@example.com"
            readOnly
            plainText
          />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword2" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Password
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword2" />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CForm, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormInputReadonlyPlainText2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4">
```

## File input

# React Input Group Component

> Easily extend form controls by adding text, buttons, or button groups on either side of textual inputs, custom selects, and custom file inputs.

## Basic example

Place one add-on or button on either side of an input. You may also place one on both sides of an input. Remember to place `<CFormLabel>`s outside the input group.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormTextarea, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon1">@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="basic-addon1" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput
          placeholder="Recipient's username"
          aria-label="Recipient's username"
          aria-describedby="basic-addon2"
        />
        <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon2">@example.com</CInputGroupText>
      </CInputGroup>

      <CFormLabel htmlFor="basic-url">Your vanity URL</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon3">https://example.com/users/</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="basic-url" aria-describedby="basic-addon3" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText>$</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput aria-label="Amount (to the nearest dollar)" />
        <CInputGroupText>.00</CInputGroupText>
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" />
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Server" aria-label="Server" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>With textarea</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormTextarea aria-label="With textarea"></CFormTextarea>
      </CInputGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormText,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputGroupField">Your vanity URL</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>https://example.com/users/</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="inputGroupField" />
      </CInputGroup>
      <CFormText>Choose a unique name for your profile.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Wrapping

Input groups wrap by default via `flex-wrap: wrap` in order to accommodate custom form field validation within an input group. You may disable this with `.flex-nowrap`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupWrappingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CInputGroup className="flex-nowrap">
      <CInputGroupText id="addon-wrapping">@</CInputGroupText>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="addon-wrapping" />
    </CInputGroup>
  )
}
```

## Sizing

Add the relative form sizing classes to the `<CInputGroup>` itself and contents within will automatically resize—no need for repeating the form control size classes on each element.

**Sizing on the individual input group elements isn't supported.**

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CInputGroup size="sm" className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-sm">Small</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-sm" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-default">Default</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput
          aria-label="Sizing example input"
          aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-default"
        />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup size="lg">
        <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-lg">Large</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-lg" />
      </CInputGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Checkboxes and radios

Place any checkbox or radio option within an input group's addon instead of text.

```html
      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>
          <CRadio value="" aria-label="Radio button for following text input" />

      </CInputGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Multiple inputs

While multiple `<CFormInput>`s are supported visually, validation styles are only available for input groups with a single `<CFormInput>`.

```html

  return (
    <CInputGroup>
      <CInputGroupText>First and last name</CInputGroupText>

      <CFormInput aria-label="Last name" />
    </CInputGroup>
```
```html
  )
}
```

## Skipping an element

CSS selectors can only account for so much. When a group carries an element that should not take part in the border-radius and negative-margin logic — a hidden input, a tooltip anchor — add `.input-group-ignore` to it and the corners flow to its visible neighbours:

```html
<CInputGroup>
  <CInputGroupText id="visible-addon">@</CInputGroupText>
  <CFormInput className="input-group-ignore d-none" placeholder="Hidden input" aria-label="Hidden input" aria-describedby="visible-addon" />
  <CFormInput placeholder="Visible input" aria-label="Visible input" aria-describedby="visible-addon" />
</CInputGroup>
```

# React Form Input Group Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Form Input Group component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CInputGroup

```jsx
import { CInputGroup } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large. |

## CInputGroupText

```jsx
import { CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `(ElementType & "symbol") \| (ElementType & "object") \| (ElementType & "span") \| (ElementType & "form") \| (ElementType & "slot") \| ... 175 more ...` | `span` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |

# React Input Group Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Input Group component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The addon declares its own tokens on `.input-group-text`, so a single addon can be repainted or resized without a modifier class. The first six are the [`--cui-control-*`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables) frame tokens, copied onto the addon so it lines up with the control next to it; `.input-group-{size}` re-points all of them but the border width, on the addon and on the `.form-control` or `.form-select` next to it. `.input-group` itself declares none — it is a layout wrapper, and a token set on it reaches neither the addon nor the control, because each declares its own.

```scss
$input-group-tokens: () !default;
$input-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-y),
    --cui-control-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-x),
    --cui-control-font-size: var(--cui-btn-input-font-size),
    --cui-control-line-height: var(--cui-btn-input-line-height),
    --cui-control-border-width: var(--cui-btn-input-border-width),
    --cui-control-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-border-radius),
    --cui-input-group-addon-font-weight: var(--cui-btn-input-font-weight),
    --cui-input-group-addon-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-input-group-addon-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-input-group-addon-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-border-color),
  ),
  $input-group-tokens
);
```

```jsx
<CInputGroupText style={{ '--cui-input-group-addon-bg': 'var(--cui-bg-1)' }}>@</CInputGroupText>
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one `.input-group-{size}` class, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$input-group-sizes: defaults(
  ("sm", "lg"),
  $input-group-sizes
);
```

# React Bootstrap Input Group Component

> Learn how to extend CoreUI’s React input fields with Bootstrap-styled input groups—add text, buttons, selects, or custom file inputs seamlessly.

## How to use React Bootstrap Input Group component

Use CoreUI’s `<CInputGroup>` components styled with Bootstrap to enhance form inputs by prepending or appending text, buttons, selects, and more—perfect for building rich form UIs.

### Basic usage

Add text or buttons on either side of the input using `<CInputGroupText>` or `<CButton>`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormTextarea, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon1">@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="basic-addon1" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput
          placeholder="Recipient's username"
          aria-label="Recipient's username"
          aria-describedby="basic-addon2"
        />
        <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon2">@example.com</CInputGroupText>
      </CInputGroup>

      <CFormLabel htmlFor="basic-url">Your vanity URL</CFormLabel>
      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="basic-addon3">https://example.com/users/</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput id="basic-url" aria-describedby="basic-addon3" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText>$</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput aria-label="Amount (to the nearest dollar)" />
        <CInputGroupText>.00</CInputGroupText>
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" />
        <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Server" aria-label="Server" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup>
        <CInputGroupText>With textarea</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormTextarea aria-label="With textarea"></CFormTextarea>
      </CInputGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Wrapping content

Input groups use `flex-wrap` by default, which allows wrapping when needed—especially useful for validation messages or long inputs.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupWrappingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CInputGroup className="flex-nowrap">
      <CInputGroupText id="addon-wrapping">@</CInputGroupText>
      <CFormInput placeholder="Username" aria-label="Username" aria-describedby="addon-wrapping" />
    </CInputGroup>
  )
}
```

To prevent wrapping, add `.flex-nowrap`.

## Input group sizing

Change size by applying `size="sm"` or `size="lg"` to `<CInputGroup>`. All inner elements will automatically adjust.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput, CInputGroup, CInputGroupText } from '@coreui/react'

export const InputGroupSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CInputGroup size="sm" className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-sm">Small</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-sm" />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup className="mb-4">
        <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-default">Default</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput
          aria-label="Sizing example input"
          aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-default"
        />
      </CInputGroup>

      <CInputGroup size="lg">
        <CInputGroupText id="inputGroup-sizing-lg">Large</CInputGroupText>
        <CFormInput aria-label="Sizing example input" aria-describedby="inputGroup-sizing-lg" />
      </CInputGroup>
    </>
  )
}
```

> 📌 Note: Do not apply size classes to individual input elements inside the group.

# React Input Mask

> React input masks allow you to regulate the format of data entered. You can enhance data entry accuracy by implementing React input masks for fields with consistent formatting requirements. This ensures that users input data correctly, such as accurately formatted phone numbers in a designated phone number field.

## Usage

While CoreUI for React does not currently include a 'mask' feature, it can be enhanced by leveraging existing libraries like `react-imask` to extend the functionality of our components.

To enable the extension of the `` component, please ensure that you have installed `react-imask` first.

```bash tab={"label":"Npm"}
npm install react-imask
```

```bash tab={"label":"Yarn"}
yarn add react-imask
```

Once you have installed react-imask, you can proceed to create a custom component with a mask.

```jsx
import { IMaskMixin } from 'react-imask'
```

```jsx
const CFormInputWithMask = IMaskMixin(({ inputRef, ...props }) => (
  <CFormInput
    {...props}
    ref={inputRef} // bind internal input
  />
))
```

Here is an example of a date mask for reference.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'
import { IMaskMixin } from 'react-imask'

const CFormInputWithMask = IMaskMixin(({ inputRef, ...props }) => (
  <CFormInput {...props} ref={inputRef} />
))

export const InputMaskExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormInputWithMask
      mask={Date}
      min={new Date(1990, 0, 1)}
      max={new Date(2020, 0, 1)}
      lazy={false}
    />
  )
}
```

## Example masks

Please take a moment to review some example masks you can use for reference. These examples serve as helpful templates for implementing input masks and can assist you in effectively controlling data entry formats.

### Phone

This example React input mask for a phone number follows the format commonly used in North America. It consists of three groups of numbers: the area code enclosed in parentheses, followed by a space, and then the seven-digit phone number separated by a hyphen.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'
import { IMaskMixin } from 'react-imask'

const CFormInputWithMask = IMaskMixin(({ inputRef, ...props }) => (
  <CFormInput {...props} ref={inputRef} />
))

export const InputMaskPhoneExample = () => {
  return <CFormInputWithMask mask="+{1}(000)000-00-00" />
}
```

### Credit Card

The provided code snippet demonstrates an implementation of a React input mask for a credit card number using the IMask library in JavaScript. The mask is set to "0000 0000 0000 0000", indicating that the input should consist of a 16-digit credit card number with spaces separating every four digits. The component renders an input field with the specified mask, allowing users to enter credit card numbers in the desired format.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'
import { IMaskMixin } from 'react-imask'

const CFormInputWithMask = IMaskMixin(({ inputRef, ...props }) => (
  <CFormInput {...props} ref={inputRef} />
))

export const InputMaskCreditCardExample = () => {
  return <CFormInputWithMask mask="0000 0000 0000 0000" />
}
```

For more information on how to use the input mask, you can refer to the following resource: https://imask.js.org/

# React Multi Select Component

> Customize the native <select>s with a powerful React Multi Select component that changes the element’s initial appearance and brings some new functionalities.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Basic example

A clear demonstration of implementing a basic React Multi Select dropdown, highlighting essential options and configurations.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CMultiSelect
      options={options}
      label="Framework"
      text="Please select your framework."
      search
      defaultValue={[3, 4, 5]}
    />
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html

          { value: 1, label: 'Bootstrap' },

          { value: 3, label: 'Vue.js' },
        ]}
      />
      <CFormText>Pick every technology you work with.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Search

You can configure the search functionality within the component. The `search` property determines how the search input element is enabled and behaves. It accepts multiple types to provide flexibility in configuring search behavior. By default is set to `true`.

### Disabled search

To disable the default search input element, please set `search` property to `false` like in the example below:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSearchDisabledExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CMultiSelect
      options={options}
      label="Framework"
      text="Please select your framework."
      search={false}
    />
  )
}
```

### Where typing goes

Typing reaches the search box from anywhere in the component — the control, the options panel, the select all button — so it never depends on where the focus happens to be.

Set `globalSearch={false}` to keep typing local. The search box then filters only while it has the focus, and a keystroke over the options list jumps to the first option starting with it. With `search="external"` the list holds only the last results, so that keystroke does nothing.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSearchLocalExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CMultiSelect
      options={options}
      label="Framework"
      text="Please select your framework."
      globalSearch={false}
    />
  )
}
```

### External search

When external search is enabled (`search="external"`), the component delegates search operations to an external API. This setup is ideal for scenarios where third-party services or custom backend implementations power search capabilities. 

```jsx
<CMultiSelect options={...} onFilterChange={...} search="external" />
```

Please check the [External Data](#external-data) section to check a working example of how to handle external data.

## Modes

### Allow create options

The `allowCreateOptions` property in the `` component allows users to create new options in addition to selecting pre-existing ones from a list.

When this property is set to true, the user can type in a new option in the search input field of the multiselect component, and if the option does not already exist in the list, it will be created and added to the list of available options. This can be useful when the list of available options is not comprehensive or when the user needs to select an option that is not already available.

> It's worth noting that this feature may not always be appropriate, depending on the specific use case of the multiselect component. In some cases, it may be preferable to restrict the user to selecting only pre-existing options, while in other cases, allowing for the creation of new options may be essential. It's important to consider the specific requirements of your application when deciding whether to enable this feature.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectAllowCreateOptionsExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
      selected: true,
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
      selected: true,
      disabled: true,
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
          selected: true,
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect allowCreateOptions options={options} />
}
```

### Clear search on select

The `clearSearchOnSelect` property is a Boolean attribute that can be used with the MultiSelect component in the CoreUI React library.

When `clearSearchOnSelect` is set to `true`, the search input field in the MultiSelect component will be cleared as soon as the user selects an option from the dropdown list. This means that the search query will be reset and the user will be able to start a new search immediately.

By default, `clearSearchOnSelect` is set to `false`, which means that the search input field will retain the user's search query even after an option has been selected. This can be useful in situations where the user needs to select multiple options from the dropdown list that match the same search query.

To use the `clearSearchOnSelect` property with the MultiSelect component in the CoreUI React library, you simply need to set it to `true` or `false` as appropriate in your code. For example:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectClearSearchOnSelectExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
      selected: true,
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
      selected: true,
      disabled: true,
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
          selected: true,
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect clearSearchOnSelect options={options} />
}
```

In this example, the `clearSearchOnSelect` property is set to `true`, which means that the search input field will be cleared as soon as the user selects an option from the dropdown list.

## Selection types

The React Multi Select component enables users to present selected items in multiple ways. Users can choose to display selected items as chips, a counter, or a list of comma-separated values.

To change the way that selected items are displayed, you can use the `selectionType` property to set the presentation type.

### Chips

By default, the `selectionType` property is set to `"chips"`, which renders selected options as removable [chips](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/chip/). Users can remove a selected option with its remove button, named by `ariaChipRemoveLabel`. `"tags"`, the v5 name of this mode, renders the same and is deprecated.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSelectionTypesChipsExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
      selected: true,
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
      selected: true,
      disabled: true,
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
          selected: true,
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} selectionType="chips" />
}
```

### Counter

In the example below, selected items from the list are counted and presented in the form of a counter. To use this option, set the `selectionType` to `"counter"`.

To further customize the counter, `selectedLabel` builds the whole text: pass a function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. `total` is the number of options in the list, disabled ones, the ones inside a group and the ones the user created included, so a disabled option shows that not everything is selected, plus any selected value the options lack, so it never falls below `count`. Pass `total` to put a number of your own in `{total}`, such as the records a search on your server can reach, when the list holds only one page of them.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSelectionTypesCounterExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
      selected: true,
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
      selected: true,
      disabled: true,
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
          selected: true,
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} selectionType="counter" />
}
```

## Select all

_Added in 5.26.0._

When `multiple` is enabled, a **select all** button is rendered in the dropdown header (toggle it with the `selectAll` property, on by default). The button works as a toggle: it selects every option and its label switches to `deselectAllLabel`, then deselects everything on the next click.

With `indicator="checkbox"` the button shows a tri-state marker that mirrors the overall selection — `none` when nothing is selected, `all` when everything is, and `indeterminate` in between. One indicator serves the whole list: the options, the group labels and this button all follow `indicator`.

The button is a control over the list rather than a value in it, so it is reached with <kbd>Tab</kbd>, not with the arrows.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSelectAllExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} search />
}
```

### Acting on filtered options

By default (`selectAllMode="all"`) the header button acts on the full list, ignoring the current filter. Set `selectAllMode="filtered"` to scope the button to the options currently matched by the search filter. The button's label and checkbox then answer "are all *filtered* options selected?". With no active filter, every option matches, so this behaves exactly like `"all"`.

To avoid a misleading "Select all" while a filter is active, the label switches to `selectFilteredLabel` / `deselectFilteredLabel` (default `Select filtered` / `Deselect filtered`) whenever the filter actually narrows the list — and falls back to `selectAllLabel` / `deselectAllLabel` when nothing is hidden.

Type into the search box below, then use select all — only the matching options are selected.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSelectAllModeExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} search selectAllMode="filtered" />
}
```

Because the scope follows the filter, a side effect is worth knowing: if you select all options while a filter is active (so the checkbox shows `all`) and then clear the search, the checkbox drops to `indeterminate` — the previously hidden, unselected options are now back in the list, so not everything in view is selected anymore.

### Hiding select all when search has no results

_Added in 5.27.0._

When `search` is enabled and the user types a query that matches no options, there is nothing left to select — so leaving the **select all** button visible above the empty "No results found" message is misleading. By default (`hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults={true}`) the component hides the whole dropdown header in that case, and brings it back as soon as the search matches at least one option again.

Type a query that matches nothing (for example `xyz`) into the example below — the select all button disappears together with the options, then returns when you clear or change the search.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectHideSelectAllExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} search />
}
```

Set `hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults={false}` to keep the header (and the select all button) visible even when the search returns no results.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectKeepSelectAllExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} search hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults={false} />
}
```

This option only affects the built-in select all button. A [custom dropdown header](#custom-dropdown-header) is always rendered, since it may contain controls unrelated to the options list.

## Selection limit

_Added in 5.26.0._

Use the `selectionLimit` property to limit how many options can be selected. The select all button stays enabled and selects options up to the limit, then toggles to deselect all once the limit is reached. The `onSelectionLimit` callback fires when a user tries to select more options than allowed — use it to show feedback.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CAlert } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSelectionLimitExample = () => {
  const [limitReached, setLimitReached] = useState(false)

  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      {limitReached && (
        <CAlert theme="warning" dismissible onClose={() => setLimitReached(false)}>
          You can select up to 3 options.
        </CAlert>
      )}
      <CMultiSelect
        options={options}
        search
        selectionLimit={3}
        onSelectionLimit={() => setLimitReached(true)}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Selectable groups

_Added in 5.26.0._

Enable `optionsGroupsSelectable` to turn each group label into its own tri-state toggle over the whole group. It reports `aria-pressed` — `true` when the group is fully selected, `mixed` when part of it is — takes its marker from `indicator`, sits in the arrow order between the options, and requires `multiple`. A label only ever toggles the options the list currently shows, so a search narrows what it takes.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSelectableGroupsExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      label: 'Frontend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 0,
          label: 'Angular',
        },
        {
          value: 1,
          label: 'Bootstrap',
        },
        {
          value: 2,
          label: 'React.js',
        },
        {
          value: 3,
          label: 'Vue.js',
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      label: 'Backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect options={options} search optionsGroupsSelectable />
}
```

## Custom dropdown header

_Added in 5.26.0._

Use the `headerTemplate` property to fully customize the dropdown header — the area above the options list — including rendering several action buttons. It replaces the built-in select all button and renders independently of `selectAll`. The render function receives a `state` object (`{ selected, total, filtered, filteredSelected }`) and an `actions` object (`{ selectAll, deselectAll, selectFiltered, deselectFiltered }`) with the component's selection methods, so you can wire your own controls. It re-renders on every selection change and search filter, so labels and `disabled` states stay up to date. `state.total` is the count of selectable options only — it excludes disabled ones and ignores the `total` prop override, unlike the `{total}` the built-in counter shows.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectHeaderTemplateExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 'angular',
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 'bootstrap',
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 'react',
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 'vue',
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      value: 'django',
      label: 'Django',
    },
    {
      value: 'laravel',
      label: 'Laravel',
    },
    {
      value: 'node',
      label: 'Node.js',
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CMultiSelect
      options={options}
      placeholder="Select frameworks"
      search
      headerTemplate={(state, actions) => (
        <div className="d-flex flex-wrap gap-3">
          <CButton
            size="sm"
            theme="primary"
            disabled={state.selected >= state.total}
            onClick={() => actions.selectAll()}
          >
            Select all ({state.total})
          </CButton>
          <CButton
            size="sm"
            theme="secondary"
            disabled={state.filtered === state.filteredSelected}
            onClick={() => actions.selectFiltered()}
          >
            Select filtered ({state.filtered})
          </CButton>
          <CButton
            size="sm"
            theme="secondary"
            variant="outline"
            disabled={state.filteredSelected === 0}
            onClick={() => actions.deselectFiltered()}
          >
            Deselect filtered ({state.filteredSelected})
          </CButton>
          <CButton
            size="sm"
            theme="danger"
            variant="outline"
            disabled={state.selected === 0}
            onClick={() => actions.deselectAll()}
          >
            Deselect all ({state.selected})
          </CButton>
        </div>
      )}
    />
  )
}
```

## Custom options and options group labels

The CoreUI React Multi Select component provides the flexibility to personalize options and group labels by utilizing custom templates. You can easily customize the options using the `optionsTemplate`, and for groups, you can use `optionsGroupsTemplate`, as demonstrated in the examples below:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { cifPl, cifDe, cifUs, cifEs, cifGb } from '@coreui/icons'
import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

type FlagsMap = {
  [key: string]: string[]
}

export const MultiSelectCustomOptionsExample = () => {
  const flags: FlagsMap = {
    de: cifDe,
    es: cifEs,
    gb: cifGb,
    pl: cifPl,
    us: cifUs,
  }

  const countries = [
    {
      value: 'pl',
      label: 'Poland',
    },
    {
      value: 'de',
      label: 'Germany',
    },
    {
      value: 'us',
      label: 'United States',
    },
    {
      value: 'es',
      label: 'Spain',
    },
    {
      value: 'gb',
      label: 'United Kingdom',
    },
  ]

  const cities = [
    {
      label: 'United States',
      code: 'us',
      options: [
        {
          value: 'au',
          label: 'Austin',
        },
        {
          value: 'ch',
          label: 'Chicago',
        },
        {
          value: 'la',
          label: 'Los Angeles',
        },
        {
          value: 'ny',
          label: 'New York',
        },
        {
          value: 'sa',
          label: 'San Jose',
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      label: 'United Kingdom',
      code: 'gb',
      options: [
        {
          value: 'li',
          label: 'Liverpool',
        },
        {
          value: 'lo',
          label: 'London',
        },
        {
          value: 'ma',
          label: 'Manchester',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CMultiSelect
          label="Select country"
          options={countries}
          optionsStyle="text"
          optionsTemplate={(option) => (
            <div className="d-flex">
              <CIcon className="me-4" icon={flags[option.value]} size="xl" /> {option.label}
            </div>
          )}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CMultiSelect
          label="Select city"
          options={cities}
          optionsGroupsTemplate={(option) => (
            <div className="d-flex align-items-center">
              <CIcon className="me-4" icon={flags[option.code]} size="xl" /> {option.label}
            </div>
          )}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Coordinated selection

The selection of React select components can be coordinated by dynamically updating city options based on the selected country. Use the `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` prop on the city select component to reset the selected city whenever the country changes, ensuring synchronized selections.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { cifPl, cifDe, cifUs, cifEs, cifGb } from '@coreui/icons'
import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Option } from '@coreui/react-pro/src/components/multi-select/types'

type FlagsMap = {
  [key: string]: string[]
}

export const MultiSelectCoordinatedSelectionExample = () => {
  const [cities, setCities] = useState([])

  const countries = [
    {
      value: 'pl',
      label: 'Poland',
      cities: [
        { value: 'warszawa', label: 'Warszawa' },
        { value: 'krakow', label: 'Kraków' },
        { value: 'lodz', label: 'Łódź' },
        { value: 'wroclaw', label: 'Wrocław' },
        { value: 'poznan', label: 'Poznań' },
      ],
    },
    {
      value: 'de',
      label: 'Germany',
      cities: [
        { value: 'berlin', label: 'Berlin' },
        { value: 'hamburg', label: 'Hamburg' },
        { value: 'munich', label: 'Munich' },
        { value: 'cologne', label: 'Cologne' },
        { value: 'frankfurt', label: 'Frankfurt' },
      ],
    },
    {
      value: 'us',
      label: 'United States',
      cities: [
        { value: 'new_york', label: 'New York' },
        { value: 'los_angeles', label: 'Los Angeles' },
        { value: 'chicago', label: 'Chicago' },
        { value: 'houston', label: 'Houston' },
        { value: 'phoenix', label: 'Phoenix' },
      ],
    },
    {
      value: 'es',
      label: 'Spain',
      cities: [
        { value: 'madrid', label: 'Madrid' },
        { value: 'barcelona', label: 'Barcelona' },
        { value: 'valencia', label: 'Valencia' },
        { value: 'seville', label: 'Seville' },
        { value: 'zaragoza', label: 'Zaragoza' },
      ],
    },
    {
      value: 'gb',
      label: 'United Kingdom',
      cities: [
        { value: 'london', label: 'London' },
        { value: 'birmingham', label: 'Birmingham' },
        { value: 'manchester', label: 'Manchester' },
        { value: 'glasgow', label: 'Glasgow' },
        { value: 'liverpool', label: 'Liverpool' },
      ],
    },
  ]

  const flags: FlagsMap = {
    de: cifDe,
    es: cifEs,
    gb: cifGb,
    pl: cifPl,
    us: cifUs,
  }

  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CMultiSelect
          label="Select country"
          multiple={false}
          onChange={(country: Option[]) => {
            setCities(country.length > 0 ? country[0].cities : [])
          }}
          options={countries}
          optionsStyle="text"
          optionsTemplate={(option) => (
            <div className="d-flex">
              <CIcon className="me-4" icon={flags[option.value]} size="xl" /> {option.label}
            </div>
          )}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CMultiSelect
          label="Select city"
          multiple={false}
          options={cities}
          optionsStyle="text"
          resetSelectionOnOptionsChange
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The component shows its validation state on the frame and on the element that takes the focus, and stops the form from being submitted while it is invalid.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CForm, CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectValidationExample = () => {
  const [planState, setPlanState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  const options = [
    { value: 0, label: 'Angular' },
    { value: 1, label: 'Bootstrap' },
    { value: 2, label: 'React.js' },
    { value: 3, label: 'Vue.js' },
  ]

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <CMultiSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Pick at least one framework."
          label="Frameworks"
          options={options}
          required
        />
      </div>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <CMultiSelect
          defaultValue={[0]}
          feedback="Angular is not available in this plan."
          label="Plan frameworks"
          onValidationStateChange={setPlanState}
          options={options}
          validationState={planState}
        />
      </div>
      <div className="col-12">
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`; `invalid` and `valid` still work as aliases. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the native select blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled`; a custom validity you set on the native select yourself stays as it is.
- A validation that reports the native select invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the frame and the control show it invalid whenever its selection is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the frame shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the native select, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the selection it was given for. When the user changes the selection, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)`; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `value` keeps it, and so does an action that leaves the selection as it is. A reset asks once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same call, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the selection given by `defaultValue` or the options' `selected` and fires `onChange` when that changes the selection; with `value` it asks through `onChange` for the `value` the component started with.

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` boolean property to give it a grayed out appearance, remove pointer events, and prevent focusing. A group given with `disabled: true` disables every option in it; a plain string option inside it reaches your templates and callbacks as `{ label, value, disabled: true }`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectDisabledExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
      selected: true,
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
      selected: true,
      disabled: true,
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
          selected: true,
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return <CMultiSelect disabled options={options} />
}
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name; it has no input to report emptiness, so the label floats on focus and on the first selection, and the component's `placeholder` is hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectFloatingLabelExample = () => (
  <CMultiSelect
    floatingLabel="Frameworks"
    id="floatingMultiSelect"
    options={[
      { label: 'Angular', value: 1 },
      { label: 'Bootstrap', value: 2 },
      { label: 'React.js', value: 3 },
      { label: 'Vue.js', value: 4 },
    ]}
  />
)
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Sizing

You may also choose from small and large multi selects to match our similarly sized text inputs.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectSizingExample = () => {
  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
      selected: true,
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: [
        {
          value: 4,
          label: 'Django',
        },
        {
          value: 5,
          label: 'Laravel',
        },
        {
          value: 6,
          label: 'Node.js',
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol md={6} className="mb-4">
        <CMultiSelect options={options} selectionType="counter" size="lg" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6} className="mb-4">
        <CMultiSelect options={options} size="lg" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CMultiSelect options={options} selectionType="counter" size="sm" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CMultiSelect options={options} size="sm" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Virtual Scroller (1000 records)

This component renders only the items currently visible on the screen, and as the user scrolls, new items are dynamically loaded and added to the view.
