## External Data

One of the key features of React Multi Select component is the ability to load data from an external source, such as an API or a server-side script. This can be useful if you have a large amount of data that you don't want to load all at once. To load external data into a React MultiSelect, you can use the Fetch API to the data source.

Here is an example of how you might use React Multi Select with external data:

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect, useDebouncedCallback } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Option } from '@coreui/react-pro/src/components/multi-select/types'

export const MultiSelectExternalDataExample = () => {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const [users, setUsers] = useState([])

  const getUsers = async (name = '') => {
    setLoading(true)
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?first_name=${name}`)
      const result = await response.json()

      setUsers(
        result.records.map((record: Option) => ({
          value: record.id,
          label: record.first_name,
        }))
      )
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error fetching users:', error)
      setUsers([]) // Optionally handle an error state
    } finally {
      setLoading(false)
    }
  }

  // Use the debounced callback for API calls
  const debouncedGetUsers = useDebouncedCallback((value: string) => {
    getUsers(value)
  }, 300)

  return (
    <CMultiSelect
      label="Users"
      loading={loading}
      onFilterChange={debouncedGetUsers} // Debounce the actual API call
      // onFilterChange={(value) => getUsers(value)} // API call without debounce
      onShow={getUsers} // Triggers the getUsers function when the dropdown is shown
      options={users}
      text="Please select your user."
      search="external"
      virtualScroller
    />
  )
}
```

This example requires the following import:

```jsx
import { useDebouncedCallback } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

* `useDebouncedCallback` is a utility hook available in `@coreui/react-pro` that allows you to debounce a callback function, ensuring it is not called too frequently (e.g., when typing in a search field).
* In this case, it is used to debounce the API call made by `getUsers` to reduce the number of requests during rapid input changes.

To handle a large amount of data and improve performance, this example uses the `` component to show the options list.

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

Both the selection and the dropdown panel work either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode — independently for each axis.

| | uncontrolled seed | controlled prop | change callback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selection | `defaultValue` | `value` | `onChange` |
| Panel | `defaultShow` | `show` | `onShowChange` |

The callbacks fire in **both** modes — `onChange` with the selected options, `onShowChange` whenever the panel requests an open-state change (a dismiss gesture like Escape or an outside click, or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle) — so you can watch either state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `defaultShow` or `show` is set.

### Selection

`defaultValue` seeds the uncontrolled selection — matched against the option values — and the select manages it from there. The per-option `selected` flags are the same seed in another spelling, read from the options the component starts with and ignored entirely when `defaultValue` or `value` is set. Options that arrive later, such as an answer to an external search, never change what the user picked, whatever they are marked; a `defaultValue` value they bring is still taken, and `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` starts from the marked options when the values change.

```jsx
<CMultiSelect defaultValue={[1, 2]} options={options} />
```

Pass `value` and the selection is fully controlled: it renders exactly what you pass, a pick only fires `onChange`, and nothing moves until you feed the change back. `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` and a native reset of the form follow the same contract — in controlled mode they only request the empty selection, or the first `value`, through `onChange`. A selection you give never fires `onChange`: `value`, `defaultValue` and options marked `selected`, also when the options it names arrive later, unless `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` puts it in place of the selection. Check **Ignore picks** below and select something to watch a dropped change revert.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Option } from '@coreui/react-pro/src/components/multi-select/types'

export const MultiSelectControlledValueExample = () => {
  const [ignorePicks, setIgnorePicks] = useState(false)
  const [value, setValue] = useState<(string | number)[]>([1, 2])

  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          checked={ignorePicks}
          id="multiSelectControlledValueIgnore"
          label="Ignore picks (watch them revert)"
          onChange={(event) => setIgnorePicks(event.target.checked)}
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CMultiSelect
        label="Frameworks"
        onChange={(selected: Option[]) => {
          if (!ignorePicks) {
            setValue(selected.map((option) => option.value))
          }
        }}
        options={options}
        value={value}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Panel

Every example above leaves the panel uncontrolled — the select manages it itself. `defaultShow` seeds it open on mount.

```jsx
<CMultiSelect defaultShow options={options} />
```

Pass `show` and the panel renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes. That includes a pick: in single selection a pick that would normally close the panel only requests the close through `onShowChange`. Here a checkbox pins the panel open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CFormField } from '@coreui/react'
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const MultiSelectControlledExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false)

  const options = [
    {
      value: 0,
      label: 'Angular',
    },
    {
      value: 1,
      label: 'Bootstrap',
    },
    {
      value: 2,
      label: 'React.js',
    },
    {
      value: 3,
      label: 'Vue.js',
    },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          checked={show}
          id="multiSelectControlledShow"
          label="Keep the panel open"
          onChange={(event) => setShow(event.target.checked)}
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CMultiSelect
        label="Framework"
        multiple={false}
        onShowChange={setShow}
        options={options}
        show={show}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the select like the checkbox above.

## Accessibility

The CoreUI React Multi Select component is designed with accessibility in mind and follows WAI-ARIA guidelines to ensure it works well with assistive technologies like screen readers.

### Built-in Accessibility Features

The Multi Select component includes several accessibility features out of the box:

- **ARIA Roles**: A `combobox` control opening a `dialog` panel, with a `listbox` inside it
- **ARIA States**: Dynamic `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, and `aria-disabled` attributes
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, Enter, Space, and Escape
- **Focus Management**: The focus moves into the panel while it is open and returns to the control when it closes
- **Screen Reader Labels**: Descriptive labels for interactive elements

### Customizing Accessibility Labels

You can customize the accessibility labels for better user experience:

```jsx
<CMultiSelect
  options={options}
  ariaCleanerLabel="Clear all selected items"
  ariaPickerLabel="Open options menu"
  placeholder="Choose your options..."
/>
```

### ARIA Attributes

The component automatically handles these ARIA attributes:

- `aria-expanded`: Indicates whether the dropdown is open or closed
- `aria-haspopup="dialog"`: Tells screen readers that the control opens a dialog
- `aria-labelledby`: Names the control and the panel after the label (`label`, `floatingLabel`, or a `<label>` pointing at the component's `id`, read when the component mounts or its `id` changes); an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` given to the component takes precedence. A `<label>` wrapping the component is left out, because its text would take in the control's own content and selection. The search box keeps a name of its own, `ariaSearchLabel`
- `aria-required`: Marks the focused control, the search box when `search` is on, as required when `required` is set or an `aria-required` is given to the component
- `aria-multiselectable="true"`: Indicates multiple selections are allowed
- `aria-selected`: Shows which options are currently selected
- `aria-disabled`: Identifies disabled options
- `aria-controls`: Points the control at the dropdown dialog and the search input at the list of options while the dropdown is open

### Keyboard Navigation

The options panel is a dialog named like the control. Opening it moves the focus inside — onto the search box when `search` is on, otherwise onto the option the list points at, which is the selection the user left or the first option. The options are focusable one at a time, so the arrows move the focus itself.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between the search box, the select all button and the options list; the focus stays in the open panel |
| <kbd>Enter/Space</kbd> | Open the panel from the control, or select the focused option; <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the search box takes the option the list points at |
| <kbd>Arrow Up/Down</kbd> | Move through the options, or enter the list from the search box |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Up/Down</kbd> | Extend the selection while moving (multiple selection) |
| <kbd>Home/End</kbd> | Focus the first/last option (not while typing in the search box), or the first/last chip from a chip |
| <kbd>Ctrl/Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select every option the list shows, from the options list (multiple selection) |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the panel and return the focus to the control |
| <kbd>Backspace/Delete</kbd> | In the empty search box, focus the last chip; on a chip, remove it and move the focus to the next chip, else the previous one, else the search box, or the field when there is none. Entering the chips closes an open panel. A single select and the `counter` and `text` selections remove the last selected item at once |
| <kbd>Arrow Left/Arrow Right</kbd> | From the start of the search box, focus the last chip; between the chips, move the focus; past the last chip, return to the search box (mirrored in right-to-left) |

### Best Practices

For optimal accessibility, consider these recommendations:

1. **Always provide a label**: Use the `label` prop or associate with a `<label>` element
2. **Use descriptive placeholder text**: Help users understand what to select
3. **Provide clear option labels**: Ensure option text is descriptive and unique
4. **Consider color contrast**: Ensure sufficient contrast for visual indicators
5. **Test with screen readers**: Verify the component works with assistive technologies

```jsx
<CMultiSelect
  label="Select your preferred programming languages"
  placeholder="Choose languages..."
  options={[
    { value: 'js', label: 'JavaScript' },
    { value: 'ts', label: 'TypeScript' },
    { value: 'py', label: 'Python' }
  ]}
  validationState={hasError ? 'invalid' : undefined}
  feedback="Please select at least one language"
/>
```

# React Multi Select Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Multi Select component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CMultiSelect

```jsx
import { CMultiSelect } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowCreateOptions` | `boolean` | - | Allow users to create options if they are not in the list of options. |
| `ariaChipRemoveLabel` | `string \| ((label: string) => string)` | `Remove` | Names a chip's remove button with the selected option's label: a string has `{label}` replaced by it, or gets it appended when there is no `{label}` ("Remove Angular"); a function receives the label and returns the whole name. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `Clear all selections` | A string that provides an accessible label for the cleaner button. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `Toggle options list` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) for the button that opens and closes the options list. |
| `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` | `string \| ((values: string[]) => string)` | `removed` | Announced after a value is removed through its chip, Backspace or the cleaner. A string follows the removed labels (`Angular removed`); a function receives them and returns the whole message. A pick in the list is not announced, since the option says it is selected. |
| `ariaSearchLabel` | `string` | `Search` | Accessible label for the search input (when `search` is enabled). |
| `ariaTagDeleteLabel` | `string` | - | Accessible label prefix for a chip's remove button. While it is set, it takes precedence over `ariaChipRemoveLabel`. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables selection cleaner element. |
| `clearSearchOnSelect` | `boolean` | - | Clear current search on selecting an item. |
| `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| (() => Element \| DocumentFragment \| null) \| null` | - | Appends the options menu to a specific element: an element, a document fragment, a function returning either, or `null` to leave the menu where it is written. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `defaultShow` | `boolean` | - | The initial open state of the uncontrolled options menu — read once on mount. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| (string \| number)[]` | - | The selection for the uncontrolled mode, matched against the option values. Options that arrive later are seeded from it as they appear, so a list loaded after mount honours it. Ignored when `value` is set. |
| `deselectAllLabel` | `ReactNode` | `Deselect all` | Sets the label of the select all button once it deselects rather than selects. The button flips when the selection reaches what it can select, which with `selectionLimit` is the limit rather than every option; with `selectAllMode="filtered"` and a narrowed list the pair in use is `selectFilteredLabel`/`deselectFilteredLabel` instead. |
| `deselectFilteredLabel` | `ReactNode` | `Deselect filtered` | Sets the label of the select filtered button once it deselects rather than selects, with `selectAllMode` set to `filtered` and the list narrowed by a search. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `globalSearch` | `boolean` | `true` | Routes typing to the search box from anywhere in the component, so a keystroke never depends on where the focus sits. Set to `false` to keep it local: the search box then filters only while it has the focus, and typing over the options list jumps to the first option that starts with what was typed, except with `search="external"`, where the list holds only the last results. Needs `search`. |
| `headerTemplate` | `((state: SelectionState, actions: SelectionActions) => ReactNode)` | - | Render a custom dropdown header (the area above the options list), replacing the built-in select all button. Receives a `state` object (`{ selected, total, filtered, filteredSelected }`) and an `actions` object (`{ selectAll, deselectAll, selectFiltered, deselectFiltered }`) so you can wire your own controls. Renders independently of `selectAll`. |
| `hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults` | `boolean` | `true` | Hide the dropdown header with the built-in select all button when a search filter leaves no matching options. Set to `false` to keep the select all button visible even when there are no results. |
| `indicator` | `ListBoxIndicator` | `checkbox` | Puts a mark in front of every option. `checkbox` draws the check the multi-value pickers use, `none` draws nothing; either way the select all button reports a partial selection as indeterminate. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | - | When set, the options list is marked busy and shows a row with a spinner and `loadingLabel` below its options while you fetch them; the options it shows can still be picked. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `Loading…` | Text of the loading row below the options, announced to screen readers when the shown list starts loading or the list shows up loading. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | It specifies that multiple options can be selected at once. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the native select the selection is submitted under. Without it the selection is not submitted with the form. |
| `onChange` | `((selected: SelectedOption[]) => void)` | - | Execute a function when the user or the component changes the selection: a pick, a native reset of the form, or `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange`. A selection you give through `value`, `defaultValue` or options marked `selected` does not fire it, unless `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` replaced the selection with it. With `value` set it is a request. |
| `onFilterChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Execute a function when the filter value changed. |
| `onHide` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired after the options menu has closed. It reports the transition, not the request, and does not fire on mount. |
| `onSelectionLimit` | `((selectionLimit: number) => void)` | - | Execute a function when the user tries to select more options than allowed by `selectionLimit`. |
| `onShow` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired after the options menu has opened. It reports the transition, not the request, and does not fire on mount. |
| `onShowChange` | `((show: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired whenever the component asks for the menu to open or close: the toggle, a dismiss gesture (Escape, outside click), a pick that closes the menu. It reports the request, not the result, so in controlled mode nothing happens until you update `show` yourself. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the selection, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the selection it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `options` | `(Option \| OptionsGroup)[]` | - | List of option elements. |
| `optionsGroupsSelectable` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes each options group label a toggle that selects or deselects all options in that group. With `indicator="checkbox"` (and `multiple`) the label shows a tri-state checkbox indicator (`none` / `all` / `indeterminate`) reflecting the group's selection. |
| `optionsGroupsTemplate` | `((option: OptionsGroup) => ReactNode)` | - | Custom template for options groups. |
| `optionsMaxHeight` | `string \| number` | `auto` | Sets maxHeight of options list. |
| `optionsTemplate` | `((option: Option) => ReactNode)` | - | Custom template for options. |
| `pickerIcon` | `ReactNode` | `true` | The button that opens the options menu: `true` for the built-in icon, a node for your own, `false` for no button. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `Select...` | Short hint shown where the selection would be: in the search input, or in its place when `search` is off. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `false` | Generates dropdown menu using createPortal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When it is present, it indicates that the user must choose a value before submitting the form. |
| `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` | `boolean` | `false` | Empties the selection when the options bring different values, then takes the options marked `selected` (or the `defaultValue` values among them), up to `selectionLimit`; with `value` set it only requests the empty selection through `onChange`. For options that depend on another field, so outdated picks do not travel on. |
| `search` | `Search` | `true` | Renders a search box in the control. `true` filters the options as the user types; `'external'` hands the filtering to your code: the component shows the options you pass and reports what the user types through `onFilterChange`. |
| `searchNoResultsLabel` | `ReactNode` | `No results found` | Sets the label for no results when filtering. |
| `selectAll` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables select all button. |
| `selectAllLabel` | `ReactNode` | `Select all` | Sets the select all button label. |
| `selectAllMode` | `"all" \| "filtered"` | `all` | Determines what the select all button operates on: all options (`'all'`) or only the currently filtered (search-visible) options (`'filtered'`). |
| `selectedLabel` | `CountLabel` | `(count: number) => `${count} item(s) selected`` | Sets the counter selection label: a function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced. `total` is the number of options in the list, disabled ones, the ones inside a group and the ones the user created included, so a disabled option shows that not everything is selected, plus any selected value the options lack, so it never falls below `count`, unless `total` gives a number of its own. |
| `selectFilteredLabel` | `ReactNode` | `Select filtered` | Sets the select filtered button label (used with `selectAllMode="filtered"`). |
| `selectionLimit` | `number` | - | Sets the maximum number of options that can be selected. The select all button stays enabled and selects options up to the limit, then toggles to deselect all once the limit is reached. The `onSelectionLimit` callback fires when a user tries to select more options than allowed. |
| `selectionType` | `"text" \| "chips" \| "counter" \| "tags"` | `chips` | Sets the selection style. `chips` renders the selection as chips; `tags` is a deprecated name for `chips` (since 6.0.0). |
| `show` | `boolean` | - | Control the open state of the dropdown panel. When set, the panel renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `total` | `number` | - | Sets `{total}` of `selectedLabel`. Leave it out to count the options in the list; with external search give the number of records your data source holds, which the component cannot see. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| (string \| number)[]` | - | The controlled selection — matched against the option values. Pair it with `onChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultValue` instead. |
| `virtualScroller` | `boolean` | - | Enable virtual scroller for the options list. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggle the visibility of multi select dropdown. |
| `visibleItems` | `number` | `10` | Amount of visible items when virtualScroller is set to `true`. |

# React Multi Select Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Multi Select component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables), so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. `className` and `style` on `CMultiSelect` land on that frame, the `.multi-select` element, so the tokens can be set on a single field. The selected chips add two of their own:

```scss
$multi-select-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-multi-select-selection-chips-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-multi-select-selection-chips-padding-y: .25rem,
  ),
  $multi-select-tokens
);
```

The options menu is the shared combobox surface, which Autocomplete renders too, so it carries its own set.

```scss
$combobox-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-combobox-popup-min-width: 100%,
  ),
  $combobox-tokens
);
```

Everything inside the panel — the options, the group labels, the select-all button and the checkbox indicator — is a [List box](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/list-box/) and takes its `--cui-list-box-*` variables. `.list-box` declares them itself, so a value set on `.combobox-popup` or on `:root` does not reach it: set them with a rule on `.combobox-popup .list-box`, which covers the panels of Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select alike.

#### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-control-border-color': 'var(--cui-primary-base)',
  '--cui-multi-select-selection-chips-gap': '.5rem',
}

return <CMultiSelect options={options} style={customVars} />
```

# React Multi Select Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility features implemented in CoreUI React Multi Select, ensuring compliance with WAI-ARIA guidelines.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Accessibility

The React Multi Select component is designed with accessibility in mind, implementing WAI-ARIA standards to ensure compatibility with screen readers and assistive technologies.

### ARIA Attributes

The component automatically includes the following ARIA attributes:

- **`role="combobox"`** on the main container to identify it as a combobox control
- **`aria-haspopup="dialog"`** indicates that the control opens a dialog holding the list of options
- **`aria-expanded`** reflects the current state of the dropdown (true when open, false when closed)
- **`aria-controls`** points the control at the dropdown dialog and the search input at the listbox while the dropdown is open
- **`role="listbox"`** on the list of options inside the dropdown
- **`aria-labelledby`** names the control and the dropdown after the label: `label`, `floatingLabel`, or a `<label>` pointing at the component's `id`, read when the component mounts or its `id` changes; an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` given to the component takes precedence. A `<label>` wrapping the component is left out, because its text would take in the control's own content and selection. The search box keeps a name of its own, `ariaSearchLabel`
- **`aria-required`** on the focused control, the search box when `search` is on, when `required` is set or an `aria-required` is given to the component
- **`aria-hidden="true"`** on the native `<select>` that carries the value into the form, so assistive technology meets only the combobox
- **Focus that reaches the native `<select>`**, from the browser's validation or from the label, goes on to the control (the search box when `search` is on), which carries `aria-invalid` and the `feedbackInvalid` description. A change of selection fires `input` and `change` on the select, as a native list does
- **`aria-multiselectable`** indicates whether multiple selections are allowed
- **`role="option"`** on each selectable option
- **`aria-selected`** on options to indicate their selection state

### Keyboard Navigation

The component supports full keyboard navigation:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Navigate to/from the component |
| <kbd>Enter/Space</kbd> | Open dropdown or select focused option |
| <kbd>Arrow Up/Down</kbd> | Navigate through options |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> | Focus the first option |
| <kbd>End</kbd> | Focus the last option |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the dropdown |
| <kbd>Backspace/Delete</kbd> | In the empty search box, focus the last chip; on a chip, remove it and move the focus to the next chip, else the previous one, else the search box, or the field when there is none. Entering the chips closes an open panel. A single select and the `counter` and `text` selections remove the last selected item at once |
| <kbd>Arrow Left/Arrow Right</kbd> | From the start of the search box, focus the last chip; between the chips, move the focus; past the last chip, return to the search box (mirrored in right-to-left) |

### Screen Reader Support

- All interactive elements have appropriate accessible names
- Selection changes are announced to screen readers
- Loading states are properly communicated
- Option groups are properly labeled and associated

### Customizable Labels

You can customize the accessible labels for better user experience:

```jsx
<CMultiSelect
  :options="options"
  aria-cleaner-label="Remove all selected items"
  aria-indicator-label="Open options menu"
/>
```

### Best Practices

- Always provide a meaningful `label` prop for the component
- Use descriptive option labels that make sense when read by screen readers
- Consider the `placeholder` text as it may be announced by some screen readers
- Test with actual screen readers to ensure the experience meets your users' needs

# React Number Input Component

> A React number field with accessible increment and decrement buttons, with min, max and step handled by the browser.

## Example

`` is a number field with a stepper you can actually hit. The browser's own spinner is tiny, appears only on hover in some engines and does not exist at all on iOS, so the component replaces it with two buttons sized like every other adornment in a form control group. You write neither the frame, the buttons nor their icons.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputExample = () => {
  return <CNumberInput aria-label="Quantity" defaultValue={3} />
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="numberInputField">Quantity</CFormLabel>
      <CNumberInput id="numberInputField" defaultValue={3} />
      <CFormText>Up to ten items per order.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Min, max and step

`min`, `max` and `step` are the native attributes — the component does not reimplement them, it calls the browser's own stepping. **A button that cannot move the value any further is disabled**, so the bound is visible rather than just unresponsive.

When the field is empty, a button steps from zero, and the result stays within `min` and `max` and on the `step` grid.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputBoundsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CNumberInput defaultValue={10} label="Quantity" max={10} min={0} />
      </div>
      <div>
        <CNumberInput defaultValue={2} label="Amount" step={0.5} />
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Sizing

Use the `size` prop to control the height and padding of the field. Sizing belongs to the frame rather than to the control inside it, so the component puts the class on the group it builds.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CNumberInput aria-label="Quantity" defaultValue={3} size="sm" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <CNumberInput aria-label="Quantity" defaultValue={3} size="lg" />
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Controlled value

Pair `value` with `onChange` to own the value yourself. Stepping reports through the same `onChange` typing does, so there is one path to handle.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputControlledExample = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('3')

  return (
    <>
      <CNumberInput
        label="Quantity"
        onChange={(event) => setValue(event.target.value)}
        value={value}
      />
      <div className="mt-3 fg-2">Value: {value === '' ? '—' : value}</div>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Disabled and read-only

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CNumberInput defaultValue={3} disabled label="Disabled" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <CNumberInput defaultValue={3} label="Read-only" readOnly />
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

Both buttons are disabled while the field is disabled or read-only.

## Holding a button

Holding a button repeats the step after a short delay, and releasing it does not add a step. Set `repeat={false}` to require a click per step.

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name; the stepper buttons ride along with the field.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const NumberInputFloatingLabelExample = () => (
  <CNumberInput defaultValue={42} floatingLabel="Quantity" id="floatingNumberInput" />
)
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating).

## Accessibility

The buttons carry labels (`Increase` / `Decrease` by default, both configurable through `ariaIncrementLabel` and `ariaDecrementLabel`) but are **kept out of the tab order**: a number field already steps with <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd>, so putting them in would add two tab stops per field for something the keyboard already reaches. A mouse press on a button, enabled or not, puts the focus in the field rather than on the button, so typing and the arrow keys act on the field you just stepped. Give the field a `label` or an `aria-label` as you would any other control.

> **Decimal separators.** `` accepts the dot as the decimal separator regardless of locale, and a value the browser rejects is reported as an empty string — the field cannot tell you what was typed. If you need locale-aware separators, currency or grouping, that is a formatted-input problem rather than a stepper one, and `type="number"` is the wrong base for it.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CNumberInput /&gt;](./api/#cnumberinput)

# React Number Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Number Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CNumberInput

```jsx
import { CNumberInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDecrementLabel` | `string` | `Decrease` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that decreases the value. |
| `ariaIncrementLabel` | `string` | `Increase` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that increases the value. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Adds a custom class name to the React Number Input. |
| `decrementIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork of the button that decreases the value. Defaults to a minus drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `incrementIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork of the button that increases the value. Defaults to a plus drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement, HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on the native `change` event of the input. A form reset or a controlled `value` does not call it. |
| `onInput` | `InputEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on every `input` event of the field. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `repeat` | `boolean` | `true` | Repeats the step while a button is held. Set to `false` to require a click per step. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |

# React Number Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Number Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The frame, the buttons and their sizing are the group's, and read the shared `--cui-control-*` properties. Set them with a rule on the `.number-input` group the component renders around the input, or on a class you pass through `className`; `style` goes to the `<input>` and does not reach the frame:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

The group takes its own icon and action sizes per size class, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$form-control-group-sizes: defaults(
  (
    "sm": (icon-size: .875rem, action-size: 1.25rem),
    "lg": (icon-size: 1.25rem, action-size: 1.75rem),
  ),
  $form-control-group-sizes
);
```

# React One Time Password (OTP) Input Component

> Create secure and user-friendly React.js one-time password input fields with automatic navigation, paste support, validation, and customizable options for modern authentication flows.

## Example

The `` and `` components create secure **React OTP input fields** with automatic character navigation and validation. Perfect for two-factor authentication, SMS verification codes, and secure login flows.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/react'
import { COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const OneTimePasswordExample = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('')

  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <COneTimePassword label="Enter OTP Code" id="basicOTP" name="otp" onChange={setValue}>
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
        </COneTimePassword>
      </div>
      {value && <div className="fg-2 small">Current value: {value}</div>}
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

The code works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultValue` | the input, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `value` | your component |

`onChange` fires in **both** modes with the joined code, and `onComplete` once every slot is filled — so you can watch the code without taking it over. A native reset of the form puts back the code the input started with: uncontrolled, it sets it and calls `onChange` when that changes the code; controlled, it asks for the first `value` through `onChange` and shows your `value` until you take it.

### Uncontrolled

Seed the slots with `defaultValue`, or leave them empty, and let the input manage the code. This is what every example above does.

```jsx
<COneTimePassword defaultValue="123456">
```

### Controlled

Pass `value` and the slots render exactly what you pass — typing only fires `onChange`. Feed the change back, or nothing moves.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const OneTimePasswordControlledExample = () => {
  const [code, setCode] = useState('')

  return (
    <>
      <COneTimePassword label="Verification code" value={code} onChange={setCode}>
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
        <COneTimePasswordInput />
      </COneTimePassword>
      <div className="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mt-3">
        <CButton theme="secondary" size="sm" onClick={() => setCode('')}>
          Clear
        </CButton>
        <span className="small fg-2">Current code: {code || '-'}</span>
      </div>
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the code belongs to something else: form state, a reset button, or a value you validate before accepting it.

## Validation

The code is validated as one value, kept in an input laid invisibly over the group. With `required` an empty or incomplete code blocks the submit, and an incomplete code blocks it even when the field is not required; the browser puts focus on the first empty slot and shows its own message over the group. The state shows on the group as the `.is-*` class, and while it is `'invalid'` every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and is described by the message after the group: the `feedbackInvalid` text, the `feedback` text while you give a state, or an `.invalid-feedback` you render after the field yourself. The hidden input holds the new code by the time `onChange` and `onComplete` run, and sends `input` and `change` once the code has rendered, also when your code changes it through `value`.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CForm } from '@coreui/react'
import { COneTimePassword, COneTimePasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const OneTimePasswordValidationExample = () => {
  const [backupCodeState, setBackupCodeState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <COneTimePassword
          feedbackInvalid="Enter the six digits we sent you."
          label="Verification code"
          name="code"
          required
        >
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
        </COneTimePassword>
      </div>
      <div className="col-md-6">
        <COneTimePassword
          defaultValue="482913"
          feedback="This backup code has already been used."
          label="Backup code"
          name="backupCode"
          onValidationStateChange={setBackupCodeState}
          validationState={backupCodeState}
        >
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
          <COneTimePasswordInput />
        </COneTimePassword>
      </div>
      <div className="col-12">
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Verify
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

The state comes from three places, in this order:

- `validationState`: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`; `invalid` and `valid` still work as aliases. While it is set, the component draws it instead of what the browser reports. While it is `'invalid'`, the code blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the component is `disabled`.
- A validation that reports the code invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which [`CForm`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/validation/) and the stepper call as well. From then on the group and the slots show it invalid whenever the code is invalid, until the form is reset, and the message after the group shows.
- In a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the hidden input, and with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give is a verdict on the code it was given for. When the user types, deletes, pastes or autofills a different code, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)`; pass your state setter there to drop the state, as the second field above does. A change your code makes through `value` keeps it, and so does a keystroke that leaves the code as it is. A reset asks once it has run, so a state you set from a `reset` listener on the form gets the same call, and your handler decides whether to drop it. A native reset of the form puts back the code given by `defaultValue`, and leaves a controlled `value` to you. An `aria-invalid` passed to the component or to a slot is not read; set the state with `validationState`.

## Accessibility

The one-time password input component is designed with accessibility in mind and follows WCAG guidelines for form inputs.

- **ARIA Labels**: Each input field automatically receives descriptive `aria-label` attributes
- **Role Attribute**: The container has `role="group"` to indicate related form controls, named by `label`
- **Label click**: clicking the label that names the group moves focus to the first empty slot, as clicking the label of an input focuses it
- **Required**: with `required`, every slot carries `aria-required="true"`, since the value input that holds `required` is hidden from assistive technologies
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, tab, and backspace
- **Screen Reader Support**: Clear announcements when values change; while the code is reported invalid, every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message
- **Focus Management**: Automatic focus handling for seamless navigation
- **Autofill**: only the first field advertises `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so SMS autofill and password managers target a single field; a code delivered that way is spread across the slots automatically, exactly like a paste

### Customizing accessibility

You can customize the aria-label generation function to provide more specific descriptions:

```jsx
<COneTimePassword
  ariaLabel={(index, total) => `Enter digit ${index + 1} of your ${total}-digit verification code`}
/>
```

### Keyboard support

The one-time password input component provides comprehensive keyboard navigation support:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> | Move focus to next input field |
| <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to previous input field |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Delete current character and move to previous field (if empty) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to next focusable element (respects linear mode) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to previous focusable element |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste clipboard content and auto-fill fields |

# React One Time Password Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React One Time Password Input components and discover how to effectively utilize their props for customization.

## COneTimePassword

```jsx
import { COneTimePassword } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `((index: number, total: number) => string)` | `(index: number, total: number) => `Digit ${index + 1} of ${total}`` | Function to generate aria-label for each input field. Receives current index (0-based) and total number of inputs. |
| `autoSubmit` | `boolean` | `false` | Automatically submit the form when all one time password fields are filled. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the React.js OTP component. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number` | - | Initial value for uncontrolled React.js one time password input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable all one time password (OTP) input fields. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `id` | `string` | - | ID attribute for the value input. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `linear` | `boolean` | `true` | Enforce sequential input (users must fill fields in order). |
| `masked` | `boolean` | `false` | Show input as password (masked characters). |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the code is submitted under. Without it the code is not submitted with the form. |
| `onChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Callback triggered when the React.js one time password (OTP) value changes. |
| `onComplete` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Callback triggered when all React.js one time password (OTP) fields are filled. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the code, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the code it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Placeholder text for input fields. Single character applies to all fields, longer strings apply character-by-character. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the code required: an empty or incomplete code blocks the submit. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Sets the visual size of the React.js one time password (OTP) input. Use 'sm' for small or 'lg' for large input fields. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `"number" \| "text"` | `number` | Input validation type: 'number' for digits only, or 'text' for free text. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class on the group; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every slot and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the code asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string \| number` | - | Current value for controlled OTP input. When set, update it yourself from `onChange`, or the rendered code stays as it is. |

# React One Time Password Input Component CSS Customization

> Learn how to customize the appearance of React One Time Password Input components using CSS classes and CSS variables.

### CSS Classes

The One Time Password Input components use the following CSS classes:

- `.form-otp` - Applied to the wrapper container
- `.form-otp-sm` - Small size variant
- `.form-otp-lg` - Large size variant
- `.form-otp-control` - Applied to individual input elements

### CSS variables

Each cell is an input, so it carries the shared `--cui-control-*` tokens on `.form-otp-control` itself. Override them on a single OTP input to restyle just that one; to restyle every text control at once, set the `--cui-btn-input-*` frame on `:root` instead.

```scss
$form-otp-control-tokens: () !default;
$form-otp-control-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-padding-x: 0,
    --cui-form-otp-control-width: 2rem,
  ),
  $form-otp-control-tokens
);
```

```scss
$form-otp-tokens: () !default;
$form-otp-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-otp-gap: .125rem,
  ),
  $form-otp-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

Each size is one entry, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$form-otp-sizes: defaults(
  (
    "sm": (
      width:         1.5rem,
      padding-y:     var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-y),
      padding-x:     0,
      font-size:     var(--cui-btn-input-sm-font-size),
      border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    ),
    "lg": (
      width:         2.5rem,
      padding-y:     var(--cui-btn-input-lg-padding-y),
      padding-x:     0,
      font-size:     var(--cui-btn-input-lg-font-size),
      border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-lg-border-radius),
    ),
  ),
  $form-otp-sizes
);
```

# React One-Time Password Input Component Accessibility

> Detailed overview of the accessibility features implemented in CoreUI React One-Time Password Input, ensuring compliance with WAI-ARIA guidelines.

## Accessibility

The one-time password input component is designed with accessibility in mind and follows WCAG guidelines for form inputs.

- **ARIA Labels**: Each input field automatically receives descriptive `aria-label` attributes
- **Role Attribute**: The container has `role="group"` to indicate related form controls
- **Label click**: clicking the label that names the group moves focus to the first empty slot, as clicking the label of an input focuses it
- **Required**: with `required`, every slot carries `aria-required="true"`, since the value input that holds `required` is hidden from assistive technologies
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, tab, and backspace
- **Screen Reader Support**: Clear announcements when values change; while the code is reported invalid, every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message
- **Focus Management**: Automatic focus handling for seamless navigation
- **Autofill**: only the first field advertises `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so SMS autofill and password managers target a single field; a code delivered that way is spread across the slots automatically, exactly like a paste

### Customizing accessibility

You can customize the aria-label generation function to provide more specific descriptions:

```jsx
<COneTimePassword
  ariaLabel={(index, total) => `Enter digit ${index + 1} of your ${total}-digit verification code`}
>
  <COneTimePasswordInput />
  <COneTimePasswordInput />
  <COneTimePasswordInput />
  <COneTimePasswordInput />
</COneTimePassword>
```

### Keyboard support

The one-time password input component provides comprehensive keyboard navigation support:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> | Move focus to next input field |
| <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to previous input field |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Delete current character and move to previous field (if empty) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to next focusable element (respects linear mode) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to previous focusable element |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste clipboard content and auto-fill fields |

# React Password Input Component

> A fully customizable React password input component with Bootstrap styling. Includes toggle visibility, validation, sizing options, and accessibility support.

## Example

The `` is a fully featured **React password input field** built with Bootstrap and CoreUI. It includes built-in **password visibility toggling**, `sm` / `lg` **sizing options**, and support for `disabled`, `readOnly`, and form validation states. Ideal for login forms, signup screens, and any secure input in your React app.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CForm } from '@coreui/react'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const PasswordInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CPasswordInput label="Password" placeholder="Enter your password" />
      </div>
      <div>
        <CPasswordInput
          label="Password with value"
          placeholder="Enter your password"
          defaultValue="Top secret"
        />
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const PasswordInputFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="passwordInputField">Password</CFormLabel>
      <CPasswordInput id="passwordInputField" placeholder="Enter your password" />
      <CFormText>At least 12 characters.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Sizing

Use the `size` prop to control the height and padding of the input. Available options:
- `size="sm"` – small input
- `size="lg"` – large input

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const PasswordInputSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CPasswordInput size="lg" placeholder="Large password input" aria-label="lg input example" />
      <CPasswordInput placeholder="Default password input" aria-label="default input example" />
      <CPasswordInput size="sm" placeholder="Small password input" aria-label="sm input example" />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` attribute to make the password input uneditable. This also dims the field to indicate it's inactive. The visibility toggle is disabled with it and leaves the tab order, so it can't change what a disabled field shows: a password revealed before stays visible, and can be hidden once the field is enabled again.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const PasswordInputDisabledExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CPasswordInput
        placeholder="Disabled password input"
        aria-label="Disabled password input example"
        disabled
      />
      <CPasswordInput
        placeholder="Disabled readonly password input"
        aria-label="Disabled password input example"
        disabled
        readOnly
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Readonly

Use the `readOnly` prop to make the input non-editable while still allowing the text to be copied. Unlike `disabled`, it keeps the default cursor.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const PasswordInputReadonlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CPasswordInput
      placeholder="Readonly password input"
      aria-label="Readonly password input example"
      defaultValue="Readonly input here..."
      readOnly
    />
  )
}
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name; the toggle button rides along with the field, and the placeholder stays hidden until the label floats.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const PasswordInputFloatingLabelExample = () => (
  <CPasswordInput floatingLabel="Password" id="floatingPasswordInput" />
)
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Controlled and uncontrolled visibility

_Added in 6.0.0._

The visibility toggle works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the visibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultShowPassword` | the input, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `showPassword` | your component |

`onShowPasswordChange` fires in **both** modes with the requested state — so you can watch the toggle without taking it over.

### Uncontrolled

`defaultShowPassword` seeds the toggle — the input starts revealed and manages itself from there. Every example above leaves it out and starts hidden.

```jsx
<CPasswordInput defaultShowPassword label="Password" />
```

### Controlled

Pass `showPassword` and the input renders the type you pass — the toggle button only fires `onShowPasswordChange`. Feed the change back, or nothing flips.

```jsx
const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false)

<CPasswordInput label="Password" onShowPasswordChange={setVisible} showPassword={visible} />
```

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CPasswordInput /&gt;](./api/#cpasswordinput)

# React Password Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Password Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CPasswordInput

```jsx
import { CPasswordInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaToggleLabel` | `string` | `Toggle password visibility` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) for the toggle password visibility button. This improves accessibility for screen readers and should describe the action, e.g. `"Show password"` or `"Hide password"`. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `defaultShowPassword` | `boolean` | - | The initial visibility of the password for the uncontrolled mode — read once on mount. Ignored when `showPassword` is set. |
| `delay` | `number \| boolean` | `false` | Enables delayed `onChange` execution for improved performance in React password inputs. - `true` delays the `onChange` callback by 500ms. - You can also pass a custom delay (in milliseconds) as a number. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Disables the password input field. When `true`, the user cannot interact with the field, and the visibility toggle is disabled with it. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `hideIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork of the toggle while the password is visible. Defaults to a crossed-out eye drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Callback triggered when the value of the password input changes. If `delay` is set, the callback is called after the specified timeout. |
| `onInput` | `InputEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on every `input` event of the field. |
| `onShowPasswordChange` | `((showPassword: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the visibility toggle requests a new state, receiving the requested visibility. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Makes the React password input read-only. Prevents user input but allows text selection. |
| `showIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork of the toggle while the password is hidden. Defaults to an eye drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `showPassword` | `boolean` | - | The controlled visibility of the password — `true` renders the input as type `"text"` instead of `"password"`. Pair it with `onShowPasswordChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultShowPassword` instead. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Sets the visual size of the password input. Use `'sm'` for small or `'lg'` for large input fields. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| string[]` | - | The value of the password input field. To make the input controlled, pair this with the `onChange` handler. |

# React Password Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Password Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

The frame — padding, colours, border and the size of the toggle button, including the icon inside it — is the group's, and it reads the shared `--cui-control-*` properties. Set them with a rule on the `.password-input` group the component renders around the input, or on a class you pass through `className`, to restyle one field, since `style` goes to the `<input>` and does not reach the frame; the group declares them itself, so a value on `:root` stops there — to restyle every field at once, change the shared [`--cui-btn-input-*` frame](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/overview/#css-variables). The focus ring is the library's own, coloured by `--cui-focus-ring-color` or the theme:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```
