# React Time Input Component

> Create React time fields with a section-based input mask. Users type the hour, minutes, and seconds in separate sections with automatic navigation and validation — like the native time input, but with full control over the format.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 5.27.0._

The React Time Input component renders a masked time field. The mask is split into hour, minute, and — depending on the locale — AM/PM sections. Click or focus a section and type, use arrow keys to adjust values, and the caret moves to the next section automatically.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput label="Meeting time" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput label="Meeting time" locale="en-US" defaultTime="14:30" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <span className="form-label">Meeting time</span>
      <CTimeInput locale="en-US" name="meetingTime" />
      <CFormText>Local time, in your own time zone.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Formats

Set an explicit format with the `format` property: `HH`/`H` for the 23-hour cycle, `hh`/`h` for the 12-hour cycle, `mm` for minutes, `ss` for seconds, and `A`/`a` for the day period. Type `a` or `p` in the AM/PM section to switch it, or use the arrow keys.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputFormatsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="HH:mm" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput format="HH:mm:ss" label="HH:mm:ss" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput format="hh:mm A" label="hh:mm A" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, the hour cycle and layout follow the locale set via the `locale` property — `en-US` gets a 12-hour clock with an AM/PM section, `pl-PL` or `de-DE` a 24-hour one.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputLocalesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput label="en-US" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput label="pl-PL" locale="pl-PL" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput label="de-DE" locale="de-DE" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Seconds

Without an explicit format, enable the seconds section with the `seconds` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputSecondsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput label="Time with seconds" seconds />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Min and max times

Constrain the selectable range with `minDate` and `maxDate` — time strings work here too. A completed time outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null`, and submits no time, until the value is corrected.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputMinMaxExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput
          format="HH:mm"
          label="Business hours (09:00–17:00)"
          maxDate="17:00"
          minDate="09:00"
          defaultTime="09:30"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The field takes its validation state [the same way as the date input](../date-input/#validation): a completed time outside `minDate`/`maxDate` makes it invalid whatever else is set, then `validationState`, then a validation that reported the field, and in a form with the `validate` property of `<CForm>` the `:user-invalid` state of its value field, with `validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state. A given state is a verdict on the time it was given for: when the user changes the time, or the form is reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)`, while a change your code makes through `time` asks nothing. A given `'invalid'` blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none. The `feedbackValid`/`feedbackInvalid` texts render like for any other form control, and while the field is invalid the error, its own or one you render after the field, describes every section.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CForm, CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputValidationExample = () => {
  const [roomState, setRoomState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a meeting time."
          format="HH:mm"
          label="Meeting time (required)"
          name="meeting"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput
          defaultTime="12:30"
          feedback="The room is taken at this time."
          format="HH:mm"
          label="Room booking"
          name="room"
          onValidationStateChange={setRoomState}
          validationState={roomState}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Floating labels

Use the `floatingLabel` property. When the field is empty and not focused, the mask placeholders are hidden so the label can rest inside the field; focusing the field floats the label and reveals the mask.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputFloatingLabelsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput floatingLabel="Meeting time" format="HH:mm" id="floatingTimeInput" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

The field renders as a `.form-control`, so the standard sizing works — set the `size` property to `lg` or `sm`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Large" size="lg" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-lg-0" lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Default" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Small" size="sm" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Disabled and readonly

Set the `disabled` property to disable the field, or `readOnly` to make it focusable but non-editable.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimeInputDisabledReadonlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput disabled format="HH:mm" label="Disabled" defaultTime="14:30" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={5}>
        <CTimeInput format="HH:mm" label="Readonly" readOnly defaultTime="14:30" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Value semantics

The component reports a `Date` object anchored to `1970-01-01` — the same convention as the CoreUI time picker — so only the time part is meaningful. `minDate`/`maxDate` therefore constrain the time of day. A native reset of the form puts back the time the field started with and calls `onTimeChange` when that changes it; with `time` set it only asks for the first `time` through `onTimeChange`.

## Accessibility

The time input shares the [accessibility model of the date input](../date-input/#accessibility): `role="group"` on the container, named by `label`, a `role="spinbutton"` with full ARIA value attributes per section, a single tab stop with roving focus, and `inputmode` hints for mobile keyboards. Clicking the label that names the field moves focus to the first empty section. The AM/PM section announces its localized name via `aria-valuetext` and can be toggled with the <kbd>A</kbd>/<kbd>P</kbd> letters or arrow keys.

The [keyboard support table](../date-input/#keyboard-support) applies unchanged, including <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> (select all), <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> (copy), and paste.

# React Time Input Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Time Input component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CTimeInput

```jsx
import { CTimeInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | - | Focus the first section right after mounting, like the native `autofocus` attribute. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `defaultTime` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial time for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `time` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | - | Specify the list of dates that cannot be selected. It can be a single `Date`, an `[start, end]` range, a matcher function, or an array of these. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | - | The mask layout. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `inputDateParse` | `((value: string) => Date \| null)` | - | Custom function to parse text pasted into the field into a `Date` object, e.g. with an external date library. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `'default'` | Sets the default locale for the component. If not set, it is inherited from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Max selectable date. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Min selectable date. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | `string[]` | - | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `onError` | `((error: DateInputError) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after the change callback, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `onTimeChange` | `((time: Date \| null, formattedTime?: string \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the time changes; receives a `Date` anchored to 1970-01-01 (or `null` while incomplete or invalid) and the formatted value. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean` | - | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived time layout. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `time` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled time — a `Date` or a time string like `'14:30'` or `'2:30 PM'`. Pair it with `onTimeChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultTime` instead. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. A field of a date range whose end is before its start draws no other state. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

# React Time Input Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Time Input component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The date, time, and date-time inputs share one set of styles under the `form-date-time` name. The field is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/input/styling/#css-variables), so its frame comes from the `--cui-control-*` tokens; the ones below style the sections inside it. Both sets sit on the field, the element `style` lands on, and can be set on a single input.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# React Time Picker Component

> React Time Picker is a customizable and user-friendly tool for selecting times in forms. It supports various locales, sizes, and states to enhance the user experience.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

To create a basic React Time Picker, use:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol className="mb-4 mb-sm-0" sm={6} lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker label="Time" locale="en-US" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker label="Time" locale="en-US" defaultTime="02:17:35 PM" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### With footer

The `footer` prop projects your own content below the time selection. Pass a node, or a function receiving the picker's context — `setTime`, `now`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isTimeSelectable`, `time` and `disabled` — so a projected button acts on the picker and reads its state. That is also how a "Now" button disables itself when the current time falls outside `minDate` or `maxDate`; the example checks when the panel renders and again on click, so a time that crosses a limit while the panel is open is not written.

Any descendant can reach the same context with the `useTimePicker()` hook.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerWithFooterExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker
          footer={({ clear, close, isTimeSelectable, now }) => (
            <>
              <CButton
                className="me-auto"
                theme="danger"
                disabled={!isTimeSelectable(new Date())}
                onClick={() => isTimeSelectable(new Date()) && now()}
                size="sm"
                variant="ghost"
              >
                Now
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={clear} size="sm" variant="ghost">
                Clear
              </CButton>
              <CButton theme="primary" onClick={close} size="sm">
                OK
              </CButton>
            </>
          )}
          locale="en-US"
          maxDate="17:00"
          minDate="09:00"
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

A native reset of the form returns an uncontrolled picker to the time it started with and drops the state a submit set; a controlled one (`time` with `onTimeChange`) asks for the time it started with through `onTimeChange` and shows the time your page gives until the page takes it.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <span className="form-label">Meeting time</span>
      <CTimePicker locale="en-US" name="meetingTime" />
      <CFormText>Local time, in your own time zone.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Floating labels

Set `floatingLabel` and the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and renders the label itself — the text also becomes the field's accessible name. No wrapper markup is needed, and the mask placeholders stay hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerFloatingLabelExample = () => (
  <CTimePicker floatingLabel="Meeting time" locale="en-US" />
)
```

Set `floatingLabelAlways` to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.


## Min and max times

Constrain the times the user can pick with `minDate` and `maxDate`, given as time strings like `'09:30'` or as dates, of which only the time of day counts. The panel disables the hours that hold no allowed time and, once an hour is chosen, the minutes and seconds outside the range, and a time picked in the panel that crosses a limit moves to it. A time typed in the field outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class, `onTimeChange` reports `null` and the picker submits no time until the value is corrected. A `maxDate` at midnight covers the whole day; any other `maxDate` before the `minDate` leaves no time to pick.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerMinMaxExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker
          label="Opening hours (09:30–17:00)"
          locale="en-GB"
          maxDate="17:00"
          minDate="09:30"
          seconds={false}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Validation

The picker takes its validation state [the way the date picker does](../date-picker/#validation): `validationState` gives `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases that ask to be dropped the same way, though only `validationState` can be cleared by the setter you pass. When the user changes the time, with a time picked in the panel, the cleaner, a footer button that changes the time through the context, or typing in the field, or the form is reset, the picker calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before `onTimeChange`, while a change your code makes through `time` asks nothing. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the sections of the field carry `aria-invalid="true"`, are described by the message after the picker, and the picker blocks the submit with its text, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CCol, CForm, CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerValidationExample = () => {
  const [roomState, setRoomState] = useState<string | undefined>('invalid')

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a meeting time."
          label="Meeting time (required)"
          locale="en-US"
          name="meeting"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker
          defaultTime="12:30:00"
          feedback="The room is taken at this time."
          label="Room booking"
          locale="en-US"
          name="room"
          onValidationStateChange={setRoomState}
          validationState={roomState}
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton color="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Custom hours, minutes and seconds

Tailor the React Time Picker to your needs by specifying custom values for hours, minutes, and seconds. Use arrays to define selectable options or functions for dynamic filtering. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale. On a 12-hour clock the column still lists 1 to 12 next to AM/PM: picking an hour that only one period allows sets that period, and the period the picked hour does not allow is disabled, so the example below offers 8 AM to 4 PM, minutes in quarters and seconds under 20.

```html
import React from 'react'

          hours={[8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]}
          minutes={[0, 15, 30, 45]}
          seconds={(s) => s < 20}
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Locale

Tailor the React Time Picker to match different locales, offering an inclusive user experience across diverse languages. Automatically adapt or set specific locales to meet your application's needs.

The locale decides whether the field and the time columns use a 12-hour or a 24-hour clock, and names the day periods in its own words, 오전 and 오후 in Korean. A `format` pins the clock in every locale, `'HH:mm'` for 24 hours and `'hh:mm a'` for 12.

### Auto

Our Time Picker component automatically detects and adapts to the user's locale, ensuring a localized experience without explicit configuration.

With server-side rendering, pass `locale` explicitly: by default the server writes the text in its own locale and the browser in the reader's, and React reports a hydration mismatch when the two differ.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerLocaleAutoExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol sm={6} lg={4}>
        <CTimePicker />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

The popup works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the open state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultShow` | the picker, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `show` | your component |

`onShowChange` fires in **both** modes whenever the popup requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle — so you can watch the state without taking it over. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `defaultShow` or `show` is set.

### Uncontrolled

Every example above is uncontrolled — the picker manages its own popup. `defaultShow` seeds it open on mount.

```jsx
<CTimePicker defaultShow />
```

### Controlled

Pass `show` and the popup renders what you pass — dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes. Here a checkbox pins the popup open, and a dismiss gesture unchecks it.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CCheckbox, CCol, CFormField, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const TimePickerControlledExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          checked={show}
          id="timePickerControlledShow"
          label="Keep the popup open"
          onChange={(event) => setShow(event.target.checked)}
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CRow>
        <CCol sm={6} lg={4}>
          <CTimePicker label="Time" locale="en-US" onShowChange={setShow} show={show} />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the open state belongs to something else — a route, a tour step, or a control outside the picker like the checkbox above.

## Accessibility

The field is a group of spinbutton sections, so its own arrow keys belong to the value and the popup opens on the native control's dropdown keys instead. The field takes its name from an `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` you pass to the picker, otherwise from `floatingLabel` or, without one, from `label`, and it is described by an `aria-describedby` you pass to the picker, then by `text` and the feedback that matches its state. Clicking the label that names the field moves focus to its first empty section.

The toggle button carries the panel's state — `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` pointing at the popup while it is open, and `aria-expanded` — so a screen reader announces what the button does and whether the panel is showing. The panel itself is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, so focus moves into it on open, stays there while it is open, and returns to the field when it closes.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the popup and move focus into it |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the popup and return focus to the field |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move within the open panel; the field is outside the dialog and stays out of the cycle |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused value |

The roll is one composite: each column is a listbox, a roving tabindex keeps a single stop for the whole body, and the arrows do the rest: <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> walk the column, <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> jump to its ends, and <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> move between columns — mirrored under RTL. While the field is empty no option is selected, and the tab stop and each column start on their first option the limits allow. Selecting a value hands focus to the next column, so a time is set in one pass.

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CTimePicker /&gt;](./api/#ctimepicker)

# React Time Picker Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Time Picker component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CTimePicker

```jsx
import { CTimePicker } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `Clear time` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that clears the value. |
| `ariaDayLabel` | `string` | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | `string` | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | - | Sets the accessible label of the time selection itself, the group its parts sit in. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | `string` | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | `string` | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | `string` | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | `string` | `Toggle time selection` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that opens the time selection. |
| `ariaPopupLabel` | `string` | `Time selection` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the time selection panel, which opens as a `role="dialog"`. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | `string` | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | `string` | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaSelectHoursLabel` | `string` | - | Sets the accessible label of the hours column. |
| `ariaSelectMeridiemLabel` | `string` | - | Sets the accessible label of the AM/PM column. |
| `ariaSelectMinutesLabel` | `string` | - | Sets the accessible label of the minutes column. |
| `ariaSelectSecondsLabel` | `string` | - | Sets the accessible label of the seconds column. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | `string` | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | `string` | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Adds a custom class name to the React Time Picker. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the button that clears the value. |
| `cleanerIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | The artwork of the cleaner button. Defaults to a cross drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| (() => Element \| DocumentFragment \| null) \| null` | - | The element the time selection is rendered into instead of `document.body`. Implies `portal`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `dayPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `defaultShow` | `boolean` | - | The initial open state of an uncontrolled time selection — read once on mount. |
| `defaultTime` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The initial time for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `time` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggles the disabled state. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingLabel` | `string` | - | Renders a floating label inside the field — the component wraps its input in `.form-floating` and the text also becomes the field's accessible name. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode \| ((context: CTimePickerContextValue) => ReactNode)` | - | The content of the panel's footer. Either a node, or a function receiving the picker's context — `setTime`, `now`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`, `isTimeSelectable`, `time` and `disabled`. |
| `format` | `string \| ((locale: string) => DateSection[])` | - | The mask layout. A string is parsed as dayjs/moment or date-fns/luxon format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout, and `undefined` derives the layout from the locale. |
| `hourPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `hours` | `number[] \| ((hour: number) => boolean)` | - | Narrows the hours to a list, or to the ones a predicate accepts. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale; on a 12-hour clock an hour that only one day period allows sets that period when picked. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `locale` | `string` | `navigator.language` | The locale the parts are formatted in. It also decides the 12 or 24-hour split. |
| `maxDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The latest time the user can pick: a time string such as `'17:00'`, or a `Date` of which only the time of day counts. The panel disables the times after it, a time picked in the panel moves back to it, and the field rejects a later time. |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The earliest time the user can pick: a time string such as `'09:30'`, or a `Date` of which only the time of day counts. The panel disables the times before it, a time picked in the panel moves up to it, and the field rejects an earlier time. |
| `minutePlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `minutes` | `boolean \| number[] \| ((minute: number) => boolean)` | `true` | Renders the minutes part, optionally narrowed the way `hours` is. |
| `monthPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | `string` | - | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `onError` | `((error: DateInputError) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the validation state changes; receives `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty. When one change moves both the value and the validation state, it fires after the change callback, so a value set from it replaces the one just reported. |
| `onHide` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the time is hidden. |
| `onShow` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the time is shown. |
| `onShowChange` | `((show: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the time selection requests an open-state change — a dismiss gesture (Escape, a click outside) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle. In controlled mode update `show` yourself, or the time selection stays as it is. |
| `onTimeChange` | `((time: Date \| null, formattedTime?: string \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired once when the value changes, whether from the field, the panel or the context methods; receives the `Date` the field holds, anchored to 1970-01-01 and cut to the units the field shows, or `null` while the field is empty or incomplete, and the formatted value. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the time, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`/`valid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `pickerIcon` | `ReactNode` | `true` | The artwork of the button that opens the time selection. Defaults to a clock drawn on `currentColor`. |
| `portal` | `boolean` | `true` | Renders the time selection through a portal: into the open `<dialog>` the field sits in, otherwise into `document.body`. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | When present, it specifies that the field must be filled out before submitting the form. |
| `secondPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | `boolean \| number[] \| ((second: number) => boolean)` | `true` | Renders the seconds part, optionally narrowed the way `hours` is. |
| `show` | `boolean` | - | Control the open state. When set, the time selection renders what `show` says and dismiss gestures only call `onShowChange` — nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Sizes the control, the way `.form-control-sm` and `.form-control-lg` size a form control. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `time` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The controlled time — a `Date` or a time string like `'14:30'`. Pair it with `onTimeChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultTime` instead. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` on every section and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. A field of a date range whose end is before its start draws no other state. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | - | Controls the visibility of the time selection. |
| `weekPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | `string` | - | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

# React Time Picker Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Time Picker component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/form-control-group/styling/#css-variables) on the element `CTimePicker` renders, so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. Pass them through `style` to restyle one field.

The picker declares its local CSS variables on its panel, `.time-picker-popup`. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is supported too.

```scss
$time-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-time-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-time-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-time-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-col-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-time-picker-col-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-width: 3rem,
    --cui-time-picker-cell-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-time-picker-cell-height: 2rem,
    --cui-time-picker-cell-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-4),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-hover-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-time-picker-cell-selected-hover-bg: oklch(from var(--cui-primary-base) calc(l * var(--cui-theme-hover-lightness)) calc(c * var(--cui-theme-hover-chroma)) h),
  ),
  $time-picker-tokens
);
```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, the combobox, autocomplete and multi select.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

#### How to use CSS variables

Each part of the panel declares its tokens itself, and the panel is rendered into `document.body` unless `portal` is `false`, so a variable set on `CTimePicker` through `style` styles the field but reaches none of them. Set them with a rule on the part that declares them:

```css
.time-picker-popup {
  --cui-popup-bg: #f8f9fa;
  --cui-time-picker-col-border-color: #dee2e6;
}
```

# React Form Layout

> Give your forms some structure—from inline to horizontal to custom grid implementations—with our form layout options.

## Forms

Every group of form fields should reside in a `<CForm>` element. CoreUI provides no default styling for the `<CForm>` element, but there are some powerful browser features that are provided by default.

- New to browser forms? Consider reviewing [the MDN form docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) for an overview and complete list of available attributes.
- `<CButton>`s within a `<CForm>` default to `type="submit"`, so strive to be specific and always include a `type`.
- You can disable every form element within a form with the `disabled` attribute on the `<CForm>`.

Since CoreUI applies `display: block` and `width: 100%` to almost all our form controls, forms will by default stack vertically. Additional classes can be used to vary this layout on a per-form basis.

## Utilities

[Margin utilities](https://coreui.io/react/docs/utilities/margin/) are the easiest way to add some structure to forms. They provide basic grouping of labels, controls, optional form text, and form validation messaging. We recommend sticking to `margin-bottom` utilities, and using a single direction throughout the form for consistency.

## Form grid

More complex forms can be built using our grid classes. Use these for form layouts that require multiple columns, varied widths, and additional alignment options.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutFormGridExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Gutters

By adding [gutter modifier classes](https://coreui.io/react/docs/layout/gutters/), you can have control over the gutter width in as well the inline as block direction.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutGuttersExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow className="g-4">
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

More complex layouts can also be created with the grid system.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCheckbox, CCol, CForm, CFormField, CFormInput, CFormSelect } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutGutters2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4">
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput type="email" id="inputEmail4" label="Email" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword4" label="Password" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormInput id="inputAddress" label="Address" placeholder="1234 Main St" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormInput
          id="inputAddress2"
          label="Address 2"
          placeholder="Apartment, studio, or floor"
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput id="inputCity" label="City" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormSelect id="inputState" label="State">
          <option>Choose...</option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={2}>
        <CFormInput id="inputZip" label="Zip" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="gridCheck" label="Check me out" />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Sign in
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Horizontal form

Create horizontal forms with the grid by adding the `.row` class to form groups and using the `.col-*-*` classes to specify the width of your labels and controls. Be sure to add `.col-form-label` to your `<CFormLabel>`s as well so they're vertically centered with their associated form controls.

At times, you maybe need to use margin or padding utilities to create that perfect alignment you need. For example, we've removed the `padding-top` on our stacked radio inputs label to better align the text baseline.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CRadio,
  CRow,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutHorizontalFormExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputEmail3" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput type="email" id="inputEmail3" />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword3" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Password
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword3" />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <fieldset className="row mb-4">
        <legend className="col-form-label col-sm-2 pt-0">Radios</legend>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormField>
            <CRadio
              name="gridRadios"
              id="gridRadios1"
              value="option1"
              label="First radio"
              defaultChecked
            />
          </CFormField>
          <CFormField>
            <CRadio name="gridRadios" id="gridRadios2" value="option2" label="Second radio" />
          </CFormField>
          <CFormField>
            <CRadio
              name="gridRadios"
              id="gridRadios3"
              value="option3"
              label="Third disabled radio"
              disabled
            />
          </CFormField>
        </CCol>
      </fieldset>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <div className="col-sm-10 offset-sm-2">
          <CFormField>
            <CCheckbox id="gridCheck1" label="Example checkbox" />
          </CFormField>
        </div>
      </CRow>
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
        Sign in
      </CButton>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Horizontal form label sizing

Be sure to use `.col-form-label-sm` or `.col-form-label-lg` to your `<CFormLabel>`s or `<legend>`s to correctly follow the size of `.form-control-lg` and `.form-control-sm`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutHorizontalFormLabelSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="colFormLabelSm" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label col-form-label-sm">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput
            type="email"
            className="form-control form-control-sm"
            id="colFormLabelSm"
            placeholder="col-form-label-sm"
          />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CRow className="mb-4">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="colFormLabel" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput type="email" id="colFormLabel" placeholder="col-form-label" />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CRow>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="colFormLabelLg" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label col-form-label-lg">
          Email
        </CFormLabel>
        <CCol sm={10}>
          <CFormInput
            type="email"
            className="form-control form-control-lg"
            id="colFormLabelLg"
            placeholder="col-form-label-lg"
          />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Column sizing

As shown in the previous examples, our grid system allows you to place any number of `<CCol>`s within a `<CRow>`. They'll split the available width equally between them. You may also pick a subset of your columns to take up more or less space, while the remaining `<CCol>`s equally split the rest, with specific column classes like `<CCol sm={7} >`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutColumnSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow className="g-4">
      <CCol sm={7}>
        <CFormInput placeholder="City" aria-label="City" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm>
        <CFormInput placeholder="State" aria-label="State" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Zip" aria-label="Zip" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Auto-sizing

The example below uses a flexbox utility to vertically center the contents and changes `<CCol>` to `<CCol xs="auto">` so that your columns only take up as much space as needed. Put another way, the column sizes itself based on the contents.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutAutoSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row gy-3 gx-4 align-items-center">
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="autoSizingInput">
          Name
        </CFormLabel>
        <CFormInput id="autoSizingInput" placeholder="Jane Doe" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="autoSizingInputGroup">
          Username
        </CFormLabel>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput id="autoSizingInputGroup" placeholder="Username" />
        </CInputGroup>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="autoSizingSelect">
          Preference
        </CFormLabel>
        <CFormSelect id="autoSizingSelect">
          <option>Choose...</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="autoSizingCheck" label="Remember me" />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

You can then remix that once again with size-specific column classes.

```html
import React from 'react'

  CFormField,
  CFormInput,

  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutAutoSizing2Example = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row gx-4 gy-3 align-items-center">
      <CCol sm={3}>
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="specificSizeInputName">
          Name
        </CFormLabel>
        <CFormInput id="specificSizeInputName" placeholder="Jane Doe" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={3}>
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="specificSizeInputGroupUsername">
          Username
        </CFormLabel>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput id="specificSizeInputGroupUsername" placeholder="Username" />
        </CInputGroup>
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={3}>
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="specificSizeSelect">
          Preference
        </CFormLabel>
        <CFormSelect id="specificSizeSelect">
          <option>Choose...</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="autoSizingCheck2" label="Remember me" />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs="auto">
```

## Inline forms

Use the `<CCol xs="auto">` class to create horizontal layouts. By adding [gutter modifier classes](https://coreui.io/react/docs/layout/gutters/), we will have gutters in horizontal and vertical directions. The `.align-items-center` aligns the form elements to the middle, making the `<CCheckbox>` align properly.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CFormSelect,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutInlineFormsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row row-cols-lg-auto g-4 align-items-center">
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="inlineFormInputGroupUsername">
          Username
        </CFormLabel>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput id="inlineFormInputGroupUsername" placeholder="Username" />
        </CInputGroup>
      </CCol>

      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormLabel className="visually-hidden" htmlFor="inlineFormSelectPref">
          Preference
        </CFormLabel>
        <CFormSelect id="inlineFormSelectPref">
          <option>Choose...</option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>

      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="inlineFormCheck" label="Remember me" />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>

      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

# React Bootstrap Form Layout Component

> Learn how to build responsive and structured form layouts using CoreUI’s React components styled with Bootstrap.

## How to use React Bootstrap Form Layout

Use CoreUI’s React form components together with Bootstrap’s layout system to build flexible, responsive, and well-structured forms.

### Form container

Wrap form elements in the `<CForm>` component to enable default browser behaviors such as validation and submission.

- CoreUI does not apply default styles to `<CForm>`, giving you full control.
- All `<CButton>` components inside `<CForm>` default to `type="submit"` unless specified otherwise.
- You can disable all fields by setting the `disabled` prop on `<CForm>`.

### Form layout using grid

Combine CoreUI form components with the Bootstrap grid system for complex form layouts.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutFormGridExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="Last name" aria-label="Last name" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Gutters

Control spacing between columns using Bootstrap's gutter utilities.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CFormInput, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const LayoutGuttersExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow className="g-4">
      <CCol xs>
        <CFormInput placeholder="First name" aria-label="First name" />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>

```

---

# React Form Validation

> Provide valuable, actionable feedback to your users with HTML5 form validation, via browser default behaviors or custom styles and JavaScript.

## Example

For custom CoreUI form validation messages, add the `validate` and `noValidate` properties to your `<CForm>`. The `validate` property renders the `data-coreui-validate` attribute, which opts in to the `:user-invalid` styling — validation styles appear only after the user interacts with a control or attempts to submit, so required fields don't show up as invalid on page load. Pass `validate="valid"` to also show success styling for valid fields. `noValidate` disables the browser default feedback tooltips and hands their job to `<CForm>`. Try to submit the form below.

When the form is submitted with an invalid control, `<CForm>` stops the submit, so `onSubmit` runs only for a submit that goes through, as with the browser's own validation. It marks every invalid control with `.is-invalid` and `aria-invalid="true"`, and adds the message the stylesheet shows for it to its `aria-describedby` while it stays invalid, so a screen reader reads the error with the field. Then it moves focus to the first invalid control, as the browser does. Under `validate="valid"` the valid controls get `.is-valid`. The state follows the corrections the user makes until the form is reset. A message placed where the stylesheet does not show it for the control can be named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` on the control. A [`CAutocomplete`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/autocomplete/#validation), a [`CMultiSelect`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/multi-select/#validation), a [`CChipInput`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/chip-input/#validation), a [`CCombobox`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/combobox/#validation), a [`COneTimePassword`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation), the [date and time fields](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-input/#validation) and the [date](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-picker/#validation), [time](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/time-picker/#validation) and [range](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-range-picker/#validation) pickers show the state on their frame and on the control that takes the focus, and `<CForm>` leaves the field that carries their value to them. So does a [`CRangeSlider`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/range-slider/#validation), with its handles, and a [`CRating`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/rating/#validation), with its radios.

Custom feedback styles apply custom colors, borders and focus styles to communicate feedback.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate="valid">
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Mark"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationCustom01"
          label="First name"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Otto"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationCustom02"
          label="Last name"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationCustomUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CFormField>
          <CInputGroup>
            <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
            <CFormInput
              type="text"
              aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend"
              id="validationCustomUsername"
              required
            />
          </CInputGroup>
          <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid city."
          id="validationCustom03"
          label="City"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Please select a valid state."
          id="validationCustom04"
          label="State"
          required
        >
          <option disabled>Choose...</option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid zip."
          id="validationCustom05"
          label="Zip"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="invalidCheck" label="Agree to terms and conditions" required />
          <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Handling the result yourself

`onValidate` is called first, with `isValid` telling whether every control passed. A validity it sets with `setCustomValidity()`, for example when two passwords differ, counts for the rest of the validation. A handler that moves focus to an element already on the page keeps it there; `<CForm>` still marks the controls and stops an invalid submit. A handler that calls `preventDefault()` takes the whole result over: `<CForm>` then neither stops the submit, nor marks the controls, nor moves focus, and `onSubmit` runs, so stop an invalid submit there yourself. Keep `event.isValid` for that rather than calling `checkValidity()`: the call reports every invalid control again, and the components that follow those reports, such as `CMultiSelect` or the date fields, then show their error. Do that for an error summary that renders only after `onValidate`, and move focus to it once it is rendered. A submit from a button with `formNoValidate` is not validated.

```jsx
const isValid = useRef(true)

<CForm
  validate
  noValidate
  onValidate={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    isValid.current = event.isValid
    showErrorSummary(event.form, event.isValid)
  }}
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    if (!isValid.current) {
      event.preventDefault()
    }
  }}
>
  {/* controls */}
</CForm>
```
