## Custom validation

In case you require custom or server-side validation, set the state yourself with the `validationState` property: `"valid"` or `"invalid"` renders the matching `is-*` class, and `"invalid"` also sets `aria-invalid` on the control. Any custom state you add to the `$form-validation-states` Sass map — `"warning"`, say — is accepted the same way. `"invalid"` also blocks the submit until it is cleared, with the text of the control's invalid feedback as the message the browser shows. A disabled control is not blocked, nor is a read-only text field, since the browser leaves them out of the validation. A control the user cannot reach, such as one in a hidden tab or a collapsed section, still blocks while the browser has nowhere to show its message, so clear the state of a field you hide. A state you give is a verdict on the value it was given for, so when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, the control calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)`; pass your state setter there to drop the state and let the browser's own validation show again, as the example below does. Only the radio the user checks hears the change, so give a radio group's state to every radio in it. The fields that build their own markup, such as [`CAutocomplete`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/autocomplete/#validation), [`CMultiSelect`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/multi-select/#validation), [`CChipInput`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/chip-input/#validation), [`CCombobox`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/combobox/#validation), [`COneTimePassword`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation), the date and time fields and the pickers, work the same way and describe the details on their pages.

Pair it with the `feedback` property: the message is rendered only while a state is set, styled after that state, and added to the control's `aria-describedby` after any `id` you pass there. `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` belong to the client-side mode above, where the browser decides the state and the stylesheet reveals the matching message. The control watches the same `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` states the stylesheet reveals the messages by, so it is described by `feedbackInvalid` while the invalid message shows and by `feedbackValid` while the valid one does. A field the form reports invalid through `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` counts as reported until the form is reset, even before the user touches it: whenever its value is invalid it gets `aria-invalid` and is described by `feedbackInvalid`, just as after the user has edited it. The [Stepper](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/stepper/#form-validation) relies on this when a step fails, so call `checkValidity()` only when the page shows the errors. The date and time fields and the pickers follow their own verdict the same way; the browser judges them by whether a `required` one holds a date they accept, and blocks them while a state you give is `"invalid"`. A `validationState` you set takes precedence over the state the browser or the field reports.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import {
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationCustomExample = () => {
  const [states, setStates] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({
    city: 'invalid',
    email: 'valid',
    repeatEmail: 'valid',
    state: 'invalid',
    terms: 'invalid',
    username: 'invalid',
    zip: 'invalid',
  })
  const clear = (field: string) => () => setStates((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field]: undefined }))

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4">
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer01"
          label="Email"
          feedback="Looks good!"
          defaultValue="name@surname.com"
          onValidationStateChange={clear('email')}
          validationState={states.email}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer02"
          label="Repeat email"
          feedback="Looks good!"
          defaultValue="name@surname.com"
          onValidationStateChange={clear('repeatEmail')}
          validationState={states.repeatEmail}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationServerUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CFormField>
          <CInputGroup>
            <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend03">@</CInputGroupText>
            <CFormInput
              type="text"
              id="validationServerUsername"
              defaultValue=""
              aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend03 validationServerUsernameFeedback"
              onValidationStateChange={clear('username')}
              validationState={states.username}
              required
            />
          </CInputGroup>
          <CFormFeedback id="validationServerUsernameFeedback" validationState="invalid">
            Please choose a username.
          </CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer03"
          label="City"
          feedback="Please provide a valid city."
          onValidationStateChange={clear('city')}
          validationState={states.city}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormSelect
          id="validationServer04"
          label="State"
          feedback="Please select a valid state."
          defaultValue=""
          onValidationStateChange={clear('state')}
          validationState={states.state}
        >
          <option disabled value="">
            Choose...
          </option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer05"
          label="zip"
          feedback="Please provide a valid zip."
          onValidationStateChange={clear('zip')}
          validationState={states.zip}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox
            id="invalidCheck"
            label="Agree to terms and conditions"
            onValidationStateChange={clear('terms')}
            validationState={states.terms}
            required
          />
          <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Form components

[`CMultiSelect`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/multi-select/#validation), [`CChipInput`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/chip-input/#validation), [`CCombobox`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/combobox/#validation), [`COneTimePassword`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation), [`CDateInput`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/date-input/#validation), [`CTimeInput`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/time-input/#validation) and the pickers built on them keep their value in a native field laid invisibly over the component. That field carries the `name`, takes part in the browser's validation and hands the focus to the component when the browser points at it. [`CAutocomplete`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/autocomplete/#validation) validates its own input, [`CRangeSlider`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/range-slider/#validation) its handles, and [`CRating`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/rating/#validation) its radios. Each of these components shows one validation state, on its frame and on what takes the focus, and decides it in this order:

1. its own error, such as a date outside `minDate` and `maxDate` or an incomplete code;
2. the `validationState` you give it;
3. the state a validation reports for its field: a submit, `<CForm>`, the [Stepper](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/stepper/#form-validation), or your own `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` call;
4. `:user-invalid` or `:user-valid` of its field, in a `<CForm validate>`.

`CAutocomplete`, `CMultiSelect`, `COneTimePassword` and the pickers also take the deprecated `invalid` and `valid` props. Pass the message with the state, through `feedback` or `feedbackInvalid`, so it is linked to the field when the state shows.

A given `'invalid'` blocks the submit, with the text of the component's invalid feedback as the message the browser shows, or `Invalid value.` when it has none. `'valid'` and a custom state such as `'warning'` do not block, and neither does a disabled component. A given `'valid'` shows over a reported error, but the browser's own constraints still apply, so an empty `required` field keeps blocking. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for: when the user changes the value, such as with a pick, a removed chip, the cleaner, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or a native form reset, the component calls `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before it reports the change. Pass your state setter there to drop the state; without it, the state stays until you clear it. A change of the value from props keeps it.

You can bring your own validation in three ways:

- **Your own rules next to the browser's.** Give `validationState` as above, or call `setCustomValidity()` on the field that carries the value, which you reach through `form.elements` by its name. The component leaves a validity you set as it is.
- **Taking the whole result over.** Call `preventDefault()` in `onValidate` and keep `event.isValid`, as [handling the result yourself](#handling-the-result-yourself) shows. No field is reported then, so the components show only `:user-invalid` or `:user-valid` of their field, as a plain field in the same form does after a submit attempt.
- **Showing the errors.** A `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()` call reports every invalid field and each component marks itself, so make that call only when the page shows the errors.

## Supported elements

Validation styles are available for the following form controls and components:

- `<CCheckbox>`
- `<CFormInput>`
- `<CFormSelect>`
- `<CFormTextarea>`
- `<CRadio>`
- `<CSwitch>`

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormSelect,
  CFormTextarea,
  CRadio,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationSupportedElementsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CFormTextarea
          feedbackInvalid="Please enter a message in the textarea."
          id="validationTextarea"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Textarea"
          placeholder="Required example textarea"
          required
        ></CFormTextarea>
      </div>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          id="validationFormCheck1"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Check this checkbox"
          required
        />
        <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">Example invalid feedback text</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CRadio
          name="radio-stacked"
          id="validationFormCheck2"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Check this checkbox"
          required
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CRadio
          name="radio-stacked"
          id="validationFormCheck3"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Or toggle this other radio"
          required
        />
        <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">More example invalid feedback text</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CFormSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Example invalid select feedback"
          aria-label="select example"
          validationState="invalid"
          required
        >
          <option selected value="">
            Open this select menu
          </option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </div>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput
          type="file"
          id="validationTextarea"
          feedbackInvalid="Example invalid form file feedback"
          aria-label="file example"
          validationState="invalid"
          required
        />
      </div>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CButton type="submit" theme="primary" disabled>
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

## Tooltips

If your form layout allows it, you can swap the text for the tooltip to display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. Be sure to have a parent with `position: relative` on it for tooltip positioning. In the example below, our column classes have this already, but your project may require an alternative setup.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationTooltipsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate="valid">
      <CCol md={4} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Mark"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationTooltip01"
          label="First name"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Otto"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationTooltip02"
          label="Last name"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4} className="position-relative">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationTooltipUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CFormField>
          <CInputGroup>
            <CInputGroupText id="validationTooltipUsernamePrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
            <CFormInput
              type="text"
              aria-describedby="validationTooltipUsernamePrepend"
              id="validationTooltipUsername"
              required
            />
          </CInputGroup>
          <CFormFeedback tooltip validationState="invalid">
            Please choose a username.
          </CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid city."
          id="validationTooltip03"
          label="City"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3} className="position-relative">
        <CFormSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Please select a valid state."
          id="validationTooltip04"
          label="State"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        >
          <option selected disabled value="">
            Choose...
          </option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid zip."
          id="validationTooltip05"
          label="Zip"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12} className="position-relative">
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

# React Form Validation Styling

> Learn how to customize the React form validation with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

### CSS variables

CoreUI for React components use local CSS variables for validation for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

A validation state names a theme colour and every value is a slot of it, so the
state follows that colour in both colour modes without a second set of variables.

### Sass maps

This is the validation Sass map from `scss/mixins/_form-validation.scss`. Override or extend this to generate different or additional states.

```scss
$form-validation-states: (
  "valid": (
    "theme": "success",
  ),
  "invalid": (
    "theme": "danger",
  )
) !default;
```

Maps of `$form-validation-states` can contain three optional parameters to override tooltips and focus styles.

### Sass mixins

Two mixins are combined together, through our [loop](#sass-loops), to generate our form validation feedback styles.

```scss
@mixin form-validation-state-selector($state) {
  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}:user-invalid,
    #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}.is-#{$state} {
      @content;
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}:user-valid,
    #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}.is-#{$state} {
      @content;
    }
  } @else {
    #{if(sass(&): "&"; else: "")}.is-#{$state} {
      @content;
    }
  }
}
```

```scss
@mixin form-validation-state(
  $state,
  $theme,
  $color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-fg),
  $tooltip-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-contrast),
  $focus-ring-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-focus-ring),
  $border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-fg)
) {
  $without-error: ":not(.is-invalid, :has(.is-invalid, > :user-invalid, > .form-floating > :user-invalid))";
  $form-otp-state: ".form-otp:is(.is-#{$state}, :has(.is-#{$state}))";
  $range-without-error: "";

  @if $state != "invalid" {
    $form-otp-state: "#{$form-otp-state}#{$without-error}";
    $range-without-error: ":not(.is-invalid)";
  }

  .#{$state}-feedback {
    @include tokens($form-feedback-tokens);

    display: none;
    width: 100%;
    margin-top: var(--cui-form-feedback-margin-top);
    font-size: var(--cui-form-feedback-font-size);
    font-style: var(--cui-form-feedback-font-style, inherit);
    color: $color;
  }

  // More specific to override base tooltip styles
  .tooltip.#{$state}-tooltip,
  .#{$state}-tooltip {
    @include tokens($form-feedback-tokens);

    position: absolute;
    top: 100%;
    z-index: 5;
    display: none;
    max-width: 100%; // Contain to parent when possible
    padding: var(--cui-tooltip-padding-y, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-padding-y)) var(--cui-tooltip-padding-x, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-padding-x));
    margin-top: .1rem;
    font-size: var(--cui-tooltip-font-size, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-font-size));
    line-height: var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-line-height, inherit);
    color: $tooltip-color;
    background-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
    opacity: 1;
    @include border-radius(var(--cui-tooltip-border-radius, var(--cui-form-feedback-tooltip-border-radius)));
  }

  // Generic sibling feedback display — works for .form-control, .form-range,
  // and any element where feedback is a direct sibling.
  @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip {
      display: block;
    }
  }

  // Form control
  .form-control {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-control-border-color: #{$border-color};
      --cui-control-focus-border-color: #{$border-color};

      &:focus,
      &.form-date-time:focus-within {
        &:not(.form-control-group .form-control) {
          @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
        }
      }
    }
  }

  // stylelint-disable selector-no-qualifying-type
  select.form-control,
  .form-control-caret,
  .form-select {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-control-border-color: #{$border-color};
      --cui-control-focus-border-color: #{$border-color};

      &:focus:not(.form-control-group .form-control) {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }
  // stylelint-enable selector-no-qualifying-type

  // Checkbox — control-level styling (border, checked bg, focus ring).
  .check {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-check-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid #{$border-color};
      --cui-check-checked-bg: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
      --cui-check-checked-border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);

      &:checked:not(:indeterminate) {
        background-color: var(--cui-check-checked-bg);
        border-color: var(--cui-check-checked-border-color);
      }

      &:focus-visible {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }

  // Checkbox — label color and feedback display via .form-field:has().
  .form-field:has(.check.is-#{$state}) {
    label { color: $color; }

    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.check:user-invalid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:has(.check:user-valid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  // Radio — control-level styling.
  .radio {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-radio-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid #{$border-color};
      --cui-radio-checked-bg: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
      --cui-radio-checked-border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);

      &:checked {
        background-color: var(--cui-radio-checked-bg);
        border-color: var(--cui-radio-checked-border-color);
      }

      &:focus-visible {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }

  // Radio — label color and feedback display via .form-field:has().
  .form-field:has(.radio.is-#{$state}) {
    label { color: $color; }

    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.radio:user-invalid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:has(.radio:user-valid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  // Switch — control-level styling.
  .switch {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      --cui-switch-border-color: #{$border-color};
      --cui-switch-checked-bg: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);
      --cui-switch-checked-border-color: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg);

      &:checked {
        background-color: var(--cui-switch-checked-bg);
        border-color: var(--cui-switch-checked-border-color);
      }

      &:focus-visible {
        @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
      }
    }
  }

  // Switch — label color and feedback display via .form-field:has().
  .form-field:has(.switch.is-#{$state}) {
    label { color: $color; }

    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.switch:user-invalid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:has(.switch:user-valid) {
      label { color: $color; }

      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  // The state has to reach the group: a custom property set on the control
  // inside it only inherits downwards, never back up to the frame.
  .form-control-group.is-#{$state},
  .is-#{$state} > .form-control-group,
  .form-control-group:has(> .form-control.is-#{$state}),
  .form-control-group:has(> .form-floating > .form-control.is-#{$state}) {
    @include form-control-group-validation-state($color, $border-color, $focus-ring-color);
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(> .form-control:user-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(> .form-floating > .form-control:user-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(> select:user-invalid) {
      @include form-control-group-validation-state($color, $border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-control:user-valid),
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-floating > .form-control:user-valid),
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> select:user-valid) {
      @include form-control-group-validation-state($color, $border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }
  }

  .form-control-group:where(.is-#{$state}, :has(> .is-#{$state}), :has(> .form-floating > .is-#{$state})) {
    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  .form-field:where(:has(.form-control-group.is-#{$state}, .form-control-group > .is-#{$state}, .form-control-group > .form-floating > .is-#{$state})) {
    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] {
      .form-control-group:has(> :user-invalid),
      .form-control-group:has(> .form-floating > :user-invalid) {
        ~ .invalid-feedback,
        ~ .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }

      .form-field:has(.form-control-group > :user-invalid),
      .form-field:has(.form-control-group > .form-floating > :user-invalid) {
        .invalid-feedback,
        .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] {
      .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> .form-floating > .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-control-group#{$without-error}:has(> select:user-valid) {
        ~ .valid-feedback,
        ~ .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }

      .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.form-control-group > .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.form-control-group > .form-floating > .form-control:user-valid),
      .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.form-control-group > select:user-valid) {
        .valid-feedback,
        .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
      }
    }

    .form-control-group.is-invalid,
    .form-control-group:has(.is-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-control-group:has(:user-invalid) {
      ~ .valid-feedback,
      ~ .valid-tooltip { display: none; }
    }

    .form-field:has(.form-control-group.is-invalid),
    .form-field:has(.form-control-group .is-invalid),
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.form-control-group :user-invalid) {
      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: none; }
    }
  }

  // Range — the validation class lives on .form-range-input, while feedback sits outside
  // the .form-range wrapper, so we use :has() to toggle it.
  .form-range-input#{$range-without-error},
  input.form-range#{$range-without-error} {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      &::-webkit-slider-thumb { background: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg); }
      &::-moz-range-thumb { background: var(--cui-#{$theme}-bg); }

      &:focus-visible {
        &::-webkit-slider-thumb {
          @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
        }
        &::-moz-range-thumb {
          @include focus-ring(true, $color: $focus-ring-color);
        }
      }
    }
  }

  .form-range:has(.form-range-input.is-#{$state}) {
    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  .rating.is-#{$state} .rating-item {
    --cui-theme-focus-ring: #{$focus-ring-color};
  }

  // Input group — feedback lives outside the input-group in the parent
  // .form-field, so we use :has() to toggle display.
  .form-field:where(:has(.input-group .form-control.is-#{$state}, .input-group .form-select.is-#{$state})) {
    .#{$state}-feedback,
    .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-field:has(.input-group .form-control:user-invalid, .input-group .form-select:user-invalid) {
      .invalid-feedback,
      .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-field:not(:has(.is-invalid, :user-invalid)):has(.input-group .form-control:user-valid, .input-group .form-select:user-valid) {
      .valid-feedback,
      .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }

  .input-group {
    > .autocomplete:focus-within,
    > .date-picker:focus-within,
    > .time-picker:focus-within,
    > .form-control-group:focus-within,
    > .multi-select:focus-within,
    > .form-control:focus,
    > .form-select:focus,
    > .form-floating:focus-within {
      @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
        @if $state == "valid" {
          z-index: 3;
        } @else if $state == "invalid" {
          z-index: 4;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  .form-otp-control {
    @include form-validation-state-selector($state) {
      @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }
  }

  #{$form-otp-state} {
    .form-otp-control {
      @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
    }

    ~ .#{$state}-feedback,
    ~ .#{$state}-tooltip { display: block; }
  }

  @if $state == "invalid" {
    [data-coreui-validate] .form-otp:has(:user-invalid) {
      .form-otp-control {
        @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
      }

      ~ .invalid-feedback,
      ~ .invalid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  } @else if $state == "valid" {
    [data-coreui-validate~="valid"] .form-otp#{$without-error}:not(:has(:user-invalid)):has(> input:not(.form-otp-control):user-valid) {
      .form-otp-control {
        @include form-otp-control-validation-state($border-color, $focus-ring-color);
      }

      ~ .valid-feedback,
      ~ .valid-tooltip { display: block; }
    }
  }
}
```

### Sass loops

Used to iterate over `$form-validation-states` map values to generate our validation styles. Any modifications to the above Sass map will be reflected in your compiled CSS via this loop.

```scss
@each $state, $data in $form-validation-states {
  @include form-validation-state($state, $data...);
}
```

# React Bootstrap Form Validation

> Learn how to use Bootstrap-style validation in React forms using CoreUI components. Show validation messages, use custom styles, and support native browser behavior.

## How to use React Bootstrap Form Validation

React Bootstrap validation lets you provide custom or native HTML5 feedback styles for form controls. CoreUI components support both approaches for a better user experience.

### Custom validation styles

Disable the browser’s native validation UI with the `noValidate` prop on `<CForm>`, and use the `validate` prop to opt in to the `:user-invalid` styling — feedback appears after the user interacts with a control or attempts to submit. Pass `validate="valid"` to also show success styling. With both props, `<CForm>` stops an invalid submit, marks the invalid controls, links their messages and moves focus to the first, as described on the [validation page](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/validation/). Try submitting the form below to see it in action.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate="valid">
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Mark"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationCustom01"
          label="First name"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Otto"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationCustom02"
          label="Last name"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationCustomUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CFormField>
          <CInputGroup>
            <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
            <CFormInput
              type="text"
              aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend"
              id="validationCustomUsername"
              required
            />
          </CInputGroup>
          <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid city."
          id="validationCustom03"
          label="City"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Please select a valid state."
          id="validationCustom04"
          label="State"
          required
        >
          <option disabled>Choose...</option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid zip."
          id="validationCustom05"
          label="Zip"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="invalidCheck" label="Agree to terms and conditions" required />
          <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Browser default behavior

If you prefer to rely on native browser validation, skip `noValidate` and `validate`. Submit the form and let the browser handle feedback based on built-in rules.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationBrowserDefaultsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4">
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationDefault01"
          label="First name"
          defaultValue="Mark"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationDefault02"
          label="Last name"
          defaultValue="Otto"
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationDefaultUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CInputGroup>
          <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend02">@</CInputGroupText>
          <CFormInput
            type="text"
            id="validationDefaultUsername"
            defaultValue=""
            aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend02"
            required
          />
        </CInputGroup>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput type="text" id="validationDefault03" label="City" required />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormSelect id="validationDefault04" label="State">
          <option disabled>Choose...</option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormInput type="text" id="validationDefault05" label="Zip" required />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox id="invalidCheck" label="Agree to terms and conditions" required />
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Manual validation

Use the `validationState` prop directly on components like `<CFormInput>` to apply validation styles manually, which is useful for server-side validation or complex form logic. `"invalid"` also blocks the submit until it is cleared; pass your state setter to `onValidationStateChange` to drop it when the user changes the value, as the example below does.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import {
  CCheckbox,
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationCustomExample = () => {
  const [states, setStates] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({
    city: 'invalid',
    email: 'valid',
    repeatEmail: 'valid',
    state: 'invalid',
    terms: 'invalid',
    username: 'invalid',
    zip: 'invalid',
  })
  const clear = (field: string) => () => setStates((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field]: undefined }))

  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4">
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer01"
          label="Email"
          feedback="Looks good!"
          defaultValue="name@surname.com"
          onValidationStateChange={clear('email')}
          validationState={states.email}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer02"
          label="Repeat email"
          feedback="Looks good!"
          defaultValue="name@surname.com"
          onValidationStateChange={clear('repeatEmail')}
          validationState={states.repeatEmail}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4}>
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationServerUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CFormField>
          <CInputGroup>
            <CInputGroupText id="inputGroupPrepend03">@</CInputGroupText>
            <CFormInput
              type="text"
              id="validationServerUsername"
              defaultValue=""
              aria-describedby="inputGroupPrepend03 validationServerUsernameFeedback"
              onValidationStateChange={clear('username')}
              validationState={states.username}
              required
            />
          </CInputGroup>
          <CFormFeedback id="validationServerUsernameFeedback" validationState="invalid">
            Please choose a username.
          </CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer03"
          label="City"
          feedback="Please provide a valid city."
          onValidationStateChange={clear('city')}
          validationState={states.city}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormSelect
          id="validationServer04"
          label="State"
          feedback="Please select a valid state."
          defaultValue=""
          onValidationStateChange={clear('state')}
          validationState={states.state}
        >
          <option disabled value="">
            Choose...
          </option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="validationServer05"
          label="zip"
          feedback="Please provide a valid zip."
          onValidationStateChange={clear('zip')}
          validationState={states.zip}
          required
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CFormField>
          <CCheckbox
            id="invalidCheck"
            label="Agree to terms and conditions"
            onValidationStateChange={clear('terms')}
            validationState={states.terms}
            required
          />
          <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">You must agree before submitting.</CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12}>
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Supported components

These CoreUI components support Bootstrap validation classes:

- `<CCheckbox>`
- `<CFormInput>`
- `<CFormSelect>`
- `<CFormTextarea>`
- `<CRadio>`
- `<CSwitch>`

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CButton,
  CCheckbox,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormSelect,
  CFormTextarea,
  CRadio,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationSupportedElementsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CFormTextarea
          feedbackInvalid="Please enter a message in the textarea."
          id="validationTextarea"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Textarea"
          placeholder="Required example textarea"
          required
        ></CFormTextarea>
      </div>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CCheckbox
          id="validationFormCheck1"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Check this checkbox"
          required
        />
        <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">Example invalid feedback text</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField>
        <CRadio
          name="radio-stacked"
          id="validationFormCheck2"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Check this checkbox"
          required
        />
      </CFormField>
      <CFormField className="mb-4">
        <CRadio
          name="radio-stacked"
          id="validationFormCheck3"
          validationState="invalid"
          label="Or toggle this other radio"
          required
        />
        <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">More example invalid feedback text</CFormFeedback>
      </CFormField>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CFormSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Example invalid select feedback"
          aria-label="select example"
          validationState="invalid"
          required
        >
          <option selected value="">
            Open this select menu
          </option>
          <option value="1">One</option>
          <option value="2">Two</option>
          <option value="3">Three</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </div>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CFormInput
          type="file"
          id="validationTextarea"
          feedbackInvalid="Example invalid form file feedback"
          aria-label="file example"
          validationState="invalid"
          required
        />
      </div>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <CButton type="submit" theme="primary" disabled>
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </div>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

### Tooltip feedback

For compact layouts, validation messages can appear as tooltips. Make sure the parent container has `position: relative` to position tooltips correctly.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CCol,
  CButton,
  CForm,
  CFormFeedback,
  CFormField,
  CFormInput,
  CFormLabel,
  CInputGroup,
  CInputGroupText,
  CFormSelect,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const ValidationTooltipsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CForm className="row g-4" noValidate validate="valid">
      <CCol md={4} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Mark"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationTooltip01"
          label="First name"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          defaultValue="Otto"
          feedbackValid="Looks good!"
          id="validationTooltip02"
          label="Last name"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={4} className="position-relative">
        <CFormLabel htmlFor="validationTooltipUsername">Username</CFormLabel>
        <CFormField>
          <CInputGroup>
            <CInputGroupText id="validationTooltipUsernamePrepend">@</CInputGroupText>
            <CFormInput
              type="text"
              aria-describedby="validationTooltipUsernamePrepend"
              id="validationTooltipUsername"
              required
            />
          </CInputGroup>
          <CFormFeedback tooltip validationState="invalid">
            Please choose a username.
          </CFormFeedback>
        </CFormField>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={6} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid city."
          id="validationTooltip03"
          label="City"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3} className="position-relative">
        <CFormSelect
          feedbackInvalid="Please select a valid state."
          id="validationTooltip04"
          label="State"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        >
          <option selected disabled value="">
            Choose...
          </option>
          <option>...</option>
        </CFormSelect>
      </CCol>
      <CCol md={3} className="position-relative">
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          feedbackInvalid="Please provide a valid zip."
          id="validationTooltip05"
          label="Zip"
          required
          tooltipFeedback
        />
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs={12} className="position-relative">
        <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">
          Submit form
        </CButton>
      </CCol>
    </CForm>
  )
}
```

# React Accordion Component

> Build vertically collapsing accordions in combination with our React Accordion component.

## How it works

The accordion is built on the native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements, so it works without JavaScript. The browser handles opening, closing, keyboard interaction and the disclosure semantics announced by screen readers.

- `<CAccordionItem>` renders the `<details>` element.
- `<CAccordionHeader>` renders its `<summary>`.
- `<CAccordionBody>` holds the panel content.

Set `defaultOpenItemKeys` on `<CAccordion>` to open items at mount and let the accordion manage them from there — it takes a single key as well as an array. To drive the open items from your own state instead, pass `openItemKeys` together with `onChange`. Without `alwaysOpen` every item shares a `name`, which is what makes the browser close the others when one opens.

> This component's animation effect relies on the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query. For more information, refer to the [reduced motion section of our accessibility documentation](https://coreui.io/react/docs/accessibility/reduced-motion/).

Click the accordions below to expand/collapse the accordion content.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={2}>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the first item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the second item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={3}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #3</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the third item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Theme variants

_Added in 6.0.0._

An open item is a neutral surface on its own. Set [`theme`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) to tint it — closed items are untouched either way, so the theme marks what is currently expanded rather than recoloring the whole control.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionVariantsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1} theme="success">
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          The open item takes its text, background and border from the theme color.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Closed items are untouched, so the tint reads as a state and not as decoration.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={3}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #3</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Any of the theme colors works: <code>primary</code>, <code>danger</code>, and so on.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Nested

Put a whole `<CAccordion>` inside a `<CAccordionBody>` to nest one. Each accordion generates its own `name`, so the outer and inner groups open and close independently — `name` groups the `<details>` elements across the whole document, not per container.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionNestedExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1}>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This item contains a nested accordion.</strong>
          <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1} className="mt-4">
            <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
              <CAccordionHeader>Nested Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
              <CAccordionBody>Body of the first nested item.</CAccordionBody>
            </CAccordionItem>
            <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
              <CAccordionHeader>Nested Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
              <CAccordionBody>Body of the second nested item.</CAccordionBody>
            </CAccordionItem>
          </CAccordion>
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Opening this closes the item above, and the nested accordion goes with it.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Small

Add `size="sm"` for a compact accordion — tighter padding, a smaller radius and the small font size, all through the component's own tokens.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionSmallExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion size="sm">
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>A compact accordion body for denser layouts.</CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>The same markup, just the small variant&#39;s tokens.</CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Flush

Add `flush` to remove the default `background-color`, some borders, and some rounded corners to render accordions edge-to-edge with their parent container.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionFlushExample = () => {

        <CAccordionBody>

          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the second item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default

      <CAccordionItem itemKey={3}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #3</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the third item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Gap

Add `gap` to space the items apart. Each one keeps its full border radius, so the accordion reads as a stack of cards rather than one block. The gap sits on the accordion, not on the panel, so opening and closing still animates only the panel's height.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const AccordionGapExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion gap defaultOpenItemKeys={1}>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Placeholder content for this accordion, which is intended to demonstrate the{' '}
          <code>gap</code> prop. Each item keeps a full border radius while the panel opens and
          closes.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Placeholder content for this accordion, which is intended to demonstrate the{' '}
          <code>gap</code> prop. Each item keeps a full border radius while the panel opens and
          closes.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={3}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #3</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Placeholder content for this accordion, which is intended to demonstrate the{' '}
          <code>gap</code> prop. Each item keeps a full border radius while the panel opens and
          closes.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

Set the distance with `--cui-accordion-gap`, which defaults to `--cui-spacer-3`.

## Always open

Add `alwaysOpen` property to make React accordion items stay open when another item is opened.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionAlwaysOpenExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion alwaysOpen defaultOpenItemKeys={2}>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the first item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the second item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={3}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #3</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          <strong>This is the second item&#39;s accordion body.</strong> It is hidden by default,
          until the collapse plugin adds the appropriate classes that we use to style each element.
          These classes control the overall appearance, as well as the showing and hiding via CSS
          transitions. You can modify any of this with custom CSS or overriding our default
          variables. It&#39;s also worth noting that just about any HTML can go within the{' '}
          <code>.accordion-body</code>, though the transition does limit overflow.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Expand & collapse all

_Added in 6.0.0._

`openItemKeys` takes an array, so opening or closing everything is one piece of state. A single item can also be driven on its own with `open` on `<CAccordionItem>`. It is the controlled form: the accordion renders exactly what you pass and reports every change through `onChange`, so remember to feed it back. Pair it with `alwaysOpen` — the HTML Standard forbids leaving more than one open item in a `name` group, so an exclusive accordion cannot show them all.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import {
  CAccordion,
  CAccordionBody,
  CAccordionHeader,
  CAccordionItem,
  CButton,
} from '@coreui/react'

const items = [1, 2, 3]

export const AccordionToggleAllExample = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<(number | string)[]>([1])

  return (
    <>
      <div className="hstack gap-3 mb-4">
        <CButton theme="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(items)}>
          Expand all
        </CButton>
        <CButton theme="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen([])}>
          Collapse all
        </CButton>
      </div>
      <CAccordion openItemKeys={open} onChange={setOpen} alwaysOpen>
        {items.map((key) => (
          <CAccordionItem key={key} itemKey={key}>
            <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #{key}</CAccordionHeader>
            <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for accordion item #{key}.</CAccordionBody>
          </CAccordionItem>
        ))}
      </CAccordion>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Findable when collapsed

Nothing to enable here: a closed `<details>` keeps its content searchable, and the browser expands the item on a find-in-page match — the capability [`<CCollapse>` opts into](../collapse/#findable-when-collapsed) with `hiddenUntilFound` is built into the disclosure element the accordion stands on.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionFindableExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1}>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>This item starts open. The interesting one is below it.</CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>
          Search this page for <strong>axolotl</strong> with your browser&apos;s find-in-page and
          this closed item opens on its own.
        </CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

Everything composes with it: in an exclusive accordion the browser closes the previously open item as it reveals the match, `onShown` fires the way it does for a click, and `<summary>` exposes the new state to assistive technology on its own. In browsers that do not search closed disclosure content the item simply is not found while collapsed.

## Headings

`CAccordionHeader` renders a `<summary>`, which accepts heading content — so put a heading inside it to keep the sections reachable by heading navigation. Pick the level that fits the page's outline; nothing in the component depends on it.

The heading takes the header's own typography rather than its default size, weight and margins, so adding one does not change how the accordion looks.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionHeadingsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1}>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
        <CAccordionHeader>
          <h3>Accordion Item #1</h3>
        </CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for the first accordion item.</CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
      <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
        <CAccordionHeader>
          <h3>Accordion Item #2</h3>
        </CAccordionHeader>
        <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for the second accordion item.</CAccordionBody>
      </CAccordionItem>
    </CAccordion>
  )
}
```

## Custom icon

_Added in 6.0.0._

Put an element carrying `accordion-icon` inside the header to give it your own icon. The header stops drawing its default chevron as soon as it finds one, so the two never double up. Sizing and placement stay with the class, so an icon component and a glyph from an icon font both fit the same box.

The rotation does not: `--cui-accordion-header-icon-transform` is a half turn, which suits the built-in chevron because it points down and ends up pointing up. Hand it a shape with a different resting direction and the half turn stops making sense — a right-pointing chevron needs a quarter turn to end up pointing down.

A second element marked `accordion-icon-active` is shown in place of the first while the item is open — which is what a plus/minus accordion needs, where the icon is swapped rather than turned. Rotation is dropped on its own there, because supplying a second shape already says the icon is not meant to rotate.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilChevronRight, cilMinus, cilPlus } from '@coreui/icons'

const rightChevron = {
  '--cui-accordion-header-icon-transform': 'rotate(90deg)',
} as React.CSSProperties

export const AccordionCustomIconExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1} className="mb-4" style={rightChevron}>
        <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
          <CAccordionHeader>
            Accordion Item #1
            <CIcon icon={cilChevronRight} className="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true" />
          </CAccordionHeader>
          <CAccordionBody>
            The icon is an element in the summary, so any icon set works. The rotation has to suit
            the shape: this chevron points right when closed, so it turns a quarter turn to point
            down, not the half turn the built-in one takes.
          </CAccordionBody>
        </CAccordionItem>
        <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
          <CAccordionHeader>
            Accordion Item #2
            <CIcon icon={cilChevronRight} className="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true" />
          </CAccordionHeader>
          <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for the second accordion item.</CAccordionBody>
        </CAccordionItem>
      </CAccordion>

      <CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1}>
        <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
          <CAccordionHeader>
            Accordion Item #1
            <CIcon icon={cilPlus} className="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true" />
            <CIcon
              icon={cilMinus}
              className="accordion-icon accordion-icon-active"
              aria-hidden="true"
            />
          </CAccordionHeader>
          <CAccordionBody>
            A second element marked <code>accordion-icon-active</code> is swapped in while the item
            is open, which is what a plus/minus accordion needs. No rotation is involved, so nothing
            has to be tuned.
          </CAccordionBody>
        </CAccordionItem>
        <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
          <CAccordionHeader>
            Accordion Item #2
            <CIcon icon={cilPlus} className="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true" />
            <CIcon
              icon={cilMinus}
              className="accordion-icon accordion-icon-active"
              aria-hidden="true"
            />
          </CAccordionHeader>
          <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for the second accordion item.</CAccordionBody>
        </CAccordionItem>
      </CAccordion>
    </>
  )
}
```

> The icon carries no accessible name in either form. The header already announces its expanded state, so keep the icon out of the accessibility tree with `aria-hidden="true"` — a bare inline `` reaches it as an unnamed image otherwise.

### Changing the icon in CSS

When the icon should change everywhere rather than per instance, set the tokens in your own stylesheet instead of putting an element in each header. The shape is a URL-escaped SVG here, which is why the element form above is the better fit inside a component:

```css
.accordion {
  --cui-accordion-header-icon: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg …plus… %3E");
  --cui-accordion-header-active-icon: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg …minus… %3E");
  --cui-accordion-header-icon-transform: none;
}
```

Drop `--cui-accordion-header-active-icon` and keep `--cui-accordion-header-icon-transform` to rotate one shape instead of swapping two.

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

The accordion works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the open items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultOpenItemKeys` | the accordion, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `openItemKeys` | your component |

Both take a single key as well as an array, and `onChange` fires in **both** modes with the new list — so you can watch the state without taking it over.

### Uncontrolled

Give the accordion a starting point and let it manage itself. This is what every example above does.

```jsx
<CAccordion defaultOpenItemKeys={1}>
```

### Controlled

Pass `openItemKeys` and the accordion renders exactly what you pass — it will not open or close on its own. Feed the change back from `onChange`, or nothing moves.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CAccordion, CAccordionBody, CAccordionHeader, CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react'

export const AccordionControlledExample = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<(number | string)[]>([1])

  return (
    <>
      <CAccordion openItemKeys={open} onChange={setOpen}>
        <CAccordionItem itemKey={1}>
          <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #1</CAccordionHeader>
          <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for the first accordion item.</CAccordionBody>
        </CAccordionItem>
        <CAccordionItem itemKey={2}>
          <CAccordionHeader>Accordion Item #2</CAccordionHeader>
          <CAccordionBody>Placeholder content for the second accordion item.</CAccordionBody>
        </CAccordionItem>
      </CAccordion>
      <p className="fg-2">Open: {open.length > 0 ? open.join(', ') : 'none'}</p>
    </>
  )
}
```

Use it when the open items belong to something else: a route, a form step, a preference you persist, or a control outside the accordion like the [expand all](#expand--collapse-all) buttons above.

A single item can be driven on its own with `open` on `<CAccordionItem>`, which overrides the accordion's list for that item. Prefer `openItemKeys` where the whole set moves together.

## Accessibility

`<summary>` is a native disclosure control. It is focusable, it is operated with <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd>, and its expanded state is exposed to assistive technology by the browser — no `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls` bookkeeping is required.

Because a bare `<summary>` is not a heading, wrap its label in an `<h2>`–`<h6>` when the accordion divides a page into sections. See [Headings](#headings) above.

The full treatment is on the [Accordion accessibility](./accessibility/) page: what the native disclosure provides, why the component adds no ARIA attributes, keyboard support, and the two decisions left to you.

# React Accordion Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Accordion component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CAccordion

```jsx
import { CAccordion } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activeItemKey` | `CAccordionItemKey` | - | Sets the initially open items when the component mounts. |
| `alwaysOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Make accordion items stay open when another item is opened |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `defaultOpenItemKeys` | `CAccordionItemKey \| CAccordionItemKey[]` | - | Sets the initially open items when the component mounts. After initialization, the component manages the open items internally. Use it for uncontrolled usage. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | - | Removes the default background-color, some borders, and some rounded corners to render accordions edge-to-edge with their parent container. |
| `gap` | `boolean` | - | Spaces the items apart and gives each one a full border radius, so the accordion reads as a stack of cards. |
| `onChange` | `((keys: CAccordionItemKey[]) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the open items change. - In controlled mode (`openItemKeys` provided), you must update `openItemKeys` yourself based on the value received. - In uncontrolled mode, this callback is called after the internal state updates. |
| `openItemKeys` | `CAccordionItemKey \| CAccordionItemKey[]` | - | Controls which items are open. When provided, the component operates in a controlled mode: update the value yourself from `onChange`. Takes a single key as well as an array — an array only opens more than one item under `alwaysOpen`, since the HTML Standard forbids leaving more than one open item in a `name` group. |
| `size` | `"sm"` | - | Tighten padding, radius and font size for a more compact accordion. |
| `theme` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Tint the open item with one of CoreUI’s themed colors. Closed items are untouched, so the theme marks what is currently expanded rather than recoloring the whole control. |

## CAccordionBody

```jsx
import { CAccordionBody } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |

## CAccordionHeader

```jsx
import { CAccordionHeader } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |

## CAccordionItem

```jsx
import { CAccordionItem } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `id` | `string` | - | The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique in the whole document. |
| `itemKey` | `string \| number` | - | Item key. |
| `onHidden` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the item has been hidden. |
| `onShown` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the item has been shown. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controls whether the item is open, overriding the accordion's own list. When provided, the item operates in a controlled mode: update the value yourself from `onShown` and `onHidden`. Prefer `openItemKeys` on the accordion where the whole set is driven together. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | - | Controls whether the item is open. |

# React Accordion Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Accordion component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

React Accordion supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$accordion-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-accordion-padding-x: 1.25rem,
    --cui-accordion-padding-y: 1rem,
    --cui-accordion-header-padding-x: var(--cui-accordion-padding-x),
    --cui-accordion-header-padding-y: var(--cui-accordion-padding-y),
    --cui-accordion-body-padding-x: var(--cui-accordion-padding-x),
    --cui-accordion-body-padding-y: var(--cui-accordion-padding-y),
    --cui-accordion-font-size: var(--cui-body-font-size),
    --cui-accordion-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-accordion-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-accordion-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), border-radius},
    --cui-accordion-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-accordion-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-accordion-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-accordion-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-accordion-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-accordion-gap: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-accordion-header-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-accordion-header-bg: var(--cui-accordion-bg),
    --cui-accordion-header-icon: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 16 16' fill='none' stroke='%23000' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round'><path d='m2 5 6 6 6-6'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-accordion-header-active-icon: #{escape-svg(var(--cui-accordion-header-icon))},
    --cui-accordion-header-icon-width: 1.25rem,
    --cui-accordion-header-icon-color: currentcolor,
    --cui-accordion-header-active-icon-color: currentcolor,
    --cui-accordion-header-icon-transform: rotate(-180deg),
    --cui-accordion-header-icon-transition: transform .2s ease-in-out,
    --cui-accordion-active-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-accordion-active-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-accordion-active-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-accordion-content-duration: .35s,
    --cui-accordion-content-easing: ease,
  ),
  $accordion-tokens
);
```

## How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-accordion-color': '#333',
  '--cui-accordion-bg': '#f8f9fa',
}

return <CAccordion style={customVars}>{/* Accordion content */}</CAccordion>
```
