# React Calendar Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Calendar component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CCalendar

```jsx
import { CCalendar } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaNavNextMonthLabel` | `string` | `Next month` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next month in the React Calendar component. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. Customize for a more accessible calendar experience. |
| `ariaNavNextYearLabel` | `string` | `Next year` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the next year in the React Calendar component. Screen readers utilize this label to inform users of the button's functionality, aiding in a more inclusive application. |
| `ariaNavNextYearsLabel` | `string` | `Next 12 years` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the next page of years. |
| `ariaNavPrevMonthLabel` | `string` | `Previous month` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous month in the React Calendar component. This label is announced by screen readers, ensuring clarity around the button's purpose. |
| `ariaNavPrevYearLabel` | `string` | `Previous year` | A string that provides an accessible label for the button that navigates to the previous year in the React Calendar component. Use it to enhance the experience for screen readers and further accessibility. |
| `ariaNavPrevYearsLabel` | `string` | `Previous 12 years` | Sets the accessible label (`aria-label`) of the button that turns the years view to the previous page of years. |
| `ariaNothingToPickLabel` | `string` | `Nothing on this page can be picked` | Sets the description (`aria-describedby`) of a grid in which nothing can be picked, such as a page wholly outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or one that `disabledDates` covers, also announced when the calendar turns to such a page. An empty string leaves the grid without a description. |
| `ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement` | `string` | `Selected date: {date}` | Sets the message announced when a click or Enter / Space picks a date, and with `range` when both ends fall on the same day. `{date}` is replaced by the full name of what was picked, such as `Wednesday, August 12, 2026` or `August 10 – 16, 2026`. An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement` | `string` | `Selected range: {start} to {end}` | Sets the message announced with `range` when a pick leaves both ends set. `{start}` and `{end}` are replaced by the full names of its ends. An empty string announces nothing. |
| `ariaWeekNumberLabel` | `((weekNumber: number) => string \| undefined)` | - | Names each week number for screen readers: a function that takes the week number and returns its name. Without it the name is the locale's word for week and the number, such as `Week 36`. Keep the number in the name, so a voice-control user can say what they see. |
| `calendarDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | `startDate \|\| endDate \|\| null` | Defines the initial date or reference date for the React Calendar component. This date can be either a Date object or a string that can be converted into a valid date. |
| `calendars` | `number` | `1` | Specifies how many individual calendars should be displayed side by side on desktop devices. Increasing this number allows your users to view multiple months (or years, etc.) simultaneously. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all classNames you want to apply to the outermost container of the React Calendar component. Use this to style or theme your calendar. |
| `dayFormat` | `"numeric" \| "2-digit" \| ((date: Date) => string \| number)` | `numeric` | Sets the format for days. Accepts either a built-in format ('numeric' or '2-digit') or a custom function to return any desired string or number for the day. |
| `disabledDates` | `DisabledDate \| DisabledDate[]` | - | Specifies one or more dates that cannot be selected by the user. This is useful for disabling weekends, holidays, or any dates that you need to restrict within your React Calendar component. In week, month, quarter and year selection a period is disabled when every day of it is. |
| `endDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Defines the initially selected ending date (applicable when using range selection). Accepts both Date objects and valid date strings. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `number` | `1` | Sets the first day of the week. This can be adjusted for different locales or preferences: - `0` = Sunday - `1` = Monday - `2` = Tuesday - `3` = Wednesday - `4` = Thursday - `5` = Friday - `6` = Saturday |
| `locale` | `string` | `default` | Indicates the locale for the React Calendar component. If not explicitly provided, it inherits the locale settings from the browser. |
| `maxDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The maximum date that can be selected. The days after its day are disabled within the calendar, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. This is often used to restrict future selections. |
| `minDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | The minimum date that can be selected. The days before its day are disabled in the calendar, and a time of day it carries leaves its own day selectable. In week selection its whole week stays selectable. Useful for preventing selection of past dates or creating limited booking windows. |
| `monthFormat` | `"numeric" \| "2-digit" \| "long" \| "narrow" \| "short"` | `short` | Sets the format for month names. Accepts built-in formats ('long', 'narrow', 'short', 'numeric', '2-digit'). |
| `navNextDoubleIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor"> <path d="m95.314 447.313-22.628-22.626L245.373 252 72.686 79.313l22.628-22.626L290.627 252z" /> <path d="m255.314 447.313-22.628-22.626L405.373 252 232.686 79.313l22.628-22.626L450.627 252z" /> </svg> )` | Customizes the icon for navigating multiple steps forward (double jump), e.g., skipping multiple months or years at once. Ideal for quick navigation through large date ranges. In right-to-left it shows on the double previous button. |
| `navNextIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor"> <path d="m179.313 451.313-22.626-22.626L329.372 256 156.687 83.313l22.626-22.626L374.627 256z" /> </svg> )` | Customizes the icon for navigating to the next view (month, year, etc.) depending on the current view. Accepts any valid `ReactNode`, enabling you to display text, images, or icons. In right-to-left it shows on the previous button. |
| `navPrevDoubleIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor"> <path d="M416.686 447.313 221.373 252 416.686 56.687l22.628 22.626L266.627 252l172.687 172.687z" /> <path d="M256.686 447.313 61.373 252 256.686 56.687l22.628 22.626L106.627 252l172.687 172.687z" /> </svg> )` | Customizes the icon for a double jump backward (e.g., jumping multiple months or years at once). This feature simplifies larger date range navigation within your React Calendar component. In right-to-left it shows on the double next button. |
| `navPrevIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor"> <path d="M324.687 451.313 129.373 256 324.687 60.687l22.626 22.626L174.628 256l172.685 172.687z" /> </svg> )` | Customizes the icon for navigating to the previous view in the calendar. Accepts any valid ReactNode to provide flexible styling or theming. In right-to-left it shows on the next button. |
| `onCalendarDateChange` | `((date: string \| Date, view: "days" \| "months" \| "quarters" \| "years") => void)` | - | Callback fired when the calendar's reference date (i.e., the date indicating which month/year is currently displayed) changes. Receives the new `Date \| string` as an argument for further handling. |
| `onEndDateChange` | `((date: Date \| null, selection?: string \| Date \| null \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback triggered when the end date of the selection changes. Handy for synchronizing the selected date range with external states or components. It receives the same two arguments as `onStartDateChange`. |
| `onSelectEndChange` | `((value: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired when toggling between selecting the start date and the end date in range selection mode. Receives a boolean indicating if the user is currently selecting the end date. |
| `onStartDateChange` | `((date: Date \| null, selection?: string \| Date \| null \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback triggered when the start date of the selection changes. Useful for updating other parts of your application or performing side effects based on the newly chosen start date. The first argument is the underlying `Date`; the second is the value formatted per `selectionType` — the `Date` itself for day selection, a string for week (`'2026W27'`), month (`'2026-01'`), quarter (`'2026Q1'`) and year (`'2026'`), with the year in at least four digits (`'0026-01'`). |
| `onViewChange` | `((view: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the view changes, and with the view `selectionType` starts in each time the calendar mounts or `selectionType` changes. |
| `onViewChanged` | `((view: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the calendar's view changes between days, months, or years. For instance, moving from day view to month view or from month view to year view. |
| `range` | `boolean` | - | Enables range selection mode in your React Calendar component, allowing users to select two dates for a range (start and end). Once enabled, the component will manage state for both dates. |
| `renderDayCell` | `((date: Date, meta: { isDisabled: boolean; isInCurrentMonth: boolean; isInRange: boolean; isSelected: boolean; isToday: boolean; label: string; }) => ReactNode)` | - | A function that allows you to customize the rendering of individual day cells within the calendar. This function receives the date and metadata (like selection and disabled status) as arguments, enabling you to apply custom styles, add tooltips, or include additional content in each day cell. The metadata carries the cell's full name as `label`, for example for visually hidden text next to a short label. |
| `renderMonthCell` | `((date: Date, meta: { isDisabled: boolean; isInRange: boolean; isSelected: boolean; label: string; }) => ReactNode)` | - | A function that allows you to customize the rendering of individual month cells within the calendar. This function receives the date and metadata (like selection and disabled status) as arguments, enabling you to apply custom styles or include additional content in each month cell. The metadata carries the cell's full name as `label`, for example for visually hidden text next to a short label. |
| `renderQuarterCell` | `((date: Date, meta: { isDisabled: boolean; isInRange: boolean; isSelected: boolean; label: string; }) => ReactNode)` | - | A function that allows you to customize the rendering of individual quarter cells within the calendar. This function receives the date and metadata (like selection and disabled status) as arguments, enabling you to apply custom styles or include additional content in each quarter cell. The metadata carries the cell's full name as `label`, for example for visually hidden text next to a short label. |
| `renderYearCell` | `((date: Date, meta: { isDisabled: boolean; isInRange: boolean; isSelected: boolean; label: string; }) => ReactNode)` | - | A function that allows you to customize the rendering of individual year cells within the calendar. This function receives the date and metadata (like selection and disabled status) as arguments, enabling you to apply custom styles or include additional content in each year cell. The metadata carries the cell's full name as `label`, for example for visually hidden text next to a short label. |
| `selectAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets whether days from adjacent months (shown at the start/end of the current view) are selectable. This only applies if `showAdjacentDays` is set to `true`. A picked day of an adjacent month keeps the month on screen and shows as selected with an outline on a subtle background instead of the solid fill. |
| `selectEndDate` | `boolean` | - | Indicates if the user's current selection is targeting the end date in range selection mode. Primarily used for controlled components where you need to manage which date (start or end) is currently active. |
| `selectionType` | `SelectionTypes` | `day` | Specifies the selection type for the React Calendar component. Supports: - `day`: Regular day selection (default) - `week`: Select an entire week - `month`: Select an entire month - `quarter`: Select an entire quarter - `year`: Select an entire year |
| `showAdjacentDays` | `boolean` | `true` | Controls whether the calendar should display dates from previous or next months (non-selectable if `selectAdjacentDays` is `false`). This can make the calendar visually continuous. |
| `showWeekNumber` | `boolean` | `false` | Toggles the display of week numbers (ISO 8601) in the calendar's left column. Particularly beneficial for applications where users need to see the week index for scheduling or reporting. |
| `startDate` | `string \| Date \| null` | - | Defines the initially selected starting date. This date can be a Date object or a string convertible into a valid date. Useful when you want to show a pre-selected date. |
| `weekdayFormat` | `number \| "long" \| "narrow" \| "short" \| ((date: Date) => string \| number)` | `2` | Sets the format or length of the weekday names displayed in the calendar header. You can use numeric values like 2 (two-letter abbreviations) or built-in string formats like `'long'`, `'narrow'`, and `'short'`, or provide a custom function to fully control how weekdays are displayed. |
| `weekNumbersLabel` | `string` | - | Defines the label that appears above the week numbers column. For example, you might label it `'WK'` or `'Week #'`. Without it the column is named for screen readers with the locale's word for week. |
| `yearFormat` | `"numeric" \| "2-digit"` | `numeric` | Sets how the year cells of the years view write the year: `'numeric'` (2026) or `'2-digit'` (26). The navigation always writes the full year. |

# React Calendar Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Calendar component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

Each panel is a `.calendar` element carrying its position in `data-coreui-calendar-index`, counted from `0`, and the content of every cell names the view it belongs to: `.calendar-cell-inner.day`, `.month`, `.quarter` or `.year`. The navigation buttons carry the class of their action: `.btn-double-prev`, `.btn-prev`, `.btn-month`, `.btn-year`, `.btn-next` and `.btn-double-next`. The vanilla, React and Vue calendars carry the same hooks, so a stylesheet written against one fits the others.

## CSS variables

CoreUI React Calendar supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$calendar-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-calendar-table-margin: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-table-cell-size: 2.75rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-calendar-nav-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid var(--cui-calendar-nav-border-color),
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-padding-y: .25rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-bg: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-border-width: 1px,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-border-color: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-hover-bg: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-hover-border-color: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-btn-focus-border-color: transparent,
    --cui-calendar-nav-date-font-weight: 600,
    --cui-calendar-nav-date-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-calendar-nav-date-hover-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-calendar-nav-icon-width: 1rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-icon-height: 1rem,
    --cui-calendar-nav-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-calendar-nav-icon-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-calendar-cell-header-inner-font-weight: 600,
    --cui-calendar-cell-header-inner-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-calendar-cell-week-number-font-weight: 600,
    --cui-calendar-cell-week-number-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-calendar-cell-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),
    --cui-calendar-cell-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-calendar-cell-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-calendar-cell-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-4),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-hover-color: var(--cui-calendar-cell-selected-color),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-hover-bg: oklch(from var(--cui-calendar-cell-selected-bg) calc(l * var(--cui-theme-hover-lightness)) calc(c * var(--cui-theme-hover-chroma)) h),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-color: var(--cui-primary-fg-emphasis),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-hover-color: var(--cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-color),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-hover-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-muted),
    --cui-calendar-cell-range-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
    --cui-calendar-cell-range-hover-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-calendar-cell-today-color: var(--cui-danger-base),
  ),
  $calendar-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-calendar-nav-date-color': '#333',
  '--cui-calendar-cell-hover-bg': '#f8f9fa',
}

return <CCalendar style={customVars} />
```

# React Callout Component

> React callout component provides presentation of content in a visually distinct manner. Includes a heading, icon and typically text-based content.

## Default callout

Callouts accommodate text of any length, along with optional elements like icons and headings. `<CCallout>` on its own is a neutral callout — a bordered surface with a thicker leading edge, inheriting the text color of its surroundings.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCallout } from '@coreui/react'

export const CalloutDefaultExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCallout>
      New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
      terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
    </CCallout>
  )
}
```

## Theme variants

[`theme`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) sets the color context. It colors the leading edge and tints the border, and it renders a `.theme-*` class — so a theme class on any element above the callout colors it just the same.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCallout } from '@coreui/react'

export const CalloutExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CCallout theme="primary">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout theme="secondary">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout theme="success">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout theme="danger">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout theme="warning">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout theme="info">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout theme="inverse">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Tinted callout

Because the theme class exposes every slot, the background utilities read from it too. Add `.theme-subtle` for a filled callout without naming a color twice.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCallout } from '@coreui/react'

export const CalloutSubtleExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CCallout className="theme-subtle" theme="primary">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout className="theme-subtle" theme="success">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
      <CCallout className="theme-subtle" theme="danger">
        New to or unfamiliar with flexbox? Read this CSS Tricks flexbox guide for background,
        terminology, guidelines, and code snippets.
      </CCallout>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Deprecated props

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

`color` still works and is removed in v7. It renders the same `.theme-{color}` class as `theme`, and loses to `theme` when both are set.

```diff
- <CCallout theme="success">Saved</CCallout>
+ <CCallout theme="success">Saved</CCallout>
```

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

# React Callout Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Callout component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCallout

```jsx
import { CCallout } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `color` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `theme` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |

# React Callout Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Callout component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

React Callout supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$callout-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-callout-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-callout-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-callout-margin-x: 0,
    --cui-callout-margin-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-callout-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-callout-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-callout-border-left-width: calc(var(--cui-border-width) * 4),
    --cui-callout-border-left-color: var(--cui-callout-border-color),
    --cui-callout-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
  ),
  $callout-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-callout-border-color': '#333',
  '--cui-callout-padding-x': '1rem',
}

return <CCallout style={customVars} />
```

## Sass loops

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

The loop that creates the deprecated `.callout-{color}` classes, pointing each one at the matching theme color. It lives in the opt-in [`coreui-legacy.css`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/optimize/#v5-compatibility-css), not in `coreui.css`.

```scss
@each $state in map.keys($theme-colors) {
  .callout-#{$state} {
    @include theme-tokens($state);
  }
}
```

# React Card Component

> React card component provides a flexible and extensible container for displaying content. Card is delivered with a bunch of variants and options.

## About

A React card component is a content container. It incorporates options for images, headers, and footers, a wide variety of content, contextual background colors, and excellent display options.

## Example

Cards are built with as little markup and styles as possible but still manage to deliver a bunch of control and customization. Built with flexbox, they offer easy alignment and mix well with other CoreUI components. Cards have no top, left, and right margins by default, so use [spacing utilities](https://coreui.io/react/docs/utilities/margin/) as needed. They have no fixed width to start, so they'll fill the full width of its parent.

Below is an example of a basic card with mixed content and a fixed width. Cards have no fixed width to start, so they'll naturally fill the full width of its parent element.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCard, CCardBody, CCardImage, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
        <CCardText>
          Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's
          content.
        </CCardText>
        <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
          Go somewhere
        </CButton>
      </CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

## Content types

CoreUI card supports a wide variety of content, including images, text, list groups, links, and more. Below are examples of those elements.

### Body

The main block of a card is the `<CCardBody>`. Use it whenever you need a padded section within a card. Sections stacked in a card are divided by a single rule in the card's own border: a `<CCardBody>`, a list group or a bottom image draws it above itself when it follows a top image, a body or a list group, while `<CCardHeader>` and `<CCardFooter>` draw their own. A border utility or a theme on the card carries over to the rule, and a section hidden with `hidden` or `.d-none` does not count.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardBodyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard>
      <CCardBody>This is some text within a card body.</CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

### Titles, text, and links

Card titles are managed by `<CCardTitle>` component. `<CCardBody>` is a flex column that spaces its children with `--cui-card-body-gap`, so a row of links is a `.hstack` of plain `<CLink>` elements.

Subtitles are managed by `<CCardSubtitle>` component. If the `<CCardTitle>` also, the `<CCardSubtitle>` items are stored in a `<CCardBody>` item, the card title, and subtitle are arranged rightly.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardSubtitle, CCardText, CCardTitle, CLink } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardTitleExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
        <CCardSubtitle className="fg-2">Card subtitle</CCardSubtitle>
        <CCardText>
          Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's
          content.
        </CCardText>
        <div className="hstack gap-4">
          <CLink href="#">Card link</CLink>
          <CLink href="#">Another link</CLink>
        </div>
      </CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

### Images

`orientation="top"` places a picture to the top of the card. With `<CCardText>`, text can be added to the card. Text within `<CCardText>` can additionally be styled with the regular HTML tags.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardImage, CCardText } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardImagesExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardText>
          Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's
          content.
        </CCardText>
      </CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

```html
}
```

## Sizing

Cards assume no specific `width` to start, so they'll be 100% wide unless otherwise stated. You can adjust this as required with custom CSS, grid classes, grid Sass mixins, or services.

### Using grid markup

Using the grid, wrap cards in columns and rows as needed.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCard, CCardBody, CCardText, CCardTitle, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardSizingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow>
      <CCol sm={6}>
        <CCard>
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardTitle>Special title treatment</CCardTitle>
            <CCardText>
              With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
            </CCardText>
            <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
              Go somewhere
            </CButton>
          </CCardBody>
        </CCard>
      </CCol>
      <CCol sm={6}>
        <CCard>
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardTitle>Special title treatment</CCardTitle>
            <CCardText>
              With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
            </CCardText>
            <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
              Go somewhere
            </CButton>
          </CCardBody>
        </CCard>
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Using utilities

Use some of [available sizing utilities](https://coreui.io/react/docs/utilities/width/) to rapidly set a card's width.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCard, CCardBody, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardSizing2Example = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CCard className="w-75 mb-4">
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
          </CCardText>
          <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
            Go somewhere
          </CButton>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard className="w-50">
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
          </CCardText>
          <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
            Go somewhere
          </CButton>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Using custom CSS

Use custom CSS in your stylesheets or as inline styles to set a width.


## Text alignment

You can instantly change the text arrangement of any card—in its whole or specific parts—with [text align classes](https://coreui.io/react/docs/utilities/text-alignment/).

`text-align` reaches the text but not the body's own flex items, so a button or a link stays at the start of the card. Move it with a margin utility: `.mx-auto` to centre it, `.ms-auto` to push it to the end.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCard, CCardBody, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardTextAlignmentExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CCard className="mb-4" style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Special title treatment</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
          </CCardText>
          <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
            Go somewhere
          </CButton>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard className="mb-4 text-center" style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Special title treatment</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
          </CCardText>
          <CButton theme="primary" href="#" className="mx-auto">
            Go somewhere
          </CButton>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard className="text-end" style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Special title treatment</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            With supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
          </CCardText>
          <CButton theme="primary" href="#" className="ms-auto">
            Go somewhere
          </CButton>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Images

Cards introduce several options for acting with images. Pick from appending "image caps" at either end of a card, overlaying images with content, or just inserting the image in a card.

### Image caps

Similar to headers and footers, cards can include top and bottom "image caps"—images at the top or bottom of a card.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardImage, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardImageCapsExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CCard className="mb-4">
        <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
            content. This content is a little bit longer.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard className="mb-4">
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
            content. This content is a little bit longer.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
        <CCardImage orientation="bottom" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
      </CCard>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Image overlays

Adapt an image into a background and overlay your text. Depending on the image, you may need additional styles or utilities.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardImage, CCardImageOverlay, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardImageOverlaysExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard className="mb-4 bg-black fg-white">

          This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
          content. This content is a little bit longer.
        </CCardText>
        <CCardText>Last updated 3 mins ago</CCardText>
      </CCardImageOverlay>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

## Horizontal

Use `layout="row"` to lay a card out along the inline axis. The sections sit side by side with a single divider between each pair, so no wrapper markup is needed. For an image cap, use `orientation="start"` or `orientation="end"` on `<CCardImage>` to round the leading or trailing edge.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardImage, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardImageHorizontalExample = () => {
  return (
    <>
      <CCard layout="row" className="mb-4" style={{ maxWidth: '540px' }}>
        <CCardImage orientation="start" src={'/assets/img/react400.jpg'} width="40%" />
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
            content. This content is a little bit longer.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard layout="row" style={{ maxWidth: '540px' }}>
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
            content. This content is a little bit longer.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
        <CCardImage orientation="end" src={'/assets/img/react400.jpg'} width="40%" />
      </CCard>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Card styles

Cards include various options for customizing their backgrounds, borders, and color.

These are general-purpose utilities applied to the card as a whole: `text-bg-*` fills the card's own background and leaves the frame, the header and the footer neutral; add the matching `.border-{color}` to frame the card in the fill color. To color the caps instead — or to color one section on its own — reach for [theme variants](#theme-variants).

### Background and color

Use the `textBgColor` property to fill the card with a theme color; the text color follows it to keep the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio. The `color` property sets the background alone.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardHeader, CCardText, CCardTitle, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardStylesBackgroundAndColorExample = () => {
  const colors = [
    { color: 'primary' },
    { color: 'secondary' },
    { color: 'success' },
    { color: 'danger' },
    { color: 'warning' },
    { color: 'info' },
    { color: 'light' },
    { color: 'dark' },
  ]

  return (
    <CRow>
      {colors.map((item, index) => (
        <CCol sm={6} key={index}>
          <CCard textBgColor={item.color} className={`border-${item.color} mb-4`}>
            <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
            <CCardBody>
              <CCardTitle>{item.color} card title</CCardTitle>
              <CCardText>
                Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the
                card's content.
              </CCardText>
            </CCardBody>
          </CCard>
        </CCol>
      ))}
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Border

Use [border utilities](https://coreui.io/react/docs/utilities/border/) to change just the `border-color` of a card. Note that you can put `fg-{color}` classes on the `<CCard>` or a subset of the card's contents as shown below.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardHeader, CCardText, CCardTitle, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardStylesBorderExample = () => {
  const colors = ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'info', 'warning', 'danger', 'inverse']

  return (
    <CRow>
      {colors.map((color) => (
        <CCol sm={6} key={color}>
          <CCard className={`mb-4 border-${color}`}>
            <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
            <CCardBody className={`fg-${color}`}>
              <CCardTitle>{color} card title</CCardTitle>
              <CCardText>
                Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the
                card's content.
              </CCardText>
            </CCardBody>
          </CCard>
        </CCol>
      ))}
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

## Card layout

In addition to styling the content within cards, CoreUI includes a few options for laying out series of cards. For the time being, **these layout options are not yet responsive**.

### Card groups

Use card groups to render cards as a single, attached element with equal width and height columns. Card groups start off stacked and become attached with uniform dimensions from the `sm` breakpoint up.

That breakpoint is measured on the nearest query container, not the viewport, so a group in a narrow column stays stacked while the same markup in a wide one attaches. Mark an ancestor with `.contains-inline` — without one the query has nothing to read and the cards never attach.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardGroup, CCardImage, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardGroupsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCardGroup>
      <CCard>
        <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
            content. This content is a little bit longer.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard>
        <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This card has supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional content.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
      <CCard>
        <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
        <CCardBody>
          <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
          <CCardText>
            This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
            content. This card has even longer content than the first to show that equal height
            action.
          </CCardText>
          <CCardText>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardText>
        </CCardBody>
      </CCard>
    </CCardGroup>
  )
}
```

When using card groups with footers, their content will automatically line up.

### Grid cards

Use the `CRow` component and set `xs|sm|md|lg|xl={{ cols: * }}` property (the top tier is spread in as `{...{ '2xl': { cols: * } }}`) to control how many grid columns (wrapped around your cards) you show per row. For example, here's `xs={{cols: 1}}` laying out the cards on one column, and `md={{cols: 2}}` splitting four cards to equal width across multiple rows, from the medium breakpoint up.

```html
import React from 'react'
import {
  CCard,
  CCardBody,
  CCardFooter,
  CCardImage,
  CCardText,
  CCardTitle,
  CCol,
  CRow,
} from '@coreui/react'

export const CardGridExample = () => {
  return (
    <CRow xs={{ cols: 1, gutter: 5 }} md={{ cols: 2 }}>
      <CCol xs>
        <CCard>
          <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
            <CCardText>
              This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
              content. This content is a little bit longer.
            </CCardText>
          </CCardBody>
          <CCardFooter>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardFooter>
        </CCard>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>
        <CCard>
          <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
            <CCardText>
              This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
              content. This content is a little bit longer.
            </CCardText>
          </CCardBody>
          <CCardFooter>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardFooter>
        </CCard>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>
        <CCard>
          <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
            <CCardText>
              This is a wider card with supporting text below as a natural lead-in to additional
              content. This content is a little bit longer.
            </CCardText>
          </CCardBody>
          <CCardFooter>
            <small className="fg-2">Last updated 3 mins ago</small>
          </CCardFooter>
        </CCard>
      </CCol>
      <CCol xs>
        <CCard>
          <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
            <CCardText>
```

## Theme variants

_Added in 6.0.0._

The [`theme`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) property paints the card's frame and caps with the theme color, with contrast text in the header and footer. The body keeps the card background.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardFooter, CCardHeader, CCardText } from '@coreui/react'

const themes = ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger', 'warning', 'info'] as const

export const CardThemingExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="d-flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      {themes.map((theme) => (
        <CCard key={theme} theme={theme} style={{ width: '15rem' }}>
          <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardText>Some quick example text to build on the card title.</CCardText>
          </CCardBody>
          <CCardFooter>Footer</CCardFooter>
        </CCard>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

Put the theme class on a single section instead and only that section follows it:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardFooter, CCardHeader, CCardText } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardThemingSectionExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard style={{ maxWidth: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardText>Some quick example text to build on the card title.</CCardText>
      </CCardBody>
      <CCardFooter className="theme-danger">Something went wrong</CCardFooter>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

Use `variant="subtle"` to swap the solid fill for the theme's subtle background and border, with emphasis text in the caps.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardFooter, CCardHeader, CCardText } from '@coreui/react'

const themes = ['primary', 'secondary', 'success', 'danger', 'warning', 'info'] as const

export const CardSubtleExample = () => {
  return (
    <div className="d-flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      {themes.map((theme) => (
        <CCard key={theme} theme={theme} variant="subtle" style={{ width: '15rem' }}>
          <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
          <CCardBody>
            <CCardText>Some quick example text to build on the card title.</CCardText>
          </CCardBody>
          <CCardFooter>Footer</CCardFooter>
        </CCard>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Translucent

_Added in 6.0.0._

Use the `translucent` property to let the background through the card and blur it. The caps thin out with it, so the whole card reads as one surface.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardFooter, CCardHeader, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardTranslucentExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard translucent style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
        <CCardText>Some quick example text to build on the card title.</CCardText>
      </CCardBody>
      <CCardFooter>Footer</CCardFooter>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

# React Card Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Card component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCard

```jsx
import { CCard } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `color` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `layout` | `"row"` | - | Specify a layout type. |
| `textBgColor` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the component's color scheme to one of CoreUI's themed colors, ensuring the text color contrast adheres to the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio standard for accessibility. |
| `theme` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Paints the card's frame and caps with one of CoreUI’s themed colors. The body keeps the card background — put the class on a single section to theme only that section. |
| `translucent` | `boolean` | - | Let the background through the card and blur it. |
| `variant` | `"subtle"` | - | Set the card variant. The default is solid. |

```jsx
import { CCardBody } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `(ElementType & "symbol") \| (ElementType & "object") \| (ElementType & "img") \| (ElementType & "slot") \| (ElementType & "style") \| ... 175 more ...` | `img` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `orientation` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "start" \| "end"` | - | Optionally orientate the image to the top, bottom, or — in a `layout="row"` card — to the start or end. |

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `(ElementType & "symbol") \| (ElementType & "object") \| (ElementType & "p") \| (ElementType & "slot") \| (ElementType & "style") \| ... 175 more ...` | `p` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |

## CCardTitle

```jsx
import { CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `(ElementType & "symbol") \| (ElementType & "object") \| (ElementType & "h5") \| (ElementType & "slot") \| (ElementType & "style") \| ... 175 more ...` | `h5` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |

# React Card Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Card component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

React Card supports CSS variables for easy customization. These variables are set via Sass but allow direct overrides in your stylesheets or inline styles.

```scss
$card-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-card-spacer-y: var(--cui-spacer-6),
    --cui-card-spacer-x: var(--cui-spacer-6),
    --cui-card-body-gap: calc(var(--cui-card-spacer-y) * .5),
    --cui-card-title-color: inherit,
    --cui-card-subtitle-color: inherit,
    --cui-card-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-card-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-card-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-card-box-shadow: none,
    --cui-card-inner-border-radius: calc(var(--cui-card-border-radius) - var(--cui-card-border-width)),
    --cui-card-cap-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-card-cap-padding-x: var(--cui-card-spacer-x),
    --cui-card-cap-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-card-cap-color: inherit,
    --cui-card-height: auto,
    --cui-card-color: inherit,
    --cui-card-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-card-img-overlay-padding-y: var(--cui-card-spacer-y),
    --cui-card-img-overlay-padding-x: var(--cui-card-spacer-x),
    --cui-card-group-margin: #{$grid-gutter-x * .5},
  ),
  $card-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-card-cap-bg': '#555',
  '--cui-card-color': '#efefef',
}

return <CCard style={customVars}>{/* Card content */}</CCard>
```

# React Bootstrap Card Component

> Learn how to use CoreUI’s React Bootstrap Card component to build flexible content containers with headers, footers, images, list groups, and responsive layouts.

## About React Bootstrap Card Component

The React Bootstrap Card component is a versatile container used to display content in a structured and responsive way. It supports images, headers, footers, background styles, and more—styled to match Bootstrap's visual language.

## Example usage

React Bootstrap Cards require minimal markup and offer maximum flexibility. They use flexbox for layout, have no default margins, and fill their parent container by default.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CButton, CCard, CCardBody, CCardImage, CCardText, CCardTitle } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardImage orientation="top" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} />
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
        <CCardText>
          Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's
          content.
        </CCardText>
        <CButton theme="primary" href="#">
          Go somewhere
        </CButton>
      </CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

## Content types supported by React Bootstrap Card

### Card body

The main block of the card is wrapped in `<CCardBody>` for consistent padding.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardBodyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard>
      <CCardBody>This is some text within a card body.</CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

### Titles, text, and links

Use `<CCardTitle>` and `<CCardSubtitle>` to structure text and links inside cards.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardSubtitle, CCardText, CCardTitle, CLink } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardTitleExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCard style={{ width: '18rem' }}>
      <CCardBody>
        <CCardTitle>Card title</CCardTitle>
        <CCardSubtitle className="fg-2">Card subtitle</CCardSubtitle>
        <CCardText>
          Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's
          content.
        </CCardText>
        <div className="hstack gap-4">
          <CLink href="#">Card link</CLink>
          <CLink href="#">Another link</CLink>
        </div>
      </CCardBody>
    </CCard>
  )
}
```

### Images

## Styling options

### Background and text color

Use the `textBgColor` property to fill the card with a theme color; the text color follows it to keep the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio. The `color` property sets the background alone.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardHeader, CCardText, CCardTitle, CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const CardStylesBackgroundAndColorExample = () => {
  const colors = [
    { color: 'primary' },
    { color: 'secondary' },
    { color: 'success' },
    { color: 'danger' },
    { color: 'warning' },
    { color: 'info' },
    { color: 'light' },
    { color: 'dark' },
  ]

  return (
    <CRow>
      {colors.map((item, index) => (
        <CCol sm={6} key={index}>
          <CCard textBgColor={item.color} className={`border-${item.color} mb-4`}>
            <CCardHeader>Header</CCardHeader>
            <CCardBody>
              <CCardTitle>{item.color} card title</CCardTitle>
              <CCardText>
                Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the
                card's content.
              </CCardText>
            </CCardBody>
          </CCard>
        </CCol>
      ))}
    </CRow>
  )
}
```

### Border customization

Apply border utilities to the card and `fg-{color}` classes to its contents to customize card borders.

# React Carousel Component

> React carousel is a slideshow component for cycling through elements—images or slides of text—like a carousel.

## How it works

The React carousel is a slideshow built on native CSS scroll snapping: the track is a scroll container, so dragging, swiping, momentum and trackpad scrolling all come from the browser. The component layers on the previous/next controls, indicators, autoplay and active-slide tracking.

In browsers where the [Page Visibility API](https://www.w3.org/TR/page-visibility/) is supported, the carousel will avoid sliding when the webpage is not visible to the user (such as when the browser tab is inactive, the browser window is minimized, etc.).

## Example

Carousels don't automatically normalize slide dimensions. As such, you may want to use extra utilities or custom methods to properly size content. While carousels support previous/next controls and indicators, they're not explicitly expected. Add and customize as you see fit.

### Slides only

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselSlidesOnlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### With controls

Adding in the previous and next controls by `controls` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselWithControlsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### With indicators

You can attach the indicators to the carousel, lengthwise the controls, too.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselWithIndicatorsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls indicators>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### With captions

You can add captions to slides with the `<CCarouselCaption>` element within any `<CCarouselItem>`. They can be immediately hidden on smaller viewports, as shown below, with optional [display utilities](https://coreui.io/react/docs/utilities/display/). We hide them with `.d-none` and draw them back on medium-sized devices with `.d-md-block`.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselCaption, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselWithCaptionsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls indicators>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
        <CCarouselCaption className="d-none d-md-block">
          <h5>First slide label</h5>
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the first slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
        <CCarouselCaption className="d-none d-md-block">
          <h5>Second slide label</h5>
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the second slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
        <CCarouselCaption className="d-none d-md-block">
          <h5>Third slide label</h5>
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the third slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### Crossfade

Add `transition="crossfade"` to your carousel to animate slides with a fade transition instead of a slide.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselCrossfadeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls transition="crossfade">
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

## Items

### Multiple items

The track lays slides out with the `--cui-carousel-items` and `--cui-carousel-items-gap` custom properties — set them through the `style` property.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselMultipleItemsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel
      controls
      style={
        { '--cui-carousel-items': 3, '--cui-carousel-items-gap': '.5rem' } as React.CSSProperties
      }
    >
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 4" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 5" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### Peeking

`--cui-carousel-items-peek` insets the track so the neighbouring slides show at the edges; add the `center` property to snap the active slide to the middle of the viewport instead of the start.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselPeekingExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel
      center
      controls
      style={
        {
          '--cui-carousel-items': 1,
          '--cui-carousel-items-gap': '.5rem',
          '--cui-carousel-items-peek': '3rem',
        } as React.CSSProperties
      }
    >
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### Variable width

Add `variableWidth` and each slide keeps its own width; snap points still land on every item.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselVariableWidthExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel
      controls
      variableWidth
      style={{ '--cui-carousel-items-gap': '.5rem' } as React.CSSProperties}
    >
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" width={320} />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" width={200} />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" width={420} />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

## Autoplay

Set the `autoplay` property to cycle automatically. Autoplay pauses on hover (the `pause` property) and turns off for good once the user takes control — a click on a control, an arrow key, a drag, or the pause button — so content never moves out from under them ([WCAG 2.2.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html)). While autoplay runs, the active indicator fills like a progress bar over the current slide's interval. The `playPause` property renders the pause/play control; set an `interval` on a single `<CCarouselItem>` to hold that slide longer.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselAutoplayExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel autoplay controls indicators playPause interval={3000}>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem interval={6000}>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

## End behavior

The `ends` property decides what happens past the last (or before the first) slide: `loop` (default) continues seamlessly where the layout allows and falls back to a wrap, `wrap` jumps to the other end, and `stop` disables the matching control at each end. When the control being disabled has focus, focus moves to the other control, or leaves the controls when both are disabled.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselEndsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls ends="stop">
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

## Dark variant

Add `dark` property to the `CCarousel` for darker controls, indicators, and captions. Under the hood it sets `data-coreui-theme="dark"` on the carousel — the chrome colours are `light-dark()` pairs resolved on the element, so the attribute flips them all.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselCaption, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselDarkVariantExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls indicators dark>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
        <CCarouselCaption className="d-none d-md-block">
          <h5>First slide label</h5>
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the first slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
        <CCarouselCaption className="d-none d-md-block">
          <h5>Second slide label</h5>
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the second slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
        <CCarouselCaption className="d-none d-md-block">
          <h5>Third slide label</h5>
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the third slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

## Custom transition

Programmatic jumps (controls, indicators, autoplay) animate the scroll position over a fixed 300ms with an ease-in-out curve, in every browser. The crossfade's timing lives in `--cui-carousel-fade-duration` and `--cui-carousel-fade-timing`. Native scrolling — dragging, swiping, momentum — is the browser's own and has no duration to configure.

## API

Check out the documentation below for a comprehensive guide to all the props you can use with the components mentioned here.

- [&lt;CCarousel /&gt;](./api/#ccarousel)
- [&lt;CCarouselCaption /&gt;](./api/#ccarouselcaption)
- [&lt;CCarouselItem /&gt;](./api/#ccarouselitem)

# React Carousel Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Carousel component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CCarousel

```jsx
import { CCarousel } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activeIndex` | `number` | `0` | index of the active item. The carousel follows post-mount changes and slides to the new index. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the carousel cycles automatically from mount. Autoplay turns off for good once the user interacts with the carousel. |
| `center` | `boolean` | - | Snap the active slide to the middle of the viewport instead of its start. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | - | Adding in the previous and next controls. |
| `dark` | `boolean` | - | Add darker controls, indicators, and captions. |
| `ends` | `"loop" \| "wrap" \| "stop"` | `loop` | What happens past the ends: `loop` continues seamlessly where the layout allows, `wrap` jumps to the other end, `stop` disables the matching control at each end. |
| `indicators` | `boolean` | - | Adding indicators at the bottom of the carousel for each item. |
| `interval` | `number` | `5000` | The amount of time to delay between automatically cycling an item. |
| `keyboard` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the carousel should react to ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keys. |
| `onSlid` | `((active: number, direction: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when a slide transition end. |
| `onSlide` | `((active: number, direction: string) => void)` | - | Callback fired when a slide transition starts. |
| `pause` | `boolean \| "hover"` | `hover` | If set to 'hover', pauses the cycling of the carousel on mouseenter and resumes the cycling of the carousel on mouseleave. If set to false, hovering over the carousel won't pause it. |
| `pauseLabel` | `string` | `Pause carousel` | `aria-label` of the play/pause control while autoplay is running. |
| `playLabel` | `string` | `Play carousel` | `aria-label` of the play/pause control while autoplay is stopped. |
| `playPause` | `boolean` | - | Render a play/pause control so users can stop an autoplaying carousel (WCAG 2.2.2). |
| `transition` | `"slide" \| "crossfade"` | - | Set type of the transition. |
| `variableWidth` | `boolean` | - | Let each slide keep its own width instead of the computed track fraction. |

## CCarouselCaption

```jsx
import { CCarouselCaption } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |

## CCarouselItem

```jsx
import { CCarouselItem } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `interval` | `number` | - | The amount of time to delay between automatically cycling this item. |

# React Carousel Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Carousel component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

React Carousel is styled entirely through CSS variables set on `.carousel`, so every part of it — layout, controls, indicators, captions — can be restyled at runtime via `style` or your stylesheets.

```scss
$carousel-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-carousel-items: 1,
    --cui-carousel-items-gap: 0px,
    --cui-carousel-items-peek: 0px,
    --cui-carousel-fade-duration: .6s,
    --cui-carousel-fade-timing: ease,
    --cui-carousel-control-color: light-dark(var(--cui-white), var(--cui-black)),
    --cui-carousel-control-width: 15%,
    --cui-carousel-control-opacity: .5,
    --cui-carousel-control-hover-opacity: .9,
    --cui-carousel-control-transition: opacity .15s ease,
    --cui-carousel-control-icon-width: 2rem,
    --cui-carousel-control-prev-icon: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 16 16'><path d='M11.354 1.646a.5.5 0 0 1 0 .708L5.707 8l5.647 5.646a.5.5 0 0 1-.708.708l-6-6a.5.5 0 0 1 0-.708l6-6a.5.5 0 0 1 .708 0'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-carousel-control-next-icon: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 16 16'><path d='M4.646 1.646a.5.5 0 0 1 .708 0l6 6a.5.5 0 0 1 0 .708l-6 6a.5.5 0 0 1-.708-.708L10.293 8 4.646 2.354a.5.5 0 0 1 0-.708'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-carousel-control-pause-icon: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 16 16'><path d='M5.5 3.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 7 5v6a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-3 0V5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1 1.5-1.5m5 0A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 12 5v6a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-3 0V5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1 1.5-1.5'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-carousel-control-play-icon: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 16 16'><path d='m11.596 8.697-6.363 3.692c-.54.313-1.233-.066-1.233-.697V4.308c0-.63.692-1.01 1.233-.696l6.363 3.692a.802.802 0 0 1 0 1.393z'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-carousel-play-pause-size: 2.5rem,
    --cui-carousel-play-pause-icon-width: 1rem,
    --cui-carousel-play-pause-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-black) 25%, transparent),
    --cui-carousel-indicator-active-bg: light-dark(var(--cui-white), var(--cui-black)),
    --cui-carousel-indicator-progress-bg: var(--cui-carousel-indicator-active-bg),
    --cui-carousel-indicator-width: 30px,
    --cui-carousel-indicator-height: 3px,
    --cui-carousel-indicator-hit-area-height: 10px,
    --cui-carousel-indicator-spacer: 3px,
    --cui-carousel-indicator-opacity: .5,
    --cui-carousel-indicator-active-opacity: 1,
    --cui-carousel-indicator-transition: opacity .6s ease,
    --cui-carousel-indicators-margin-bottom: 1rem,
    --cui-carousel-caption-color: light-dark(var(--cui-white), var(--cui-black)),
    --cui-carousel-caption-width: 70%,
    --cui-carousel-caption-padding-y: 1.25rem,
    --cui-carousel-caption-spacer: 1.25rem,
  ),
  $carousel-tokens
);
```

### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-carousel-items': 3,
  '--cui-carousel-items-gap': '.5rem',
}

return <CCarousel style={customVars}>{/* Carousel items */}</CCarousel>
```

# React Bootstrap Carousel Component

> Discover how to use the React Bootstrap Carousel component from CoreUI to build responsive, customizable image and content sliders with indicators, captions, and transitions.

## How the React Bootstrap Carousel component works

The React Bootstrap Carousel component is a responsive slideshow for cycling through a set of images, text, or custom HTML content. It supports controls, indicators, captions, transitions, and responsive behavior out of the box.

The component also supports the [Page Visibility API](https://www.w3.org/TR/page-visibility/), ensuring slides don’t transition when the browser tab is inactive.

## React Bootstrap Carousel examples

### Slides only

Basic React Bootstrap Carousel with no controls or indicators.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselSlidesOnlyExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### With controls

Add `controls` prop to include previous/next navigation arrows.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

export const CarouselWithControlsExample = () => {
  return (
    <CCarousel controls>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### With indicators

Include slide indicators alongside the navigation arrows for better user interaction.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCarousel, CCarouselItem, CImage } from '@coreui/react'

  return (
    <CCarousel controls indicators>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/react.jpg'} alt="slide 1" />

      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/vue.jpg'} alt="slide 2" />
      </CCarouselItem>
      <CCarouselItem>
        <CImage className="d-block w-100" src={'/assets/img/angular.jpg'} alt="slide 3" />
      </CCarouselItem>
    </CCarousel>
  )
}
```

### With captions

Enhance each carousel slide with a caption using the `<CCarouselCaption>` component. Use responsive utility classes like `.d-none` and `.d-md-block` to control visibility across devices.

```html
          <p>Some representative placeholder content for the third slide.</p>
        </CCarouselCaption>
      </CCarouselItem>

  )
}
```
