
### Narrow visibility helpers

Use the sidebar visibility helpers to swap content between regular, narrow, and narrow-unfoldable variants:

- `.d-sidebar-narrow` shows content only in the narrow state.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-none` hides content in the narrow state.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-unfoldable` shows content only when the sidebar uses the unfoldable variant.
- `.d-sidebar-narrow-unfoldable-none` hides content when the sidebar uses the unfoldable variant.

### Sizes

The default width is `--cui-sidebar-width`. Set `size="sm"`, `size="lg"` or `size="xl"` for the other widths from the `$sidebar-widths` map; each size also sets the space the sidebar reserves for the content next to it, so the layout follows the width.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CSidebar, CSidebarNav, CNavItem } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarSizeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CSidebar className="border-end" size="lg">
      <CSidebarNav>
        <CNavItem active href="#">
          <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilSpeedometer} /> Dashboard
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Components
        </CNavItem>
      </CSidebarNav>
    </CSidebar>
  )
}
```

## Navigation

Use `CSidebarNav` as the main navigation container inside a sidebar. It supports plain links, section titles, nested groups, tree navigation, compact navigation, and custom group indicators.

### Basic navigation

Use the following building blocks inside `CSidebarNav`:

- `<CNavTitle>` for section headings.
- `<CNavItem>` for each navigation entry.
- `<CNavLink>` for standalone navigation links.
- `CIcon` with `customClassName="nav-icon"` for optional leading icons.
- `<CBadge>` or utility classes such as `ms-auto` for trailing metadata.

### Navigation groups

Use `<CNavGroup>` for expandable navigation sections. The `toggler` prop defines the clickable label, and nested `CNavItem` or `CNavGroup` components become the group content.

Set `defaultShow` on `CNavGroup` when the group should be expanded by default; `show` is the controlled form — see [Controlled and uncontrolled groups](#controlled-and-uncontrolled-groups).

Use the `compact` prop on `CNavGroup` to reduce spacing only for that nested group.

### Compact navigation

Add the `compact` prop to `CSidebarNav` to reduce the vertical padding across the entire navigation.

Use the `compact` prop on `CNavGroup` to compact only a nested section.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CSidebar, CSidebarNav, CNavGroup, CNavItem, CNavTitle } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilLayers, cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarCompactExample = () => {
  return (
    <CSidebar className="border-end">
      <CSidebarNav compact>
        <CNavTitle>Compact nav</CNavTitle>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilSpeedometer} /> Dashboard
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilLayers} /> Components
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Nested group
            </>
          }
          defaultShow
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Compact item</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Compact item</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CSidebarNav>
    </CSidebar>
  )
}
```

### Tree navigation

Add `variant="tree"` to `CSidebarNav` to render nested groups as a tree. Nested groups automatically keep their hierarchy, making deeper navigation levels easier to scan.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CSidebar, CSidebarNav, CNavGroup, CNavItem } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilFolder } from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarTreeExample = () => {
  return (
    <CSidebar className="border-end">
      <CSidebarNav variant="tree">
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilFolder} /> Parent item
            </>
          }
          defaultShow
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">
            <span className="nav-icon">
              <span className="nav-icon-bullet"></span>
            </span>{' '}
            Child item
          </CNavItem>
          <CNavGroup
            toggler={
              <>
                <span className="nav-icon">
                  <span className="nav-icon-bullet"></span>
                </span>{' '}
                Nested group
              </>
            }
            defaultShow
          >
            <CNavItem href="#">
              <span className="nav-icon">
                <span className="nav-icon-bullet"></span>
              </span>{' '}
              Nested child
            </CNavItem>
            <CNavItem href="#">
              <span className="nav-icon">
                <span className="nav-icon-bullet"></span>
              </span>{' '}
              Nested child
            </CNavItem>
          </CNavGroup>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CSidebarNav>
    </CSidebar>
  )
}
```

### Group indicator

By default, `CNavGroup` renders the standard group indicator through the `.nav-group-toggle` styles, so no additional markup is required.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CSidebar, CSidebarNav, CNavGroup, CNavItem } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilPuzzle } from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarGroupIndicatorExample = () => {
  return (
    <CSidebar className="border-end">
      <CSidebarNav>
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Items group
            </>
          }
          defaultShow
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CSidebarNav>
    </CSidebar>
  )
}
```

### Custom group indicator

To replace the default indicator, pass custom indicator markup inside the `toggler` prop using a `.nav-group-toggle-indicator` element. The `toggler` prop can also be a render function, which receives `{ visible }` so you can swap icons yourself.

Use `.show` and `.hide` classes inside `.nav-group-toggle-indicator` to control which icon is visible when the group is expanded or collapsed, or render a single icon conditionally from the `visible` state.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CSidebar, CSidebarNav, CNavGroup, CNavItem } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import {
  cilChevronCircleDownAlt,
  cilChevronCircleUpAlt,
  cilMinus,
  cilPlus,
  cilPuzzle,
} from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarCustomIndicatorExample = () => {
  return (
    <CSidebar className="border-end">
      <CSidebarNav>
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={({ visible }) => (
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Items group
              <span className="nav-group-toggle-indicator">
                <CIcon className="icon icon-sm" icon={visible ? cilMinus : cilPlus} />
              </span>
            </>
          )}
          defaultShow
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={({ visible }) => (
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Alternate indicator
              <span className="nav-group-toggle-indicator">
                <CIcon
                  className="icon icon-sm"
                  icon={visible ? cilChevronCircleUpAlt : cilChevronCircleDownAlt}
                />
              </span>
            </>
          )}
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Items group item</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
      </CSidebarNav>
    </CSidebar>
  )
}
```

### Controlled and uncontrolled groups

_Added in 6.0.0._

`CNavGroup` works uncontrolled by default — clicking the toggler expands and collapses it, and `defaultShow` seeds the group expanded on mount.

```jsx
<CNavGroup toggler="Components" defaultShow>
```

_Added in 6.0.0._

To control a group from the parent, set `show` and handle `onShowChange`. `show` is purely controlled: the group renders what the prop says, and the toggler — or an accordion close request when a sibling opens — only requests a change through `onShowChange`, so the parent has the final say. `onShowChange` fires in both modes.

This makes it possible to keep a section open even when the user clicks to collapse it—useful for a route-aware sidebar that must keep the active section expanded. Toggle the lock and try to collapse the group: while locked, the parent rejects the change and the group stays open.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CNavGroup, CNavItem, CSidebar, CSidebarFooter, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilCloudDownload, cilLayers, cilPuzzle, cilSettings, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarControlledGroupExample = () => {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true)
  const [locked, setLocked] = useState(true)

  const handleVisibleChange = (value: boolean) => {
    if (!value && locked) {
      return
    }

    setVisible(value)
  }

  return (
    <CSidebar className="border-end">
      <CSidebarNav>
        <CNavItem href="#">
          <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilSpeedometer} /> Dashboard
        </CNavItem>
        <CNavGroup
          onShowChange={handleVisibleChange}
          toggler={
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Active section
            </>
          }
          visible={visible}
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Overview</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Settings</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilLayers} /> Components
            </>
          }
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Base</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Buttons</CNavItem>
          <CNavGroup
            toggler={
              <>
                <span className="nav-icon">
                  <span className="nav-icon-bullet"></span>
                </span>{' '}
                Forms
              </>
            }
          >
            <CNavItem href="#">Inputs</CNavItem>
            <CNavItem href="#">Selects</CNavItem>
          </CNavGroup>
        </CNavGroup>
        <CNavGroup
          toggler={
            <>
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilSettings} /> Settings
            </>
          }
        >
          <CNavItem href="#">Profile</CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">Security</CNavItem>
        </CNavGroup>
        <CNavItem href="https://coreui.io">
          <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilCloudDownload} /> Download CoreUI
        </CNavItem>
      </CSidebarNav>
      <CSidebarFooter className="border-top">
        <CButton theme="primary" size="sm" onClick={() => setLocked(!locked)}>
          {locked ? 'Unlock collapsing' : 'Lock the active section open'}
        </CButton>
      </CSidebarFooter>
    </CSidebar>
  )
}
```

## Theme variants

Add a [`.theme-{color}` class](https://coreui.io/react/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) to the sidebar and it paints its surface, text, icons and the hover and active links from that color's slots — the background from `--cui-theme-bg`, the text from `--cui-theme-contrast`, the hovered and active links from `--cui-theme-hover` and `--cui-theme-active`.             <CNavItem href="https://coreui.io/pricing/">
```html
              <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilLayers} /> Try CoreUI <strong>PRO</strong>
            </CNavItem>
          </CSidebarNav>
          <CSidebarFooter className="border-top d-flex">
            <CSidebarToggler />
          </CSidebarFooter>
        </CSidebar>
      ))}
    </>
  )
}
```

## Placement

By default, placement for sidebar components is on the left side of the viewport, but you can change it with the `placement` prop:

- `placement="start"` places the sidebar on the left side of the viewport.
- `placement="end"` places the sidebar on the right side of the viewport.

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

The sidebar works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode.

| | prop | who owns the open state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uncontrolled | `defaultShow` | the sidebar, from that starting point |
| Controlled | `show` | your component |

`onShowChange` fires in **both** modes whenever the sidebar requests an open-state change — a close gesture (the mobile backdrop click, an outside click or a nav link selection on mobile) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle. The deprecated `visible` prop keeps its old behavior and is ignored when `defaultShow` or `show` is set.

### Uncontrolled

Seed the starting state and let the sidebar manage itself — on mobile it still closes on the backdrop click.

```jsx
<CSidebar defaultShow={false}>
```

### Controlled

Pass `show` and the sidebar renders what you pass — close gestures only call `onShowChange`, so feed the change back, or nothing closes. This is the classic app-shell case: a header toggler owns the state, and the sidebar follows.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CNavItem, CNavTitle, CSidebar, CSidebarNav } from '@coreui/react'

import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import { cilCloudDownload, cilPuzzle, cilSpeedometer } from '@coreui/icons'

export const SidebarControlledExample = () => {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(true)

  return (
    <div className="d-flex align-items-start">
      <CSidebar className="border-end" show={show} onShowChange={setShow}>
        <CSidebarNav>
          <CNavTitle>Navigation</CNavTitle>
          <CNavItem href="#">
            <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilSpeedometer} /> Dashboard
          </CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="#">
            <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilPuzzle} /> Components
          </CNavItem>
          <CNavItem href="https://coreui.io">
            <CIcon customClassName="nav-icon" icon={cilCloudDownload} /> Download CoreUI
          </CNavItem>
        </CSidebarNav>
      </CSidebar>
      <CButton className="m-4" theme="primary" onClick={() => setShow(!show)}>
        {show ? 'Hide sidebar' : 'Show sidebar'}
      </CButton>
    </div>
  )
}
```

# React Sidebar Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Sidebar component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

## CSidebar

```jsx
import { CSidebar } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `(ElementType & "symbol") \| (ElementType & "object") \| (ElementType & "div") \| (ElementType & "slot") \| (ElementType & "style") \| ... 175 more ...` | `div` | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `colorScheme` | `'dark' \| 'light'` | - | Pin the sidebar to one color scheme whatever the page uses, so a dark navigation column can sit on a light page. |
| `defaultShow` | `boolean` | - | The initial open state of an uncontrolled sidebar — read once on mount. |
| `narrow` | `boolean` | - | Make sidebar narrow. |
| `onHide` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the component requests to be hidden. |
| `onInViewportChange` | `((inViewport: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the sidebar enters or leaves the viewport — the sidebar is off-canvas on narrow screens, so this reports whether it is on screen, not the `show` state. |
| `onShow` | `(() => void)` | - | Callback fired when the component requests to be shown. |
| `onShowChange` | `((show: boolean) => void)` | - | Callback fired when the sidebar requests an open-state change — a close gesture (the mobile backdrop click, an outside click or a nav link selection on mobile) or, in uncontrolled mode, any internal toggle. In controlled mode update `show` yourself, or the sidebar stays as it is. |
| `onVisibleChange` | `((visible: boolean) => void)` | - | Event emitted after visibility of component changed. |
| `overlaid` | `boolean` | - | Set sidebar to overlaid variant. |
| `placement` | `'start' \| 'end'` | - | Components placement, there’s no default placement. |
| `position` | `"fixed" \| "sticky"` | - | Place sidebar in non-static positions. |
| `show` | `boolean` | - | Control the open state. When set, the sidebar renders what `show` says and close gestures — the mobile backdrop click, an outside click or a nav link selection on mobile — only call `onShowChange`; nothing closes until the parent flips the prop. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | - | Size the component small, large, or extra large. |
| `unfoldable` | `boolean` | - | Expand narrowed sidebar on hover. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the visibility of sidebar component. |

# React Sidebar Component Styling

> Learn how to customize the React Sidebar component with CSS classes, variables, and Sass for flexible styling and seamless integration into your design.

## CSS variables

React sidebars use local CSS variables on `.sidebar` and `.sidebar-backdrop` for enhanced real-time customization. Values for the CSS variables are set via Sass, so Sass customization is still supported, too.

```scss
$sidebar-tokens: () !default;
$sidebar-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-sidebar-zindex: var(--cui-z-sidebar),
    --cui-sidebar-width: #{$sidebar-width},
    --cui-sidebar-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-sidebar-padding-x: #{$sidebar-padding-x},
    --cui-sidebar-padding-y: #{$sidebar-padding-y},
    --cui-sidebar-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-sidebar-brand-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-sidebar-transition: #{margin-left .15s, margin-right .15s, box-shadow .075s, transform .15s, width .15s, z-index 0s ease .15s},
    --cui-sidebar-toggler-height: .5rem,
  ),
  $sidebar-tokens
);
```

```scss
$sidebar-overlaid-tokens: () !default;
$sidebar-overlaid-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-sidebar-overlaid-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
```

### How to use CSS variables

```jsx
const customVars = {
  '--cui-sidebar-bg': '#121212',
  '--cui-sidebar-color': '#eee',
}

return <CSidebar style={customVars}>{/* Sidebar content */}</CSidebar>
```

## Sass variables

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Sass variables set these defaults at build time and are removed in v7. The CSS variables above reach the same values without recompiling, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
$sidebar-width:                            16rem !default;
$sidebar-padding-y:                        var(--cui-spacer) !default;
$sidebar-padding-x:                        var(--cui-spacer) !default;
```

## Sass maps

Each entry is one `.sidebar-{width}` class and the width it sets — on the sidebar itself and on the space it reserves for the content next to it. Add a key to define a width, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
$sidebar-widths: (
  sm: 12rem,
  lg: 20rem,
  xl: 24rem
) !default;
```

# React Bootstrap Sidebar Component

> Learn how to use the React Bootstrap Sidebar component from CoreUI to build customizable side navigation panels with support for branding, dropdowns, dark mode, and responsive behavior.

## React Bootstrap Sidebar Component

The React Bootstrap Sidebar component provides a flexible vertical navigation layout with support for branding, navigation links, toggling, and theming. It’s perfect for admin panels, dashboards, and mobile navigation.

## Supported sub-components

The sidebar includes built-in support for these components:

- `<CSidebarHeader>` – optional top section.
- `<CSidebarBrand>` – brand or logo section.
- `<CSidebarNav>` – main vertical navigation area.
- `<CSidebarFooter>` – optional bottom section.
- `<CSidebarToggler>` – toggler for sidebar minimization or expansion.

## React Bootstrap Sidebar examples

## Sidebar placement

By default, the React Bootstrap Sidebar appears on the left. Use the `placement` prop to change this:

- `placement="start"` – left side (default)
- `placement="end"` – right side

# React Smart Pagination Component

> Documentation and examples for showing smart pagination to indicate a series of related content exists across multiple pages.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Overview

React smart pagination component consists of button-like styled links, that are arranged side by side in a horizontal list.

We use a large block of connected links for our pagination, making links hard to miss and easily scalable—all while providing large hit areas. SmartPagination is built with list HTML elements so screen readers can announce the number of available links. SmartPagination also use a wrapping `<nav>` element to identify it as a navigation section to screen readers and other assistive technologies.

In addition, as pages likely have more than one such navigation section, SmartPagination provide a descriptive `aria-label` for the `<nav>` to reflect its purpose. For example, if the pagination component is used to navigate between a set of search results, an appropriate label could be `aria-label="Search results pages"`.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartPaginationExample = () => {
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)
  return (
    <CSmartPagination activePage={currentPage} pages={10} onActivePageChange={setCurrentPage} />
  )
}
```

## Features

- Determine behavior, style and functionality of pagination
- Smart automatic items generation

## Working with icons

The four navigation buttons take their content from `firstButton`, `previousButton`, `nextButton` and `lastButton`. A string is rendered as HTML — that is where the default `&laquo;` and friends come from — so pass a node instead to put an icon there.

Mark the icon `aria-hidden`: the buttons already carry their own accessible names, and an icon announced on top of them would read twice.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import CIcon from '@coreui/icons-react'
import {
  cilChevronDoubleLeft,
  cilChevronDoubleRight,
  cilChevronLeft,
  cilChevronRight,
} from '@coreui/icons'

export const SmartPaginationIconsExample = () => {
  const [activePage, setActivePage] = useState(3)

  return (
    <CSmartPagination
      activePage={activePage}
      pages={10}
      onActivePageChange={setActivePage}
      doubleArrows
      firstButton={<CIcon icon={cilChevronDoubleLeft} aria-hidden="true" />}
      previousButton={<CIcon icon={cilChevronLeft} aria-hidden="true" />}
      nextButton={<CIcon icon={cilChevronRight} aria-hidden="true" />}
      lastButton={<CIcon icon={cilChevronDoubleRight} aria-hidden="true" />}
    />
  )
}
```

## Sizing

Fancy larger or smaller pagination? Add `size="lg"` or `size="sm"` for additional sizes.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartPaginationSizingLargeExample = () => {
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)
  return (
    <CSmartPagination
      size="lg"
      activePage={currentPage}
      pages={10}
      onActivePageChange={setCurrentPage}
    />
  )
}
```

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartPaginationSizingSmallExample = () => {
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)
  return (
    <CSmartPagination
      size="sm"
      activePage={currentPage}
      pages={10}
      onActivePageChange={setCurrentPage}
    />
  )
}
```

## Alignment

Change the alignment of pagination components with `align="start"`, `align="center"` or `align="end"`.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartPaginationAlignmentCenterExample = () => {
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)
  return (
    <CSmartPagination
      align="center"
      activePage={currentPage}
      pages={10}
      onActivePageChange={setCurrentPage}
    />
  )
}
```

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartPaginationAlignmentEndExample = () => {
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)
  return (
    <CSmartPagination
      align="end"
      activePage={currentPage}
      pages={10}
      onActivePageChange={setCurrentPage}
    />
  )
}
```

# React Smart Pagination Component API

> Explore the API reference for the React Smart Pagination component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CSmartPagination

```jsx
import { CSmartPagination } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activePage` | `number` | `1` | Current page number. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `start` | Horizontall align. |
| `arrows` | `boolean` | `true` | Show/hide arrows. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `dots` | `boolean` | `true` | Show/hide dots. |
| `doubleArrows` | `boolean` | `true` | Show double arrows buttons. |
| `firstButton` | `ReactNode` | `<React.Fragment>&laquo;</React.Fragment>` | The content of `firstButton` button. |
| `lastButton` | `ReactNode` | `<React.Fragment>&raquo;</React.Fragment>` | The content of `lastButton` button. |
| `limit` | `number` | `5` | Maximum items number. |
| `nextButton` | `ReactNode` | `<React.Fragment>&rsaquo;</React.Fragment>` | The content of `nextButton` button. |
| `onActivePageChange` | `((activePage: number) => void)` | - | On active page change callback. |
| `pages` | `number` | - | Number of pages. |
| `previousButton` | `ReactNode` | `<React.Fragment>&lsaquo;</React.Fragment>` | The content of `previousButton` button. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size of pagination, valid values: 'sm', 'lg'. |


---

# React Smart Table Component (DataTable)

> A React Smart Table provides a full set of features for displaying and manipulating tabular data. It allows you to easily create dynamic and interactive tables with features such as sorting, filtering, pagination, and searching. React Smart Table Component (DataTables) makes it easy to work with large datasets, and it is widely used in a variety of applications, including web-based applications, e-commerce sites, and more.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Features

- Filter items by one or all columns
- Sort items by column
- Integrated with CPagination component by default
- Customize style of specific rows, columns and cells
- Customize display of columns
- Load with initial filters and sorter state
- Loading state visualization
- Default header labels generation based on column names

## Usage

Here is an example of how to create a basic DataTable:

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CAvatar, CBadge, CButton, CCollapse } from '@coreui/react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Item } from '@coreui/react-pro/components/smart-table/types'

const getBadge = (status: string) => {
  switch (status) {
    case 'Active': {
      return 'success'
    }
    case 'Inactive': {
      return 'secondary'
    }
    case 'Pending': {
      return 'warning'
    }
    case 'Banned': {
      return 'danger'
    }
    default: {
      return 'primary'
    }
  }
}

export const SmartTableExample = () => {
  const [details, setDetails] = useState<number[]>([])
  const columns = [
    {
      key: 'avatar',
      label: '',
      filterable: false,

      key: 'name',
      headerStyle: { width: '20%' },
    },
    {
      key: 'registered',
      sorter: (item1: Item, item2: Item) => {
        const a = new Date(item1.registered)
        const b = new Date(item2.registered)
        return a > b ? 1 : b > a ? -1 : 0
      },
    },
    {
      key: 'role',
      headerStyle: { width: '20%' },
    },
    'status',
    {
      key: 'show_details',

    {

          <td>
            <CBadge theme={getBadge(item.status)}>{item.status}</CBadge>
          </td>
        ),
        show_details: (item: Item) => {
          return (
            <td className="py-3">
              <CButton
                theme="primary"
                variant="outline"
                shape="square"
                size="sm"
                onClick={() => {
                  toggleDetails(item.id)
                }}
              >
                {details.includes(item.id) ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}
              </CButton>
            </td>
          )
        },
        details: (item) => {
          return (
            <CCollapse show={details.includes(item.id)}>
              <div className="p-4">
                <h4>{item.name}</h4>
                <p className="fg-2">User since: {item.registered}</p>
                <CButton size="sm" theme="info">
                  User Settings
                </CButton>
                <CButton size="sm" theme="danger" className="ms-1">
                  Delete
                </CButton>
              </div>
            </CCollapse>
          )
        },
      }}
      selectable
      defaultSorterValue={[{ column: 'status', direction: 'asc' }]}
      globalFilter
      tableProps={{
        className: 'add-this-custom-class',
        responsive: true,
        striped: true,
        hover: true,
      }}
      tableBodyProps={{
        className: 'align-middle',
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

## Custom layout

_Added in 6.0.0._

Without children `<CSmartTable>` renders the layout above — the global filter and the cleaner over the table, the pagination and the items per page select under it. Pass children and that layout is not rendered at all: the table becomes a state provider and you place the parts yourself, in any order, next to your own markup.

| part | renders |
| --- | --- |
| `` | the global filter input with its label — `label` and `placeholder` override `globalFilterLabel` and `globalFilterPlaceholder` |
| `` | the button that resets the filters and the sorter — `ariaLabel` and `icon` override `ariaCleanerLabel` and `cleanerIcon` |
| `` | the table itself: header, body, footer and the loading cover — `tableProps`, `tableHeadProps`, `tableBodyProps` and `tableFootProps` override the props of the same name |
| `` | the pagination bound to the active page — it takes every `CSmartPagination` prop and falls back to `paginationProps` |
| `` | the items per page select with its label — `label` and `options` override `itemsPerPageLabel` and `itemsPerPageOptions` |

The `globalFilter`, `cleaner`, `itemsPerPageSelect` and `pagination` props keep configuring the state, so leave the ones you use set; a placed part renders wherever you put it. `pagination` still decides whether the items are cut into pages.

`useSmartTableContext()` reads the same state, so a part of your own is a component that calls it — here a row counter:

```jsx
const RowCounter = () => {
  const { activePage, currentItems, totalItems, totalPages } = useSmartTableContext()

  return (
    <span>
      {currentItems.length} of {totalItems} rows, page {activePage} of {totalPages}
    </span>
  )
}
```

It returns the same state `useSmartTable()` builds: `activePage`, `itemsPerPage`, `itemsPerPageOptions`, `globalFilterValue`, `columnFilterValue`, `sorterValue`, `selected`, `items` (filtered and sorted), `currentItems` (the page), `totalItems`, `totalPages`, `loading`, a setter for each piece of the state (`setActivePage`, `setItemsPerPage`, `setGlobalFilterValue`, `setColumnFilterValue`, `setSorterValue`, `setSelected`) and `clean()`, which resets the filters and the sorter.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCol, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import {
  CSmartTable,
  CSmartTableCleaner,
  CSmartTableContent,
  CSmartTableFilter,
  CSmartTableItemsPerPage,
  CSmartTablePagination,
  useSmartTableContext,
} from '@coreui/react-pro'

const RowCounter = () => {
  const { activePage, currentItems, totalItems, totalPages } = useSmartTableContext()

  return (
    <span className="fg-2">
      {currentItems.length} of {totalItems} rows, page {activePage} of {totalPages}
    </span>
  )
}

export const SmartTableCustomLayoutExample = () => {
  const columns = [
    {
      key: 'name',
      headerStyle: { width: '40%' },
    },
    'registered',
    'role',
  ]
  const items = [
    { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2017/01/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 7, name: 'Avram Tarasios', registered: '2016/02/12', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 8, name: 'Quintin Ed', registered: '2023/01/21', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 9, name: 'Enéas Kwadwo', registered: '2024/03/10', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 10, name: 'Agapetus Tadeáš', registered: '2015/01/10', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 11, name: 'Carwyn Fachtna', registered: '2014/04/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 12, name: 'Nehemiah Tatius', registered: '2013/01/05', role: 'Staff' },
  ]

  return (
    <CSmartTable
      cleaner
      columns={columns}
      columnSorter
      defaultItemsPerPage={5}
      globalFilter
      items={items}
      itemsPerPageSelect
      pagination

      <CRow className="align-items-center mb-4">
        <CCol xs="auto" className="me-auto">
          <CSmartTableItemsPerPage label="Show:" />

          <CSmartTableFilter label="" placeholder="Search a user..." />
        </CCol>
        <CCol xs="auto">
          <CSmartTableCleaner />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
      <CSmartTableContent />
      <CRow className="align-items-center">
        <CCol xs="auto" className="me-auto">
          <RowCounter />
        </CCol>
        <CCol xs="auto">
          <CSmartTablePagination />
        </CCol>
      </CRow>
    </CSmartTable>
  )
}
```

## Column groups

The React Smart Table component allows users to group related columns under a common header. This can be useful when displaying data that has multiple categories or when comparing different sets of data. A group is a column entry that carries a `label` and its `children`. When the Smart Table is rendered, the header group will be displayed as a single header cell that spans the width of the columns included in the group. The group header cells feature can help to make the Smart Table component more organized and easier to read by grouping related data together and making it more visually distinct from other columns.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartTableColumnGroupsExample = () => {
  const columns = [
    {
      label: 'Group 1',
      children: [
        {
          label: 'Subgroup 1',
          children: [
            {
              label: 'Subgroup 1A',
              children: [
                {
                  key: 'name',
                  headerStyle: { width: '20%' },
                },
                'registered',
              ],
            },
            {
              label: 'Subgroup 1B',
              children: [{ key: 'role', headerStyle: { width: '20%' } }],
            },
          ],
        },
        {
          label: 'Subgroup 2',
          children: [
            {
              label: 'Subgroup 2A',
              children: [{ key: 'status', headerStyle: { width: '20%' } }],
            },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ]
  const items = [
    {
      id: 0,
      name: 'John Doe',
      registered: '2022/01/01',
      role: 'Guest',
```

## Column sorter

The column sorter feature enables sorting React.js table data by column values. You can enable sorting by adding `columnSorter` to `<CSmartTable>`. If you want to disable sorting for a specific column, add `sortable: false` to the desired column.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CAvatar } from '@coreui/react'
```

### Sort multiple columns

Enables sorting by multiple columns simultaneously by adding `columnSorter={{ multiple: true }}` The sorting order will be maintained across multiple columns based on the order of user interaction. This means you can sort by multiple columns, and each column will keep its order.

```jsx
<CSmartTable
  columns={[...]}
  columnSorter={{ multiple: true }}
  items={[...]}
/>
```

### Resettable sorter state

When `columnSorter={{ resettable: true }}` is set, clicking the sorter toggles through three states: ascending, descending, and unsorted. After the third click, it resets the sorting, returning the table to its initial state.

```jsx
<CSmartTable
  columns={[...]}
  columnSorter={{ resettable: true }}
  items={[...]}
/>
```

### Custom sorter

By default, sorting is done automatically by the component and works as expected when the values in the column are of a single data type: either string (case-insensitive) or number.

In case you want to sort non-string and non-number data, define a custom sorting function for the column. You can use this option to control how the values are compared and sorted. The function receives two arguments (`a`, `b`) corresponding to two row values and must return:

- a negative value if `a` should appear before `b`,
- zero if `a` and `b` are equal,
- a positive value if `a` should appear after `b`.

```jsx
<CSmartTable
  columns={[
    ...
    {
      key: 'registered',
      sorter: (date1, date2) => {
        const a = new Date(date1.registered)
        const b = new Date(date2.registered)
        return a > b ? 1 : b > a ? -1 : 0
      }
    },
    ...
  ]}
  items={[...]}
/>
```

### Custom filters

CoreUI React Smart Table (React DataTables) provides the ability to use custom filtering functions. Custom filters offer advanced filtering capabilities. You can define and integrate custom filtering logic by adding a `filter` function to the desired column, enabling more complex data filtering strategies.

#### Date Range Picker

Here is an example of how you might use the `` component to apply custom filters to a React DataTable component:

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CDateRangePicker, CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Item, Column } from '@coreui/react-pro/components/smart-table/types'

export const SmartTableCustomFilterDateRangePickerExample = () => {
  const items = [
    { id: 0, name: 'John Doe', registered: '2022/01/01' },
    {
      id: 1,
      name: 'Samppa Nori',
      registered: '2022/01/01',
    },
    {
      id: 2,
      name: 'Estavan Lykos',
      registered: '2022/02/07',
    },
    { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2022/02/07' },
    {
      id: 4,
      name: 'Derick Maximinus',
      registered: '2022/03/19',
    },
    { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/01/21' },
    { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2022/01/01' },
    {
      id: 7,
      name: 'Avram Tarasios',
      registered: '2022/02/07',
    },
    { id: 8, name: 'Quintin Ed', registered: '2022/02/07' },
    { id: 9, name: 'Enéas Kwadwo', registered: '2022/03/19', role: 'Member', status: 'Pending' },
    { id: 10, name: 'Agapetus Tadeáš', registered: '2022/01/21' },
    { id: 11, name: 'Carwyn Fachtna', registered: '2022/01/01' },
    { id: 12, name: 'Nehemiah Tatius', registered: '2022/02/07' },
    { id: 13, name: 'Ebbe Gemariah', registered: '2022/02/07' },
    {
      id: 14,
      name: 'Eustorgios Amulius',
      registered: '2022/03/19',
    },
    { id: 15, name: 'Leopold Gáspár', registered: '2022/01/21' },
    { id: 16, name: 'Pompeius René', registered: '2022/01/01' },
    { id: 17, name: 'Paĉjo Jadon', registered: '2022/02/07' },
    {
      id: 18,
      name: 'Micheal Mercurius',
      registered: '2022/02/07',
    },
    {
      id: 19,
      name: 'Ganesha Dubhghall',
      registered: '2022/03/19',
    },
    { id: 20, name: 'Hiroto Šimun', registered: '2022/01/21' },
    { id: 21, name: 'Vishnu Serghei', registered: '2022/01/01' },
    { id: 22, name: 'Zbyněk Phoibos', registered: '2022/02/07' },
    {
      id: 23,
      name: 'Aulus Agmundr',
      registered: '2022/01/01',
    },
    {
      id: 42,
      name: 'Ford Prefect',
      registered: '2022/05/25',
    },
  ]
  const [startDate, setStartDate] = useState(new Date('2022-01-21'))
  const [endDate, setEndDate] = useState(new Date('2022-02-07'))
  const minDate = new Date(Math.min(...items.map((element) => Date.parse(element.registered))))
  const maxDate = new Date(Math.max(...items.map((element) => Date.parse(element.registered))))
  const columns: Column[] = [
    {
      key: 'name',
      headerStyle: { width: '50%' },
    },
    {
      key: 'registered',
      headerStyle: { width: '50%' },
      filter: (_, onChange) => {
        return (
          <CDateRangePicker
            footer
            size="sm"
            startDate={startDate}
            endDate={endDate}
            minDate={minDate}
            maxDate={maxDate}
            onStartDateChange={(date: Date) => {
              setStartDate(date)
              onChange((value: string) => {
                if (date) {
                  const itemDate = new Date(Date.parse(value))
                  return endDate ? itemDate >= date && itemDate <= endDate : itemDate >= date
                }
                return true
              })
            }}
            onEndDateChange={(date: Date) => {
              setEndDate(date)
              onChange((value: string) => {
                if (date) {
                  const itemDate = new Date(Date.parse(value))
                  return startDate ? itemDate <= date && itemDate >= startDate : itemDate <= date
                }
                return true
              })
            }}
          />
        )
      },
    },
  ]
  const convertToDate = (date: string) => {
    const _date = new Date(Date.parse(date))
    return _date.toLocaleDateString()
  }
  return (
    <CSmartTable
      columns={columns}
      columnFilter
      defaultColumnFilterValue={{
        registered: (date: string) =>
          new Date(Date.parse(date)) >= startDate && new Date(Date.parse(date)) <= endDate,
      }}
      columnSorter
      items={items}
      itemsPerPageSelect
      defaultItemsPerPage={5}
      pagination
      scopedColumns={{
        registered: (item: Item) => <td>{convertToDate(item.registered)}</td>,
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

#### Multi Select

Here is an example of how you might use the `` component to apply custom filters to a React DataTable:

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CMultiSelect, CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Column } from '@coreui/react-pro/components/smart-table/types'

export const SmartTableCustomFilterMultiSelectExample = () => {

    {
      key: 'name',
      headerStyle: { width: '50%' },

      key: 'role',
```

## Selection

Add `selectable` to render a checkbox in every row and a select-all checkbox in the header; `selectAll={false}` leaves out the header one. The selection is a list of items — seed it with `defaultSelected` or own it with `selected` and `onSelectedChange` — and `onRowChecked` reports the single row the user just toggled. A row with `_selectable: false` in the data cannot be checked, and select-all skips it. Set `itemKey` so the selection matches rows by that property instead of by the whole object, which keeps a selected row selected across a re-fetch.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { Item } from '@coreui/react-pro/components/smart-table/types'

export const SmartTableSelectionExample = () => {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Item[]>([{ id: 2 }])

  const items = [
    { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin', _selectable: false },
    { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      <p className="fg-2">
        Selected: {selected.length > 0 ? selected.map((item) => item.id).join(', ') : 'none'}
      </p>
      <CSmartTable
        columns={['name', 'registered', 'role']}
        itemKey="id"
        items={items}
        onRowChecked={(item, checked) => console.log(item, checked)}
        onSelectedChange={(items) => setSelected(items)}
        selectAll
        selectable
        selected={selected}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Loading

`loading` dims the table, marks it as `aria-busy` and covers the body; `loadingContent` replaces what the cover shows.

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CButton, CSpinner } from '@coreui/react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartTableLoadingExample = () => {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)

  const items = [
    { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      <CButton
        className="mb-4"
        onClick={() => {
          setLoading(true)
          setTimeout(() => setLoading(false), 2000)
        }}
      >
        Reload
      </CButton>
      <CSmartTable
        columns={['name', 'registered', 'role']}
        itemKey="id"
        items={items}
        loading={loading}
        loadingContent={
          <div className="d-flex align-items-center gap-3">
            <CSpinner size="sm" />
            Fetching users...
          </div>
        }
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Data sources

You can use Fetch API to load data from different sources and then pass them to `<CSmartTable>`

### External Data (10.000+ records)

One of the key features of React Smart Table (React DataTables) is the ability to load data from an external source, such as an API or a server-side script.
This can be useful if you have a large amount of data that you don't want to load all at once. To load external data into a React Smart Table (React DataTables), you can use the Fetch API to the data source.

Set `external` when the items arrive already filtered, sorted and sliced by the data source. The table then renders `items` as they are and only reports the requested state through the callbacks, while `totalItems` tells it how many records there are in total, so it can compute the number of pages.

Here is an example of how you might use React Smart Table with external data:

```html
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'

import type { ColumnFilterValue, SorterValue } from '@coreui/react-pro/components/smart-table/types'

export const SmartTableExternalDataExample = () => {
  const [activePage, setActivePage] = useState(3)
  const [columnFilter, setColumnFilter] = useState<ColumnFilterValue>({})
  const [columnSorter, setColumnSorter] = useState<SorterValue[]>([
    { column: 'country', direction: 'asc' },
  ])
  const [itemsPerPage, setItemsPerPage] = useState(10)
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const [users, setUsers] = useState([])
  const [records, setRecords] = useState(0)

  const columns = [
    { key: 'first_name', headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' } },
    { key: 'last_name', headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' } },
    'email',
    { key: 'country', headerStyle: { minWidth: '120px' } },
    { key: 'ip_address', label: 'IP' },
  ]

  useEffect(() => {
    const fetchData = async () => {
      try {
        setLoading(true)
        const offset = (activePage - 1) * itemsPerPage
        const params = new URLSearchParams()

        Object.keys(columnFilter).forEach((key) => {
          params.append(key, columnFilter[key])
        })

        if (columnSorter[0]) {
          params.append('sort', `${columnSorter[0].column}%${columnSorter[0].direction}`)
        }

        const response = await fetch(
          `https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?offset=${offset}&limit=${itemsPerPage}&${params}`
        )

        const result = await response.json()

        setRecords(result.number_of_matching_records)
        setUsers(result.number_of_matching_records ? result.records : [])
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Error fetching users:', error)
        setUsers([]) // Optionally show an error state
      } finally {
        setLoading(false)
      }
    }

    fetchData()
  }, [activePage, columnFilter, columnSorter, itemsPerPage])

  return (
    <CSmartTable
      activePage={activePage}
      columns={columns}
      columnFilter
      columnSorter
      external
      footer
      items={users}
      itemsPerPage={itemsPerPage}
      itemsPerPageSelect
      loading={loading}
      pagination
      sorterValue={columnSorter}
      tableProps={{
        hover: true,
        responsive: true,
      }}
      totalItems={records}
      onActivePageChange={(page) => setActivePage(page)}
      onColumnFilterChange={(filter) => {
        setActivePage(1)
        setColumnFilter(filter)
      }}
      onItemsPerPageChange={(pageSize) => {
        setActivePage(1)
        setItemsPerPage(pageSize)
      }}
      onSorterChange={(value: SorterValue[]) => setColumnSorter(value)}
    />
  )
}
```

### JSON (10.000+ records)

The Fetch API can be used to load JSON data by making a GET request to the endpoint where the data is located.
In this example, the `fetch()` method is used to make a GET request to the endpoint `https://apitest.coreui.io/fake_data/users.json`, which returns a response.
The `response.json()` method is then used to parse the response as a JSON object.
The resulting JSON object is stored in the `users` and loaded by ``.

```html
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartTableJSONDataExample = () => {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const [users, setUsers] = useState([])

  const columns = [
    { key: 'first_name', headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' } },
    { key: 'last_name', headerStyle: { minWidth: '130px' } },
    'email',
    { key: 'country', headerStyle: { minWidth: '120px' } },
    { key: 'ip_address', label: 'IP' },
  ]

  useEffect(() => {
    const fetchData = async () => {
      try {
        setLoading(true)
        const response = await fetch('https://apitest.coreui.io/fake_data/users.json')
        const result = await response.json()
        setUsers(result)
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Error fetching user data:', error)
        setUsers([]) // Optionally handle error state
      } finally {
        setLoading(false)
      }
    }

    fetchData()
  }, [])

  return (
    <CSmartTable
      columns={columns}
      columnFilter
      columnSorter
      footer
      items={users}
      itemsPerPageSelect
      loading={loading}
      pagination
      tableProps={{
        hover: true,
        responsive: true,
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

_Added in 6.0.0._

Every piece of the table's state works either way, and the prop you reach for is what picks the mode — independently for each piece.

| controlled prop | uncontrolled seed | change callback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activePage` | `defaultActivePage` | `onActivePageChange` |
| `columnFilterValue` | `defaultColumnFilterValue` | `onColumnFilterChange` |
| `globalFilterValue` | `defaultGlobalFilterValue` | `onGlobalFilterChange` |
| `itemsPerPage` | `defaultItemsPerPage` | `onItemsPerPageChange` |
| `selected` | `defaultSelected` | `onSelectedChange` |
| `sorterValue` | `defaultSorterValue` | `onSorterChange` |

The callbacks fire with the requested state in **both** modes when the user acts — so you can watch a state without taking it over. Passing a new value into a controlled prop does **not** echo its own callback back at you.

A `default*` prop seeds the state once, on mount, and the table manages it from there:

```jsx
<CSmartTable columnSorter defaultSorterValue={[{ column: 'name', direction: 'asc' }]} items={items} />
```

Pass the controlled prop and the table renders exactly what you pass — an interaction only fires the callback, and nothing moves until you feed the change back. That includes the page clamp: when the items shrink below the current page, an uncontrolled table jumps to page one itself, while a controlled one only requests it through `onActivePageChange(1)`. Here the parent owns the active page and the sorter:

```html
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'
import type { SorterValue } from '@coreui/react-pro/components/smart-table/types'

export const SmartTableControlledExample = () => {
  const [activePage, setActivePage] = useState(1)
  const [sorterValue, setSorterValue] = useState<SorterValue[]>([
    { column: 'name', direction: 'asc' },
  ])

  const items = [
    { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2017/01/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 7, name: 'Avram Tarasios', registered: '2016/02/12', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 8, name: 'Quintin Ed', registered: '2023/01/21', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 9, name: 'Enéas Kwadwo', registered: '2024/03/10', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 10, name: 'Agapetus Tadeáš', registered: '2015/01/10', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 11, name: 'Carwyn Fachtna', registered: '2014/04/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 12, name: 'Nehemiah Tatius', registered: '2013/01/05', role: 'Staff' },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      <p className="fg-2">
        Page {activePage}, sorted by <code>{sorterValue[0].column}</code> (
        {sorterValue[0].direction})
      </p>
      <CSmartTable
        activePage={activePage}
        columns={['name', 'registered', 'role']}
        columnSorter
        defaultItemsPerPage={5}
        items={items}
        onActivePageChange={setActivePage}
        onSorterChange={(value: SorterValue[]) => setSorterValue(value)}
        pagination
        sorterValue={sorterValue}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Headless

_Added in 6.0.0._

`useSmartTable(options)` is the state behind the component — the filters, the sorter, the pages and the selection — with no markup of its own. Call it with the state props you would pass to `<CSmartTable>` and render whatever you like from what it returns; here a list of cards instead of a table.

```jsx
const { activePage, currentItems, globalFilterValue, setActivePage, setGlobalFilterValue, totalPages } =
  useSmartTable({ defaultItemsPerPage: 3, globalFilter: true, itemKey: 'id', items, pagination: true })
```

The options are the state props of `CSmartTable`: `items`, `columns`, `itemKey`, `columnFilter`, `columnSorter`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, `external`, `totalItems`, `itemsPerPageOptions`, every controlled and uncontrolled pair (`activePage` / `defaultActivePage` / `onActivePageChange` and the five others) and `onFilteredItemsChange`. Controlled and uncontrolled work exactly as they do on the component.

Next to the state and its setters you get the selection helpers — `isSelected(item)`, `toggle(item)`, `toggleAll()` and `selectedAll`, which is `true`, `false` or `'indeterminate'` — so a checkbox of your own is one call each way.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CCard, CCardBody, CCardText, CCardTitle, CCol, CFormInput, CRow } from '@coreui/react'
import { CSmartPagination, useSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'

export const SmartTableHeadlessExample = () => {
  const items = [
    { id: 1, name: 'Samppa Nori', registered: '2021/03/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Estavan Lykos', registered: '2018/02/07', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 3, name: 'Chetan Mohamed', registered: '2020/01/15', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 4, name: 'Derick Maximinus', registered: '2019/04/05', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 5, name: 'Friderik Dávid', registered: '2022/03/25', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 6, name: 'Yiorgos Avraamu', registered: '2017/01/01', role: 'Member' },
    { id: 7, name: 'Avram Tarasios', registered: '2016/02/12', role: 'Staff' },
    { id: 8, name: 'Quintin Ed', registered: '2023/01/21', role: 'Admin' },
    { id: 9, name: 'Enéas Kwadwo', registered: '2024/03/10', role: 'Member' },
  ]

  const {
    activePage,
    currentItems,
    globalFilterValue,
    setActivePage,
    setGlobalFilterValue,
    totalItems,
    totalPages,
  } = useSmartTable({
    defaultItemsPerPage: 3,
    globalFilter: true,
    itemKey: 'id',
    items,
    pagination: true,
  })

  return (
    <>
      <CFormInput
        aria-label="Search a user"
        className="mb-4"
        onChange={(event) => setGlobalFilterValue(event.target.value)}
        placeholder="Search a user..."
        value={globalFilterValue}
      />
      <CRow className="g-4">
        {currentItems.map((item) => (
          <CCol key={item.id as number} md={4}>
            <CCard>
              <CCardBody>
                <CCardTitle>{item.name as string}</CCardTitle>
                <CCardText className="fg-2">
                  {item.role as string} · {item.registered as string}
                </CCardText>
              </CCardBody>
            </CCard>
          </CCol>
        ))}
      </CRow>
      <div className="d-flex align-items-center justify-content-between mt-4">
        <span className="fg-2">{totalItems} users</span>
        <CSmartPagination
          activePage={activePage}
          onActivePageChange={setActivePage}
          pages={totalPages}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  )
}
```

# React Smart Table Component (DataTable) API

> Explore the API reference for the React Smart Table component and discover how to effectively utilize its props for customization.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=react&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## CSmartTable

```jsx
import { CSmartTable } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activePage` | `number` | - | The controlled active page. Pair it with `onActivePageChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultActivePage` instead. Only applicable when `pagination` prop is enabled. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | `string` | `Clear filters and sorting` | A string that provides an accessible label for the cleaner button. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. |
| `ariaSelectAllLabel` | `string` | `Select all rows` | A string that provides an accessible label for the checkbox that selects every row. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the checkbox. |
| `ariaSelectRowLabel` | `string` | `Select row` | A string that provides an accessible label for the checkbox that selects a single row. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the checkbox. |
| `cleaner` | `boolean` | - | When set, displays a button above the table that resets `globalFilterValue`, `columnFilterValue` and `sorterValue`, next to the global filter. The button is disabled when there is nothing to reset. |
| `cleanerIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor" > <path d="M40 16v37.828L109.024 136h41.791L76.896 48H459.51L304 242.388v158.985L241.373 464H240v-96h-32v128h46.627L336 414.627V253.612l160-200V16z" /> <path d="m166.403 248.225 60.461-60.462-22.627-22.628-60.462 60.462-60.462-60.462-22.626 22.628 60.461 60.462-60.461 60.462 22.626 22.627 60.462-60.462 60.462 60.462 22.627-22.627z" /> </svg> )` | The icon of the cleaner button. |
| `clickableRows` | `boolean` | - | Style table items as clickable. |
| `columnFilter` | `boolean \| ColumnFilter` | - | When set, displays additional filter row between table header and items, allowing filtering by specific column. Column filter can be customized, by passing prop as object with additional options as keys. Available options: - lazy (Boolean) - Set to true to trigger filter updates only on change event. |
| `columnFilterValue` | `ColumnFilterValue` | - | The controlled column filter values. Pair it with `onColumnFilterChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultColumnFilterValue` instead. To set pass object where keys are column names and values are filter strings e.g.: `{ user: 'John', age: 12 }` |
| `columns` | `(string \| Column \| ColumnGroup)[]` | - | Table columns configuration. When omitted, the columns are generated from the keys of the first item, skipping the keys that begin with an underscore. Each array item is either a column name, a column object or a group of columns: - `key` (required)(String) - the name of the item property the column displays. - `label` (String) - the visible label of the column. When omitted, it is generated from `key` by splitting kebab-case and snake_case into words and capitalizing each of them. - `sortable` (Boolean) - set to `false` to exclude the column from sorting. - `sorter` (Function) - a custom comparator for the column, called with two items. - `filterable` (Boolean) - set to `false` to remove the filter from the column. - `filter` (Function) - a custom filter for the column, called with the column values, a change handler and the current filter state. - `headerStyle` (Object) - inline styles for the column header (useful for defining widths). - `headerProps` (Object) - properties for the column header cell. - `cellStyle` (Object) - inline styles for every data cell in the column. - `cellProps` (Object) - properties for every data cell in the column. - `children` (Array) - columns grouped under one header; a group carries `label` and `children` only. |
| `columnSorter` | `boolean \| Sorter` | - | Enables table sorting by column value. Sorting will be performed corectly only if values in column are of one type: string (case insensitive) or number. Sorter can be customized, by passing prop as object with additional options as keys. Available options: - multiple (Boolean) - Enables sorting by multiple columns simultaneously. The sorting order will be maintained across multiple columns based on the order of interaction. - resettable (Boolean) - If set to true, clicking on the sorter cycles through three states: ascending, descending, and null (no sorting). The third click on the sorter will reset the sorting and restore the table to its original order. |
| `defaultActivePage` | `number` | - | The initial active page for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `activePage` is set. |
| `defaultColumnFilterValue` | `ColumnFilterValue` | - | The initial column filter values for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `columnFilterValue` is set. |
| `defaultGlobalFilterValue` | `string` | - | The initial global filter value for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `globalFilterValue` is set. |
| `defaultItemsPerPage` | `number` | - | The initial number of items per page for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `itemsPerPage` is set. |
| `defaultSelected` | `Item[]` | - | The initial selected items for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `selected` is set. |
| `defaultSorterValue` | `SorterValue[]` | - | The initial sorter state for the uncontrolled mode. Ignored when `sorterValue` is set. |
| `external` | `boolean` | - | The items are already filtered, sorted and sliced by the data source, so the table renders them as they are and only reports the requested state through the callbacks. Use `totalItems` to let it compute the number of pages. |
| `footer` | `boolean \| (string \| FooterItem)[]` | - | If `true` Displays table footer, which mirrors table header. (without column filter). Or Array of objects or strings, where each element represents one cell in the table footer. Example items: `['FooterCell', 'FooterCell', 'FooterCell']` or `[{ label: 'FooterCell', props: { theme: 'success' }, ...]` |
| `globalFilter` | `boolean \| GlobalFilter` | - | When set, displays a filter input above the table that filters the items by the values of all columns. The global filter can be customized, by passing prop as object with additional options as keys. Available options: - lazy (Boolean) - Set to true to trigger filter updates only on change event. |
| `globalFilterLabel` | `string` | `Filter:` | The element represents a caption for the global filter input. |
| `globalFilterPlaceholder` | `string` | `type string...` | Specifies a short hint that is visible in the global filter input. |
| `globalFilterValue` | `string` | - | The controlled value of the global filter. Pair it with `onGlobalFilterChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultGlobalFilterValue` instead. |
| `header` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to false to remove table header. |
| `itemKey` | `string` | - | The name of the item property that identifies a row. When set, selection and row keys compare that value instead of the whole item. |
| `items` | `Item[]` | `[]` | Array of objects, where each object represents one item - row in table. Additionally, you can add style classes to each row by passing them by '_props' key and to single cell by '_cellProps'. Example item: `{ name: 'John' , age: 12, _props: { theme: 'success' }, _cellProps: { age: { className: 'fw-bold'}}}` |
| `itemsPerPage` | `number` | - | The controlled number of items per page. Pair it with `onItemsPerPageChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultItemsPerPage` instead. Only applicable when `pagination` is enabled. |
| `itemsPerPageLabel` | `string` | `Items per page:` | Label for items per page selector. |
| `itemsPerPageOptions` | `number[]` | `[5, 10, 20, 50]` | Items per page selector options. |
| `itemsPerPageSelect` | `boolean` | - | Adds select element over table, which is used for control items per page in pagination. Only applicable when `pagination` is enabled. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | - | When set, table will have loading style: loading spinner and reduced opacity. |
| `loadingContent` | `ReactNode` | - | The content of the cover displayed over the table while `loading` is set. |
| `noItemsLabel` | `ReactNode` | `No items found` | ReactNode or string for passing custom noItemsLabel texts. |
| `onActivePageChange` | `((value: number) => void)` | - | Page change callback. |
| `onColumnFilterChange` | `((value: ColumnFilterValue) => void)` | - | Column filter change callback. |
| `onFilteredItemsChange` | `((items: Item[]) => void)` | - | Filtered items change callback. |
| `onGlobalFilterChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | - | Global filter change callback. |
| `onItemsPerPageChange` | `((value: number) => void)` | - | Pagination change callback. |
| `onRowChecked` | `((item: Item, value: boolean) => void)` | - | Row checked callback. |
| `onRowClick` | `((item: Item, index: number, columnName: string, event: MouseEvent<Element, MouseEvent>) => void)` | - | Row click callback. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `((items: Item[]) => void)` | - | Selected items change callback. |
| `onSorterChange` | `((value: SorterValue[]) => void)` | - | Sorter value change callback. |
| `pagination` | `boolean` | - | Enables default pagination. The number of pages is generated from the number of items and `itemsPerPage`; with `external` set it is generated from `totalItems` instead. |
| `paginationProps` | `CSmartPaginationProps` | - | Properties to `CSmartPagination` component - https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/smart-pagination#csmartpagination |
| `scopedColumns` | `ScopedColumns` | - | Scoped columns. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | - | Add checkboxes to make table rows selectable. |
| `selectAll` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables select all checkbox displayed in the header of the table. |
| `selected` | `Item[]` | - | The controlled selected items — array of objects, where each object represents one item - row in table. Pair it with `onSelectedChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultSelected` instead. Example item: `{ name: 'John' , age: 12 }` |
| `sortAscendingIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor" > <path d="M390.624 150.625 256 16 121.376 150.625l22.628 22.627 95.997-95.998v417.982h32V77.257l95.995 95.995z" /> </svg> )` | Sorter icon when items are sorted ascending. |
| `sortDescendingIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor" > <path d="m367.997 338.75-95.998 95.997V17.503h-32v417.242l-95.996-95.995-22.627 22.627L256 496l134.624-134.623z" /> </svg> )` | Sorter icon when items are sorted descending. |
| `sorterValue` | `SorterValue[]` | - | The controlled state of the sorter. Pair it with `onSorterChange`; for the uncontrolled mode use `defaultSorterValue` instead. Each entry names a column and the direction, `'asc'` or `'desc'`. |
| `sortNeutralIcon` | `ReactNode` | `( <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor" > <path d="M384 433.373V160h-32v274.51l-69.823-69.823-22.627 22.626 107.882 107.883 107.881-107.883-22.626-22.626zM159.432 17.372 51.55 125.255l22.627 22.627L144 78.059V352h32V79.195l68.687 68.687 22.626-22.627z" /> </svg> )` | Sorter icon when items are unsorted. |
| `tableBodyProps` | `CTableBodyProps` | - | Properties to `CTableBody` component - https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/table/#ctablebody |
| `tableFootProps` | `CTableFootProps` | - | Properties to `CTableFoot` component - https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/table/#ctablefoot |
| `tableHeadProps` | `CTableHeadProps` | - | Properties to `CTableHead` component - https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/table/#ctablehead |
| `tableProps` | `CTableProps` | - | Properties to `CTable` component - https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/table/#ctable |
| `totalItems` | `number` | - | The total number of items. Use it when you pass a portion of the data from an external source to let the component know how many items there are in total. |

## CSmartTableCleaner

```jsx
import { CSmartTableCleaner } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the active state for the component. With `toggle` it is the controlled active state of the toggle button. For the uncontrolled toggle use `defaultActive`; manage the controlled state from `onClick`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | - | A string that provides an accessible label for the cleaner button. Defaults to `ariaCleanerLabel` of `CSmartTable`. |
| `as` | `ElementType` | - | Component used for the root node. Either a string to use a HTML element or a component. |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the base component. |
| `color` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. |
| `defaultActive` | `boolean` | - | The initial active state of an uncontrolled toggle button — read once on mount. Ignored when `active` is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `href` | `string` | - | The href attribute specifies the URL of the page the link goes to. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon of the cleaner button. Defaults to `cleanerIcon` of `CSmartTable`. |
| `iconOnly` | `boolean` | - | Square the button for a lone icon - remember to give it an `aria-label`. |
| `link` | `boolean` | - | Render the button as a link. It behaves like a button but takes its color from the link color rather than from a theme, so `theme` and `variant` do not apply to it. |
| `role` | `string` | - | The role attribute describes the role of an element in programs that can make use of it, such as screen readers or magnifiers. |
| `shape` | `'rounded' \| 'rounded-top' \| 'rounded-end' \| 'rounded-bottom' \| 'rounded-start' \| 'rounded-circle' \| 'rounded-pill' \| 'rounded-0' \| 'rounded-1' \| 'rounded-2' \| 'rounded-3' \| string` | - | Select the shape of the component. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component extra small, small or large. |
| `theme` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'info' \| 'inverse' \| string` | - | Sets the color context of the component to one of CoreUI’s themed colors. Pair it with `variant` for the shape — a button is a shape plus a colour. The class may also sit on any ancestor, so theming a toolbar themes the buttons inside it. |
| `toggle` | `boolean` | - | Make the button behave as a toggle button. It manages its own active/pressed state, toggling it on click and reflecting it via the `aria-pressed` attribute. |
| `type` | `"button" \| "submit" \| "reset"` | - | Specifies the type of button. Always specify the type attribute for the `<button>` element. Different browsers may use different default types for the `<button>` element. |
| `variant` | `"ghost" \| "outline" \| "solid" \| "subtle"` | - | Set the shape of the button — how much ink it uses. Defaults to `solid` when `theme` is set. |
