- **New: `hiddenUntilFound`** hides the collapsed area with `hidden="until-found"` rather than
  taking it out of the layout, so find-in-page searches it and the browser expands it on a match.
  `onShow` fires when that happens — set `visible` from it, or the stylesheet hides the content the
  reader was just sent to. Off by default; the attribute is left off entirely below Chrome 102 /
  Firefox 148 / Safari 26.2.

### CConditionalPortal

- **`CConditionalPortal` resolves its target while rendering.** It used to render its children in
  place for one commit and then teleport them, which remounted the subtree and dropped any focus
  those children had taken.

### CContextMenu

- **New component.** `<CContextMenu>` is the trigger area: a right-click, or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> /
  the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key while it has focus, opens the `<CMenuContent>` inside it at the pointer
  and suppresses the browser's own menu. It is a `CMenu` positioned against the pointer with
  `position: fixed`, so items, submenus, keyboard navigation and `autoClose` are the Menu's. Focus
  moves into the menu on open and returns to the area on close; the page does not scroll while
  the menu is open. A row's own `onContextMenu` handler runs first — call `preventDefault()` there
  to keep both menus closed.

### CDateInput, CDateRangeInput, CTimeInput

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **A required field blocks the form.** The value
  moved from an `<input type="hidden">`, which the browser leaves out of validation, to a `<textarea>`
  laid invisibly over the field, with `tabIndex={-1}` and `aria-hidden="true"`; a textarea, unlike a
  text input, leaves Enter submitting a form that has no submit button. A `required` field that is
  empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date now stops the submit, and the browser puts focus on its
  first empty section with its own message over the field. The field marks itself invalid whenever a
  validation reports it, also outside a submit, and its value field fires native `input` and
  `change` events when the date changes, which `onInput` on a form sees and React's `onChange` does
  not. This applies to the pickers and to both ends of a date range as well. Code that
  selects `input[type="hidden"]` inside the field needs `.form-date-time > textarea`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **A given state is a verdict on one value.**
  `validationState="invalid"` now blocks the submit, with the text of the message after the field,
  until it is cleared. The user's next change of the value and a native form reset call
  `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` before the change is reported, so pass your state setter
  there; a value your code sets keeps the state. Without a given state the field shows what a
  validation reports and, in a form with `validate`, the `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` states of
  its value field, as a native field does. `aria-invalid` sits on the sections, not on the group,
  and an `aria-invalid` you pass is not read as a state. This applies to the pickers and to both
  ends of a date range as well.

### CDatePicker, CDateRangePicker, CTimePicker

The pickers are no longer monoliths. Each is a composition of a **section field**, a **calendar or
time selection**, and an **anchored panel** — which is what removes most of the props below: the
field and the panel are now the same primitives you can use directly.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CDatePicker` is its own component.** In v5
  it was a thin wrapper over `CDateRangePicker` and inherited its props; it now has its own,
  single-date API (`date`, `defaultDate`, `onDateChange`).
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The button-configuration props are gone** —
  `todayButton`, `todayButtonColor`, `todayButtonSize`, `todayButtonVariant`, `cancelButton*`,
  `confirmButton*` and `rangesButtons*`. Project the content instead: the `footer` prop takes a
  node, or a function receiving the picker's context, so a button you render yourself can act on
  the picker and read its state. The same context is available to any descendant through
  `useDatePicker()`, `useDateRangePicker()` and `useTimePicker()`.

  ```jsx
  <CDatePicker
    footer={({ today, clear, close, isDateSelectable }) => (
      <>
        <CButton disabled={!isDateSelectable(new Date())} onClick={() => isDateSelectable(new Date()) && today()} size="sm">Today</CButton>
        <CButton onClick={clear} size="sm">Clear</CButton>
        <CButton onClick={close} size="sm">OK</CButton>
      </>
    )}
  />
  ```

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CDateRangePicker`: `ranges` is a projected
  region too.** It takes a node or a function receiving the context, so a preset button calls
  `setRange` with its own dates; `rangesButtonsColor`/`-Size`/`-Variant` are gone with it. The
  controlled range is `startDate`/`endDate` (with `defaultStartDate`/`defaultEndDate` for the
  uncontrolled mode), and the two fields take `startName`/`endName`.
- **A picker action shows its date in the calendar.** `setRange`, `reset`, `setDate` and `today`
  from the picker's context turn the calendar to the date they set (a range's start, else its end)
  in the view it is in, also when the value does not change and over a `calendarDate` you pass, so a
  preset clicked again after browsing brings its range back. `clear` and an invalid date leave the
  calendar where it is; a typed date, a picked time and the dates you pass move it as before.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **A date field is submitted only once you name
  it.** `CDatePicker` and `CDateRangePicker` built the name of their inputs from `id` when `name`
  was absent, so `` posted `delivery-date` and the range posted
  `delivery-start-date` / `delivery-end-date`. That fallback was deprecated in 5.3.0 and is gone:
  an `id` names the element for a label, it does not put the value in the payload. Pass `name`, or
  `startName`/`endName`, for the field to reach the server.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The field props are gone**:
  `inputDateFormat`, `inputOnChangeDelay`, `inputReadOnly`, `placeholder`, `separator`. The value
  is a mask now — pass `format` (or a section layout) and, for the placeholder text, one prop
  per section — `dayPlaceholder`, `monthPlaceholder`, `yearPlaceholder` and the rest. The
  range placeholder also named the two fields; `CDateRangePicker` names them with
  `ariaStartLabel` and `ariaEndLabel` now ("Start date" and "End date" by default), or with
  `floatingLabels` when set. Use `readOnly` for a read-only control and `separatorIcon` for the
  artwork between the two range fields.
- **Kept.** `timepicker` still adds the time half to `CDatePicker`, now as a row of time selects
  under the calendar rather than a second panel beside it. Because the two halves own different
  parts of one value, a picker with time does not auto-close: picking a day keeps the time and
  picking a time keeps the day. `hours`, `minutes` and `seconds` narrow what the time half offers.
- **Changed.** With `timepicker`, a `minDate` or `maxDate` that carries a time of day bounds the
  time on its day: the time selects disable the hours, minutes and seconds before `minDate` or
  after `maxDate` there, a time the panel sets beyond the limit (the current time when that day is
  picked) moves to the limit, and a typed time beyond it marks the field invalid. A limit without a
  time of day covers its whole day.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`hours` is 0 to 23 in every locale.** v5 read
  the list and the filter in the column's cycle, so on a locale whose v5 columns were 12-hour (the
  ones that write AM and PM in Latin letters, such as `en-US`) `hours={[1, 3, 5, 7]}` meant 1, 3, 5
  and 7 in the morning and in the afternoon, `12` meant noon and midnight, and a filter received 1
  to 12. The 12-hour column still lists 1 to 12 next to AM/PM, but each entry now stands for the
  24-hour hours the list allows: picking an hour that only one period allows sets that period, and
  the period the picked hour does not allow is disabled. To keep such a list, name both halves:
  `hours={[1, 3, 5, 7, 13, 15, 17, 19]}`, with `0` and `12` for `12`. More locales get 12-hour
  columns than in v5, because the columns follow the field's clock, Korean, Traditional Chinese,
  Arabic and Mexican Spanish among them; their v5 columns were 24-hour, so a list written for them
  keeps its meaning. The day period column also speaks the locale, 오전 and 오후 in Korean, where it
  read "AM" and "PM". A longer name widens its column, so `--cui-time-picker-cell-width` is now the
  narrowest a cell gets, and `--cui-time-picker-cell-padding-x` keeps the name off the cell's edges.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The time picker's roll classes lose the `roll`
  infix, and the date picker's time controls carry its own name.** `.time-picker-roll-col` and
  `.time-picker-roll-cell` are `.time-picker-col` and `.time-picker-cell`, with
  `--cui-time-picker-col-*` and `--cui-time-picker-cell-*` in place of their `-roll-` spellings;
  `.time-picker-roll` was always present on `.time-picker-body`, so it is gone rather than renamed,
  and `--cui-time-picker-body-padding` went with it. `.time-picker-inline-icon` and
  `.time-picker-inline-select` are `.date-picker-time-icon` and `.date-picker-time-select`, with
  `--cui-date-picker-time-*` tokens, because they belong to the date picker's panel. Custom CSS
  written against any of these names needs the new one.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CTimePicker`: `variant` is gone.** Each
  picker has one time rendering — the time picker shows the roll, and the date picker's time half
  shows the selects, which is what v5 rendered inside a date picker with time. The selects ship in
  the date picker stylesheet, so a page that only uses the time picker no longer downloads them.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The time selection is one tab stop.**
  <kbd>Tab</kbd> reaches the body once, <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> and <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> move
  between the hour, minute, second and AM/PM parts and stop at the ends, and <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> /
  <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> change the focused value. Both renderings answer the same keys.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CTimePicker`: `ampm` is gone.** The hour
  cycle follows the field's mask when it names one (`HH` vs `hh a`) and the locale otherwise.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`closeOnSelect` and `previewDateOnHover` are
  gone.** A complete selection closes the panel unless a `footer` projects actions the user still
  needs.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`indicator` is gone.** The button that opens
  the panel is always rendered; `pickerIcon` replaces its artwork. The button that clears the
  value is the one you can switch off, with `cleaner`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The v1 shell class names are gone**:
  `date-picker-input`, `date-picker-input-wrapper`, `date-picker-input-preview`,
  `date-picker-cleaner`, `time-picker-input`, `time-picker-cleaner`, and the `-dropdown` panels are
  now `.date-picker-popup` / `.time-picker-popup`.
- **The panel is rendered through a portal by default** (`portal`), into `container` when given.
  It is built on the first open, not on mount.
- **New props across the family**: `cleaner` and `cleanerIcon`, `pickerIcon`, `disabled`,
  `visible`, `onShow`/`onHide`, `size`, and the accessible labels `ariaCleanerLabel` /
  `ariaPickerLabel`.
- **Pickers open on the platform's dropdown keys.** `Alt`+`ArrowDown` and `F4` open the panel and
  move focus into it — onto the selected date, else today or the `minDate` / `maxDate` today falls
  outside of, also when that date cannot be picked. The
  field's own arrows keep editing the value, as `<input type="date">` does. Opening with the mouse
  moves focus in too.

### CDropdown

- **Placements are mirrored once now, by Floating UI.** The `-start`/`-end` half of a placement is
  logical — Floating UI resolves it from the writing direction of the floating element — and the
  library was mirroring it a second time, which cancelled it. In a right-to-left context that moves
  every placement whose suffix you set: `alignment="end"` now hangs from the inline end, and an
  explicit `placement="bottom-start"` opens from the right edge instead of the left. The sides are
  the other way round: Floating UI never mirrors `left`/`right`, so a logical `start`/`end` side
  still maps to the physical one the direction asks for and `dropend`/`dropstart` still swap. Also
  in this change: a `dropup` aligned to the end keeps its side (it resolved to `bottom-end`
  before), `direction="center"` resolves to `bottom` rather than `bottom-start`, a submenu in a
  right-to-left context anchors to the top of its trigger rather than the bottom, and
  `useDropdownWithFloating` asks Floating UI for a plain `bottom-start`. `CMenu`, `CSubmenu`,
  `CContextMenu` and the picker panels all resolve a placement the same way. `CTooltip` and
  `CPopover` keep mirroring a physical `left`/`right` as a v5 compatibility fallback, which is
  removed in v7.
- **A panel sent through a portal carries the direction of its trigger.** Out in `document.body` it
  no longer inherits the direction that resolves the suffix, so it would have been laid out as
  left-to-right while its trigger sat in a `dir="rtl"` subtree. A `dir` you set yourself on the
  panel is left alone.
- **`CDropdown` is now a compatibility layer over `CMenu`.** The v5 markup, class names, props and
  callbacks keep working — the two share one engine underneath, so the dropdown also gained
  `Escape` closing regardless of `autoClose`. **Deprecation notice: `CDropdown` may be removed in
  v7** — prefer `CMenu` for new work.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> `popperConfig` → `floatingConfig`, see
  [Dependencies](#dependencies).

### CFocusTrap

- **`CFocusTrap`'s `additionalContainer` accepts an element**, not only a ref. A ref is read once,
  when the trap activates, which is too early for a panel that is built on open.

### CFooter

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CFooter` is removed.** It rendered a `.footer`
  class whose nine declarations utilities already cover, so a footer is plain markup now:
  `<footer className="d-flex flex-wrap align-items-center justify-content-between bg-3 border-top px-5 py-3">`.
  The `min-height: 3rem` floor has no utility — set it yourself where it matters, or pad with `py-4`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The `position` prop goes with it.** Use
  `.sticky-bottom` in place of `position="sticky"` (it pins the same way, on `--cui-z-sticky` rather
  than `--cui-z-fixed`) and `.fixed-bottom` in place of `position="fixed"`, which emitted a
  `.footer-fixed` class the PRO stylesheet has never defined.

### CForm

- **`validate` with `noValidate` validates the form on submit.** `<CForm>` stops an invalid submit
  (`onSubmit` runs only for a submit that goes through), marks the invalid controls with
  `.is-invalid` and `aria-invalid`, links the message of each to it with `aria-describedby` while it
  stays invalid, and moves focus to the first. A hand-written `onSubmit` that only called
  `checkValidity()` and `preventDefault()` can go. The new `onValidate` callback runs first; call
  `preventDefault()` on its argument to handle the result yourself.

### CFormCheck

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`hitArea` is removed.** It rendered the label
  as a `stretched-link` so a whole list group item would toggle the box; the list group item can
  be the label itself now — `<CListGroupItem as="label"> Text
  </CListGroupItem>` — which is what the stylesheet is written for.

### CFormFloating

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The placeholder shows once the field has
  focus.** It used to stay transparent in every state; it now appears under the floated label while
  the field, or the control inside a field component, has focus, and stays hidden while the label
  rests in the field. A `plainText` control keeps it hidden.
- **New: `always`** on `<CFormFloating>` and **`floatingLabelAlways`** on every form control that
  renders a floating label keep the label floated and the placeholder showing while the field is
  empty. See [Always floating](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating).

### CFormLabel

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`customClassName` is removed.** It was the one
  prop in the library that *replaced* `className` instead of adding to it, and only `CFormCheck` and
  `CFormSwitch` used it internally to render a label without `.form-label`; they render a plain
  `<label>` now. Pass `className` for extra classes; a label without the base class is a plain
  `<label>` element.

### CFormRange

- **Changed.** **A pressed thumb takes `--cui-primary-bg-muted`**, the theme's `bg-muted` under a
  `.theme-*` class, instead of a 30% tint of the primary color.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`<CFormRange>` renders a wrapper.** The input
  sits inside `<div class="form-range">` as `.form-range-input`; `className`, `style`, `theme`,
  `dir` and `hidden` land on the wrapper, which carries the tokens, while every other prop still
  reaches the input and `ref` still points at it. A `label` without an `id` gets a generated one, so
  the label names the input. The component writes `--cui-range-fill` (0–1) from the value, so the
  track fills up to the thumb, a shade lighter than it, in every browser. An uncontrolled range
  seeds from `defaultValue` (the native midpoint without it).
- **`tooltips` and `tooltipsFormat`** show the value above the thumb, on hover, drag and focus or
  `"always"`; **`ticks`** renders tick marks from an array of values, labels or `{ value, label,
  className, style }` objects, labels beneath. Both follow the vanilla `Range` plugin, which also
  reads a `<datalist>`, and share names with `<CRangeSlider>`. `onChange` gets the value as a
  number in its second argument, `onChange(event, value)`. Several handles, `distance`, clickable
  ticks and a vertical orientation are what `<CRangeSlider>` adds.

### CHeader

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`position` renders position utilities.**
  `position="sticky"` emits `.sticky-top` in place of `.header-sticky`, which the stylesheet no
  longer defines — the two rules were identical, so the header pins exactly as before.
  `position="fixed"` emits `.fixed-top`; the `.header-fixed` class it used to render was never
  defined anywhere, so that value had no effect at all. For the bottom variants, or a responsive
  one like `.sticky-md-top`, pass the utility through `className` instead.

### CInputGroup

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Validation feedback moves out of the group.**
  The `.has-validation` class is gone, and a group keeps its corner logic by having the control as
  its last child — a `CFormFeedback` left inside squares off the end of the control it belongs to.
  Wrap the group in a `CFormField` and put the feedback after it, so the message renders under the
  whole frame. Inside a group that means a standalone `CFormFeedback` rather than the `feedback`,
  `feedbackValid` or `feedbackInvalid` props, which render it next to the control.

  ```jsx
  <CFormField>
    <CInputGroup>
      <CInputGroupText>@</CInputGroupText>
      
    </CInputGroup>
    <CFormFeedback validationState="invalid">Please choose a username.</CFormFeedback>
  </CFormField>
  ```

### CLoadingButton

- **`spinnerType` is deprecated in favour of `spinnerVariant`** — the same word `CSpinner` uses for
  `border` / `grow`; the old name loses to the new one. `onClick` receives the click event, as on
  `CButton`, instead of nothing.
- **The spinner takes the button's font size.** It no longer asks `CSpinner` for `size="sm"` — a
  spinner is `1em` square in v6, so inside a button it already lands where the small size used to
  put it. Custom CSS targeting `.btn-loading-spinner.spinner-border-sm` or `.spinner-grow-sm` has
  nothing to match; the sizing classes are gone from that element.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`disabledOnLoading` no longer renders the
  `disabled` attribute.** A disabled button drops focus, so a keyboard or screen reader user who
  pressed it landed on the page body. While loading, the button now gets `aria-disabled="true"` and
  `.disabled`, keeps focus, and ignores clicks and form submission until it stops. CSS or tests that
  read `:disabled` on a loading button should read `[aria-disabled="true"]` instead.
- **The start and the end of loading are announced** when the button has focus: its name followed
  by the new `ariaLoadingLabel` prop, then its name again. The spinner no longer renders
  `role="status"` or the "Loading..." text that Safari read on an idle button; while loading it is
  a `role="img"` named by `ariaLoadingLabel`.

### CMenu

- **New: `custom` on `CMenuToggle`.** With it the single child element receives the toggle
  behaviour — `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, the click handler and the ref — and keeps its own
  markup and classes, instead of the toggle rendering a `CButton`. `CDropdownToggle` has carried
  the same prop since v4; this closes the gap in the component that replaces it.

### CModal, COffcanvas

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Both render a native `<dialog>`.** The
  browser provides the top layer, the `::backdrop`, focus trapping, background inertness and the
  dialog ARIA semantics, so the markup drops `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-hidden` and
  `tabIndex={-1}`, and the component no longer renders a backdrop, a focus trap or a portal of its
  own.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CModalDialog` and `CModalContent` are
  removed.** `.modal > .modal-dialog > .modal-content` flattens to a single
  `<dialog className="modal">` holding the header, body and footer directly. `CModal` rendered
  both for you, so markup written against the components is unchanged; custom CSS targeting those
  two classes is not.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`portal` and `container` are gone.** They
  existed to lift the modal out of a stacking context. A dialog opened with `showModal()` renders
  in the top layer, above every stacking context on the page, so there is nothing left to escape.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`focus` is gone** — a modal dialog always
  traps focus, and the option could only have turned off something the browser does.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`alignment` is gone** — the browser centers
  a modal dialog. `alignment="top"` has no replacement; a dialog that must sit at the top is a
  positioning override in your own CSS.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`.modal-dialog-scrollable` is
  `.modal-scrollable`**, and `.modal-backdrop` / `.offcanvas-backdrop` are gone with the elements
  they styled — the backdrop is the `::backdrop` pseudo-element, themed through
  `--cui-modal-backdrop-*` and `--cui-offcanvas-backdrop-*`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Animation opt-out is a class now.**
  `transition={false}` renders `.modal-instant` / `.offcanvas-instant` instead of dropping
  `.fade`; the offcanvas `.showing` state class is replaced by the native `open` attribute, and
  `.hiding` carries the exit.
- **New: `modal={false}` on `CModal`** opens the dialog non-modally, leaving the rest of the page
  interactive. **New: `animation` on `COffcanvas`.**
- **Scroll locking moved to the root element** — `dialog-open` with `scrollbar-gutter: stable`,
  instead of inline `overflow` and `padding-right` on the body.

### CNavGroup

- **The stylesheet owns the group animation where the browser can interpolate a size to `auto`.**
  `CNavGroup` no longer writes an inline `height`/`display` on `.nav-group-items`; the run is
  marked with `.collapsing` and the open state with `.show` on the group, and the duration and
  easing come from `--cui-sidebar-nav-group-items-transition-*`. Browsers without
  `interpolate-size` keep the measured path. Custom CSS keyed on the inline height needs updating.
- **A group that renders open no longer plays the opening animation on mount** — `defaultShow`,
  a controlled `show` and an active nav link all reveal the branch straight away.

### COneTimePassword

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Only `COneTimePassword`'s hidden input
  carries the field's `name`.** Each `COneTimePasswordInput` was given `<name>-<index>` on top of
  it, so a six-slot field submitted seven keys where the prop is documented as the name of the
  hidden input. The slots are unnamed now, and a `name` you pass to a slot is left alone instead of
  being overwritten.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The code is validated as one value.** It
  moved from an `<input type="hidden">`, which the browser leaves out of validation, to a text
  input laid invisibly over the group, with `tabIndex={-1}`, `aria-hidden="true"`, a `pattern` for
  the full length of the code and the `required` that the slots used to carry. A `required` code
  that is empty or incomplete stops the submit, so does an incomplete code that is not required,
  and the browser puts focus on the first empty slot. Once the browser reports the code, every slot
  carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message while the code stays invalid, as it already
  did for `validationState="invalid"`, and the stylesheet shows the message after the group, which
  it never did for a slot marked invalid. Code that selects `input[type="hidden"]` inside the field
  needs `.form-otp > input:not(.form-otp-control)`, and a `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` written on
  the slots goes on `COneTimePassword`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`COneTimePassword` blocks the submit while
  `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is `'invalid'`**, and asks to drop the state with
  `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` when the user changes the code or the form is reset. The
  state class moved from each `COneTimePasswordInput` to the `.form-otp` group, which the stylesheet
  colours as a whole, so CSS or tests keyed on `.form-otp-control.is-invalid` need
  `.form-otp.is-invalid`. An `aria-invalid` passed to the component or to a slot is no longer put on
  the group or the slot, the hidden input sends `input` and `change` whenever the code changes, also
  through `value`, and a native form reset puts back the code given by `defaultValue`. See
  [Validation](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/one-time-password-input/#validation).
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The `readOnly` prop is removed, and every slot is
  editable.** A code the user cannot type has no use in a form, so a `readOnly` on
  `COneTimePassword` or on a `COneTimePasswordInput` no longer makes a slot read-only; use
  `disabled` to show a code the user cannot change.

### CPasswordInput

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **Renamed `ariaLabelToggler` to
  `ariaToggleLabel`.**
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The toggle icon is rendered by the component
  instead of being drawn by CSS**, and is replaceable through the new `showIcon` / `hideIcon`
  props. `.form-password-action-icon` is gone, the frame is `.form-control-group` and the button is
  `.form-control-action`.

### CPlaceholder

- **`animation="wave"` is a sweeping highlight and the recommended loading animation.** A narrow
  bright band crosses the placeholders every 1.6s instead of a wide gradient every 2s, and it also
  works on text. The opacity pulse is `animation="pulse"` now; `animation="glow"` stays as its alias.
  The prop still has no default. The keyframes are renamed to `placeholder-pulse` with it.
  With reduced motion the wave stops and drops its mask.
- **Placeholders are paler, taller and rounded.** The resting opacity is `.18` (was `.5`) and the
  pulse dips to `.1` (was `.2`); the default height is `1.25em` (was `1em`), capped a quarter em
  below the line height so a placeholder never makes a heading taller, and `.75em`, `1em` and
  `1.75em` for the `xs`, `sm` and `lg` sizes (were `.6em`, `.8em`, `1.2em`). Each placeholder has a
  `--cui-radius-3` corner; a `CButton`, `CAvatar`, `CBadge` or `CChip` with the `placeholder` class
  keeps its own height and corners. The wave reads its own `--cui-placeholder-wave-opacity-max` and
  `-min`.

### CPopover, CTooltip

- **`onShow` and `onHide` fire when the tip starts showing or hiding**, after `delay` and only when
  the visibility actually changes. `onShow` used to fire on the trigger gesture, before
  `delay.show`, and again for a second trigger on a visible tip, while `onHide` also fired after a
  hover that ended before the tip appeared. `onShowChange` reports the requests; a deprecated
  `visible` kept in step through `onShow` and `onHide` belongs on `show` and `onShowChange`.
- **New: `onShown` / `onHidden`**, fired once the entry or exit transition has finished.

### CProgress, CProgressBar

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`thin` is removed from `CProgress`.** It
  rendered `.progress-thin`, which v6 does not ship; set `height` for a slimmer bar.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`color` no longer takes a gradient.** v6
  removes the `bg-*-gradient` utilities the value mapped to, so the `Gradients` union is gone from
  the prop's type. Reach for `.bg-gradient` alongside the color if you want the sheen.

### CRangeSlider

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The slider renders the markup of the
  range.** It is a `<div class="form-range">` with one native `.form-range-input` per handle;
  `className`, `style`, `theme`, `dir`, `hidden`, `role`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and the `ref` land on that `div`, and other input attributes, such
  as `id` (on the first handle) and `aria-describedby`, reach the handles. The classes follow:
  `.range-slider` → `.form-range`, `.range-slider-input` → `.form-range-input`,
  `.range-slider-vertical` → `.form-range-vertical`, `.range-slider-tooltip` →
  `.form-range-tooltip` (now a `<div>`), `.range-slider-ticks`/`.range-slider-tick` →
  `.form-range-ticks`/`.form-range-tick` with the text in `.form-range-tick-label`, and the
  per-tick `.clickable` → `.form-range-ticks-clickable` on the container;
  `.range-slider-inputs-container`, `.range-slider-track` and the `.disabled` class are gone. The
  handles no longer carry `role="slider"`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` or `aria-valuenow`: the
  native inputs expose them.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The handles and the track read the range's
  tokens.** `--cui-range-slider-*` is gone: set `--cui-range-thumb-*`, `--cui-range-track-*`,
  `--cui-range-track-fill-bg` (was `-track-in-range-bg`), `--cui-range-track-disabled-bg` (was
  `-disabled-track-in-range-bg`) and `--cui-range-tick-label-color` and `-font-size` (were
  `--cui-range-slider-label-*`) on the slider. The label padding has no counterpart, the tooltips
  sit like the range's without `--cui-range-slider-tooltip-margin-*`, and a vertical slider's
  height is `--cui-range-vertical-height` and its track width `--cui-range-track-height`.
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`ariaLabels` is `ariaLabel`**, an array with
  one name per handle or a function `(index, total) => string`.
- **The slider is a group named after the field.** The `.form-range` gets `role="group"` with the
  `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you pass, so a screen reader announces the field when the focus
  enters it. With several handles, each handle carries only its own name ("Minimum value"); a
  single handle takes the name of the group. `aria-describedby` describes every handle, and a
  `role` you pass replaces `group` on the slider.
- **The slider takes a validation state.**
  `validationState` shows on the slider and on the handles, and `'invalid'` blocks the submit
  through the first handle until the user moves a handle or the form is reset; the slider calls
  `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` then. See [Validation](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/range-slider/#validation).
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`labels` is `ticks`, `clickableLabels` is
  `clickableTicks`.** An entry is a number (a tick without text), a string (a
  label placed by its position), or `{ value, label, className, style }`; a bare element is no
  longer an entry, pass it as `{ label: <strong>High</strong> }`.
- **Interaction follows the native control.** Pressing a handle no longer moves it; a press on the
  track or a clickable tick moves the nearest handle and it follows the pointer (mouse, touch or
  pen); a form reset restores `defaultValue`. A controlled slider whose parent ignores `onChange`
  keeps the handle on its value instead of letting it follow the pointer until the drag ends.
- **`tooltips` takes `"always"`.** `true` shows a handle's tooltip on hover, drag and focus;
  `"always"` keeps them on.

### CRating

- **A read-only rating submits its value under the `name` you give it.** `readOnly` used to
  disable the radios, so the form left the value out; now they stay enabled, the mouse and the
  keyboard cannot change them, only the checked star takes focus (the first star while no star is checked), and the group carries
  `aria-readonly="true"`. A read-only rating without `name` still submits nothing.
- **A star with keyboard focus shows the focus ring.**
- **A read-only rating shows no tooltips.**
- **The rating takes a validation state and can be required.** `validationState` colours the
  focus ring, and `'invalid'` sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit until
  you drop the state; the rating asks for that with `onValidationStateChange(undefined)` when the
  user picks or clears a star or the form is reset. `required` makes every radio required. See
  [Validation](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/rating/#validation).
- **Empty stars are `--cui-fg-4`**: gray-500 in the light scheme and gray-600 in the dark one, the
  lightest grays that keep 3:1 against the page background. The empty stars of v5 were 38% of the
  text colour, below 3:1 against the page in the light scheme.

### CSidebar

- **`onVisibleChange` is deprecated in favour of `onInViewportChange`.** The callback reports
  whether the sidebar is on screen — it is off-canvas on narrow viewports — not the `show` state,
  and the old name read like the latter's twin. Both fire while the old name is set.
- **`colorScheme="light"` joins `colorScheme="dark"`.** Either value pins the sidebar to one
  scheme whatever the page uses, so a dark navigation column can sit on a light page.
- **Theme variants.** `className="theme-{color}"` paints the surface, text, icons and the
  hover/active links from that colour's slots.
- **Hover and active links read the foreground ladder.** Their text was the pure black/white
  `--cui-emphasis-color` and their background the Sass-computed `--cui-tertiary-bg-translucent`;
  they are `--cui-fg-body` and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--cui-fg-body) 10%, transparent)` now.
  Slightly stronger than before on a light sidebar, slightly weaker on a dark one.

### CSmartTable

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The props are renamed.** Every filter prop
  says which filter it means, the column configuration drops the v3 underscores and the sorter
  icons take the names the other data components use:

  | v5 | v6 |
  | --- | --- |
  | `elementCover` | `loadingContent` |
  | `itemsNumber` | `totalItems` |
  | `onSelectedItemsChange` | `onSelectedChange` |
  | `sortingIcon`, `sortingIconAscending`, `sortingIconDescending` | `sortNeutralIcon`, `sortAscendingIcon`, `sortDescendingIcon` |
  | `tableFilter`, `tableFilterValue`, `defaultTableFilterValue`, `onTableFilterChange` | `globalFilter`, `globalFilterValue`, `defaultGlobalFilterValue`, `onGlobalFilterChange` |
  | `tableFilterLabel`, `tableFilterPlaceholder` | `globalFilterLabel`, `globalFilterPlaceholder` |
  | `columnSorter={{ resetable: true }}` | `columnSorter={{ resettable: true }}` |
  | `Column._style`, `Column._props` | `Column.headerStyle`, `Column.headerProps` |
  | `Column._colStyle`, `Column._colProps` | `Column.cellStyle`, `Column.cellProps` |
  | `Column.sorter: false` | `Column.sortable: false` (`sorter` is the comparator only) |
  | `Column.filter: false` | `Column.filterable: false` (`filter` is the custom filter only) |
  | `FooterItem._props` | `FooterItem.props` |
  | `onSelectAll` | — (`onSelectedChange` carries the same information) |

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **A column group is `{ label, children }`.**
  The group label moves from `group` to `label` and a group no longer needs a `key`:
  `{ group: 'Address', key: 'address', children: [...] }` becomes
  `{ label: 'Address', children: [...] }`.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **One `external` prop replaces the six
  `external` options.** `columnFilter`, `tableFilter`, `columnSorter`, `pagination`,
  `itemsPerPageSelect` and `selectAll` each carried an `external` flag; `external` on the table
  says the same thing once — the items arrive already filtered, sorted and sliced, so the table
  renders them as they are and only reports the requested state. Pair it with `totalItems` so it
  can compute the number of pages. Where the option only meant "let the parent own this piece of
  state", pass the controlled prop instead.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`SorterValue` is `{ column, direction }` and
  the sorter value is always an array.** `state: 'asc' | 'desc' | 0` becomes
  `direction: 'asc' | 'desc'`, with an absent entry standing for "not sorted", and
  `sorterValue`, `defaultSorterValue` and the `onSorterChange` payload are `SorterValue[]` whether
  or not `columnSorter={{ multiple: true }}` is set — no more `Array.isArray` at the call site.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`Item._selected` is removed.** Seed the
  selection with `defaultSelected`, or own it with `selected` — the flag in the data was a second
  source of truth and the two drifted apart.

- **The selection checkboxes and the cleaner button have accessible names.**
  `ariaSelectAllLabel` (`'Select all rows'`), `ariaSelectRowLabel` (`'Select row'`) and
  `ariaCleanerLabel` (`'Clear filters and sorting'`) are read by screen readers; before, none of
  the three controls had a name at all.

- **`itemKey` identifies a row.** With it set, selection and React keys compare `item[itemKey]`
  instead of the whole object, so a selected row survives a re-fetch of the data.

- **`cleanerIcon` replaces the cleaner button's icon**, the way the sorter icons already could.

- **The selection checkboxes render `CCheckbox`.** The select-all control in the head and the
  per-row control in the body are `<input class="check">` now, not `.form-check-input`, so custom
  CSS keyed on the old class needs updating.

- **The chrome is composable.** `CSmartTable` renders the layout it always did as long as it has
  no children; pass children and it renders them instead, so `CSmartTableFilter`,
  `CSmartTableCleaner`, `CSmartTableContent`, `CSmartTablePagination` and
  `CSmartTableItemsPerPage` go wherever you put them, next to your own markup.
  `useSmartTableContext()` reads the same state — the items, the page, the filters, the sorter and
  the selection — so a part of your own is a component that calls it.

- **`useSmartTable(options)` runs the table without any of its markup.** The whole state — the
  filters, the sorter, the pages, the selection with `isSelected`, `toggle`, `toggleAll` and
  `selectedAll` — is a hook you can call with the state props of `CSmartTable` and render however
  you like, tables included or not. `CSmartTable` itself is that hook plus the layout.

### CSpinner

- **`visuallyHiddenLabel` is deprecated in favour of `ariaLoadingLabel`**, which works as
  `ariaLoadingLabel` does on `CLoadingButton`: the text defaults to `'Loading'` instead of
  `'Loading...'`, and an empty string hides the spinner from screen readers. `visuallyHiddenLabel`
  still sets the text while `ariaLoadingLabel` is unset.

- **Spinners are sized in `em`, not `rem`.** A spinner is `1em` square now, so it takes the font
  size of whatever it sits in instead of being a fixed 32 px block. Inside a button or a heading it
  lands at the size you previously had to ask for with `size="sm"`; standalone it is half of what it
  was. Set `--cui-spinner-width` / `--cui-spinner-height` to go back to a fixed size.

- **`size="sm"` renders `.spinner-sm`, not `.spinner-border-sm` / `.spinner-grow-sm`.** The prop is
  unchanged; only custom CSS targeting the old per-type classes needs updating.

- **`.spinner-grow` eases with `ease-in-out`** instead of pulsing linearly. Override
  `--cui-spinner-animation-timing-function` to change either spinner's easing.

- **`.spinner-rotate` is new.** Pass it through `className` on any element to spin your own artwork
  without inheriting the bordered circle.

### CStepper

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`--cui-stepper-step-indicator-active-bg` is removed.** The active step's
  indicator background is a 5% tint of the stepper's theme color, or of
  `--cui-stepper-step-indicator-active-color` without one. To give it another background, set
  `--cui-stepper-step-indicator-bg` on `.stepper-step-button.active` in your stylesheet.

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`activeStepIndex` and
  `defaultActiveStepIndex` are removed.** Deprecated since 5.16.0 for their 0-based indexing; use
  `activeStepNumber` / `defaultActiveStepNumber`, which count from 1.
- **A failed step moves focus to the first invalid control, and the panes are no longer live
  regions.** With a `noValidate` form the invalid controls also get `aria-invalid`, and the message
  is read with the field: the stepper adds the `.invalid-feedback` that follows the control, which
  covers `feedbackInvalid`, or the elements named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback`, to its
  `aria-describedby`. The panes used to read out every message that appeared in them; a message that
  changes while the user types is now silent, so pass the ones that have to be heard to
  [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages).
- **`onStepValidationComplete` runs before the stepper decides.** A validity it sets with
  `setCustomValidity()` blocks the step, and `isValid` tells whether every control passed before
  it ran. A `noValidate` step form is marked each time the step is validated, also when it passes,
  so `data-coreui-validate="valid"` now marks the valid controls of a passing step with `.is-valid`.
- **A non-linear stepper validates the step being left.** With `linear={false}`, clicking a later
  step used to skip validation; it now runs it like `next()` does and stays put while the step is
  invalid. Going back is never blocked. Add `validation={false}` for the old behaviour.

### CTable

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`caption` is the caption and `captionTop` is
  a boolean.** `caption="top"` no longer carries a magic value and `captionTop` no longer carries
  text: `<CTable caption="top"><CTableCaption>…</CTableCaption></CTable>` becomes
  `<CTable captionTop>…</CTable>`, and `` becomes
  ``.
- **New: `card`** wraps the table in a card's border and corner radius, clips its cells and drops
  its bottom margin and the borders that would stack on the frame. With `responsive` the class lands on the same
  wrapper. See [Card-like tables](https://coreui.io/react/docs/components/table/#card-like-tables).

### CToast, CToaster

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CToaster.push` is gone; toasts come from a
  store.** `createToaster({ placement, limit, timeout })` builds the store outside the React tree
  and `` renders it: `add(options)` returns the id (an existing id
  updates in place and bumps `updateKey`, a closing one is replaced), `update(id, options | fn(prev))` rewrites a
  toast, `close(id?)` hides one or all, `promise(p, { loading, success, error })` follows an
  asynchronous operation. A toast is options — `title`, `description`, `theme`, `timeout`
  (`0` = sticky), `priority` (`'normal'` or `'high'`, the polite or the assertive live region), `dismissible`, `action`,
  `render` — instead of a `<CToast>` element. `limit` keeps the newest toasts visible and leaves
  the oldest in the DOM as `inert` and hidden. `useToaster()` returns the store inside the
  container. `<CToaster>` without `toaster` stays a container for `<CToast>` children.

  ```jsx
  // v5
  const [toast, addToast] = useState()
  <CButton onClick={() => addToast(<CToast><CToastBody>Saved</CToastBody></CToast>)} />
  

  // v6
  const toaster = createToaster({ placement: 'top-end' })
  <CButton onClick={() => toaster.add({ description: 'Saved' })} />
  
  ```
- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **`CToast` drops `index` and `innerKey`, and
  `onClose` / `onShow` fire without an argument** — they were the plumbing of `push`, and a toast
  rendered by the store is identified by its `key` and `data-coreui-toast-id`.
- **Placement is one class.** `<CToaster placement>` renders `.toast-container-{placement}` in
  place of the `position-fixed top-0 end-0` utility stack; the edge inset comes from
  `--cui-toast-container-inset`. The container is a `region` landmark named `Notifications`.
- **The store carries the rest of the behavior.** `ariaLabel` names the landmark, `enter` and
  `leave` pick the edges a toast slides in from and out to, `pauseOnHover` (on by default) stops
  every timer while the pointer or focus is inside the container, and `stack: true` piles the
  toasts up newest-in-front and spreads them out on hover. `<CToaster portal={false}>` keeps the
  container where it is written instead of portalling it onto `document.body`.
- **Announcements moved off the toast.** A toast rendered by the toaster carries no `role`,
  `aria-live` or `aria-atomic`; every `add()` and `update()` passes the string parts of `title`
  and `description` to `announce()`, which reads them at the priority `priority` selects. A standalone `<CToast>` keeps its own
  `role="alert"` defaults.
- **New: `translucent`** renders `.toast-translucent` — the background shows through the toast,
  blurred, and the header thins out with it.
- **The fade moved to CSS.** The toast no longer renders the `fade` and `showing` helper classes
  and no longer drives its own opacity — `show` alone drives the transition, with
  `@starting-style` supplying the state to animate from and a discrete `display` transition
  keeping the toast laid out until the fade-out finishes. `animation={false}` now renders
  `.toast-instant` instead of dropping `fade`, and finishes both directions immediately.
  The prop itself is unchanged; only custom CSS targeting `.toast.fade` or `.toast.showing`
  needs updating. Tune the motion with `--cui-toast-transition-duration` and
  `--cui-toast-transition-timing`.

### CWidgetStatsA – CWidgetStatsF

- <span className="badge bg-danger">Breaking</span> **The six widget components are removed.** They
  were the one family in the library with no stylesheet of their own: each rendered a `CCard` and a
  fixed stack of utility classes, so they carried a layout decision rather than styling you cannot
  write in place. Compose the same markup directly, which also lets a widget diverge from the six
  shapes we happened to ship:

```jsx
// Before
<CWidgetStatsF color="primary" icon={<CIcon icon={cilSettings} height={24} />} title="Users" value="87.500" />

// After
<CCard>
  <CCardBody className="d-flex flex-row align-items-center">
    <div className="me-4 fg-white bg-primary p-4">
      <CIcon icon={cilSettings} height={24} />
    </div>
    <div>
      <div className="fs-6 fw-semibold fg-primary">87.500</div>
      <div className="fg-2 text-uppercase fw-semibold small">Users</div>
    </div>
  </CCardBody>
</CCard>
```

- **The six shapes live on as [blocks](https://coreui.io/react/docs/blocks/widgets/).** Every one of them is on that page as
  markup to copy, with the names they go by now: `CWidgetStatsA` is the stat with a chart,
  `CWidgetStatsB` the stat with a progress bar, `CWidgetStatsC` the one with an icon and a progress
  bar, `CWidgetStatsD` the stat group, `CWidgetStatsE` the compact stat and `CWidgetStatsF` the stat
  with an icon.
- **Three of them did not survive the v6 stylesheet unchanged, which is the other half of the
  reason they are going.** `CCardBody` became a flex column in v6, so `CWidgetStatsA` stacked its
  menu under the figure instead of putting it in the corner, `CWidgetStatsF` stacked its icon above
  the text, and `CWidgetStatsD` stacked its values instead of laying them in a row. The blocks carry
  the `flex-row` and `w-100` those layouts now need.

# React Form Controls

> React input and textarea components. Give textual form controls like `<input>`s and `<textarea>`s an upgrade with custom styles, sizing, focus states, and more.

## Example

```html
import { CForm, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormTextarea } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlExample = () => (
  <CForm>
    <div className="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="exampleFormControlInput1">Email address</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput type="email" id="exampleFormControlInput1" placeholder="name@example.com" />
    </div>
    <div className="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="exampleFormControlTextarea1">Example textarea</CFormLabel>
      <CFormTextarea id="exampleFormControlTextarea1" rows={3}></CFormTextarea>
    </div>
  </CForm>
)
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`<CFormField>`](https://coreui.io/react/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
import React from 'react'
import { CFormField, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CFormText } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlFormFieldExample = () => {
  return (
    <CFormField>
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="formControlField">Email address</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput type="email" id="formControlField" placeholder="name@example.com" />
      <CFormText>We will never share your email with anyone else.</CFormText>
    </CFormField>
  )
}
```

## Sizing

Set heights using `size` property like `size="lg"` and `size="sm"`.

```html
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlSizingExample = () => (
  <>
    <CFormInput type="text" size="lg" placeholder="Large input" aria-label="lg input example" />
    <CFormInput type="text" placeholder="Default input" aria-label="default input example" />
    <CFormInput type="text" size="sm" placeholder="Small input" aria-label="sm input example" />
  </>
)
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` boolean attribute on an input to give it a grayed out appearance and remove pointer events.

```html
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlDisabledExample = () => (
  <>
    <CFormInput
      type="text"
      placeholder="Disabled input"
      aria-label="Disabled input example"
      disabled
    />
    <CFormInput
      type="text"
      placeholder="Disabled readonly input"
      aria-label="Disabled input example"
      disabled
      readOnly
    />
  </>
)
```

## Readonly

Add the `readOnly` boolean attribute on an input to prevent modification of the input's value. Read-only inputs appear lighter (just like disabled inputs), but retain the standard cursor.

```html
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlReadonlyExample = () => (
  <CFormInput
    type="text"
    placeholder="Readonly input here..."
    aria-label="readonly input example"
    readOnly
  />
)
```

## Readonly plain text

If you want to have `<input readonly>` elements in your form styled as plain text, use the `plainText` boolean property to remove the default form field styling and preserve the correct margin and padding.

```html
import { CCol, CFormInput, CFormLabel, CRow } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlReadonlyPlainTextExample = () => (
  <>
    <CRow className="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="staticEmail" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
        Email
      </CFormLabel>
      <CCol sm={10}>
        <CFormInput
          type="text"
          id="staticEmail"
          defaultValue="email@example.com"
          readOnly
          plainText
        />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
    <CRow className="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword" className="col-sm-2 col-form-label">
        Password
      </CFormLabel>
      <CCol sm={10}>
        <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword" />
      </CCol>
    </CRow>
  </>
)
```

```html
import { CButton, CCol, CForm, CFormInput, CFormLabel } from '@coreui/react'

export const FormControlReadonlyPlainTextInlineExample = () => (
  <CForm className="row g-4">
    <CCol xs="auto">

        Email
      </CFormLabel>

        Password
      </CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword2" placeholder="Password" />
    </CCol>
    <CCol xs="auto">
      <CButton theme="primary" type="submit" className="mb-4">
        Confirm identity
      </CButton>
    </CCol>
  </CForm>
)
```

## API

### CFormInput

```jsx
import { CFormInput } from '@coreui/react-pro'
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the component. |
| `delay` | `number \| boolean` | `false` | Delay onChange event while typing. If set to true onChange event will be delayed 500ms, you can also provide the number of milliseconds you want to delay the onChange event. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `feedback` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback for the current `validationState` — rendered only while the state is set, and styled after it. For the client-side mode, where the browser owns the state, use `feedbackValid` and `feedbackInvalid` instead. |
| `feedbackInvalid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is invalid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `feedbackValid` | `ReactNode` | - | Feedback the stylesheet reveals while the control is valid — always rendered, so it works with client-side validation, where the browser decides the state. |
| `floatingClassName` | `string` | - | A string of all className you want applied to the floating label wrapper. |
| `floatingLabel` | `ReactNode` | - | Provide a floating label for the component — the text rests inside the field and floats once it has focus or a value. |
| `floatingLabelAlways` | `boolean` | - | Keeps the floating label floated and the placeholder visible while the field is empty. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control invalid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Add a caption for a component. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called immediately after the `value` prop changes. |
| `onInput` | `InputEventHandler<HTMLInputElement>` | - | Method called on every `input` event of the field. |
| `onValidationStateChange` | `((validationState: ValidationState \| undefined) => void)` | - | Callback fired with `undefined` when the user changes the value, or the form is reset, while `validationState` (or the deprecated `invalid`) is set. A given state is a verdict on the value it was given for; clear it here to let the browser's own validation show again. |
| `plainText` | `boolean` | - | Render the component styled as plain text. Removes the default form field styling and preserve the correct margin and padding. Recommend to use only along side `readonly`. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | - | Toggle the readonly state for the component. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg"` | - | Size the component small or large. |
| `text` | `ReactNode` | - | Add helper text to the component. |
| `tooltipFeedback` | `boolean` | - | Display validation feedback in a styled tooltip. |
| `type` | `string` | `text` | Specifies the type of component. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | - | Mark the control valid. |
| `validationState` | `'valid' \| 'invalid' \| string` | - | The validation state, rendered as the `is-{state}` class; `'invalid'` also sets `aria-invalid` and blocks the submit. Any custom state declared in the `$form-validation-states` Sass map is accepted. The user's next change of the value asks to drop it through `onValidationStateChange`. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| string[]` | - | The `value` attribute of component. |

# React Form Components

> Examples and usage guidelines for form control styles, layout options, and custom components for creating a wide variety of forms.

## Overview

CoreUI’s form controls expand on our Rebooted form styles with classes. Use these classes to opt into their customized displays for a more consistent rendering across browsers and devices.

Be sure to use an appropriate `type` attribute on all inputs (e.g., `email` for email address or `number` for numerical information) to take advantage of newer input controls like email verification, number selection, and more.

Here’s a quick example to demonstrate CoreUI’s form styles. Keep reading for documentation on required classes, form layout, and more.

```jsx
<CForm>
  <div className="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel htmlFor="exampleInputEmail1">Email address</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput type="email" id="exampleInputEmail1" aria-describedby="emailHelp" />
    <CFormText id="emailHelp">We'll never share your email with anyone else.</CFormText>
  </div>
  <div className="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel htmlFor="exampleInputPassword1">Email Password</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput type="password" id="exampleInputPassword1" />
  </div>
  <CFormField className="mb-4">
    <CCheckbox
      label="Check me out"
      onChange={(e) => {
        console.log(e.target)
      }}
    />
  </CFormField>
  <CButton type="submit" theme="primary">
    Submit
  </CButton>
</CForm>
```

## Form text

Block-level or inline-level form text can be created using `<CFormText>`.

Associating form text with form controls
Form text should be explicitly associated with the form control it relates to using the aria-describedby attribute. This will ensure that assistive technologies—such as screen readers—will announce this form text when the user focuses or enters the control.

Form text below inputs can be styled with `<CFormText>`. If a block-level element will be used, a top margin is added for easy spacing from the inputs above.

```jsx
<CForm>
  <div className="mb-4">
    <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword5">Password</CFormLabel>
    <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword5" aria-describedby="passwordHelpBlock" />
    <CFormText id="passwordHelpBlock">
      Your password must be 8-20 characters long, contain letters and numbers, and must not
      contain spaces, special characters, or emoji.
    </CFormText>
  </div>
</CForm>
```

Inline text can use any typical inline HTML element (be it a `<span>`, `<small>`, or something else) with nothing more than the `.form-text` class.

```jsx
<CRow className="g-4 align-items-center">
  <CCol xs="auto">
    <CFormLabel htmlFor="inputPassword6" className="col-form-label">
      Password
    </CFormLabel>
  </CCol>
  <CCol xs="auto">
    <CFormInput type="password" id="inputPassword6" aria-describedby="passwordHelpInline" />
  </CCol>
  <CCol xs="auto">
    <CFormText as="span" id="passwordHelpInline">
      Must be 8-20 characters long.
    </CFormText>
  </CCol>
</CRow>
```

## Disabled forms

Add the `disabled` boolean attribute on an input to prevent user interactions and make it appear lighter.

```jsx
<CFormLabel id="disabledInput" type="text" placeholder="Disabled input here..." disabled />
```

Add the `disabled` attribute to a `<fieldset>` to disable all the controls within. Browsers treat all native form controls (`<input>`, `<select>`, and `<button>` elements) inside a `<fieldset disabled>` as disabled, preventing both keyboard and mouse interactions on them.

However, if your form also includes custom button-like elements such as `<CButton>...</CButton>`, these will only be given a style of `pointer-events: none`, meaning they are still focusable and operable using the keyboard. In this case, you must manually modify these controls by adding `tabindex="-1"` to prevent them from receiving focus and `aria-disabled="disabled"` to signal their state to assistive technologies.

```jsx
<CForm>
  <fieldset disabled>
    <legend>Disabled fieldset example</legend>
    <div className="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="disabledTextInput">Disabled input</CFormLabel>
      <CFormInput id="disabledTextInput" placeholder="Disabled input" />
    </div>
    <div className="mb-4">
      <CFormLabel htmlFor="disabledSelect">Disabled select menu</CFormLabel>
      <CFormSelect id="disabledSelect">
        <option>Disabled select</option>
      </CFormSelect>
    </div>
    <CFormField className="mb-4">
      <CCheckbox id="disabledFieldsetCheck" label="Can't check this" disabled />
    </CFormField>
    <CButton theme="primary" type="submit">Submit</CButton>
  </fieldset>
</CForm>
```

## Accessibility

Ensure that all form controls have an appropriate accessible name so that their purpose can be conveyed to users of assistive technologies. The simplest way to achieve this is to use a `<CFormLabel>` element, or — in the case of buttons — to include sufficiently descriptive text as part of the `<CButton>...</CButton>` content.

For situations where it's not possible to include a visible `<CFormLabel>` or appropriate text content, there are alternative ways of still providing an accessible name, such as:

- `<CFormLabel>` elements hidden using the `.visually-hidden` class
- Pointing to an existing element that can act as a label using `aria-labelledby`
- Providing a `title` attribute
- Explicitly setting the accessible name on an element using `aria-label`

If none of these are present, assistive technologies may resort to using the `placeholder` attribute as a fallback for the accessible name on `<input />` and `<textarea>` elements. The examples in this section provide a few suggested, case-specific approaches.

While using visually hidden content (`.visually-hidden`, `aria-label`, and even `placeholder` content, which disappears once a form field has content) will benefit assistive technology users, a lack of visible label text may still be problematic for certain users. Some form of visible label is generally the best approach, both for accessibility and usability.

## Customizing

Many form values are set once on `:root` as `--cui-btn-input-*` tokens and re-used by every form component. Each field points its own `--cui-control-*` tokens at them and declares those on itself, so one field is restyled through its `--cui-control-*` tokens and every field at once through `--cui-btn-input-*`. The checkbox, radio and switch share a few `--cui-control-*` tokens on `:root` as well.

### CSS variables

Buttons and form controls share the size and type of one frame, declared once on `:root`: padding, minimum height, font size, weight and line height, border width and radius, and the transition duration and timing. Retuning those there moves buttons and fields together. The color tokens (`-fg`, `-bg`, `-border-color`, `-box-shadow` and `-focus-*`) belong to the fields; a button takes its colors from its variant. A component that needs its own frame overrides the token on itself.

```scss
--cui-btn-input-fg: var(--cui-fg-body),
--cui-btn-input-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
--cui-btn-input-font-weight: var(--cui-body-font-weight),

--cui-btn-input-gap: .375rem,
--cui-btn-input-min-height: calc(var(--cui-btn-input-line-height) * 1em + var(--cui-btn-input-padding-y) * 2 + var(--cui-btn-input-border-width) * 2),
--cui-btn-input-padding-y: .375rem,
--cui-btn-input-padding-x: .75rem,
--cui-btn-input-font-size: var(--cui-body-font-size),
--cui-btn-input-line-height: var(--cui-body-line-height),
--cui-btn-input-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
--cui-btn-input-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
--cui-btn-input-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
--cui-btn-input-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-inset),
--cui-btn-input-focus-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
--cui-btn-input-focus-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-primary-base) 50%, var(--cui-bg-body)),
--cui-btn-input-transition-property: "border-color, box-shadow",
--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property: "color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow",
--cui-btn-input-transition-duration: .15s,
--cui-btn-input-transition-timing: ease-in-out,
--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity: .65,

--cui-btn-input-xs-gap: .25rem,
--cui-btn-input-xs-min-height: calc(var(--cui-btn-input-xs-line-height) * 1em + var(--cui-btn-input-xs-padding-y) * 2 + var(--cui-btn-input-border-width) * 2),
--cui-btn-input-xs-padding-y: .125rem,
--cui-btn-input-xs-padding-x: .5rem,
--cui-btn-input-xs-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-xs),

--cui-btn-input-xs-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),

--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-y: .25rem,
--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-x: .5rem,
--cui-btn-input-sm-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
--cui-btn-input-sm-line-height: var(--cui-line-height-sm),
--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),

--cui-btn-input-lg-gap: .375rem,
--cui-btn-input-lg-min-height: calc(var(--cui-btn-input-lg-line-height) * 1em + var(--cui-btn-input-lg-padding-y) * 2 + var(--cui-btn-input-border-width) * 2),
```
